author: ksharma-xyz
body:
## What

Adds `NetworkError`, a typed vocabulary for why a network call failed, plus `NetworkException` as the single throwable services put into a failed `Result`. Nothing produces one yet: the classifier is #1985 and the service migration is later in the stack.

Until now every network failure reached the UI as `isError: Boolean`, so airplane mode, an NSW outage and a changed response shape were indistinguishable and produced the same screen.

## Changes

- `NetworkError`: eight cases. The two easiest to confuse are deliberately separate. `Offline` means the device has no transport, which is the rider's connection. `Unreachable` means transport was fine but the host could not be reached, which is not their fault and is worth retrying. Neither can be told apart from the thrown exception alone, which is why the classifier in #1985 takes the observed transport state as a second input.
- `isRetryable`, `recoversOnReconnect` and `isConnectionProblem` live beside the type rather than at call sites, and each is an exhaustive `when` with no `else`. A new case cannot compile until someone has decided what it means for all three. Two screens can no longer disagree about whether an NSW outage is the rider's fault.
- `Offline` is deliberately not retryable even though it obviously can succeed later. Retrying immediately just burns the connect timeout again, so it recovers through the reconnect path instead.
- `kind` is written out rather than derived from the class name, so renaming a case cannot silently split an analytics metric in two. It ignores the status code so upstream failures aggregate into one bucket.
- `NetworkException` keeps `kotlin.Result` rather than introducing a sealed `ApiResult`. A sealed type makes failure impossible to ignore, which is better in the abstract, but rewrites every service signature, call site and fake in a codebase where `suspendSafeResult` already threads `Result` and already handles `CancellationException` correctly. The looseness accepted is that `Result` allows a failure to be dropped silently; the trigger for revisiting that is recorded in the doc later in the stack.
- `asNetworkError()` falls back to `Unknown` rather than throwing. A call site handling a failure is the worst possible place to raise a second one.

## Testing

- `./gradlew :core:network:testAndroidHostTest` green, 12 new tests
- `./gradlew :core:network:compileKotlinIosSimulatorArm64` green
- `./scripts/fullQualityChecks.sh` green
- `./gradlew testAndroidHostTest --continue` green
- detekt green

The tests pin the decisions the compiler cannot check: that a 4xx is never retried, that `Offline` is the only case recovery waits for, and that an upstream outage is never presented as the rider's connection problem.

body:
The pages move from `apps/docs/` into `apps/docs/src/`, which `@viteplus/versions` serves at the root of the site. Folders under `archive/` become frozen copies of older versions, and a Version entry in the navigation moves between them.

`archive/` is empty. The first copy is worth making when the pages in `src/` stop describing the published packages. Freezing a copy of what is already at the root would only double the site and the search index.

The two generated directories follow the move. The core build writes the error pages to `src/errors/`, and `scripts/typedoc.mjs` writes the API reference to `src/reference/`.

A code block tagged `ts twoslash` is compiled by TypeScript at build time and renders the types it found on hover. Two blocks use it, in the dialogs and data models guides, where the types are the point. It is opt-in per block because it runs the compiler, and because a block that stops compiling fails the build. `@vttforge/core` is a dev dependency of the docs app so those blocks resolve their imports.

The app's own readme was being built as a page at `/docs/README`. It is excluded now.

Checked locally: `pnpm build`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm knip`, and `node scripts/assemble-site.mjs`. The assembled site serves the landing page, `/docs/` and `/design-system/` as before. The version switcher and the twoslash hovers were checked in a browser against the assembled site.

author: sionic-khope
body:
## Feature Report

This PR implements #1458, #1457, #1456, #1454 and #1453, including the
explicitly approved canonical-prefetch prerequisite #1452. Local validation,
exact-head CI and the independent final gate review passed.

### What Changed

OMH preserves an explicitly active workflow across follow-ups, binds context
budgets to the effective model route, escalates delegated decisions to the
parent, reports synchronization fidelity, and diagnoses expected-memory
failures using canonical selection and record-bound prefetch receipts.

### Why This Exists

A neutral reply could lose the operating workflow, while a context plan could
outlive its model-capacity assumptions. A delegated question could look like
implementation failure. Memory availability and aggregate recall counts could
not explain partial synchronization or where an expected memory stopped.
The live provider also had a reduced ranking implementation that disagreed
with handoff recall about scope, lifecycle, priority and budgets.

### User / Operator Impact

- A user can answer an interjection and continue the active checklist without
  repeating its workflow name.
- A changed route gets a capacity comparison: equivalent capacity preserves
  the plan, smaller capacity requires recovery, and unknown limits stay unknown.
- The supervising session asks one bounded delegated question and explicitly
  resumes the affected unit without discarding completed sibling evidence.
- Memory-sync distinguishes complete, truncated, skipped, failed and unknown
  synchronization, without contacting a provider during inspection.
- A recall complaint can distinguish local storage/eligibility/selection from
  provider rendering and explain the remaining uncertainty without rewriting
  memory automatically.
- Live prefetch and handoffs use one selection contract. Cross-project
  preferences have an explicit user-global label rather than inheriting
  authority from their storage directory.

Normal users express these intents in Hermes. The documented backend commands
are agent/operator controls, not a new everyday command checklist.

### How It Works

Session-bound workflow and route-capacity records produce bounded projections
at `pre_llm_call`. Explicit lifecycle changes take precedence over continuation.
The projection does not claim compaction, provider usage or execution.

Fanout results accept validated `input_required` metadata. Parent decisions
bind to contract, workspace, attempt and round identities; redispatch uses the
atomically validated answer and preserves lineage. Clarification rounds and
process retries are separate. The integration with current main maps a waiting
decision to `awaiting_input`, not a generic failed unit.

Synchronization posture adds provider-neutral fidelity dimensions and
per-attempt outcomes. An explicit reservation API prevents cooperating,
independently approved hosts from reusing attempt/input identities. It does
not call a provider or grant write approval.

The standalone plugin and handoff facade share `select_memory_recall`.
The provider supplies reviewed snapshots and explicit scopes, then renders
a ranked prefix under its separate section budget. Its redacted receipt binds
selected/rendered IDs, digests, exclusions, truncation and configuration.
Served counts follow the returned pack and reset across sessions.

Incident diagnosis checks receipt integrity, session, store, configuration,
scope and rendered-record digest. Missing evidence stays unknown. The retained
retrieval suite now compares both the real adapter and provider lifecycle
against canonical selection; injected divergences fail the case.

### Files And Contracts Touched

- Workflow state, `active_workflow_context*`, `context_budget_plan*`, context
  and state commands, canonical plugin hook declarations and guidance.
- `src/coding/fanout_clarification*`, result validation, dispatch, journal,
  status, root commands and wrapper follow-up projection.
- `memory_sync_fidelity*`, `memory_sync_reservations.py`, posture commands
  and memory-sync routing/guidance.
- `memory_recall_selector.py`, `memory_recall_support.py`, provider snapshot
  and rendering paths, `memory_prefetch_receipt.py`, incident modules and
  `memory_evaluation.py`.
- Canonical generated skills/references and workflow documentation; new
  fidelity, incident and prefetch references; focused contract and regression
  tests with positive and negative controls.

### Affected Surfaces

- [x] Hermes chat or wrapper
- [x] Codex
- [x] Claude Code
- [x] Hermes runtime or handoff
- [x] Generic executor
- [x] Not executor-specific

## Validation

Current integrated head: `0ed43c0fa4d7f3b79697dde12fc4742ebb5b233b`.

- [x] `uv run --group lint ruff check src tests`
- [x] `PYTHONPATH=tests uv run python -m unittest discover -s tests -v`
  Local final run: 11,303 tests, exit 0, three conditional skips.
- [x] `uv run python -m compileall -q src tests`
- [x] `uv run python -m omh.cli docs workflows --check`
- [x] `uv run python -m omh.cli docs roles --check`
- [x] `uv run python -m omh.cli docs capability-families --check`
- [x] `uv run python -m omh.cli harness validate`
- [x] `uv run python -m omh.cli release checklist --json`
- [x] `uv run python -m omh.cli release hermes-smoke`
  Exercised through the final installed-wheel smoke in plan mode.
- [x] `git diff --check`
- [x] `omh --help`
- [x] Installed-wheel CLI/help and nested command-content smoke in fresh
  temporary homes with `--include-command-smoke`; cleanup checked.
  The outer setup smoke is plan mode, not observed live setup execution.
- [ ] Workflow-learning review queue smoke: those contracts did not change.
- [x] All 36 local acceptance scenarios and the separate native W3 scenario
  passed on the integrated tree, with cleanup receipts.
- [x] Native Windows CI, including both full-suite shards.
- [x] Manual supervising Hermes conversation: three actual model turns with
  the real plugin; interjection answered and checklist resumed.

Additional generated/documentation gates passed: navigation, claims,
ULW inventory/site and the shipped model chain table. Offline source/wheel
builds passed. The merge-specific regression run passed 303 tests; the
credential-fixture correction passed 15 policy/prefetch tests.

### Observed Evidence

[CI run 34663093109](https://github.com/rlaope/oh-my-hermes/actions/runs/34663093109)
passed all 14 checks at the current head: Linux Python 3.11/3.12, native
Windows shards and quarantine lanes, distribution on Linux/macOS, aggregate
and DCO. All nine shard/quarantine records account for every planned ID
without missing, duplicate or unexpected execution. Every lane executed all
99 feature tests and the S2 regression without skipping them.

The local discovery run contains 38 repeated IDs; its 11,265 unique IDs
exactly match the CI plan. Native-platform conditional skips remain explicit,
not relabeled as execution.

The parent reran every local B/W/Q/F/M scenario on the integrated tree.
Native W3 separately used the installed Hermes `AIAgent`, the real OMH plugin
from this commit, and the configured `openai-codex/gpt-5.6-sol` route.
All three turns carried active workflow context; the interjection was answered
and the checklist resumed. Only metadata and response hashes were retained.
The isolated profile, checkout and process group were removed.

The Phase E DAG completed all six nodes without restarting its four completed
producers during docs recovery. Its independent verifier ran all 11 required
commands and actual M2/M6/M7/M8 scenarios successfully. Synthetic delivery/use
classification is explicitly separate from actual provider-class rendering
and from native Hermes evidence.

Earlier failures remain historical failures. The pre-integration local suite
ran 11,039 tests and found one fake AWS-shaped literal in a new test; it was
replaced with the existing assembled fixture, not an excluded scanner path.
An earlier local S2 probe failure is also preserved

author: ksharma-xyz
body:
## What

Implements `toNetworkError`, the `expect`/`actual` that turns a thrown exception plus the transport state observed when it landed into a typed `NetworkError`. Nothing calls it yet; the services start returning it later in the stack.

## Changes

- The signature takes two inputs, and that is the crux of the design. Neither source can classify alone. The OS transport state is a hint rather than a fact, because a device behind a captive portal, on a dropped VPN or on a carrier blackholing packets all report a usable network. And the exception alone cannot do it either: on Android, airplane mode and a genuine DNS failure on a working network both surface as `UnknownHostException`. The same throwable therefore classifies as `Offline` or `Unreachable` depending on what the OS was reporting, which are different sentences to a rider and only one of them is their fault.
- Note the parameter polarity: `isTransportDown`, matching `TransportState.mayClaimOffline`, which stays false while the state is still `Unknown`. An app that has not yet heard from the OS must not tell a rider they are offline.
- Everything Ktor raises above the engine is classified once in `toSharedNetworkError` and delegated to from both actuals, so the shared behaviour cannot drift between platforms. That drift has bitten this codebase before, see `docs/learning/2026-08-22-two-platforms-two-vocabularies.md`.
- `CancellationException` is rethrown rather than classified. A rider leaving a screen cancels the job, and turning that into a failure paints an error state over a screen nobody is looking at.
- `CaptivePortalException` exists so a Wi-Fi login page can be told apart from a genuine schema change. Both surface as a failure to read the body and only the content type separates them, so the distinction has to be drawn while the response headers are still in hand. The validator that raises it lands with the client factory work.

## Testing

- `./gradlew :core:network:testAndroidHostTest` green, 10 new tests
- `./gradlew :core:network:compileKotlinIosSimulatorArm64` green
- `./scripts/fullQualityChecks.sh` green
- `./gradlew testAndroidHostTest --continue` green
- detekt green

The Android tests drive a **real** Ktor OkHttp client at real addresses rather than constructing exception instances by hand: an unresolvable `.invalid` host (RFC 2606), an unrouted TEST-NET-3 address (RFC 5737) and a closed loopback port. A test that hand-builds `UnknownHostException` proves the branch is wired and proves nothing about whether OkHttp throws that type for the condition in question. If an engine upgrade changes the exception surface, this fails instead of silently reclassifying live failures.

None of those addresses leave the machine in a way that reaches a third party, and none depend on the network being in any particular state, so this runs the same on CI as locally.

**The iOS mappings are not verified.** They are written from Apple's documented `NSURLErrorDomain` codes and have not been exercised against a real network change, because an iOS simulator shares the host's network stack and has no airplane mode, so the no-transport case cannot be produced there at all. The file says so at the top. The codes should be checked against observed `origin.code` values the first time this runs on a device.

author: bartytime4life
body:
## Outcome and exact target

Close the CLI-owned event source before run terminalization. This is a bounded #68 caller-lifecycle correction, not capture activation, a shutdown deadline, or independent approval. Keep draft.

- Base/main: `bc0189dc20783b44aaabd15defd570dfdebb0da4`, tree `f62b7f536a9aefb90d3bc66b10c26f0619064ab9`.
- Head: `3e2d7bd99ec42a70be2ce182ad2949dd64ed4091`, tree `07482cd0b2c515231c2f2d4ac709d9e044d54a12`.
- Branch: `agent/cli-source-ownership-20260911`.
- One commit ahead / zero behind at creation; exactly three paths, +503/-8.

## Bounded implementation

- `megalodon/cli.py` (+40/-3): introduce one owned-source context boundary around ingestion while the scoped SIGTERM handler is active. Call the selected iterator's close method, when present, before writing terminal status. Open CLI-selected JSONL files lazily and close their streams explicitly. Stdin remains borrowed and is not closed.
- `tests/test_cli_source_ownership.py`: 18 standard-library unittest methods, including negative error-precedence matrices, and 6 real CLI/service/SQLite pytest cases. Retained source references prevent accidental garbage collection from satisfying closure assertions. Socket, DNS and subprocess guards are present; no Scapy or real capture is used.
- `docs/ingestion-integrity.md` (+86/-5): correct event-limit/exhaustion sequencing and document ownership, failure precedence, fixed diagnostics, committed-prefix preservation, historical-receipt limits and remaining shutdown work.

A standalone ordinary cleanup error becomes fixed `CaptureError`, `failed/failed` with `CAPTURE_ERROR`, exit 2, and no terminal success JSON. Earlier capture/I/O/validation/storage failures keep their existing categories, interruptions keep the existing handled exit path, and reconciliation-required errors are not retried or normally finalized on the poisoned writer. Cleanup never reads the next event. Already committed per-event evidence remains intact.

## Relationship to PR #89

Live #89 remains open, non-draft and unmerged at `11d49bb2ee7d2e111d544cf2bbe5bfa8991b9ff2`, with no submitted reviews at this readback. Its ready transition was externally observed in the prior task, not performed here.

This PR starts from main rather than stacking on #89 and changes none of #89's three paths. #89 addresses producer-side Scapy diagnostics/error precedence; this PR addresses caller ownership and JSONL stream lifetime. Neither substitutes for the other's proof. A producer that internally masked a primary error before returning to the CLI still requires its producer correction.

When integrating both changes, revalidate the combined exact content and reconcile #89's `docs/capture-failure-policy.md` paragraph describing absent CLI-owned closure against this new contract. No combined-head test or permission to merge either PR is claimed here. The older dashboard-recovery branch/ZIP remains held and was not applied.

## Validation at creation

VERIFIED: original CLI blob `60eddba52771e31ab7e1175ed9dbb05d268e6138` and original documentation blob `d82542ced695597e4340fd83a27376b81eca5a3c` matched their complete local reconstructions. All three new remote blob hashes match the local candidate. AST comparison confirms unchanged existing CLI functions except `_events_for` and `_run`; two helpers are added. Python compilation, Python 3.11 syntax parsing and whitespace checks passed.

VERIFIED local synthetic execution: Python 3.13.5 standard-library unittest, **18 methods passed**, including subtests. This was a byte-verified partial reconstruction with import-only stand-ins, not a complete checkout or native Store run. Eight applicable behavior methods against original CLI produced **18 failed assertions/subtests and 0 errors**, distinguishing the missing-closure behavior without counting absent new helper names as defects.

BLOCKED locally: full Git checkout failed DNS (exit 128). Local pytest 9 is outside the repository constraint and was not used as acceptance. The six actual CLI/service/SQLite cases, full repository pytest, supported Python 3.11/3.12 execution, package builds and safe CLI smokes require hosted validation. Those exact-head CI results are **PENDING at creation** and will be recorded as a later receipt. No native browser, installed-Scapy, live sensor, or native Windows acceptance is claimed.

## Limits and authority

This establishes deterministic ownership and handling of surfaced close errors, not bounded duration. `next()` and `close()` can still block; async sniffer death, partial startup cleanup, stop/join deadlines, native release, kernel loss and repeated-signal resilience remain under #68. Exception notes are not a new SQLite field or printed CLI warning; suppressed display context remains inspectable in memory. The existing schema has no separate shutdown-verification field. Historical successful receipts are not retroactive proof that this ownership boundary ran.

The Advancement Blueprint's Phase 2B (page 18) and Local Command Center Integration Blueprint's A5 (page 20) inform this resource/failure sequence. Their old repository snapshots and future integrations are not current implementation evidence. Python 3.11 primary language references are linked in the document.

No capture.py, detector, service, storage schema, dashboard, rule, dependency, workflow, dataset, runtime adapter, notifier, or firewall behavior changes. No ready transition, approval, merge, auto-merge, protection change, release, deployment, live capture, sensor/service installation, host mutation, remote exposure, secret handling or telemetry sharing was performed. Issue #3 remains the independent-review gate; #68 remains open. Safest next gate: exact-content hosted checks, then eligible independent review of this three-path diff.

author: kh3rwa1
body:
## Summary
- explicitly bundle the nested `assets/animations/avatars/` directory so Flutter includes all six Lottie files
- require the complete avatar catalog in the generated AssetManifest instead of silently showing one broken fallback
- add regression coverage proving every catalog avatar is available through the production provider
- keep repeating Lottie animations enabled in normal use while making widget tests deterministic through reduced-motion and non-animated test fixtures

## Root cause
Flutter directory asset entries are not recursive. `pubspec.yaml` registered `assets/animations/` but not its `avatars/` subdirectory. The production manifest therefore contained none of the avatar JSON files, so the picker displayed only the name initial and the fallback Olitun tile; that tile rendered a generic icon because its Lottie file was also absent.

## Result
The existing Profile avatar picker now receives all six real bundled choices: Olitun, Sunrise, River, Forest, Festival, and Night sky. No new screen or route is introduced.

## Scope
- no backend changes or fabricated records
- existing persistence, color selection, rollback, accessibility, and reduced-motion behavior retained
- no changes under `functions/translator/**`

## Validation
- all 28 head checks passed across branch, pull-request, release, artifact, and security validation
- Flutter unit, widget, and coverage suites passed on both branch and pull-request runs
- generated AssetManifest regression confirms the provider returns every ordered catalog avatar
- formatting/static analysis, web integration, Android E2E, web and Android release budgets, Appwrite schema/permission checks, Node tests, dependency gate, artifact integrity, Release Gate, Gitleaks, OSV, CodeQL, and action-pinning checks passed

author: aladyinsane
body:
## What this changes

The "?" button now shows different help depending on whether the app is already installed, and the install steps themselves are corrected for current iOS Safari.

## Which ADR does this implement?

None needed — this is UI copy inside [ADR-0002](docs/adr/0002-pwa-instead-of-native-ios-app.md)'s existing scope (installing to the home screen), not a new decision.

## Two bugs, both found by using the app rather than reading the code

**The "?" button always showed "Add to Home Screen" instructions, even once the app was already on the home screen.** That's explaining a step that already happened, with no way to answer the only thing left to ask at that point: how to get this list onto someone else's phone. `shouldPromptInstall()` already knew how to detect standalone mode — that's what correctly hides the auto-banner once installed — it just was never asked by the "?" button. `InstallHelp` now checks this itself and renders one of two things: install steps in a browser tab, sharing steps once installed. The auto-banner and the post-create landing screen are unaffected, since both only ever render in a browser tab.

**The install steps were stale.** iOS Safari no longer surfaces the Share icon directly in the toolbar — it's behind the ••• menu, and "Add to Home Screen" is sometimes behind a "More" tap within the Share sheet. Rewritten to match what's actually on screen (confirmed against real screenshots).

The "sharing this list" content is new: press and hold the icon, tap "Share Bookmark," send the link.

## How it was tested

**Automated:** `install-help.test.ts` (4 new tests) renders both branches through `react-dom/server` — no jsdom needed, matching this repo's existing style of testing pure logic rather than rendered markup — and asserts on which heading comes back for each of `navigator.standalone` and the `display-mode: standalone` media query, since either signal alone has to be trusted. 111 tests total (was 107).

This PR doesn't touch sync, so the two-device checklist doesn't apply.

## Anything to look at closely

The "already installed" content assumes the only thing left to explain is inviting someone else. If either of you would rather it say something else at that point, that's a one-line change in `InstallHelp.tsx`.

## Checklist

- [x] Serves the [principles](docs/PRINCIPLES.md) — #3 (a feature that needs explaining, and an explanation that no longer applies, are both the wrong thing to leave on screen)
- [x] CI green, including `npm run check:docs`

### Documentation check

- [x] `README.md` — status still accurate, no edit
- [x] `docs/adr/` — no undocumented decision here; index current
- [x] `docs/SETUP.md` — **corrected the install steps to match**, added an FAQ entry for sharing to a third phone, and noted that the `?` button's content now depends on whether the app is installed
- [x] `docs/OPERATIONS.md` — no new command, nothing to add
- [x] `docs/ROADMAP.md` — doesn't touch anything listed there
- [x] `apps/*/README.md` — still describes what's in the directory, no edit
- [x] `CLAUDE.md` — no new convention; existing ones covered this

body:
## What

Adds `docs/NETWORK_RELIABILITY.md` and points `CLAUDE.md` at it. The proposal that argued for this work stops being true once the work lands; this is what survives it.

## Changes

- **The taxonomy table** is the specification for `toNetworkError` and the fixture its tests are written from, so it lives in one place rather than being copied into the classifier, the tests and eventually the UI copy. Three consumers, one table.
- **A verification column that says plainly the iOS half is a hypothesis.** Those mappings come from Apple's documented `NSURLErrorDomain` codes and have never been exercised against a real network change, because an iOS simulator shares the host's network stack and has no airplane mode. The Android half is verified against a real Ktor OkHttp client. Recording that asymmetry is the point: a classifier that is confidently wrong is worse than the boolean it replaced.
- **A decisions table** borrowing the column that makes `docs/ANALYTICS_ASSUMPTIONS.md` work: "would revisit if". Not "consequences", which nobody rereads, but the specific observation that should reopen the question. All five triggers are concretely observable, including the one that settles the `Result` versus `ApiResult` argument with a single real instance of a silently dropped failure.
- **A checklist for adding an upstream API**, and the two absolute rules in `CLAUDE.md`: never add a per-feature `HttpClient`, never present the OS connectivity flag as the truth.
- **The service register**, present but empty. It gets populated as the services migrate to one contract, along with the guard test that holds it. Writing the register before the contract exists would be writing fiction.

Deliberately not a `docs/adr/` directory. All five decisions are scoped to one subsystem, the rule docs here already carry their rationale, and a new genre seeded with five entries and no second customer is one that rots. The section lifts out into `docs/adr/0001` unchanged on the day a second subsystem needs the same treatment.

author: mangpijasuan
body:
## 1. The duplication (the main change)

The scanner re-evaluates the whole watchlist every tick and `record_signal()` had no guard, so the same setup was re-recorded on every pass. Measured in the Aug 28 assessment: **70,798 rows representing ~1,568 real (ticker, action, day) signals — about 45× duplication.**

That's not just wasted rows. It's why a ~1,568-signal sample reads as 70k, and it's what blew the resolver's time budget (~65k rows against a 120s scheduler limit) so `check_pending_outcomes()` was killed mid-pass every run — leaving a labelled subset selected by DB iteration order which, as that investigation put it, *"reads exactly like real data."*

`record_signal()` now keeps the **first** signal per (ticker, action, UTC day) and returns that row's id for later re-emissions. First is the right one to keep: it's the moment the setup became actionable, before the day's price action moved the entry/stop/target under it.

Two implementation details worth a look:

- The window is a **half-open range**, not `date(generated_at)` — so it uses the existing `idx_signal_outcomes_generated_at` and carries no dependence on the session's timezone setting.
- A `generated_at` parsed from an offset-less string comes back **naive**; it's normalized to UTC before deriving the day boundary, or the window lands on the wrong day.

## 2. Why there's no UNIQUE constraint here

Deliberate, and worth flagging. ~69k historical duplicates still exist, so adding a unique index would make the next `alembic upgrade head` fail — and that runs automatically as step 4 of `deploy/hetzner/update.sh`. **It would break your deploy.**

So: `scripts/dedupe_signal_outcomes.py` drains the history first (dry-run by default, per `backfill_signal_outcomes.py`'s precedent), and the index can follow once history is clean. The module docstring records this sequencing.

**The cleanup deliberately does not just "keep the earliest row."** Duplicates were resolved independently, so the earliest is frequently still `pending` while a later twin already carries a real label — and dropping the labelled twin to keep an unlabelled original would destroy exactly the scarce data this subsystem exists to collect. The rule is: resolved outranks pending (`expired` in between), earliest wins among equals. The dry run reports how many groups that rescued, so you can see what a naive version would have cost before applying anything.

## 3. Three unrelated correctness fixes

**A false safety claim.** `_heuristic_score`'s docstring claimed it applies "a higher effective threshold internally (0.72 instead of 0.65) to compensate for lack of probabilistic calibration." It does not and never did — `0.72` appears nowhere in the module; `score()` compares against `settings.effective_signal_score_threshold` (0.65, or **0.35** under paper-visibility). I removed the claim rather than implementing it: inventing a margin now would silently change live gating, and that should be a deliberate configured change. This matters because the heuristic is the *live* scoring path — `signal_model` reports `scoring_mode: "heuristic"`.

**Duplicated risk limits** (the one still-open finding from `ARCHITECTURE_AUDIT.md`). `portfolio_greeks` restated RiskManager's 0.30 / 0.15 as its own literals, so raising a limit in the module that actually gates trades left this one quietly reporting against the old value. It now imports them. Separately, `is_delta_neutral()`'s bare inline `0.15` becomes `DELTA_NEUTRAL_BAND` — a reporting band, not a risk limit, equal to the vega cap only by coincidence and with nothing that should keep them in step.

**Trades/day vs the charter.** `TRADING_POLICY.md` now records that this is the one limit *looser* than the charter (6 vs "3, no exceptions"). The enforcement mechanism is unchanged — `guardrails.py` still hard-stops — only the number differs, and it's been 6 for as far back as repo history goes. The likely rationale (the charter's 3 predates equity + spreads + CSP each proposing trades independently) is written down **and explicitly marked as reconstructed, not recorded**, with an owner decision flagged. I didn't change the value: that's a risk decision, not mine.

## Verification

- **Full backend suite: 1,725 tests, 5 failures** — the same 5 pre-existing `ta`-package environment failures that pass in CI (confirmed again on this branch; `ta` won't build in my container).
- Running the full suite caught **6 failures I'd introduced** in `test_opportunity_score_capture.py` — its hand-rolled `_Session` stub had no `execute`, so the new dedup lookup raised into `record_signal`'s broad except and silently skipped the insert. Fixed by giving the stub a no-duplicate `execute`. Worth noting as a review point: that broad `except Exception` will convert future mistakes into silent no-ops the same way.
- 4 new tests for the dedup (duplicate skipped, window bounded on both sides, naive timestamp handled, BUY vs SELL not conflated), and 5 for the cleanup's survivor selection — that logic decides which production rows get deleted, so it's pinned down rather than trusted by inspection.
- Also refactored 3 copies of identical session-mock boilerplate into one `_mock_session()` helper.

## Suggested order on the box

1. Merge + deploy (stops new duplicates immediately; no migration needed).
2. `bash deploy/hetzner/backup_db.sh`
3. `docker compose -f docker-compose.hetzner.yml exec backend python scripts/dedupe_signal_outcomes.py` — read the dry run.
4. Same with `--apply` once the numbers look right.
5. Then a unique index becomes safe to add, as a follow-up.

author: joshuasknott
body:
## Summary

Fixes demonstrated Google Calendar date/time and event-semantics defects in the TypeScript adapter (`packages/connectors/src/providers/google-calendar.ts`), with a new Calendar-specific fixture suite.

## Reproduction

`packages/connectors/src/providers/google-calendar.test.ts` was added first and run against the unmodified adapter: **14 of 19 tests failed**, demonstrating:

- All-day events were always shaped as `{ dateTime }`, so date-only values (not RFC3339) were rejected by Google or misread as timed events; updates silently downgraded existing all-day events to timed ones.
- Missing/inverted start-end, mixed all-day/timed kinds, and all-day `end.date == start.date` were sent to Google to fail with generic 400s.
- Approved `attendees`/`recurrence` payload fields were silently dropped from the request body.
- Bare event-list reads never defaulted to upcoming events (contradicting the documented behavior) and sent `orderBy=startTime` with no bounds.
- Date-only `timeMin`/`timeMax` and inverted list bounds were sent unvalidated.
- `calendarId`/`eventId` were interpolated into URL paths unencoded.

## Fixes

- **All-day vs timed**: date-only values map to `{ date }` (no `timeZone`, per Google); timed values stay `{ dateTime, timeZone }` and pass through verbatim — no browser-local conversion anywhere. Exclusive `end.date` is preserved untouched.
- **Fail closed before egress** on: missing `start`/`end`, mixed date/dateTime kinds, timed `end <= start` (compared only when both carry explicit UTC offsets), all-day `end.date <= start.date`, non-RFC3339-with-offset list bounds, and `timeMax <= timeMin`.
- **Bare lists** default to `timeMin = now` (RFC3339 UTC via an injectable `now` option for deterministic tests), matching the documented "upcoming events only" behavior.
- **Identifiers** are `encodeURIComponent`-encoded in every path segment (calendar.list, single read, create, update, cancel, delete).
- **Attendees/recurrence** now fail closed with a clear prerequisite instead of silently dropping approved payload fields. No recurrence engine or scheduling product is added; recurring-series vs instance reads keep `recurrence`, `recurringEventId`, `originalStartTime`, and `status` (including cancelled instances) intact.

Cancellation semantics remain `PATCH { status: "cancelled" }` per Google; delete remains `DELETE`. No operation is described as a harmless local draft, and no attendee notifications are sent (Google's `sendUpdates` default is no-notification and the adapter never writes attendee email addresses).

## Verification

- `pnpm --filter @fable/connectors test` — 529 passed (44 files)
- `pnpm typecheck` (full repo, includes desktop) — clean
- `eslint packages/connectors/src/providers/google-calendar.ts --max-warnings=0` — clean
- `node scripts/quality/check-explicit-any.mjs` — passed
- `git diff --check` — clean

## Limitations

- `attendees` and `recurrence` are rejected rather than applied; writing them (and any attendee notifications) is intentionally out of scope.
- Timed `end > start` validation only compares instants when both values carry explicit UTC offsets; timezone-less values pass through for Google to interpret with the calendar default (documented Google behavior).
- This is adapter-level shaping only; the desktop shell wiring and live-credential behavior remain unchanged and are not exercised here.

body:
## Summary

RouterOS 7.23 adds a hardware offload flag and renders the legend in uppercase:

```
Flags: X - DISABLED, R - RUNNING; H - HW-OFFLOADED
```

The `Start` rule accepted only the lowercase pair, so the parse failed on the first line with a State Error, before reaching any interface.

## Evidence

Captured from 17 live devices spanning RouterOS 7.6 to 7.23.4:

| Legend | Versions |
|---|---|
| `Flags: X - disabled, R - running` | 7.6 - 7.20.8 |
| `Flags: X - DISABLED, R - RUNNING; H - HW-OFFLOADED` | 7.23.4 |

The rule now accepts either case plus the optional hw-offloaded clause — exactly the two forms observed, nothing further.

## Test case

Test case 3 is the 7.23.4 legend. Those devices have no VLANs configured, so it parses to no records (`parsed_sample: []`, as 19 existing fixtures in the repo do) — which is what makes it a regression test for the legend itself: it raised a State Error before this change and parses cleanly after.

## Known limitation

`STATUS` matches `X` or `R`, not `H`, so a hardware-offloaded VLAN row may not parse. No capture contains one — those devices have no VLANs — and inventing that row's shape would go beyond the samples. Left for a real capture.

body:
Implements item 2 of [recoupable/app#2080](https://github.com/recoupable/app/issues/2080). Contract: [recoupable/docs#339](https://github.com/recoupable/docs/pull/339). **Merge order: docs#339 → this PR → the Stripe re-tag in the issue.**

## Why

An account can be tagged (`metadata.accountId`) on more than one Stripe customer. Seeker Music's org has its $5k invoiced plan on one customer and, since 2026-09-08, a card saved on another (currently tagged to a personal account). The customer lookup was a `limit: 1` search, so with two tagged customers the card, invoice list and auto top-up would resolve non-deterministically.

## What changes

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `lib/stripe/listStripeCustomersForAccount.ts` (new) | search `metadata['accountId']` with `limit: 10`, return every match |
| `lib/stripe/pickPrimaryStripeCustomer.ts` (new) | pure: the customer holding `invoice_settings.default_payment_method` (newest first), else the newest |
| `lib/stripe/findStripeCustomerForAccount.ts` | list + pick; same `string \| null` signature, so all read callers (payment-method GET/DELETE, auto top-up, `accountHasPaymentMethod`) inherit it |
| `lib/stripe/resolveStripeCustomerForAccount.ts` | list + pick; create on miss unchanged (same idempotency key) |
| `lib/billing/listCustomerInvoicesBefore.ts` (new) | one customer's page, optional `created[lt]` |
| `lib/billing/listAccountInvoices.ts` | takes `customerIds[]`, fetches each in parallel, merges by `created` desc, caps at `limit`; `startingAfter` is resolved to its `created` so one cursor works across customers; `hasMore` = cut at limit or any page has more |
| `lib/billing/getPaymentsHandler.ts` | lists all tagged customers; empty list short-circuits without calling Stripe |

Not changed: `POST /portal` (opens on the active subscription's customer, unrelated to the lookup) and every subscription read (matched on the subscription's own tag). Single-customer behaviour is unchanged except pagination now uses `created[lt]` instead of `starting_after` (same ordering). Response shapes are unchanged, so `app` needs no change.

## Tests (RED → GREEN)

- `lib/stripe/__tests__/listStripeCustomersForAccount.test.ts`, `pickPrimaryStripeCustomer.test.ts` (new)
- `findStripeCustomerForAccount.test.ts`, `resolveStripeCustomerForAccount.test.ts`: card holder wins, newest fallback, `limit: 10`
- `lib/billing/__tests__/listAccountInvoices.test.ts`: merge order, cap, `hasMore`, cursor by creation time, empty ids
- `getPaymentsHandler.test.ts`: merged customers, empty short-circuit

`vitest run lib/stripe lib/billing lib/credits`: 111 files / 495 tests pass. `tsc --noEmit` clean for touched files. eslint clean.

## Preview verification

See the results comment: two-customer fixture on the preview, merged list + cross-customer cursor + card null + 400/401/403 probes all match the docs.

author: fourwardhabits
body:
Founder physical QA, iOS 1.0.1 build 11, reproduced twice on clean accounts.

Rank the first movie on a new account and the app dies. The picker draws
correctly behind it — "Pick another one", 1 of 5, posters loaded, its own
"Not now" and "Use a different account" beneath — and the screen takes no
touches. Force quitting recovers it every time and onboarding continues from the
right place.

**The data was never involved.** Production shows the first ranking completed: no
leftover `ranking_sessions` row, six rankings against six `user_media` rows, no
orphan. Progress is derived from `rankings`, so a relaunch re-derives 1 of 5 —
which is why the recovery is clean and why this is not a query, routing or
ranking-state defect.

**Two `<Modal>`s swapped in one commit.** Choosing a bucket unmounted the bucket
sheet and mounted the comparison sheet in the same render. UIKit will not present
a view controller over one that is still dismissing: the presentation is refused,
React believes it succeeded, and the transparent window left behind sits above the
picker and eats every touch. It is process-local, so force quitting clears it.

**Why the first movie and no other.** `rank_start` "places it outright when its
band is empty" (20260825000200) — film one on a new account has no comparisons at
all, so the comparison sheet presents and is dismissed again inside one round
trip, while the bucket sheet's 300ms slide-out is still running. Films two to five
are held open by a person answering comparisons, so that dismissal finished long
before.

PR #133 made `step` a single value, which stopped the two sheets being *visible*
together and was the right fix for the dead end it was written for. It did not
stop them being *swapped*, and swapping is what UIKit objects to.

**The fix is two more states.** `handoff` sits between `bucket` and `ranking`, and
`returning` between `ranking` and `picking`: the outgoing sheet stays mounted with
`visible={false}`, and nothing else is asked for until iOS says the presentation
is gone. `Sheet` gained an optional `onDismissed` — forwarded to `<Modal
onDismiss>` — and a `pointerEvents` guard so nothing on a dismissing sheet answers
a tap, which is one rule instead of a guard per control. `RankingSheet` and
`TasteBucketSheet` take the same optional `visible`/`onDismissed`; every other
caller passes the literal `true` and is unaffected.

Android branches at the call site rather than in an effect: `onDismiss` is
iOS-only, an Android modal is a view in the same window with no presentation to
serialise against, and parking in `handoff` would strand the flow on the platform
that never had the bug.

**No timeout.** An earlier note here claimed a missed `onDismiss` would cost only
a tap; that was wrong and a review said so — if the callback never came the
dismissal never completed and the picker is as untappable as before. What
justifies no watchdog is that the callback is not best-effort: RN dismisses on
`visible=false` while mounted and calls `onDismiss` from the completion on both
renderers, checked in `Modal.js`, `RCTModalHostView.m` and
`RCTModalHostViewComponentView.mm`.

The regression test stands inside the gap: it holds the dismissal, asserts
`rank_start` has not been called, presses a second bucket chip to prove the
dismissing sheet answers nothing, releases, and asserts the run continues. It
fails against the pre-fix swap, verified by mutation.

`jest.setup.js` gained a `<Modal>` that reports its own dismissal, because jest
has no UIKit and every handover test would otherwise wait forever — which is the
fix working, not failing. It is faithful in the ways that matter: children stay
rendered through the dismissal, and a modal unmounted while still visible reports
nothing.

**The rest of this class is known and deliberately not here.** The audit found the
same unserialised swap in six other places — log sheet <-> comparison on the
Search tab and the title screen, the season picker, the Ranked options rows, and
the profile menu's Report and Block — none of them ever reported. On the founder's
decision they are held for a separate post-1.0.1 change so the release carrying
the reproduced fix stays small enough to trust. That work, with a `useSheetHandoff`
hook generalising what this screen does by hand, is on
`defer/modal-handoff-audit`; `Sheet`'s note names each surface and warns that the
audit's own list was wrong twice before it was right.

Gates: typecheck clean, lint 0 errors at the 38-warning baseline, 3748 jest pass
(the one failure is the pre-existing `product-docs` link to an untracked
founder-local file). **No native or config file is touched and none of these are
fingerprint sources, so the runtime version does not move.**

What no Jest test can prove, and what physical QA must cover: that iOS really
serialises these presentations. The first ranking on a clean account is the case,
and a deliberately fast tap on the next poster after a placement is the boundary.

A final review round found four things in the test double and the prose, none in
the product logic — which it verified against RN 0.86.2's own `Modal.js`,
`RCTModalHostView.m` and `RCTModalHostViewComponentView.mm` rather than against
these comments.

The mock kept a closed modal's children rendered for ever when nothing was
waiting on the dismissal: without an `onDismiss` there is no callback to trigger
another render, so `closing` never cleared. It is gated on `onDismiss` now, which
is the mock's one honest limitation and is written down where it lives. It also
dropped RN's `visible` default, so a bare `<Modal>` with no prop rendered null in
tests while presenting on a device.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------
THE EXIT HAS TO WAIT FOR THE ENTRANCE

A further review round found the freeze reachable once more, on the other leg,
and it is the same first title that reaches it.

`handOver` mounts the comparison sheet — a ~350ms presentation — and `Session`
fires `rank_start` in the same commit. On film one the band is empty, so the
server places it outright and `onPlaced` comes back inside that window.
**UIKit refuses a dismissal issued while the presentation is still animating and
never runs its completion**, so flipping `visible` there would ask for a dismissal
that never finishes: `onDismiss` would never arrive, `returning` would be
terminal, and the sheet would sit over a dead picker. The freeze, on the way out.

The earlier note ruling out a watchdog verified that `onDismiss` is *wired to* the
completion block. It did not establish that UIKit ever *runs* it, and that is the
gap.

So the exit waits for the entrance. `Sheet` gained `onShown` — the mirror of
`onDismissed`, forwarded to `<Modal onShow>` — and the `ranking` step carries
`shown` and `placed`, leaving for `returning` only when both are true, in either
order. Still no timer: this is the platform's own signal for the platform's own
constraint.

The jest Modal reports the entrance as well as the dismissal, and starts `prev`
false so a modal that mounts already visible still counts as one — without which
every handover test would have waited forever.

A further round found the freeze reachable through the state added to prevent it.

`onPlaced` read the step from `stepRef` and wrote the whole object back. The ref is
updated in a parent effect and lags a commit, so an `onShow` landing in the same
batch — exactly the first-title case — would have its `shown: true` discarded, and
the run would sit in `ranking` for ever: an empty sheet with no Close control over
a dead picker. The update is functional now; the ref is still right for the
subject, which does not change for the life of the step.

`choose` guarded `handoff` and `returning` but not `ranking`, leaving a narrow
window between the bucket sheet's dismissal and the comparison sheet appearing
where a pick would unmount a presenting `<Modal>` to mount another.

Three comments corrected as well, and they matter in a fi

author: izzybps
body:
Shipping a change to the panel required publishing the SDK to npm first. That requirement was never real, and it cost a release per iteration today.

## The panel never used npm

Vite **inlines** the SDK into the bundle:

```
C:\fayz-shell\node_modules\@fayz-ai   does not exist
@fayz-ai in dist/assets/*.js          0 references
```

What ships is a self-contained bundle pushed over SSH by the machine that built it. `npm run panel` — build, ship, restart, ~40s.

## Only CI insisted otherwise

It ran `npm ci` on a clean runner and resolved the SDK from the registry, so it went red on any SDK change that had not been released — making a release a prerequisite for a deploy that never involved npm.

CI now checks the SDK out beside the app and builds from source, which is what the deploying machine does.

`tsconfig.ci.json` points TypeScript at the same tree. `FAYZ_SDK_DIR` is a **bundler** alias and `tsc` cannot see it — that gap is exactly why `npm run typecheck` and `vite build` disagreed all afternoon, one reading node_modules and the other the worktree.

`npm run typecheck` now reads the source too, so local and CI agree. `typecheck:published` keeps the old behaviour for checking against a released SDK.

## Vercel is gone

`VERCEL.md` records why. A totem is not a site: it runs inside an Electron shell on a panel with a USB thermal printer bolted to it. Vercel imposed the clean-machine, registry-resolved build that created the whole problem, in exchange for a preview URL nobody opens.

If a real web build of the totem ever exists, this reopens — and then a release genuinely makes sense, because then the SDK really would come from npm.

> The GitHub integration still has to be disconnected in the Vercel dashboard; this removes the repo-side link only.

﻿## TF-009 — Shared optical receive pipeline + full browser pixel reconstruction

**Issue:** #45

**STACKED PR — do not merge independently.**
This PR is stacked on **PR #44** (spike/tf-008-wechat-mini-receiver). Base branch: spike/tf-008-wechat-mini-receiver. It does **NOT** target main.

## Evidence terminology (hard rule)
- **SIMULATION evidence only.** No physical optical ingress, no physical acquisition PASS, no Net Goodput.
- Only a real display → optical path → phone camera → reconstruction → SHA-256 exact match can qualify as physical Net Goodput.

## What this PR does
- Extracts the browser-lab receiver stages into a platform-neutral shared receive core (SharedOpticalReceiveCore) — DOM/canvas/camera/WebSocket/wx-free.
- Adds a standalone file sender mode that renders a deterministic 64 KiB file through the real visual protocol (orientation → preamble → Manifest → fountain-encoded OptiGrid symbols).
- Browser pixel simulation consumes rendered pixels only and reconstructs 64 KiB with an exact SHA-256 match (repeated 3× deterministic).

## Status

author: lzvxck
body: Fixes https://github.com/Seriora-Research/seri-agent/issues/123 ## Why `read_file` used to load every byte, decode the whole buffer as UTF-8, then keep 30k characters of head and tail. The model already saw a cap. The process still paid RAM and decode for the rest. A sibling batch of reads would make that worse. This change reads a prefix for image sniff first, then for large regular text reads both ends and counts the middle without keeping it as a string. The cap string, omitted wording, and surrogate trim stay the same. ## How `readFile` opens one handle and snapshots the EOL epoch. - FIFOs, non-regular files, and `stat.size === 0` (procfs) still slurp that handle. Do not consume a prefix and reopen. - Regular files sniff 12 bytes with `sniffImageMime`. Scheduled runs refuse without reading the body. Attended files over 4 MiB return `IMAGE_TOO_LARGE` from `stat.size`. - Text at or under `2 * WINDOW_BYTES` still slurps so small files stay exact. - Larger text reads 45004 bytes from each end, drops a torn UTF-8 sequence at the cuts, and scans the middle in 64 KiB chunks only to count UTF-16 length and `\r\n`. - Positioned reads return the byte count they actually got. A short head or a short tail means `stat.size` is not the file: slurp the readable bytes and `finishText`. Unfilled buffer bytes are not treated as content. - A claimed size above 64 GiB is refused before the windowed scan, so a readable `/proc/kcore` cannot loop over 140TB. - Leading UTF-8 continuation skip is capped at 3 bytes, matching the trailing incomplete walk. - `capFromBoundedWindows` in `capToolResult.ts` owns the marker. `capToolResult` still uses it, so MCP `flattenContent` is unchanged. ## Tradeoffs - The middle is still read from disk so the omitted count and EOL cache stay exact. Peak RAM is the windows plus a 64 KiB chunk, not the full UTF-16 string. - A decoder class, `tools/read/` modules, and a sequential `TextDecoder` rewrite were rejected. The extra types hid little and split one policy across files. Head and tail I/O stays random-access for stable regular files. ## Blast Radius `readFile` and `capToolResult` are the only production callers of the new helper. MCP still calls `capToolResult` on a full string. FIFO overlap, abort, image refusal strings, and `writeFile` EOL cache stay on the same tests. The safety fact is that a windowed read equals `capToolResult` of a full decode. Proven by tests and a script that also checks a small file, MCP flatten, and an oversized PNG. A sysfs size-liar (`/sys/class/net/lo/mtu`) must match `readFileSync` and contain no NULs. A windowed size-liar with a short tail must match `capToolResult` of the readable bytes. ## Verification - [x] `bun run typecheck` - [x] Targeted `readFile` / `capToolResult` / `writeFile` tests after the short-tail fix (37 pass) - [x] `bun test` (3792 pass, 30 skip, 0 fail) on the previous short-read commit - [x] `bun run build` on the first commit; CI rebuilds each follow-up - [x] Blast-radius script: windowed result equals full cap, small file unchanged, MCP flatten unchanged, oversized PNG refused - Windows CI failed once on `hooks/interop.test.ts` (`block-dangerous.ps1` hit a 15s timeout at 15224ms). That test now uses `DEFAULT_HOOK_TIMEOUT_MS` (30s), matching POSIX. Linux, macOS, and Windows were green on the short-read commit. ## Cross-platform impact - [x] Touches file I/O (`fs.promises.open`, positional `FileHandle.read`, `stat`) - [ ] PowerShell not exercised for `readFile`. FIFO tests stay `skipIf(win32)`. Regular-file `open`/`read`/`stat` is covered by Windows CI. The sysfs size-liar test is `skipIf` the path is missing. The windowed short-tail test spies `fs.promises.open` so it runs on every OS. ## Notes for the reviewer Out of scope: raising the cap, changing omitted wording, making `read_file` a new tool, changing bash/PowerShell stream caps. Async `read_file` already landed on `dev`. Abort is still polled between reads, not on each `FileHandle.read`.

author: waldren
body:
The blocking CI gate — `pnpm audit --audit-level=high --prod --no-optional` — started failing on **every branch**. Three high-severity `multer` advisories were disclosed against `<2.3.0`:

| Advisory | Issue |
| --- | --- |
| [GHSA-wc9g-mqfw-jrwm](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-wc9g-mqfw-jrwm) | DoS via crafted multipart field names |
| [GHSA-qfvm-cv95-jqjf](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-qfvm-cv95-jqjf) | DoS via file descriptor leak on aborted uploads |
| [GHSA-g5hg-p3ph-g8qg](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-g5hg-p3ph-g8qg) | DoS via oversized array index in field names |

Reached through `apps__api > @nestjs/platform-express > multer@2.2.0`, present since P1.S1. Nothing in the repo added or moved it — the advisories are new, not the dependency.

## Why an override rather than a bump

There is nothing to bump to. `@nestjs/platform-express@latest` **is** `12.0.1`, the version already in use, and it still pins `multer@2.2.0` exactly. Until NestJS releases against a patched multer, an override is the only route to one.

The rationale is recorded in `package.json` next to the entry, including the removal condition — whoever deletes it should know it becomes unnecessary the moment `@nestjs/platform-express` ships a release depending on `>=2.3.0`.

Ranged (`multer@<2.3.0` → `^2.3.0`) rather than pinned, so a later 2.3.x patch is picked up without another commit.

## Why this is low risk here

Verified rather than assumed: **`apps/api` performs no multipart handling at all.** No `FileInterceptor`, no `@UploadedFile`, no `multer` import anywhere in `src/` — and none is planned, since SRS_v2 §4 routes photo uploads through S3 presigned URLs, so image bytes never transit the API. `multer` is dead weight that `@nestjs/platform-express` drags in regardless of whether any route uses it.

So all three advisories are unreachable in this codebase today. The fix is still worth making now rather than suppressing the gate: the gate is what will catch a *reachable* advisory later, and a gate that is red for unrelated reasons stops being read.

## Verification

- `multer` resolves to `2.3.0` in the lockfile
- The exact CI gate command reports `No known vulnerabilities found`
- `pnpm verify` green — 300 tests

## Scope

Deliberately its own branch rather than folded into #11, which it was blocking. The advisory affects every branch and has nothing to do with that sprint; #11 picks it up on rebase or merge.

The manager runs every 15 minutes, so a situation it can't act on alone produces the same decision ~96 times a day. The recent-decisions list showed each one, so all eight slots held a single repeated line — burying everything else and reading as if it were escalating over and over.

Consecutive identical decisions now collapse into one entry with a count and how long the run has been going.

On today's data — **8 identical rows become 5 meaningful entries**:

```
x 17 | Escalate to Gavin — "Increase Prospect Discovery volume by 100%..."
x  4 | No code-diagnosable bottleneck to act on this cycle...
x 15 | Escalate to Gavin — "Increase Prospect Discovery volume by 100%..."
x 10 | No code-diagnosable bottleneck to act on this cycle...
x 10 | Goal "new_clients" is NOT_STARTED — no intervention needed this cycle.
```

The rows are untouched in the table; this is a display concern only.

Paired with ai-workforce `c457a22`, which fixes the underlying dishonesty: the dedup was working (one escalation, one email, nothing re-raised), but every suppressed cycle was *logged* as "Escalate to Gavin". It now records "Waiting on Gavin — ... not re-raised this cycle."

author: thedotmack
body: Fixes #3895. **Root cause:** `bun-runner.js` writes the hook payload to the spawned `bun` child's stdin with no `'error'` listener attached. If the child exits before the write completes (a race more likely with larger payloads), the resulting EPIPE has zero listeners and Node re-throws it as an unhandled exception, crashing the wrapper process. **Fix:** One-line addition — attach a no-op `child.stdin.on('error', () => {})` before the write block. This is the standard Node pattern for suppressing EPIPE on best-effort writes. Consistent with the script's existing exit-0-on-error contract for hook failures.

author: twodragon0
body:
`branch-protection.md` 는 Phase 2 를 두 사실 위에 세운다. 둘 다 **측정이 아니라 서술**이었다. 이 저장소는 서술보다 실측을 요구하므로 채워 넣는다.

## 1. "required check 는 직접 푸시를 막는다" → 실측

`refs/heads/ruleset-probe/*` 만 대상으로 하는 임시 룰셋(`required_status_checks`, context `quality`, `bypass_actors: []`)을 만들고 그 패턴의 브랜치에 직접 푸시했다. **main 은 범위에 넣지 않았다.**

```
remote: error: GH013: Repository rule violations found for refs/heads/ruleset-probe/push-test
remote: - Required status check "quality" is in progress.
 ! [remote rejected]  (push declined due to repository rule violations)     rc=1
```

거부 사유가 `check failed` 가 아니라 **`is in progress`** 라는 게 핵심이다. 자동 푸시는 체크가 돌기 *전에* ref 를 갱신하므로, 체크가 통과할 수 있느냐와 무관하게 항상 이 지점에서 막힌다. `github-actions[bot]` bypass 는 "있으면 좋은 것" 이 아니라 **전제 조건**이다.

룰셋과 로컬 브랜치는 즉시 삭제했고, 푸시가 거부됐으므로 원격에 프로브 브랜치는 생기지 않았다.

## 2. bypass 422 제약 — 재확인 + 새 사실

2026-08-07 실측이 지금도 유효하다. 추가로 알게 된 것:

```
enforcement: disabled                          # 발효 안 함
conditions: refs/heads/ruleset-probe-nonexistent/*   # main 아님
-> 여전히 422
```

**검증이 생성 시점에 일어난다.** "일단 만들어 두고 나중에 켠다" 도 불가능하다.

같은 날, 이 문서를 읽지 않은 채 *"bypass actor 를 먼저 등록하고 수집기 런을 관찰하자"* 는 계획이 제안됐다. 그 계획은 422 로 시작조차 못 한다. 다음 사람이 같은 길로 들어서지 않도록 **경로가 아님**을 명시했다.

## 3. required check 이름은 job id 가 아니다

실행 계획에서 `security-scan.yml` 의 job id 를 그대로 옮겨 적는 실수가 나왔다:

| 잘못 적은 것 | 실제 컨텍스트 |
|---|---|
| `bandit` | `Python SAST (Bandit)` |
| `gitleaks` | `Secret Detection` |
| `actions-permissions` | `Workflow Permissions Audit` |
| `gate` | `Falsifiability gate` |

틀린 이름은 **생성되지 않는 체크**라 모든 PR 이 영구 대기한다 — 이 문서의 "샤드를 직접 required 로 걸지 않는다" 와 같은 실패 양식이다. 등록 전 확인 명령을 넣었고, PR #1306 에서 5종이 모두 나타남을 확인한 기록을 남겼다.

## 4. 인벤토리 표는 원래 맞았다 — 파생 카운터가 틀렸다

파싱된 `uses:`/`run:` 기준으로 다시 세니 **17 + 6 = 23** 으로 문서의 표와 정확히 일치했고 6건의 이름도 같았다. 반면 `component_counts.py` 는 **25** 를 내고 있었다(주석 오탐 2건, 하나는 같은 날 #1302 가 넣은 상호참조 주석).

탐지 수정은 #1306 이다(머지됨). 이 PR 은 그 경위를 문서에 남긴다.

문서 상단이 "개수를 여기 적지 않는다" 고 한 이유는 손 유지보수 드리프트였는데, 이번 건은 **반대 방향**이다 — 파생이 손으로 적은 표보다 틀렸다. 파생이라는 사실 자체는 정확성을 보장하지 않는다. 탐지 근거가 실행되는 내용인지가 보장한다.

## 범위

문서만 변경(`+73 / -3`). 룰셋은 그대로 Phase 1 하나이고, 2026-08-07 의 "보류, Phase 1 을 상한으로 유지" 결정은 **바꾸지 않는다** — 오히려 이 PR 의 실측이 그 결정을 뒷받침한다.

body:
## Problema

**Coordenador multiunidades (e líder) logado no app:**
- Não havia botão "Atribuir" (o sinal `isLeader` estava codificado como `is_super_admin`, então só o super admin via dropdown).
- Só aparecia "Começar Atendimento" (claim), que dava **403** porque o coordenador não tem a Action `ticket.claim` (apenas `tec` + super admin têm).

**Técnico atribuído (ex.: Geovana):**
- O chamado aparecia "atribuído a ela", mas não havia botão para dar continuidade (em `aberto`, o `nextStatus` é `a_caminho` e havia `nextStatus !== 'a_caminho'`, além do claim exigir `unassigned`).

## Correção

- `isLeader` passa a incluir os cargos de liderança RBAC 2.0 (`lider`/`coordinator`) via `useLeadership()`, além do super admin.
- Novo `canClaim`: botão "Começar Atendimento" restrito a técnico + super admin (liderança gerencia via `ticket.assign`, não executa).
- Reintroduzido o passo `aberto → a_caminho` ("Ir ao local") somente para o próprio responsável (`claimedByMe`), desbloqueando o fluxo até "Fechar".

Sem alterações de backend/migrations (o backend já estava correto — a origem era a detecção de liderança no frontend).

## Testes

- `TicketDetail.test.tsx`: 3 casos novos (coordenador vê seletor e não vê claim; coordenador atribui; técnico atribuído avança para `a_caminho`).
- 14 testes passando; `tsc --noEmit` limpo.

body:
## Qué pasó en la ejecución #35 del botón (v1196)

| Paso | Resultado |
|---|---|
| Compuertas 0–3 | verde; producción sirvió `nexusmed-v1196` al primer intento |
| Firestore · REGLAS | verde; sello `dca8f9d3…` = sha256 del árbol `15b2b91` |
| Firestore · ÍNDICES | verde; el catorce enviado |
| **Storage · REGLAS** | **rojo · 403 `firebasestorage.defaultBucket.get`** |
| Seguridad · producción / Smoke / Portal | 57/57 · 10/10 · 401 sin enlace |
| Acta | dijo `PRODUCTION_RELEASE=SUCCESS` sin contar Storage → **REG-668** |

## Qué hace este PR

- **Sello**: `firestore.rules.estado.json` pasa al hash de v1196 con el run #35 y lo que devolvió el acta, sin ocultar que el job terminó en rojo por Storage.
- **Pendientes**: la tabla de Firestore en `docs/ops/REGLAS-DE-FIRESTORE.md` queda vacía; nace **«PENDIENTE DE DESPLIEGUE · Storage»** con la fila de `storage.rules`, el 403 literal y cómo se cierra (rol `roles/firebasestorage.admin` a la cuenta de servicio del botón; si ya estaba, vincular el bucket en Firebase → Storage; volver a pulsar).

author: vbhanuchander-lang
body:
Closes #18052.

The BOM adds every leaf project, but `iceberg-kafka-connect-runtime` builds ZIP distributions rather than Maven artifacts and [disables its publishing tasks](https://github.com/apache/iceberg/blob/main/kafka-connect/build.gradle#L237-L240), so its POM is never published — the [1.11.0 POM](https://repo.maven.apache.org/maven2/org/apache/iceberg/iceberg-kafka-connect-runtime/1.11.0/iceberg-kafka-connect-runtime-1.11.0.pom) returns 404. The BOM therefore advertises a coordinate that cannot resolve.

The grouping project `iceberg-kafka-connect` is already excluded by the existing `childProjects.isEmpty()` check, so the runtime module is the only affected one — it is the only publishing-disabled *leaf* project in the build.

## Verifying this change

`./gradlew :iceberg-bom:generatePomFileForApachePublication`, then inspecting `bom/build/publications/apache/pom-default.xml`:

| | artifacts in BOM | `iceberg-kafka-connect-runtime` |
|---|---|---|
| before | 30 | present |
| after | 29 | absent |

Exactly one entry is removed. `iceberg-kafka-connect`, `iceberg-kafka-connect-events` and `iceberg-kafka-connect-transforms` are real published artifacts and remain.

I used an explicit exclusion list rather than deriving "does not publish" from the project state, because publishing is disabled inside that project's `afterEvaluate` while the BOM's `constraints` block is evaluated during configuration, so keying off task state here would depend on configuration ordering. Happy to switch to a shared property (for example a `skipPublish` flag set by the project and read here) if you would prefer something that cannot be forgotten when the next distribution-only module is added.

author: c01dsummer
body:
自检跑完写一份**入口认领**记录，审计读它，汇总行多报一个数。口径（判据格里怎么写、认领了算不算数）是第二片，硬失败是落地 4。

体量：源码 163 行新增（闸门 350）、测试 81（450）、文档 83（600）。

## 两份记录，不是一份里多一栏

落地 3 原文写的是「写进覆盖记录的新字段」。真做时改成两份（`ENTRY_CLAIMS_PATH`），理由逐字记在 `claims.ts`：

1. **一份文件两个写方会互相抹掉。** 拥有的一方开跑前先清、跑完整份重写 —— 单独跑 `npm test` 会连自检上一轮写下的那一栏一起清掉，而审计读到的是一份**形状合法、内容却少了一半**的记录：它会照着报「红线判据没有测试认领」，把人支到那些判据上，而毛病在记录。改成读改写更坏 —— 旧那一栏会带着新指纹活下来，变成一句不响的假话。
2. **两者买到的东西不一样**（原文就这么写）。一条单元断言与一条端到端夹具证的不是同一件事；合进同一个名单就分不出来，而落地 4 那条硬失败（「只由自检认领的判据必须有一条 `by: selfcheck` 的负片」）正要靠这个分辨。

形状故意与单元那份完全一样：`claimsWellFormed` / `claimsFresh` / `claimsPublishable` 同一套守两份。自检不认领需求级与交点级，那两栏恒空 —— 同形而已，不是说它认领了 0 条需求。

审计那边四道闸（读不出、不是合法 JSON、形状不对、指纹过期）抽成 `readClaims` 共用，**两份都走它**：各写一份的话，症状是「有一份记录的坏法没人说得清」。

今天认领两条：`P3.b`（四半端到端跑全）与 `D6.f`（四条收尾各跑一次）—— 正是那两条豁免逐字说「缺省那个验证者够不到入口」的。汇总行现在报：

```
验收判据 99 条 · 有测试认领 21 · 入口认领 2 · 其中红线 17 条（测试认领 15 · 入口认领 1 · 显式豁免 2）
```

## 负片：`M-H28-a`

把入口那份记录的路径改成与单元那份同一个。

**这条第一版抓不到。** 当时那一处断言只检查「两份都在 `.check-cache` 底下」，两个路径相同时它照样为真；旁边的注释还替它编了个理由，说「不是同一个路径」写成断言会被编译器当场否掉，所以运行时不必再写。**那句话是错的**：编译器拒的是断言本身（两个字面量类型无交集，那个比较被判为没有意义），而拒的时机是**好的那一版**；真指到同一处时它反倒编译得过。一道只在正确时拦人、出错时放行的闸，守不住任何东西。改成把一边放宽成 `string` 再比，变异当场红在这条断言上。

同一个形状的第三次（#97 第三轮 `M-H14-v`、5c 第二片那条，都是「负片没有真的制造出它声称的违规」）。这次是自己反向验证时发现的：逐条应用、跑、看它红在哪条断言上 —— 这一条跑出来一个 `✗` 都没有。

## 认领写在哪儿

写在它认领的那几条断言**之后**（与 `test.ts` 同一个约定）。`P3.b` 起初写在「续跑从断点起算」那一半之前，而注释声称四半都跑到了 —— 已挪到整段之后。

落在条件分支里的那几处（夹具没造起来就整段跳过）不会写下假认领：每一处跳过都是**先记了一次失败**才跳的，而 `claimsPublishable` 要求这一跑全绿 —— 这个理由现在写在 `criterion` 的说明里，不再靠默契。

## 第一轮评审（`00c529c`）

两条都成立。

**① 架构图没同步。** `selfcheck.ts` 新 import 了 `claims.ts` 与 `lib/atomic.ts`，依赖方向变了，`docs/SYNC.md` 那一行要求同步 `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`；`npm run arch` 查的是锚点覆盖与顺序契约，散文是否为真它自己末行就写着查不了 —— 这条靠人守，我漏了。三行都改。

**② 入口认领那个数没有负片。** 评审说把 `audit.ts` 读记录那一行换成空集合、整条链照样全绿 —— **实测坐实**：三步都是 0 退出，只有「入口认领」从 2 变成 0。拆两半：

- **数得对不对** —— 那一行汇总原先拼在入口脚本里，抽进 `audit-rule.ts` 的 `coverageSummary`，配两条断言、三条负片 `M-H29-a/b/c`。与 `criterionMutations` 上一次被指出时同一个形状、同一条纪律（`CONVENTIONS.md` 第 10 条）。
- **喂得对不对** —— 抽取买不到：纯函数看不见调用方交进来的是不是真的那份记录，入口改交空集合，rule 的断言与三条负片照样全绿。评审给的办法杀不掉它自己点名的那条变异，那一半是下面的欠条。

⚠️ `M-H29-c` 第一版同样抓不到（夹具里三份名单都数出 1），三份改成各覆盖不同的条数之后才红。**加上 `M-H28-a`，「负片没有真的制造出它声称的违规」这个形状在这一片里出现了两回。**

## 欠条

> ⚠️ **入口那一半 —— 自检真写了、审计真读了 —— 一条负片也没有。** 写方在 `selfcheck.ts`、读方在 `audit.ts`，两处都是入口：缺省那个验证者够不到，`by: selfcheck` 也够不到（自检不跑审计，自检也不断言自己写下的那份记录）。今天守着它的只有检查链本身（自检排在审计前面，不写的话审计当场硬失败），那是整条链跑出来的，不是一条负片 · 重启条件：落地 3 第二片

它与 ADR-70 里「入口把什么喂给判定，仍然没人守着」那条是**同一个机制**，而那条的重启条件逐字写的是「落地 3」。落地 3 开工了，**第一片没碰它** —— 第一片只让自检**写**记录，没让自检**起审计**；不起审计就量不到「入口喂对了没有」，那条欠条原样还在。

## 验证

`npm run check` 全绿，306 条变异全部被抓到（`M-H28-a`、`M-H29-a/b/c` 在内）。

body:
The project's Windows SessionStart hook starts a second PowerShell process with a double-quoted command. The outer shell expands `$root` before the inner shell receives it, so startup exits with `The term '=' is not recognized` and loads no project knowledge.

Run the command in Codex's existing PowerShell shell and change to the resolved repository root before invoking the loader. This also loads the correct knowledge when Codex starts in a subfolder. Only the project's Windows hook registration changes.

Validation: reproduced the original exit code 1; the corrected registered command exits 0, loads the knowledge manual, and produces no stderr from both the repository root and `knowledge/`. All four repository checks passed outside the sandbox (the initial sandbox runs blocked Git subprocesses with EPERM). `git diff --check` passed.

After landing, Codex may require review of the changed project hook through `/hooks`. Hook trust was not changed. The separate voice status hook returned OFF/idle during diagnosis; this change does not claim audio playback was tested or that every generic hook warning has the same cause.

author: w7tcv2m7tk-netizen
body:
## Prospecting launch-boundary defects
The live Discovery, Pipeline, Reports and Follow-up pages were using generic platform session context rather than their canonical Prospecting feature gates. Reports also exposed operator-only Growth actions, including creating/linking a DigitalGate client organisation, and multiple pages surfaced implementation details such as `DATABASE_URL` requirements.

## Fix
- require `prospecting.prospects.write` for Discovery
- require `prospecting.prospects.read` for Pipeline, Reports and Follow-up
- use standard denied-route behaviour rather than rendering pseudo-signed-out states inside the authenticated shell
- replace database/configuration implementation messages with customer-safe unavailable states
- catch Follow-up/Reports load failures and keep raw errors server-side
- remove `ConvertProspectToOrgButton` from customer Reports; that action creates/links a DigitalGate tenant and belongs to operator onboarding
- remove the customer-visible `Mark sent` control that calls the `command.growth.manage` mutation path
- keep safe report viewing/sharing and Pipeline handoffs
- replace raw public-token/path language with customer-facing report language

## Feature-completeness checkpoint
Customer expectation: Prospecting pages respect their role permissions and only expose actions that belong to the customer acquisition workflow.
Existing capability: the underlying data is tenant-scoped, but page discovery and some actions were still inherited from the internal Command Centre implementation.
Missing capability: clean customer authority and separation from operator onboarding/configuration.
Severity: Broken/Missing – Launch critical customer boundary.
Decision: fix now; keep operator tenant-creation and command mutations outside customer Prospecting.

## Scope
Four customer-facing pages only. No schema, Growth Engine, report persistence, public report token, discovery provider or tenant-authority changes.

## Description ##

Use a per-bridge counter for packet capture IDs instead of the number of currently active captures. Also aggregate capture-stop errors while removing stopped entries.

## Motivation and context ##

Capture IDs were reused after an earlier capture stopped. Starting captures on two VM interfaces, stopping one, and starting another could overwrite the remaining capture's entry. A subsequent `capture pcap delete vm <name>` then failed with `unknown capture ID` and left a capture running.
