author: calebhendren
body:
Stacked on #1 (merged). Five commits.

## The grid fits the hours actually in play

The grid was always 7:00 AM–8:30 PM, so a centre that opens at 9:00 spent a third of the page on empty mornings. Now:

- **While editing** — 9-to-5, widened to every hour any tutor is available, so there is always somewhere to place a shift someone offered to work.
- **On the handout** — 9-to-5, widened to every hour actually scheduled. Nobody working before 9:00 means the PDF starts at 9:00, and the grid grows to fill the space it saves.

The underlying week is unchanged at 7:00 AM–8:30 PM: that is still where availability is painted and where a tutor can be scheduled. Only the drawing narrows.

**Coverage and Uncovered time now report over those same open hours.** They used to count all 135 half hours whatever the roster looked like, so a 9-to-5 roster read as "79 / 135 covered" behind a wall of 7:00 AM gaps nobody could ever fill. It now reads 79 / 80.

## The handout

- **Semester** on its own line under the title (defaulted to Fall 2026), on both the jsPDF download and the Print / Save as PDF page.
- **Important notes** box under the grid — the closure dates and the last day of tutoring, editable under Schedule settings. The note is measured *before* the grid is laid out, so a long one shortens the grid rather than running off the page (verified: tallest case draws to y=578 of a 584pt safe area).

## Undo

**Ctrl+Z** undoes, **Ctrl+Shift+Z** / **Ctrl+Y** redo, and there is an **Undo** button that greys out at the start of history. Every change already funnels through `store.commit()`, so history lives there rather than asking each caller to record itself — which makes a dragged shift, a deleted tutor, an auto-optimize and even **Start over** undoable for 60 steps without any of them knowing undo exists. In a text field the shortcut is left to the browser.

## Sample roster

Approved hours are a department decision and are the same **15 for everyone**. What varies is which of those hours a student hands in — these tutors are students first. Two offer the full 15, most a few afternoons around their classes, two can manage a single shift: **80 hours offered** between them, nobody before 9:00 AM, covering 9:00–6:00 every day.

Auto-optimize places **78 of the 80** offered hours with **every open half hour covered**; the two it cannot place have no legal shift left that reaches them, and nine of the ten work exactly the hours they handed in.

Three tests described the old roster and had quietly stopped meaning anything: an 80 h budget no longer binds when the roster only offers 80 (Config A moves to 70, where it binds and still leaves nobody starved); the break-threshold check named a tutor who no longer works those days (now asked of every tutor on every day, with a note that the fuzz pass is what really presses that rule); and the duplication check named a pairing that no longer exists (now Tuesday lunchtime, where both tutors offer Biology, asserting the stronger thing it was always about — that a second tutor goes on anyway).

## One thing I did *not* change

You asked whether hours are maximised — coverage first, then subject pairing, then using everyone's willing hours. **It already worked that way**, so I left the optimizer alone. The evidence:

- A tutor approved for 15 and available for exactly 15 works 15.0 h in all six seeds on the untouched optimizer.
- Against a max-flow upper bound (relaxing shift length, breaks and daily caps), the optimizer lands within ~2 h of a ceiling that is itself not attainable.
- Of the half hours left under the 2-tutor cap with a free tutor, **none** are placeable — every one is blocked by minimum shift length, the break rule, a daily cap, or the tutor already working.

I did build and benchmark a rework (willing-hours model, proportional shortfall fairness, a targeted fill move). It was neutral-to-worse across six seeds in three configs and dropped budgeted coverage from 133.5 to 132.7, so I reverted it rather than ship churn.

## Testing

148 assertions pass (was 127). New: the window helpers in both modes, and undo/redo including redo-branch clearing and undoing past the beginning. Verified in headless Chrome — the grid in both themes, a 9-to-5 roster narrowing to 16 rows, the print table, the generated PDF's content stream (semester, notes, time labels 9:00 AM–5:00 PM only, all six day dividers), and Ctrl+Z driven through real key events including the text-field exemption.

## Removing a shift

Removing was **Delete** on a focused block and nothing else, so with a mouse the only way to undo a misplaced shift was **Clear schedule**. Each block now carries an **×** beside its padlock, on the same rule as the padlock: there while you are looking at the block, gone when you are not. Both routes go through one function, so the button and the key cannot drift apart, and both name what they removed and point at Ctrl+Z.

**Delete used to remove a locked shift.** It no longer does, and a locked shift has no **×** at all — locking is what protects a shift from being taken away, here as much as from Clear schedule.

## Contact details scrubbed

`contactName` and `contactEmail` no longer ship as defaults — they are blank and filled in under **Schedule settings**, which is where they belonged. Every piece of the header line is optional now, separator included; the print and PDF headers leave the block out entirely rather than printing an empty one; and a first run says where to put them.

Two references remain and are load-bearing rather than incidental: the GitHub Pages URL and the releases link in the README both contain the account name, because that is the repo's own address. Git history and commit authorship also still carry the name and address — rewriting that is a force-push over shared history, so say the word if you want it.

Verified in headless Chrome: the header line hidden when empty, name-only, and name + mailto link; the PDF and print header building correctly in each state.

## The printed schedule is two pages again

The QR code, the legend and the listing were spilling past page 1 — a four-page handout for a one-page schedule.

Two causes, both measured by actually printing rather than eyeballing:

- **Page 1 cleared the page by eight pixels**, so the footer's `page-break-inside: avoid` tipped the QR and legend onto a page of their own. Type and spacing through the header, grid, notes and footer are now a little tighter, leaving ~90px of room.
- **The listing is a narrow list on a landscape page** — a third of the width, one and a half pages of height. It now runs in two columns, with each day an unbreakable unit so a column never splits a heading from its shifts.

Verified: page 1 holds calendar + notes + QR + legend, page 2 holds the listing — with and without the browser's own header/footer, and on a roster dense enough to fill the week. Two pages in every case.

author: ciresnave-bot
body:
**The fuel architect found this in fuel's ratchet and it generalises to every gate in this portfolio.**

Measured at fuel `d37e446e`: it enumerates `git ls-files "*.rs"` and reports **834/834** while **203 tracked source files sit outside its population** — 147 `.slang`, 20 `.glsl`, 19 `.py`, 16 `.metal` — three carrying third-party copyright with no SPDX at all.

> ⚠️ **A property asserted over the wrong population is still the wrong population** — and a scoped ratchet's number goes **up** as the blind spot grows, because the denominator never learns about the new files.

**Any tracked extension that is source must now be in `EXTENSIONS` or declined in `NOT_STAMPED` by name, with a reason.** An entry naming an extension the tree no longer has **also reds**.

## Measured across all four repos carrying this gate

| repo | outside `EXTENSIONS` | |
|---|---|---|
| kiss-ref | nothing | clean |
| vulkane | `.spv` generated, `.xml` = `vk.xml` | clean, both now declared |
| synapse | **4** — 2 `.ps1`, 1 `.sh`, 1 `.sql` | 🔴 was blind |
| OverMind | **3** — 2 `.ts`, 1 `.sh` | 🔴 was blind |

⚠️ **Two of four had exactly fuel's blindness**, so *"a pure-Rust tree has nothing outside it"* would have been wrong for half of them. **That is the value of the measurement over the default.**

## 🔴 The only principled ground for a decline is that the file is GENERATED

`vulkane` declines `.spv` because those are **compiled SPIR-V — build outputs of the `.wgsl`/`.comp` sources already in its list.**

> **"Is it generated from something else in this tree?" is a property with a checkable answer. "Is it schema or source?" is a taxonomy argument with no test.**

**That rule is written into `NOT_STAMPED`'s docstring**, where the next decline will be made — not left in a commit message.

## And a bug in the staleness check, found by recording vulkane's two declines

`stale = set(NOT_STAMPED) - source_present` reported `.spv` and `.xml` as **stale while both sit in the tree** — neither is in `SOURCE_EXTENSIONS`, so neither appeared in `source_present`.

⚠️ **The effect: a decline of a non-source extension could never be recorded without redding** — which would have pushed every such reason back into a comment, **the exact artifact class this gate exists to replace.** Compared against every present extension now, **fixed in all four gates in the same pass.**

## ⚠️ It does not fully close, and saying so is the point

`SOURCE_EXTENSIONS` is **itself a hand-written list** — the exact defect class this gate keeps finding in its own author. **It turns a silent omission into a loud one, which is the whole of the win:** the failure mode moves from *nobody ever knows* to *somebody has to decline it by name with a reason.*

**Verified by RUNNING each gate rather than reading the diff.** ⚠️ **A port is the one change whose diff is guaranteed to look correct, because it was produced by copying something correct from somewhere else** — measured on `synapse#26`, where a port silently dropped the empty-file skip.

Not merging this myself.

author: sisyphusmd
body:
## Description

**What problem does this PR solve?**
With exercise-library access enabled through Family & Friends Sharing, an Apple Health import can select a family member's Active Calories exercise instead of the importing user's own exercise. If a later sync selects a different exercise ID for the same day, the existing-entry lookup misses the previous import and inserts another row. Both rows belong to the importing user, but their cumulative totals are added together, inflating the day's active calories.

**How did you implement the solution?**
Keep the daily import tied to the importing user's own exercise regardless of family-library visibility, and reuse same-day, same-source legacy imports linked to another exercise. A migration removes recognized duplicate daily imports caused by shared definitions, retaining the most recently updated import. It leaves groups with manual edits, unknown metadata or attached workout data unchanged.

Linked Issue: None.

## How to Test

1. Run the server validation and test suite. The existing migration checks also run the new cases in `rlsPermissionMatrix.integration.test.ts` against PostgreSQL.
2. In Family & Friends Sharing, grant a second user View Exercise Library access to a user with an Active Calories exercise. Import 300 HealthKit calories for the second user, revoke that access, and import 350 for the same day. Verify one entry remains with 350 calories and an exercise owned by the second user. Native tests also cover public exercise sharing, which exposes the same lookup defect.
3. Seed bare autogenerated HealthKit entries for the same person and day: 300 calories using an owned exercise and a newer 350-calorie import using a shared exercise. Apply the migration and verify only the 350-calorie row remains, with its original ID and metadata. Repeat the migration to verify idempotence.
4. Sync a corrected total of 250 for that day. Verify the remaining row is updated to 250. Also verify a newer 250-calorie duplicate takes precedence over an older 350-calorie duplicate during migration. Native tests also check user/date/source boundaries and preservation of manual metadata and all five attached-data tables.

## PR Type

- [x] Issue (bug fix)
- [ ] New Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Documentation

## Checklist

**All PRs:**

- [x] **[MANDATORY - ALL] Integrity & License**: I certify this is my own work, free of malicious code, and I agree to the [License terms](https://github.com/CodeWithCJ/SparkyFitness/blob/main/LICENSE).

**New features only:**

- [ ] **[MANDATORY for new feature] Alignment**: I have raised a GitHub issue and it was reviewed/approved by maintainers or it was approved on Discord.

**Frontend changes (`SparkyFitnessFrontend/`):**

- [ ] **[MANDATORY for Frontend changes] Quality**: I have run `pnpm run validate` and it passes.
- [ ] **[MANDATORY for Frontend changes] Translations**: I have only updated the English (`en`) translation file.

**Backend changes (`SparkyFitnessServer/`):**

- [x] **[MANDATORY for Backend changes] Code Quality**: I have run typecheck, lint, and tests. New files use TypeScript, new endpoints have Zod schemas, and new endpoints include tests.
- [x] **[MANDATORY for Backend changes] Database Security**: I have updated `rls_policies.sql` for any new user-specific tables.

**UI changes (components, screens, pages):**

- [ ] **[MANDATORY for UI changes] Screenshots**: I have attached Before/After screenshots below.

**Mobile changes (`SparkyFitnessMobile/`):**

- [ ] **[MANDATORY for Mobile changes] Tested on device or emulator**: I have verified the changes work on iOS or Android.

## Screenshots

Not applicable.

## Notes for Reviewers

The survivor uses `updated_at`, which records the last write to Sparky, not source measurement time. Equal timestamps prefer the higher cumulative total, then an owned exercise and stable creation time/ID. A later sync can still correct the retained value downward. Cleanup requires a foreign-owned exercise definition in the group and recognized autogenerated entries throughout; unknown groups remain unchanged. No new tables or RLS policy changes. Source selection for an existing exact-exercise match is unchanged.

body:
Five Docker images, each based on the glibc CI builder with one SSL library built from source at /usr/local (static, system libssl-dev removed):

| Image suffix | Library | Pony `-D` flag |
|---|---|---|
| `libressl-3.9.2` | LibreSSL 3.9.2 | `-Dlibressl` |
| `libressl-4.2.1` | LibreSSL 4.2.1 | `-Dlibressl` |
| `openssl-1.1.1w` | OpenSSL 1.1.1w | `-Dopenssl_1.1.x` |
| `openssl-3.6.2` | OpenSSL 3.6.2 | `-Dopenssl_3.0.x` |
| `openssl-4.0.0` | OpenSSL 4.0.0 | `-Dopenssl_4.0.x` |

Three workflows:

- **`net-ssl-tests.yml`** — triggers on PRs touching `packages/net/`. One build job (ponyc debug, installed with symlinks off), then 5 matrix test jobs each compiling and running `packages/net/` with the right `-D` flag in the matching SSL container.
- **`rebuild-ssl-builder-images.yml`** — cascades when the base `ubuntu26.04-builder` is rebuilt. Three triggers: `repository_dispatch` from `build-builder-image.yml`, `registry_package` (best-effort for local pushes), `workflow_dispatch`.
- **`build-builder-image.yml`** — gains the 5 SSL builders in its dispatch choice list and a cascade trigger step on the `ubuntu26.04-builder` job.

author: adam-dalloul
body:
`parsers::pi::tests::settings_json_session_dir_is_honored` fails on `Rust server on windows-latest`, and it fails on main too (run 34542650449 at a6918223), so every open PR inherits one red job.

The test hard-codes `/srv/pi-sessions`. `session_dir_from_settings` only honors an absolute `sessionDir`, and `Path::is_absolute` wants a drive or UNC prefix on Windows, so that literal is not absolute there. The gate correctly refuses it, the resolver falls back to `<agent_dir>/sessions`, and the assertion fails. The `~`-rooted case right below it has the same problem for the same reason, it just never got to run.

The product code looks right to me, so this only changes the test: both paths now get a `C:` prefix when the test runs on Windows. Verified by extracting the resolver and running it here with a windows-gnu toolchain: the current form fails both cases and the new form passes, alongside the env-var and relative-path cases which were never platform dependent.

body:
## Defect

Two demonstrated text-chunking correctness problems in `packages/knowledge/src/ingestion/chunk.ts`:

1. **UTF-16 surrogate pairs were split at window edges.** `fixedWindowOffsets` sliced by code-unit index with no code-point alignment. A boundary landing between the two halves of a surrogate pair emitted lone surrogates. Reproduced with `"a".repeat(99) + "\uD83D\uDE00" + "b".repeat(80)` at `maxChars: 100`: the old code produced `[0,100)` (1 lone high surrogate) and `[100,181)` (1 lone low surrogate), which corrupt to replacement characters when the text is encoded — i.e. dropped/corrupted content, a violation of "no text lost".
2. **ATX-style lines inside fenced code blocks were treated as headings.** `chunkMarkdown` scanned for `^#{1..6}` anywhere, so `# not a heading` inside a ``` fence became a fake chunk heading and split the code block.

## Fix

- **Code-point-safe boundaries:** `alignEndBoundary`/`alignStartBoundary` refuse to split a surrogate pair. END pushes right past the low surrogate (kept with its high half); START only ever pushes right, and the skipped low surrogate is already covered by the previous aligned window, so content is never dropped or duplicated. This is O(1) per boundary and does not change chunk/overlap limits.
- **Fence-aware headings:** `findAtxHeadings` tracks ``` / ~~~ fences (3+ chars, optional info string, indented up to 3 spaces; closing run >= opening length) and only records headings outside fences. CRLF is handled (the `\r` is kept for offsets).

## Tests

16 new tests in `chunk.test.ts` plus an adversarial-invariants block: exact spans (`chunk.text === text.slice(charStart, charEnd)`), no lone surrogates (code-unit-level detection), zero-loss reconstruction at overlap 0, emoji at window edges (text + markdown), long unbroken emoji runs, combining characters, CRLF, exact size boundaries, empty input, backtick/tilde/CRLF fences, and mixed text/markdown/yaml fixtures. Existing 44 tests unchanged and passing.

## Performance evidence

New guardrail added to `packages/knowledge/src/performance-baseline.test.ts` (`perf:runtime` gate): a 73 KB markdown document with fences + emoji chunks in ~19-30 ms (guardrail 1500 ms). Before/after on a 519 KB markdown document (5-run average): old ~54-82 ms, new ~61-78 ms — equivalent within noise, no asymptotic change (fence scan is a single O(n) pass).

## Compatibility note

Chunk boundaries/ids change **only** for markdown containing a `#...`-style line inside a fenced code block — precisely the defective case. All other markdown (no fences, fences without heading-like lines), and all text/yaml/csv/json input, produce identical chunk identities and offsets. Offsets remain exact for every type; chunk/overlap limits, deterministic ordering, and content hashes are unchanged.

author: wtadler
body:
A bill's description leads with the sections it affects — "An Act to amend 6.86 (1) (a) 2.; to create 5.02 of the statutes; Relating to: ..." — and that text is already in the keyword haystack. A statute chapter is therefore a usable intake signal with no bill text needed. It just wasn't expressible.

**Two things blocked it.**

The boundary class was `[a-zA-Z]`, so a digit didn't block a boundary and `5.` matched section `115.385` of an unrelated chapter — measured 607 hits on a 2,751-bill corpus, 9% precision. Adding a star didn't help: `5.*` compiles to the same left boundary, because the glob only relaxes the right-hand side, which was never the problem.

And `*` is unbounded, so `5.*` also matched the subdivision at the tail of any citation — `(1) (b) 5.,` — which a chapter gate must not catch.

**The change.** The class is `[a-zA-Z0-9]` on both sides, and `#` matches exactly one digit, so `5.#*` reads as "a section of chapter 5". Symmetric rather than left-only because the right-hand class only affects starless keywords, and one rule is easier to hold than two. An exact cite also gets stricter, and more correct: `19.85` no longer matches `19.851`, a different section.

**Measured cost of the class change:** across 32,750 bills in seven tenants, replayed against each tenant's own keyword list, **zero bills change verdict** and no keyword in use has a digit directly abutting it. It does flip `election` against "election2024", which two tests asserted; `election*` covers that case and no keyword in use relies on it.

**Measured benefit,** on the corpus that motivated it: 100% precision and 100% recall on all 16 chapters tracked, versus 32% precision for the unbounded `5.*` form.

Claiming `#` is a one-way door — there's no escape syntax, so no keyword can carry a literal `#` from here on. No tenant used one; the doc comment says so deliberately.

`keywordSweep` strips `#` from the provider query for the same reason it strips `*`. That path is OpenStates-only, and a comment now says so — LegiScan's `fetchKeywordMatches` is an empty generator and the deployed LegiScan entrypoint never calls the sweep, so reading that strip as proof of provider-side search is a mistake the code previously invited.

Full suite green.

author: bfbryan
body:
The dashboard card counted referrals and then listed people, so a reader could not tell whether three names meant three staff or three referrals from fewer. The subject is people, because people are what the admin acts on.

Copy becomes "N unconfirmed staff members: names. Confirm the ones who work at your office." The render gate moves to staffNames.length, which is the more correct gate — staffNames is built from the same query that produces referralCount, so the two differ only when every matching referral has an unresolvable staff lookup, and in that case the card should not fire.

The card also gains the heading tier its sibling announcement card has. It previously put its whole message in the 10px uppercase eyebrow with nothing in the 14px Montserrat slot, which is why it read flat beside a card that has that step.

author: casselc
body:
## Purpose

Add a reproducible, production-path benchmark that can qualify Durable admission for realistic ClickStack-shaped OTel log batches against explicit targets:

- 512-row encoding-inclusive p50 at or above 25,000 rows/s (at most 20.48 ms/batch)
- 512-row encoding-inclusive p99 at or above 20,000 rows/s (at most 25.60 ms/batch)

This PR establishes the measurement and correctness gate. It does not claim current main meets those targets.

## What the harness measures

- encoding-inclusive Durable admission before flush;
- pre-encoded Durable admission before flush;
- persisted throughput at an explicit flush cadence;
- ordinary JDBC and direct prepared/native controls;
- isolated exporter encoding, placeholder rewriting, UTF-8 sizing, and generic `data.json` WAL encoding;
- one instrumented causal control over the production Durable path; and
- reopen/recovery aggregates from a fresh immutable reader.

Qualification uses 100 batches per trial and five trials per mode, yielding 500 batch-latency samples across trials. Smoke, probe, and diagnostic profiles are explicitly nonqualifying.

## Correctness and causal evidence

The benchmark deliberately leaves the production `publish-wal!` closure in place, including its operation retry budget and lease-aware stop predicate. It instruments the backend to observe immutable WAL PUT and head CAS instead of replacing publication logic.

Every Durable run asserts the pending statement count, performs exactly one measured flush, reopens from immutable storage, and reconciles row count, trace-flag and severity sums, body bytes, question-mark bodies, and min/max trace and span IDs. The causal control also proves the expected classification, native execution, WAL PUT, and head-CAS counts.

The retained current-main diagnostic separates the bottlenecks and prevents an attractive but invalid optimization: WAL construction may not overlap native execution under Durable V1 because an encoder failure after native success could leave engine state without replay state.

## Current-main diagnostic

At base `5bbe8651b6c24cd713a826a8a9a0f3fcb56fcd24`, Jolt 0.8.3, Chez 10.4.1, and chDB 26.7.2-rc.2, a 348,877-byte 512-row statement produced these two-sample diagnostics:

| Path or stage | p50 batch latency |
| --- | ---: |
| Durable, encoding included | 2,633.86 ms |
| Durable, pre-encoded | 2,028.54 ms |
| Ordinary JDBC, pre-encoded | 529.30 ms |
| Exporter encoding | 645.64 ms |
| Placeholder rewrite | 718.15 ms |
| Generic `data.json` WAL encoding | 1,314.97 ms |
| Direct prepared/native insert | 10.32 ms |

These are causal diagnostics, not a qualification result. The direct native control shows the engine can execute this workload inside the 20.48 ms p50 budget, leaving about 10.16 ms for all managed work. Current managed stages exceed that remainder independently, so a long qualification run would only consume resources while the implementation is known to miss.

The older #63 numbers used a different 136 KB pre-encoded statement, omitted exporter encoding, and did not commit their harness. This PR makes future claims rerunnable and comparable.

## Validation

Exact head: `560f7424bd89f391d553a994799286a178bb061f`

- Chez selection verified through `/home/chuck/ai-src/tools/jolt-with-chez-10.4.1`: exactly 10.4.1.
- Durable control suite passed, including ambiguous retry/reconciliation and the 40-case Hegel gate.
- Exact smoke profile completed in 10.7 seconds across every mode/stage with one WAL PUT, one head CAS, and successful reopen/recovery.
- Smoke artifact digest: `c976cc0b8cbadfd607026acfb68e35fe250b9052c2d4b8ad393654b2590bfc0f`.
- `git diff --check` passes.
- Independent exact-head review: READY with no blockers; it confirmed production retry/fencing preservation, honest sampling/thresholds, nonvacuous recovery assertions, nonqualifying smoke/probe separation, and report hygiene.

## Report hygiene and remote scope

Reports contain aggregate values, operation labels/counts, byte counts, timings, version/host characterization, and the native library basename/size/digest. They omit credentials, signed URLs, headers, SQL, payload bodies, bucket names, object prefixes, and local native-library paths. Generated reports remain ignored under `target/profiles/`.

The documentation defines a later OIDC-protected S3 qualification curve using the same workload and correctness checks. This PR does not claim an S3 measurement and does not introduce multipart uploads; remote work should follow only after local admission is near its target.

## Delivery

- Adds the benchmark alias and ignored artifact directory.
- Documents invocation, interpretation, optimization order, and the S3 follow-up design.
- Adds an Unreleased changelog entry.
- Tracks the remaining optimization work in #64.

M4-A 병합 `f097295` 이후 **M4-C 단계별 지원 결과 기록**을 구현합니다. 개인용 포트폴리오 초안이며 외부 모델 API는 호출하지 않았습니다.

- #10: 새 테이블 대신 기존 `application_events` JSON 확장. 이력/정정 저장소 하나, 기존 reset 경로 유지.

## 구현

- 선택적 정규화 단계·발생 시점·출처와 version 2 최소 이벤트.
- `historyMode`는 생략하면 `append`(새 진행)입니다. `replace`는 명시할 때만 적용되며 **이전 결과 이력 전체를 집계에서 제외**합니다 (리뷰 반영 `c2a862a`). 특정 이벤트 하나의 정정이 아닙니다. 과거 감사 행은 reset 전까지 남습니다.
- 메모-only 변경은 이력을 유지하고, 단계 지우기는 이전 단계 집계를 철회합니다. 동일한 즉시 재시도는 no-op입니다. 중간 변경 이후의 지연 요청까지 request ID로 중복 제거하지는 않습니다.
- 단계 도달/직무별 진행은 distinct application ID 기준, verdict × stage와 단계·날짜 coverage는 현재 상태 기준. 기존 last-updated 필터와 100개 상세 상한은 유지하고 집계에는 전체 매칭 기록을 포함합니다.
- 옛 JSON을 수정하지 않는 migration 2(index 추가), conservative legacy mapping. 과거 stage/date는 unknown; 정정 여부가 불명확한 옛 스냅샷들로 진행 이력을 재구성하지 않습니다.
- strict 위젯 소비자에 맞춰 URI v4, compact 단계 표시, 합성 데모 정정 버튼. ChatGPT descriptor refresh 필요.
- 영문/한글 README, 계획 확정, `docs/MILESTONE_4C.md`에 계약/제약/예시 기록.

## 검증 — `c2a862a` 기준 재실행

- `pnpm typecheck` · `pnpm lint` · `pnpm build` · `git diff --check`: 통과
- `pnpm test`: **157/157 (shared 7 + server 150)**, 신규 outcome test 16개(기본 append·v1 no-op 회귀 포함) + 기존 MCP 회귀 시나리오 보강
- `pnpm eval --no-save`: **28/28**, reportVersion 2, **modelCalls 0**. 모델 정확도 검증 아님; 사람 fit-label 검토는 여전히 28개 대기.
- 같은 fit/다른 탈락 단계, append/즉시 재시도, 전체 이력 정정/철회, 날짜 unknown, 메모 배제, legacy DB upgrade/restart, migration rollback, reset, 101개 집계/100개 상세 제한 검증.
- 브라우저: 합성 3개 지원에서 진행 **0 → 1 → 0**, 서류 탈락 **0 → 1**, 원래 REALISTIC 유지. 390×844 가로 overflow 없음.
- 최초 테스트는 sandbox의 HTTP/tsx IPC `EPERM`로 실패했고, 로컬 소켓 허용 후 전체 재실행 통과. 테스트 unused binding도 커밋 전에 수정했습니다.
- 브라우저 최초 favicon 404 외 위젯 오류 없음. 기존 설치 의존성 재사용; lockfile/의존성 변경 없음.

1. 전체 이력 replace 범위와 stage/date omission·clear 규칙이 명확한지 확인 부탁드립니다. 세부 이벤트 단위 편집은 후속입니다.
2. legacy 이력은 보수적으로 제한하며, 지원 횟수는 저장된 application ID 기준이지 실제 중복 공고 제거 결과가 아닙니다.

병합하지 않았습니다. 리뷰 후 소유자가 직접 병합합니다.

author: chrisuthe
body:
# What does this implement/fix?

Implements spec [#163](https://github.com/Sendspin/spec/pull/163). `client_stream/start` and`client_stream/end` become `client-stream/start` and `client-stream/end` on the wire.

The discriminator accepts both spellings for the same message, driven by one map of superseded names in `models/types.py`, so a later rename joins it rather than growing a second mechanism. A source still on the old spelling is served and flagged, exactly as the legacy `client/state` field and the pre-rename artwork dimension keys already are — which means a server running `allow_noncompliant_clients=False` will drop it, that being what opting into strict mode has always meant. The name a message arrived under survives on the parsed message, so nothing has to be recorded alongside it.

NOTE:

- **The Python identifiers are deliberately unchanged**, unlike the sibling rename in #351.   There, a word changed (`static` → `output`). Here only the separator moved, and a hyphen  is not a Python identifier character — `on_client_stream_start` already spells  `client-stream/start` as closely as a method name can. `Role.on_client_stream_start` is an  ABC hook with a no-op default, so renaming it would silently stop delivering the callback  to any embedder who did not follow, and buy nothing.

- The client emits the new spelling, so it requires a server that understands it. That is the same trade as the other renames in this series.

**Related issue (if applicable):**

- n/a

## Types of changes

- [x] Refactor (no behaviour change) — `refactor`

## Checklist

- [x] The code change is tested and works locally.
- [x] `pre-commit run --all-files` passes.
- [x] `pytest` passes, and tests have been added/updated under `tests/` where applicable.

author: argamboad
body:
## What

The QA plan covered **the platform only**. A search of its 2,300 lines for "cocktail", "shelf", "makeable" or "ingredient" returned **nothing** — nineteen merged app slices and not one case — while its scope section still listed as out of scope *"any app-specific domain features not yet built on this platform"*. True when it was written; false since the first slice merged.

Docs only. No code.

## Six new suites, §10d–§10i, 54 cases (150 → 204)

Following the document's own conventions: Gherkin **plus** walkthrough for 🔴/🟠, one-line walkthroughs for 🟢, priority markers, and the ⚙️ marker where a browser journey already covers the path.

| Suite | Covers |
|---|---|
| **§10d** the shelf | ticking, rollback, search, custom ingredients, counts, the jump bar, the payoff footer, keyboard + screen reader |
| **§10e** the catalog | browse, paging, a recipe, filters, the measurement preference, cross-household 404 |
| **§10f** what I can make | makeable, one-away, the ranked bottle, the recipe's own badge, the home screen, both empty states |
| **§10g** making it mine | forking, the snapshot rule, authoring, what the form refuses |
| **§10h** the first minute | the wizard, and the rule that nothing is written until Finish |
| **§10i** Marga and the chrome | her lines, the tab bar, the boot state, reduced motion, Spanish |

**§10d comes first on purpose.** Until a household has told the app what it owns, "what can I make right now" has no answer — so a failure there cascades into §10f and §10h, and the suite says so.

## Two stale claims corrected

- The scope paragraph above.
- The automation figure: **34 journeys claimed, 52 actual**, 17 of them the app's own.

## Three test-data needs the platform's cases never had

Now in §1.2, because a tester cannot improvise them:

- **A never-touched shelf.** You cannot get back to it by unticking, because unticking records a decision rather than erasing one (JJ-023).
- **A screen reader.** The shelf's controls are hidden checkboxes styled through their labels, so "does it still announce as a checkbox" is not something you can see.
- **A Spanish reader.** Whether Marga's lines read as *written* Spanish rather than as a translation is a judgement, not a check.

Plus a note that **which catalog is loaded changes the counts** — and makes `QA-MAKE-10` unreachable outright, since single-ingredient recipes mean an empty shelf is one bottle away from several drinks. That case tells the tester to record **N-A** and note the catalog size.

## Details worth flagging

- **Case ids avoid the platform's.** `QA-INV-*` is already invitations, so the shelf is `QA-SHELF-*`.
- Every new case has a **traceability row (§15)** and a **sign-off row (§16)** — 54 and 54.
- The app's half is **the least automated part of the plan by design**, and §2 now says so. What a browser journey cannot check is whether a count is *honest*, whether a suggestion is *useful*, whether her Spanish reads as Spanish.

## Why it drifted, and what stops it next time

The plan's own §17 already said: *"When you add an app-specific domain feature on top of this platform, add a matching suite here and a row in the traceability matrix."* That instruction sat there unfollowed through every app slice.

So the **slice ritual in `docs/PLAN.md` now carries the step** (7b), and the maintainer note says why it is there — a reminder in the document being maintained is not enough on its own.

## Checks

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Cases defined | 204 |
| Sign-off rows for the new cases | 54, one per case |
| Duplicate case ids | none |
| Api.Tests | 873 passed |
| Ui.Tests / Core.Tests | 73 / 80 passed |

The `ClaudeMdQaCaseCount_MatchesTheQaPlan` gate caught the doc-map row: it reads a plain `(N cases:` and markdown bold broke the pattern. Fixed rather than the gate loosened.

body:
## Scope

Add an opt-in `-Dnative-make-environment` bridge for native private artifact preparation. The bounded, canonical, versioned private contract supplies only explicit shell, M4, Bison, temporary, and cache paths. The facade emits a fixed set of Make assignments, including `UMASK=0077`.

Default builds, canonical passwd HOME, and the stable host-wide facade lock remain unchanged. Arbitrary inherited environment variables and expanded `-Dmake-arg` control channels remain refused.

author: yea-80y
body:
## What

Closes the residual of #505: a stale `absent` from a lagging RPC replica on the recovery panel's OWN mount-time read could turn "add another backup" into an `install` that replaces the guardian set. The panel had nothing to contradict, so the #505 guard could not fire.

- **`recovery-landing-block.ts`** (new): a per-device, per-account, MONOTONIC memory of the last block a recovery write landed in (`woco:recovery:landing-block:<kernel>`, localStorage + in-memory mirror, every access in try/catch). Pure `decidePinnedBlock({ head, minBlock })`: head below the bound ⇒ lagging; otherwise pin the HEAD (never the bound itself — that would hide later changes made on another device). Pinning every read of a batch to one specific block also makes them atomic against load balancing: a second replica that lacks the block errors → `unknown`.
- **`readRecoveryRouteNoOlderThan`** (`kernel-account.ts`): head → decide → route + WoCo set at the same pinned block; a lagging replica is NEVER asked about the route. Used by the panel (`readBackupProtection`), the store's pre-write reads in `setupAccountRecovery`, and `removeAllBackups`' pre-read.
- Every proven write records its landing block AFTER its read-back proves the change: `setupRecovery`, `addGuardianOnChain`, `revokeGuardianOnChain`, `removeAllBackups`, and the recovery rotation.
- **`decideProtection`** gains the contradiction cell: chain `absent` + hint `configured:true` ⇒ `isProtected: null` ("couldn't check"), never a confident answer in either direction — a forgeable hint must not mint a safety claim against a chain read, and one replica must not mint "not protected".
- The panel shows the set the write PROVED after an add (returned from `setupAccountRecovery`) instead of re-reading a chain that may still lag; its "adding is safe either way" clause is gone because it was false on exactly this path.
- Sign-out does not sweep the memory on purpose: it holds no secret, and clearing it would reopen the window on the next sign-in on that device.

**Honest limit (in the DEVLOG):** a device that has never seen this account's route change has no bound to demand and falls back to today's behaviour, where the #505 guard is the only protection.

## Verification (Fable, in-context)

- web 756/756 (+22), shared 341 (ratchet), `check` clean, `build:web` green
- Mutations re-run by the gate, each red: lagging check removed; panel read back to "latest"; the install write forgets its block; contradiction cell back to `false`
- The builder ran 17 mutations; its 8th (aliasing the unpinned read into the pinned name) SURVIVED and was closed in the second commit — the source pin now refuses the rename too

Closes #510.

author: vyncint
body:
termlens 0.11.0 is on crates.io — that project's **stability candidate**, after which no promised item changes incompatibly before its 1.0. This repository's job is to check a published release from outside, and this bump paid for itself twice: both behaviour changes below were found by a test **failing**, not by reading the changelog.

**A pin that inverted, as it was written to.** `survey_0_10.rs` pinned termlens#320 as a defect: taskboard's badge blinks and its titles are struck through — `hard.rs` asserts both — and `unsupported()` named those sequences as unimplemented anyway. The pin said, in the test body, that it *should become* the opposite assertion once the defect was fixed:

```rust
"termlens#320 — if this fails the defect is fixed, and this pin
 should become `assert!(!listed.contains(...))`: {listed:?}"
```

Against 0.11.0 it fails, so it is now that assertion. None of the four sequences the attribute shadow recovers is listed while its attribute is on a cell; `^[[59m` still is, correctly. Independent confirmation of an upstream fix, driving the real binary.

**A contract change caught by a stale assertion.** `cli.rs` asserted `inspect`'s trailer appeared in **stdout**. termlens#340 moved it to stderr so that `termlens inspect prog > file` saves a screen the tool reads back. The test now asserts the split *and* the round trip it enables: stdout parses as a `Screen`, and the captured file is accepted by both `render --text` and `diff`. That is a stronger test than the one it replaces, and it exists because the old one broke.

**`tests/survey_0_11.rs` is new** — nine probes of the candidate's surface, written the way a consumer would write them:

- the `Unsupported` view that replaced `&[Arc<str>]`: the whole surface, plus **a record driven past its retention bound** with hand-written escapes (40 distinct unimplemented modes against a retention of 32) — no application here produces that on its own, and it is the case the old two-call shape could get wrong. The view is unequal to the list of what it kept, and `Debug` says `(+8 more)`.
- `cursor_visible`; the `Location` accessors (with needles chosen so the grid-wins tie is not what is being measured); `ScreenDiff::changed_rows` and `style_changes`, cross-checked against the `cells()` dedup they replace; `Display for Color` round-tripping through a real styles block; the nameable `ScreenWithStyles`, stored in a struct field; and the JSON's format number, including that a 0.10 file without the field still reads and a later one is refused **by number**.

**Verified:** `cargo test` **201 passed, 0 failed**; clippy `-D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` clean. The CLI under test is installed from crates.io at the lockfile's version, so the library and the tool are one release. Requirement `0.10.1 → 0.11`; lockfile moved `termlens` and nothing else.

From crates.io, never a path dependency or `[patch.crates-io]`.

body:
Replaces the hook→payoff→CTA caption composer (and the `--llm` rewrite) with the **8 fixed templates**, each interpolating `{place}`/`{category}`/`{state}` exactly as written.

## Caption goes to the caption output, NOT the image
Confirmed: `composite.ts` puts only the place name + "Category · State" on the image. The 8-template caption is written to `caption.txt` / `caption.json` (the IG caption output). *Confidence: literal / directly verified (read composite.ts + generate.ts).*

## Rotation + persistence
- Default: **least-recently-used** template (`pickLruTemplate`) from a durable log table (`pin_of_week_caption_history`, migration `20260911010000`), then logs the pick. This is the caption-level analog of `featured_at` — but because a template is chosen *per generate* and rotation is *global*, it's a small append-only table, not a per-place column (justified in the migration header). LRU → no immediate repeat, cycles evenly through all 8.
- `generate --id <uuid> --caption-template N` forces template N (1–8). **Forced picks are not logged** so they don't perturb the rotation.
- `{category}` uses the humanized label ("Campground", "Park Feature") — raw enums read unnaturally in the sentences.

## Verified end-to-end on TEST (all *literal / directly verified*)
Migration applied via `db:push-verify -- --test`; table confirmed by direct query. 3 auto generates rotated **1 → 2 → 3** (no repeats), all logged with place + timestamp; forced templates left the history at 3 rows.

**Real generated captions (auto rotation):**

> **#1 — Gold Bluffs:** We verified Gold Bluffs Beach Campground - Prairie Creek Redwoods State Park so you don't have to guess. Campground · CA. Want the full route notes before you go? Link in bio to get every verified spot straight to your inbox.

> **#2 — Palouse Falls:** Palouse Falls State Park almost didn't make the list — here's why it did. Verified Recreation Area pick in WA. We send the ones that actually make the cut to our mailing list first. Join up via the link in bio.

> **#3 — Point Bonita:** Not every spot with a pin on a map is actually worth the drive. Point Bonita Lighthouse is. Park Feature · CA — Yo Trippin verified. Get next week's pick before it's posted — sign up at the link in bio.

> **#8 (forced) — Boulder Basin:** Boulder Basin: one of the ones that made the cut. Campground, CA. Not every submission gets verified. The ones that do go straight to our mailing list first — link in bio to join.

## ⚠️ Edge cases flagged (not silently shipped)
- **Category/name redundancy:** Gold Bluffs' name ends "State Park" but its category is "Campground" → "…State Park. Campground · CA" reads repetitively. *Literal / observed.*
- **Long place names** make templates wordy (that 63-char name in template 1). *Literal / observed.*
- **Null state** (~788 eligible places) would interpolate `{state}` empty → "Campground · ." The test set all have states. *Strong inference — flagged, not hit.*

- Builds on **#419** (its `photo_override` migration is applied on TEST, so this migration had to stack on that ledger — basing on main failed the push). Chain: #418 → #419 → this.

author: ndizazzo
body:
## Original problem

`cargo build` and `cargo test` fail to link on macOS whenever Homebrew lld falls behind the macOS SDK, while `cargo check` stays green. Today that is LLVM 23.1.1 against the 27.0 SDK:

```
ld64.lld: error: could not load TAPI file at
  /Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/SDKs/MacOSX.sdk/usr/lib/libSystem.tbd: malformed file
libSystem.tbd:4:20: error: unknown target
                   arm64e.x1-macos, arm64e.x1-maccatalyst ]
```

After that every libSystem symbol is undefined. It is SDK-ahead-of-lld skew, so downgrading lld does not help, and it reproduces on `main` with plain `clang -fuse-ld=ld64.lld hello.c`.

Three places committed cargo to lld without checking it: the `# BEGIN Mesh-LLM lld config` block in `.cargo/config.toml` (also hardcoded to `/opt/homebrew`), `just with-lld`, and `scripts/build-host.sh`. `scripts/package-native-runtime.sh` only checked that `ld64.lld` existed.

## Diagnostics

On unmodified `origin/main` (d4ffbbacd):

```
$ cargo test -p mesh-llm-build-info --no-run
error: linking with `cc` failed: exit status: 1
  ld64.lld: error: could not load TAPI file at .../MacOSX.sdk/usr/lib/libSystem.tbd: malformed file
```

## Fix

New `scripts/lib/lld.sh` resolves lld and probes it with a one-line C link through `cc` (the same driver rustc uses) before anything uses it. Usable: used exactly as before. Installed but unusable: the linker's own diagnostic is printed once and the build continues with the platform linker. Not installed: still a hard error with install instructions.

`just with-lld`, `build-host.sh`, and `package-native-runtime.sh` all go through it. The `.cargo/config.toml` lld block is removed, so a bare `cargo test` no longer depends on a linker nothing has probed. When Homebrew ships an lld that parses the new SDK, the probe passes and lld returns on its own.

CI macOS is unaffected: `setup-macos-lld` already fail-louds on its own probe and sets `CARGO_ENCODED_RUSTFLAGS` job-wide, which takes precedence over anything here.

## Validation

- [x] `cargo test -p mesh-llm-build-info` links and passes with no lld config.
- [x] `just with-lld cargo test -p mesh-llm-build-info` prints the fallback note once, links, 9 tests pass.
- [x] `scripts/build-host.sh --profile dev` builds `target/debug/mesh-llm` end to end on this machine.
- [x] `python3.12 -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests -p 'test_*.py'`: failing set is identical to `origin/main` on this machine (pre-existing, unrelated), plus 10 new tests passing.
- [x] `shellcheck -x` clean on the three scripts.
- [ ] UI changes: none.

  * Improved macOS and Linux build reliability by verifying LLVM’s linker compatibility with the active SDK before use.
  * Automatically falls back to the platform linker when LLVM’s linker is unavailable or incompatible.

  * Improved native runtime packaging by using only verified linker configurations.

author: eagmon
body:
## Problem

`V2ECOLI_SKIP_CACHE_VERIFY=1` is documented as the escape hatch for deliberate cross-commit / cross-version cache work — but it was only honored by `core.load_cache_bundle`'s own pre-check. Any caller that invokes `verify_cache_version` **directly** on the staging path — the ray-batch entrypoint's cache verify (via `run_pbg`) — ran the check unconditionally and ignored the env.

Real impact (CD2 tonight): the Run 2 J3 re-fire reused a cache copied from an older commit into the new commit's slot, which is exactly what the flag is *for*. It failed at staging in ~13s with `inputs_hash mismatch; files differ: ['v2ecoli/composites/reactor_bird_coupled.py']` despite `V2ECOLI_SKIP_CACHE_VERIFY=1` being set. The Run 1 cell-only re-fire only got past because its cache happened to lack `cache_version.json` (the entrypoint guards the verify on that file's presence) — luck, not the flag. The same bug will hit the Run 3 shared-ParCa re-fire and the with_trp re-fire, which also reuse cross-commit caches.

## Fix

Honor the env at the **single verification chokepoint** — `verify_cache_version` itself — so *every* caller respects it (core, `parca_bundle`, `parca_study`, and any staging path), matching `load_cache_bundle`'s existing skip semantics: skip the whole verify, warn once per process. Reads the env at call time (not import) so a dispatch's `task_env` toggles it. No behavior change when the flag is unset.

## Tests
3, stdlib-only: raises `StaleCacheError` without the flag; skips (returns `None`) with it set on the same would-be-stale dir; warns exactly once per process. ruff clean.

author: markgoho
body:
Closes #1150

Four readers answered "what happened to this thing?" and three of them hand-wrote it: the Engagement ledger, the Membership roster history, and the Client's own history each carried their own copy of the Practice and subject scoping, the actor-name join, the newest-first cursor and the one-row-past-the-page sentinel. They bypassed the generic `activityfeed.ListForSubject` for one reason — all three are diff-aware and that reader carries no diff.

## What triage found, which outranks the refactor

The three copies do not agree, and four of the five differences are disagreements about a fact rather than about a caller:

- **A departed Staff actor had four spellings.** `staff_practice_visibility` reaches a `staff` row only through a live Membership, so the actor join finds nothing the moment a person leaves. The roster feed and the Membership history said `activity.DepartedStaffName` ("a former colleague", the word #887 settled). The Engagement ledger rendered the **empty string** — `staffName.String` on a NULL — so the Who column was simply blank. The Client history returned **null** and the Client detail screen printed **"Unknown staff"**. One absence, three words and a blank, across four screens of one Practice.
- **The product's own name was spelled on the app side for one reader.** Three readers returned `activity.SystemActorName` ("Doula Cloud", ADR-0022). The Client history returned null and the screen hardcoded `'Doula Cloud'` in TypeScript.
- **One reader did not filter the Practice in the app layer.** The Client reader relied on `activity_practice_visibility` alone where the other three deliberately filtered `practice_id` as well.
- **One reader was not paginated at all.** The issue body says all three share "the same one-row-past-the-page-size trick, the same newest-first `(created_at, id)` cursor". That is false for the Client reader: no `LIMIT`, no cursor, no sentinel, and `ORDER BY a.created_at` **ascending**, with `mergedHistory` re-sorting newest-first afterwards — which is why nobody noticed, and which also left its ordering not tie-broken by id.

The fifth difference is a real one: the Membership history deliberately omitted the `clients` actor join, because a Client never acts on a Membership.

## The shared thing, and why its interface stays narrow

`api/internal/activitypage` owns the whole of the shape: Practice and subject scoping, the optional action exclusion, the newest-first `(created_at, id)` cursor, the sentinel row that answers "is there more?" without a second query, the page trim, the cursor mint, and the actor's resolved name. Its interface is three values — a `Query` naming the page, a `Projection[T]` carrying a caller's own joins, columns and row builder, and a `Page[T]` envelope. A caller writes no SQL predicate, no cursor arithmetic, no sentinel, and no actor switch.

It does not grow a flag per caller. The one thing each caller varies is *what it selects*, and that is data on the projection rather than a branch in the reader. A diff is one of those extra columns and is never a field of `Row`, which is how "a Client cannot receive a diff by default" holds at the SQL level: the Client-facing projection names no columns, so the statement her request issues has no `a.diff` in it at all. Withholding is the absence of a line, not a check this code runs — asserted directly in `TestStatement_OmitsTheDiffForAProjectionThatDoesNotAskForIt`.

The excluded actions are bound as parameters rather than written into the query. Both callers used to build a quoted SQL fragment (`engagement.moneyActionsNotIn`, `portal.staffingActionsNotIn`), each carrying its own paragraph arguing that a fragment built from compile-time constants is safe; the shared `Query` takes a `[]string` of action names instead, which deletes both paragraphs and the `gosec` exemption on the read. The only text a caller still contributes is its projection's own joins and columns — every request-influenced value is bound.

The package sits below `activityfeed`, which imports `staffauth` and `client` and so cannot host a reader both of those call. The two Client naming rules move down to `personname` for the same reason; `client.LegalName`/`client.PreferredName` re-export them, so no call site moves.

## Where visibility is enforced now

Unchanged at each caller's own gate, and the shared reader still applies no gate of its own: `activitygate.CanAccessSubject` plus the role declaration on the route mount for the Engagement ledger and the Membership history, `Reader.CanAccessClient` for the Client detail, `clientauth.Middleware`'s ownership check plus the staffing-action exclusion and the Staff-name redaction for the portal. Beneath all of them, every read runs on the caller's own transaction under `activity_practice_visibility` (00051), and `activitypage` now *always* writes the `practice_id` predicate as the app-layer half of that pair — which the Client reader did not have before. `TestList_RefusesAnotherPracticesRows` covers it.

The Engagement ledger's money filter moves from a `$3 OR …` bool parameter to an exclusion built only when the reader is a contractor, so an Owner's read carries no exclusion predicate at all and a contractor's carries one. #1077's JIT canary now EXPLAINs the statement `activitypage` actually issues, for the contractor variant — the heavier of the two plans — rather than a hand-copied literal beside it.

## The one app-visible change

The Client history's `actorName` is now always present rather than nullable, because fixing the departed and system spellings is exactly what removes the null. The screen prints the name it is given; `'Unknown staff'` and the app-side `'Doula Cloud'` are gone.

## Not fixed here

#1256 (a departed member's name on the practice-wide feed) stays open. That name is resolved by the feed's own cross-subject `subj` join in `activityfeed.practice.go`, a different query from the subject-scoped one widened here, and its `queryBatch` still reads no `a.diff` — so the "carry the name in the event" route wants that query changed too, on top of the write side.

## What changed

Connecting an Epic hospital now retains the linked clinical document bodies that the provider exposes, rather than saving only DocumentReference or DiagnosticReport listings. The frozen patient-bound catalog covers 40 all-history query slices across 17 clinical families, with explicit registrations for document categories and supporting Binary reads. DiagnosticReport study images use one bounded, scope-checked Media-to-Binary hop and remain supporting evidence alongside the native report.

Large charts continue page by page through immutable batch manifests and a portable checkpoint. Each page and document is independently claimed, streamed, integrity checked, and persisted with its exact parent revision. Original attachment bytes are retained separately, supported text and PDF extraction feed the existing importer, and missing, oversized, malformed, or unauthorized bodies become explicit incomplete coverage. No prior import migration is included because this feature is unlaunched.

## Architecture and reuse

- Existing systems reused: Epic SMART connection, Web control boundary, encrypted runtime tickets, clinical raw manifest, vault checkpoint, importer, and canonical clinical write owners.
- New logic: linked document ticket issuance, streamed Binary fetch, bounded Media-to-Binary study-image resolution, original-byte validation, and page-batch continuation.
- New abstractions: one document fetch callback and attachment evidence fields in the existing clinical checkpoint/manifest flow.
- Complexity intentionally avoided: no new scheduler, provider credential store, database migration, general reference traversal, or canonical document identity owner.

## Product UX and changelog

The connect flow remains one hospital authorization. Members receive readable notes and preserved original files when the hospital exposes them; unavailable files remain visible as incomplete coverage. The member-facing changelog entry is included at `apps/web/changelog/entries/2026-09-10/epic-hospital-documents.json`.

## Direct evidence

The real-Codex linked-document journey read a synthetic hospital report, preserved the historical date and recommendation, and did not turn a past naproxen course into a current medication or create unrelated canonical writes. Focused tests cover patient binding, redirects, malformed and oversized bodies, Media-to-Binary study images, multiple attachments, parser extraction, retry/preemption, and continuation batches.

## Changelog

- Changelog: updated

## Complexity impact

- Guard: pass from `pnpm complexity:diff`; changed source stays within the repository gate.
- Hotspots: document parsing and pagination were split into bounded helpers; no new high complexity hotspot was left above the guard delta.
- Agent judgment: the added transport and checkpoint branches are required for linked files and resumable all-history imports, with no replacement owner or speculative traversal.

## Deployment concerns

- Deployment: applicable
- Supported skew: the v4 runtime checkpoint is the new runner floor; older external v2/v3 manifests remain importer-readable.
- Safe order: register Epic APIs and deploy the compatible Web reader before admitting the runtime writer.
- Rollback floor: retain the deployed v4-capable runner and current Web document callback until all active runs drain.
- Expected exposure: no member-visible exposure before the unlaunched feature is enabled and provider grants are configured.
- Reversibility: this additive code can be disabled without a data migration; saved evidence remains immutable.
- Convergence proof: retrying the same run resumes the checkpointed page or document claim without duplicate canonical writes.
- Post-deploy checks: verify a small and large chart, linked document readback, authorization loss, and a repeated import.
- Epic app registration must include the listed patient-facing searches and Binary/Media reads before rollout.
- Provider grants and actual exposed history remain the acquisition boundary; unavailable or withheld bodies stay explicitly incomplete.
- The feature is unlaunched, and this PR does not enable monthly polling, webhooks, or background token refresh.

## Rollout notes

The feature remains unlaunched. Epic app registration and provider grants remain deployment prerequisites. Monthly polling or webhooks are outside this change; the current contract supports an explicit future reconnect/import generation.

author: geekshiv
body:
## What changed and why

Two related fixes to the PR Guardrail comment-link flow, found while manually testing #393's deep links live.

**1. Live scan status.** `PrGuardrailLog` fetched the scan log once (`useAsyncData`, no polling) and never refetched. The backend already creates the `PRGuardrailScan` row with `status="running"` the moment a scan starts -- including the server-side webhook path (#245), which nobody viewing this page necessarily triggered -- but the page never looked again after its initial load. A scan that started while the page was already open never appeared as running; it only showed up, already finished, after a manual reload.

Adds adaptive polling: 3s while something in the visible log is `running`, 20s otherwise (since the only thing being watched for then is a scan someone else's webhook just started). Mirrors this codebase's existing `useActiveScans`/`useActivePrScans` convention -- "the server is the source of truth for what is in flight" -- rather than inventing a new pattern.

**2. One-click "request ignore".** #393 wired the link's `ignore_finding` param to auto-open the reason input for that specific finding -- but that's still a second step (type a reason, click Confirm) for a link whose entire point was skipping the dashboard. Per user decision, this is now a genuine one-click action: clicking the link fires the ignore request immediately with a fixed reason ("Requested via PR comment link"), landing straight in the Approval Queue with nothing to type.

Login is still required (this is still a same-origin authenticated POST, not an unauthenticated action a bare GET could safely trigger -- an actual no-auth-required mutation on link click would be exploitable by any link-preview bot/prefetcher that fetches PR comment URLs), so "one click" means one click on the PR comment link, not zero page loads. If the automatic request itself fails (network blip, etc.), it falls back to the manual button+reason dialog rather than a dead end. Also guards against re-firing on an already-reviewed finding (a stale or re-clicked link): `submit_ignore_request` resets `ignore_reviewed_by`/`ignore_reviewed_at` on every call, so blindly re-submitting could silently wipe out a security reviewer's already-made approve/reject decision.

## How this was tested

- `tsc --noEmit`, `eslint`, `next build` all clean.
- Manually traced the auto-submit effect against this repo's `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect`/`react-hooks/refs` lint rules (which blocked an earlier, different approach in #393): the effect only calls an already-defined async function reference (`api.requestIgnoreFinding(...).then(...)`), no synchronous `setState` call appears directly in the effect body, and no ref is read/written during render.
- No backend changes, so no new backend tests.

## Checklist

- [x] I ran the relevant checks locally (frontend typecheck/lint/build; see above)
- [ ] I added or updated tests covering this change (no existing frontend test suite covers this component; the changes are UI wiring/timing, not new backend logic)

author: sridharkalaibala
body:
The first screen of a device's life was a text box, which assumes the person holding the phone knows the shop code. **The owner knows it. A waiter handed a phone five minutes into their first shift does not**, and had no way to find out. Off the shop Wi-Fi there was nothing else to try.

The choice is now explicit, in the order a shop will use it:

| | |
|---|---|
| **Scan** | Point at the code by the till. Nothing to know, nothing to type. |
| **Search this Wi-Fi** | Finds the till by itself. Nothing to know either, but the till has to be on. |
| **Type it** | A shop code or an address, for whoever does know one. |

jsQR is **bundled rather than fetched**: setting up a handset has to work in a shop with no internet, which is the whole point of scanning the till's own code. What a code may carry is deliberately loose - a bare code, a full address, or a link with either in a `server=` parameter - because it gets made by whatever is to hand and reprinted by somebody in a year.

Opening the sheet no longer starts a network sweep. That was a guess at what the user wanted, and it held the screen for seconds against a network with no till on it.

**The camera is declared on both platforms.** Without it the scanner does not fail loudly: Android rejects with `NotAllowedError` and the screen blames a permission the app never asked for, and iOS kills the app outright.

## An address that stops working

"No connection" reads as a problem with the phone, so people restart the phone. It is nearly always the till. The screen now:

- names the **till** or the **connection**, whichever it is
- shows the address it is trying
- says what would fix it
- counts down to the next automatic attempt, so **waiting is visibly a choice** rather than looking like the app is stuck waiting for a tap

29/29 tests pass, including a device with no camera, a blocked camera, a scanned code that belongs to something else, and a till that goes down and comes back.

author: mumbak2-cell
body:
Implements `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-10-stock-take-variance-flags-design.md`.

Detective control for cashier phantom-stock fraud (inflate a closing count → "sell" the phantom for cash next day). Owner-facing only — cashiers stay blind to expected stock, variance, and flags.

## What ships

- **Migration 121** (`supabase/migrations/121_stock_count_expected.sql`): `stock_counts.expected_units` (frozen snapshot of `product_stock.quantity`, stamped by a `BEFORE INSERT` trigger) + `flag_kind` (`near_empty` / `value` / `unit_ceiling` / `session_spread` / `pattern`, priced at `selling_price` never `cost_per_unit`, `is_prepared` products exempt). A `BEFORE UPDATE` trigger re-flags an *edited* count line and protects both columns from a direct client rewrite (migration 119 leaves `stock_counts` writable by `role='member'`). CHECK constraint on `flag_kind`. **Owner applies by hand in the SQL Editor, outside trading hours, then `migration repair --status applied 121` — before this PR is merged.**
- **`scripts/verify-stock-count-flags.mjs`** — read-only dry-run replay of the flag logic for threshold tuning against real data (`--org "Destiny" --days 60`).
- **Stock Count page**: flag badges, a pending-banner flag summary, an uncounted-with-stock list (the "don't count what you took" surface), a review-ack checkbox before Confirm (client-side friction, not a DB gate), optional per-line notes, a stock-moved warning, and a "Flagged only" filter with flagged rows sorted to the top (owner view only).
- **Team settings**: read-only per-person variance rollup (30/60/90 days — sessions, flagged over/under, rand exposure) — the control that survives an owner who confirms without reading every flag.

## Deliberately not in v1

No `SECURITY DEFINER` confirm RPC, no RLS tightening, no hard gate on Confirm — three independent reviews found a preventive gate is largely defeated by owner rubber-stamping on a shared-tablet login. v2 once real flag data exists. The spec's `audit_logs` write was dropped (append-only table, no client INSERT policy).

## Process

Built via subagent-driven development from a written spec + plan (both committed to this branch). Every task got an implementer + an independent spec/quality review; Task 3 needed one fix round. The final whole-branch review (before this PR) found 2 Critical + 4 Important issues — a trigger gap that let an *edited* count line evade re-flagging, prepared-food rows wrongly picking up the `session_spread` badge, a stale-vs-frozen variance mismatch, an incoherent banner count, a dropped filter/sort requirement, and the evidence columns being writable by the cashier the control targets. All fixed in one wave + verified by a scoped re-review, which itself caught one new regression (a flagged-first sort leaking row-order information to cashiers) — fixed and re-verified.

`tsc --noEmit` clean and no new eslint errors on any touched file, branch-wide. No test runner in this repo — verification is type-checking, lint-diffing against `main`, SQL assertions in the migration's own footer, the dry-run script, and manual browser-check steps in the plan.

author: idrinth
body:
## Description

Fixes the reported issue where Save / Save & Compile in the desktop app's code viewer appeared not to reliably surface fixable findings after re-linting — e.g. adding code with wrong indentation and not seeing the expected "Apply fixes" button.

The re-lint itself was working fine. The actual bug was in `hasFixableFindings` (`app/src/main.ts`), which gates the "Apply fixes" button (both in the code viewer and the per-file results list). It only recognized a fixable finding by hardcoded message-text matching against trailing-whitespace and missing-semicolon messages, while the per-finding "Fix this issue" button already used the correct, more general `isFixableFinding` check (based on `FIXABLE_RULE_IDS`, which also includes `indentation`, `comma-spacing`, `identifier-casing`, `property-sorting`, and every other auto-fixable rule).

So after a Save/Save & Compile re-lint turned up a fresh indentation (or any non-whitespace/semicolon) finding, the individual "Fix this issue" button on that finding correctly appeared, but the file/viewer-level "Apply fixes" button stayed hidden, since `hasFixableFindings` didn't know that rule was fixable.

`hasFixableFindings` now simply reuses `isFixableFinding` per finding, so the two checks can no longer drift apart.

Updated `app/src/main.test.ts` accordingly: added a `rule` field to existing fixable-finding test fixtures that relied on message-text matching (now required since `isFixableFinding` keys off `finding.rule`), and added new cases covering an indentation finding (previously unrecognized) and a fixable-rule finding explicitly marked "no automatic fix" (should still be excluded).

author: zacxdev
body:
Close-out of the `find-session-archive-window` effort. Everything the previous revision listed as outstanding is done.

| was outstanding | now |
|---|---|
| the handoff itself (#1418) open, content stale | **MERGED** `3a4a057d` — with its three false claims corrected *before* the merge |
| the tmux gate flake, unfiled, tagged `forcing: none` | **filed as #1473**, re-tagged `forcing: gate` |
| two orphaned worktrees | **removed**, with their three local branches |

## Two things this close-out records that are worth more than the status

**A squash merge makes every worktree look like it holds unsaved work.** All three of this effort's worktrees reported commits "not in main" (7, 1, 2) *after* their PRs had merged — because a squash merge never makes the branch head an ancestor. The right instrument is `git diff origin/main <tip> -- <files it touched>`, which returned **0 lines** for each. Checking ancestry would have either stranded three worktrees indefinitely, or invited a `--force` removal on a reading that was never evidence of anything.

**`forcing: none` is a decision, not a neutral tag.** The tmux flake sat under it because it felt like a nit. It had truncated two full `gate.sh` runs at the 3600s cap — that is `forcing: gate`. Under the handoff gate's own rule, `none` means *not eligible to be worked*, so as originally tagged it would never have been picked up. Corrected here.

## The ladder's final tally — deliberately moved to an APPEND heading

`State now` is REPLACED on every update, and the tool's durable-content warning caught that this close-out would have dropped it. Six rounds: **0 🔴, 23 🟡, ~16 🟢**; payload lines per round **155 → 90 → 33 → 12 → 8 → 2**. Exactly one substantive correctness bug in the whole run, and it predated the PR. **The severity never dropped while the payload did** — 🟡 counts stayed 3–5 every round — which is the signature of a ladder auditing its own scaffolding rather than the change. That, not the round count, is what said stop.

No `clawgate-task:` field: `clawgate_handoff.sh resolve` exited 5. Its positive control confirms the board is reachable, but an unknown session id also answers 200 with an empty array, so that 0 is not a clean bill of health.

author: aviatesk
body:
Clients can retain pull diagnostics after `didClose` when `diagnostic.all_files=false` but workspace diagnostic support remains advertised. Repeated empty reports would keep workspace pulls from becoming idle instead of fixing the client-side retention policy.

JETLS now matches `workspaceDiagnostics` to the effective `all_files` setting. Dynamic registration waits for initial configuration loading, and setting changes replace the fixed-ID registration on the message worker so concurrent configuration handlers cannot interleave updates. An initial configuration error or empty response completes registration with the existing settings.

File configuration is loaded before `InitializeResponse` so clients without dynamic registration can also start without workspace pulls. Their capability is fixed from `.JETLSConfig.toml` at startup: changing it requires updating that file and restarting the server. Push-based diagnostic reporting still follows runtime configuration changes.

The registration, configuration, and full lifecycle tests pass.

## Summary

Senior-auditor catch-all finding (unit-escalation trip on `0509-sneaker-resale-recall-canary.service`, 2026-09-11T03:33Z):

`openrouter/google/gemma-4-31b-it:free` has been **dead on arrival** — every pick since registration (2026-09-06T02:03Z, fleet-ops#3722) has returned upstream HTTP 429 *"temporarily rate-limited upstream"* from the shared Google AI Studio free pool. The ledger at `lanes/seats/openrouter__google_gemma-4-31b-it_free.json` shows `consecutive_failure_count=20`, `health_class=rate_limited`, `seat_dead=false`.

The structural gap: the `rate_limited` class is retryable-forever — each failure writes `usable_at` ≈ +15 min, then `pick_seat` re-draws the seat and burns another worker spawn. It never converges to `seat_dead` (nothing sets seat_dead on a 429 class). Observed harm: `pi-issue@0509-2724` (a critical-path deploy-unblock issue) hit **StartLimitBurst twice** (03:17:35Z, 03:33:51Z) because its respawns kept landing on this seat.

## Change

`config/seat-caps.json`: `google/gemma-4-31b-it:free` → `cap: 0`, `max_probe_ceiling: 0`, `intentional_cap_zero: "retired"`, dated measured reason. Registration `_note` preserved with RETIRED marker. Precedents: #2435 (permanently dead seat retirement), #3941 (47 consecutive spawn failures → bench).

## Out of scope (noted for follow-up, not built here)

The mechanism gap — a `rate_limited` seat at consecutive_failure_count ≥ N never escalating to a longer park or `seat_dead` — is a seat-health design question. Retiring this seat removes the observed harm; whether upstream-429-on-shared-pool should auto-converge is a separate issue if other free seats hit the same wall.

author: snakajima
body:
## Summary

The last upstream example that needed language work, `Dodecahedron.shape`, now renders. Follow-up to #3072.

- **Shapes as values**: `define ico icosphere { detail 0 }` keeps its mesh; `ico` (with optional `position` / `orientation` / `size` on the call) places it; members `polygons` and `triangles` (each with `.center`, `.points`, `.bounds`), `bounds` (`.min` `.max` `.center` `.size` `.width` `.height` `.depth`) and `volume`.
- **Icosphere in Euclid's order**: built vertex for vertex and face for face as `Mesh.icosahedron` + `subdivide()` upstream, so a script that indexes `ico.polygons` (the dodecahedron's face table) gets the same faces. Test pins the first face's centre to the formula.
- **`for` / `if` as expressions**: `define scales for i in 1 to 3 { i / 3 }`, `define c if big { red } else { white }` (with `else if`).
- **Shape-building functions**: `define face(data) { polygon { … } }` runs in the converter and returns what it built (one value, or a tuple); a function called bare as a statement (`face data`) places its result, or contributes it inside `mesh`.
- **`polygon { point … }`** with 3D points (a tuple per point allowed), a colour per face, loops and defines; **`mesh { … }`** assembles the polygons and meshes its body produces into one flat-shaded, vertex-coloured mesh.
- Line breaks inside parentheses and call arguments; a keyword a script `define`s as a value (`define hull (…)` then `color hull`) keeps reading as that value (a workspace script relied on it).
- A value a statement produces that is not a shape is an "unused value" error, as upstream.

### Implementation
`meshValues.ts` holds the value types, Euclid's icosphere, triangulation and polygon → geometry. The evaluator gains the value family and two hooks the converter provides (`shape`: build a node as a value; `call`: run a shape-building function). The converter collects produced values through a sink while building `mesh { }` and function bodies, and places mesh/polygon values in the scene otherwise.

### Versioning
`@mulmoclaude/shapescript-plugin` 2.1.0 → 2.2.0 (additive), launcher range `^2.2.0`, changelog + Ships line, plan file updated.

- [x] Plugin tests: 154 pass (new "shapes as values" suite; Dodecahedron now in the rendering fixtures with bounds asserted)
