author: undivisible
body:
Implements the first hardening set from the burn audit (R1, R2, R3, R5).

## Changes
- **Scalar-only generate:** metadata capabilities are derived from inventory instead of advertising every reactive flag. `cargo eqts` already accepts explicit `kind: function` on schema v3; this makes README-style crates honest and adds a scalar-only parse test.
- **Panic-safe reactive ABI:** `catch_unwind` on reactive ctor, poll, invoke (sync/async), and the napi/wasm bridges, returning `ABI_PANIC` / `"eqts panic"` instead of unwinding across `extern "C"`. Integration tests panic in ctor, `poll`, and `invoke`.
- **Bun pointers:** generated loaders no longer `Number()` a heap pointer. Reads go through `__eqtsReadOwned` (`toArrayBuffer(address, …)` with bigint address, capped length) and free still uses the same bigint triple.
- **Poll locking / handle IDs:** registry lock is dropped before `poll()` (and before callback encode / object invoke). Handle allocation skips live IDs and panics if the `u64` space is exhausted instead of wrapping to `1`.

## Tests
`cargo fmt --check` via `cargo fmt --all`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked`.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)
- Cooperative AbortSignal / join of worker threads (R4)
- Unknown native `dispose`/`cancel` → `ABI_UNKNOWN_HANDLE` (JS currently treats cancel `14` as throw; second dispose is still `ABI_OK` for idempotency)
- Mutually exclusive napi/wasm features (R6), JS identifier unification (R7), CI/release/target path work (R8–R9), UTF-8/Result parity (R10), DX cleanup (R11–R12)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes reactive registry locking, handle allocation, and many FFI entry points; incorrect behavior could cause deadlocks, handle reuse bugs, or silent pointer truncation on Bun, though coverage is strong.
> 
> **Overview**
> This PR hardens the eqts FFI/reactive boundary and Bun codegen from the burn audit (R1, R2, R3, R5).
> 
> **Metadata** now derives `capabilities` from the export inventory (scalar-only crates no longer advertise reactive features). Tests assert the new capability shape for empty and reactive fixtures.
> 
> **Reactive runtime** refactors handle registration (`insert_entry`, `allocate_handle` skips in-use IDs and panics when `u64` space is exhausted). `poll_reactive`, `cancel_reactive`, and callback enqueue clone `Arc`s and **drop the registry mutex** before `poll()` / `cancel()` / encoding, avoiding deadlocks when user code re-enters the registry.
> 
> **Panic safety** wraps reactive constructors, scalar/json exports, and `setup!` ABI bridges (poll, invoke, dispose, cancel) plus napi/wasm shims in `catch_unwind`, returning `ABI_PANIC` / `"eqts panic"` instead of unwinding across `extern "C"`. Integration tests cover ctor, poll, and invoke panics.
> 
> **Bun loaders** stop coercing heap addresses with `Number()`; owned buffers are read via generated **`__eqtsReadOwned`** (`toArrayBuffer` with bigint address, length cap) while frees still use the bigint triple. Generator tests lock this in.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit e14f188246e1ab5271d6cc8b9c3cd3640f3f93e3. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

author: markgoho
body:
Adds `docs/research/books/jobs-to-be-done.md`, the read-back of *Jobs to be Done: Theory to Practice* (Anthony W. Ulwick, Idea Bite Press, October 2016, ISBN 978-0-9905767-4-7, foreword by Alex Osterwalder) on the eight-section template in `docs/agents/literature.md`. The book was read front to back from the `pdftotext -layout` extraction; the PDF was opened only for the figures and tables the text lost.

**Page rule.** The printed page equals the PDF index, offset zero: PDF page 2 prints "2" and PDF page 203 prints "203"; PDF page 1, the title page, carries no number. The Contents page is wrong for the last four chapters (it lists chapter 6 at 162, 7 at 176, 8 at 185, 9 at 195; the headings are on 163, 177, 187, 197), so the file cites the page the text is printed on, never the Contents. Citations read "(ch. 4 §III, p. 91)" or "(ch. 6, step 40, p. 170)".

**What each section holds.** Section 3 states the thesis in the author's frame (a needs framework plus customer-defined metrics tied to the job, backed by one study of 86% against 17%) and the eight things the author says the claim is not. Section 4 walks the Foreword, the Introduction, and the nine chapters with every figure, company, and example the book rests on. Section 5 lists thirteen places the author limits his own claim, from the three failed launches in his own study to "In a small organization with only 1 product, we recommend hiring Strategyn". Section 7 checks every company and figure against a September 2026 source: Kroll Ontrack, Abbott Medical Optics, Hussmann, Cordis, and Nest have all been sold since or before publication, Microsoft retired the training-voucher benefit the Microsoft case is built on, the Bosch CS20 was recalled in 2005, the field has split into two named schools, and the 86% study, the Coloplast case, and every client-reported growth figure are marked unchecked because only the author's own publications carry them. Section 8 records where the book is weakest: a self-graded headline number, every case being the firm's own client, correlation read as cause, unsourced rules of thumb, and a method sized for a corporation.

**What section 6 found.** Nineteen entries, each a claim with its page and then the record that holds the matter, with no sentence after the record. The book meets the repo at the proto-personas (`docs/personas/README.md`, `CONTEXT.md` **Persona**, #994), the interview guide on #994 and #991's frameworks table, the audience and primary-buyer question on #991 and #999, positioning and message on #999 and #1001, the competitor feature survey on #173 and the messaging survey of #995, the $20 Credit decision on #439, the non-software alternatives on #999 and the persona files, the journey maps' two layers, `CONTEXT.md` and ADR-0005 as the common language, the pilot price question on #243, the PracticeLite onboarding survey and **Day zero**, the search question in #991's Not yet specified beside ADR-0016, the no-ranking rule in `CLAUDE.md` and **Finding** against the book's Opportunity Algorithm, the sample sizes the book needs against #991's one customer contact, and the solo-versus-agency segment question on #991 and #994. Open tickets are named as the record of a question, not a decision; #173 closed as a research deliverable that recommends nothing.

`docs/agents/literature.md` is not edited; the orchestrator moves the book table in one sweep after the last read-back lands.

author: monthop-gmail
body:
`care-agent-platform` **ไม่ได้อ่านร่างแล้วตอบ** — เขียนตัวไล่ทุก leaf ของ audit event จริง **112 ใบ** ตามกฎที่เราร่างไว้ แล้วถามว่า leaf ไหนไม่ใช่ตัวชี้

```text
actor.display_name                   112/112 ใบ   ← ทุกใบที่ระบบเคยเขียน
evidence.recorded_by.display_name      9 ใบ
metadata.policy_reason                26 ใบ
transition.reason                     37 ใบ
```

**ชื่อคนจริง ในทุก event ตั้งแต่ใบแรก ในที่ที่ลบไม่ได้** — และสิทธิ์การอ่านไม่ผูกกับ consent แบบเดียวกับตารางของโดเมน

## ทำไมไม่มีใครเห็น — และทำไมไม่ใช่แผลเดียวกับ ADR-0030

> รอบนี้ของที่รอดมา **ไม่ได้รอดเพราะไม่มีใครเอ่ยชื่อมัน แต่รอดเพราะทุกคนคิดว่ามันเป็นของแพลตฟอร์ม ไม่ใช่ของตัวเอง** · มันไม่ใช่ฟิลด์ที่โดเมนใส่ **มันเป็นฟิลด์ของสัญญาเอง**

รวมเป็น **สามรูปของแผลเดียวกันภายในสองวัน**:

```text
ชื่อที่กว้างเกิน          → คนใส่ของผิดเข้าไปโดยไม่รู้ตัว          (เคส reason)
ฟิลด์ที่ไม่มีใครเอ่ยชื่อ    → ไม่มีใครไปดูว่ามีอะไรอยู่ในนั้น        (ADR-0030 · error/v1.details)
ฟิลด์ของสัญญาเอง         → ทุกคนคิดว่าเป็นของอีกฝ่าย ไม่มีใครดู   (ใบนี้ · identity/v1.display_name)
```

**ไม่มีอะไรใน JSON Schema ตรวจได้เลยสักรูป**

## Decision: D

เขียนคำกำกับที่ **ต้นทางของฟิลด์** ใน `identity/v1` — คำเตือนจะเดินทางไปกับ `Principal` ทุกที่ที่มันถูกฝัง แทนการไล่ปิดทีละสัญญาซึ่งเป็นการไล่ตามอาการ

- **ปฏิเสธ B (ลบฟิลด์)** — breaking และทำลายของที่ใช้ได้จริงใน request context ที่อายุสั้น
- **ปฏิเสธ C (บังคับที่ `event/v1`)** — `event/v1` derive semantics จาก `devfactory-core` เราเขียนกฎเองไม่ได้ และปัญหาไม่ได้อยู่ที่ `event/v1` ที่เดียว

## `v1.1.0` → `v1.2.0` — ไม่ breaking

`display_name` เป็น optional มาตั้งแต่ `v1.0.0` (`required` มีแค่ `type` กับ `id`) → **ผู้ผลิตตัดออกได้วันนี้โดยยัง conform** ไม่ต้องรอสัญญาเวอร์ชันใหม่ · `care-agent-platform` ทำไปแล้ว (`#23`) ตัดที่ emit ที่เดียว รวม `on_behalf_of` ที่ซ้อนกัน + ratchet ใน `payload_check`

## สิ่งที่ consumer ควรทำ

author: kevincodex1
body:
#23 made a bad Coinbase response keep the last good price instead of blanking USD, which was right, but with no upper bound a long outage left an old dollar figure on every page and every dollar-based sort, silently. Order on each refresh is now: fresh Coinbase spot; else the Chainlink ETH/USD feed on Base when its round is under 30 minutes old (it fails independently of Coinbase and updates on a 0.15% move or every 20 minutes); else the last good value for at most 15 minutes after it was confirmed; else null, which the UI already renders as ETH-only figures.

The feed address was verified on-chain before use: description() "ETH / USD", decimals() 8, and a live round within a few dollars of Coinbase. The read reuses the stock feeds' aggregator ABI and round-to-USD helper with a 30-minute max age instead of the equities' five days, under the same 5s timeout as the Coinbase call, and is injectable for tests like the fetch already was. One warning is logged when the source switches and one when both are down past the bound.

Tests: the existing six pin Chainlink down so they still describe Coinbase alone; new cases cover the feed conversion boundaries, Coinbase down with Chainlink up, an unusable Coinbase body with a live or a stale feed round, the 14/15-minute bound with recovery from either source, and a cold double outage. Display and sorting only: nothing on-chain reads these prices.

author: greksazoo
body:
## A változtatás típusa / Type of change
- [x] Hibajavítás (bugfix)

## Rövid leírás / Summary
HU: Mind a három git-hook telepítő (`install-prod-tree-guard-hook.sh`, `install-git-guard-hook.sh`, `install-secret-gate-hook.sh`) a `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` válaszát csupasz `cd`-vel oldotta fel. A `git -C "$ROOT"` jelenléte megtévesztő: a kérdés a helyes repót címzi, a VÁLASZ viszont a repóhoz képest relatív (".git"), ezért a `cd` a HÍVÓ könyvtárához oldja fel. Mérve: idegen checkout gyökeréből indítva mindhárom telepítő az IDEGEN repó `.git/hooks` mappájába írta a hookot, kiírta a sikeres sorát és exit 0-val lépett ki, miközben a védendő fa védtelen maradt. Nem-git könyvtárból `cd: .git: No such file or directory`, idegen linkelt worktree-ből (ahol a `.git` egy fájl) `Not a directory`. A javítás a relatív választ `$ROOT`-hoz normalizálja, ugyanúgy, ahogy az `install-graphify-refresh-hook.sh` már teszi. A frissítési út nem volt érintett (az `update.sh` előbb belép a telepítési könyvtárba), tehát éles üzemzavar nem keletkezett; a kitettség a kézi vagy ágens általi indítás más könyvtárból.

EN: All three git-hook installers asked `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` with `-C "$ROOT"` and then resolved the answer with a bare `cd`. The `git -C` only makes the shape look safe: the answer is relative TO THE REPO (".git"), so the `cd` resolves it against the CALLER's cwd. Measured: started from a foreign checkout root, each installer wrote its hooks into THAT repository's `.git/hooks`, printed its success line and exited 0, while the repo it was meant to protect got nothing. From a plain directory they die with "cd: .git: No such file or directory"; from a linked worktree (where `.git` is a FILE) with "Not a directory". The fix normalises the relative answer against `$ROOT`, the same resolution `install-graphify-refresh-hook.sh` already carries. The update path is unaffected (`update.sh` cd-s into the install dir first), so this was never a live production failure; the exposure is any hand or agent invocation from another cwd.

## Kapcsolódó issue / Related issue
Nincs nyitott GitHub issue -- kanban #1234.

## Ellenőrzőlista / Checklist
- [x] Piros próba először: a javítás előtti szövegen (47d352b) telepítőnként pontosan 4-4-4 eset bukik a 15-ből; a 3 zöld a telepítőnkénti, gyökérből futtatott negatív kontroll. A javítás után 15/15 zöld.
- [x] Az új teszt viselkedés-alapú, nem szöveg-illesztés: a telepítő ténylegesen lefut, és utána a `.git` tartalmát nézzük. Öt eset telepítőnként: gyökér, alkönyvtár, nem-git könyvtár, idegen checkout (az idegen `.git` érintetlenségével együtt) és idegen linkelt worktree.
- [x] A teljes halmaz kimondva: hat `scripts/install-*hook*.sh` szkript van, háromban állt a minta (mind javítva), három nem érintett. A hármat mérés zárta ki, nem olvasás: mindegyik kétszer futott, a repó gyökeréből és egy idegen checkout gyökeréből, külön sandbox HOME-ba, és a keletkezett fa bájtra azonos a HOME normalizálása után. Egy szándékosan cwd-függő kontroll-telepítő ugyanezen a szondán eltérést adott.

author: dhananjaythomble
body:
Closes #394.

**Root cause:** the redirect resolves links from a DynamoDB projection the worker populates by draining `projection_outbox` on a 1-minute EventBridge schedule. A link created right after a drain tick is unresolvable (404) for up to ~60s.

**Fix:** `ProjectionNudgeService` (apps/api) fires an async, fire-and-forget Lambda Invoke of the worker with `{"task":"projection"}` right after every `enqueueProjection()` outbox insert (link create/edit/delete/expiry-sweep). `InvocationType: Event` returns as soon as Lambda accepts the request, so this adds no latency to the link-create response. A failed/throttled invoke is caught and logged, never surfaced to the caller — the outbox row is already durably committed and the scheduled drain still picks it up regardless. No-op when `WORKER_FUNCTION_NAME` is unset (every non-AWS profile).

Added a dedicated `"projection"` worker task that runs only `runProjection`, not the full `frequent` job (click-queue drain + rollups) — a link-create should not pay for unrelated work.

**Explicitly rejected:** a Postgres-fallback-on-miss in the redirect's resolver (one of the issue's suggested fixes). The AWS-profile redirect deliberately leaves Postgres and the VPC entirely (#288 3b) — reintroducing a DB dependency there for this bugfix would quietly undo that architecture decision.

**Known gap, left out of scope:** `ReportsService`'s abuse-flag path enqueues `projection_outbox` directly (not through `LinksService.enqueueProjection`) and does not get the nudge — it still resolves within the next scheduled drain. Can fold in as a follow-up if that latency matters.

## Verification
- `apps/api` type-check clean, build clean, 175/175 tests pass (incl. 3 new `projection-nudge.service.test.ts` cases: no-op when unset, correct Invoke shape when set, swallows a rejected invoke).
- `apps/worker` type-check clean, build clean, 103/103 tests pass (incl. new dispatch test proving `"projection"` runs only `runProjection`, not `runFrequent`/`runMaintenance`).
- `infra` type-check clean, `cdk synth` clean with the live stack's context flags.
- Not yet verified against a real deploy (that happens after merge, per the standing PR→review→CI-gate→merge→deploy flow) — will re-run the live create-link-then-follow-within-1s repro from the issue once deployed.

author: kangwoo
body:
Closes #115
Closes #117

## What changed, and why

#113 gave both agent executors one reading of a response cut at `max_tokens` (`at.aimon.core.agent.budget.TruncatedResponses`): every tool call of a cut response is refused rather than run, a cut final answer is marked and ends `TRUNCATED`, and on a turn three refused responses in a row trip the stalled-iteration guard and end `ERROR`. Three places next to that change still answered differently. This PR brings them onto the same reading.

- **A slash skill's tool loop (`LlmSkillExecutor`)** never read the stop reason. Now it refuses every call of a cut response on both dispatch paths and appends the truncation marker to a cut final answer. Both cases log a WARN naming the skill. `ReActLlmDeriver` has the same loop, and it refuses cut calls too.
- **A subagent fork** refused cut calls but had no stalled-iteration guard, so it could repeat refused `max_tokens`-sized requests up to its default 1000 iterations. A new public `StalledIterationGuard` is now the single stall definition shared by the turn, the fork and a skill's loop. A fork that trips it ends `ERROR`, and a skill fails with the stop message.
- **The Task tool** printed `Status: SUCCESS` for a fork whose answer was cut. It now appends `Completion reason: <REASON>` after the result whenever the reason is not `COMPLETED`. The header the CLI parses is unchanged, and so is `getStatus()`.
- #117's smaller items:
  - `ChunkAggregator`'s parse-failure WARN no longer logs argument text.
  - Tests pin that a refused call reaches no PermissionRequest/PreTool/PostTool hook, on all three loops.
  - `orca-executor.md` §2.2 now describes what shipped.
  - A test comment in `aimon-llm-anthropic` carries the javadoc's qualification.

The approved design is committed as `docs/design/agent-execution/skill-loop-truncation-and-fork-stall.md`. Its §11 records where the build departed from it.

## Behaviour a user can already observe that changes

All of these are named in the new `CHANGELOG.md` `[Unreleased]` entry.

1. **A slash skill's cut tool call is no longer run**, and a cut final answer ends with `[System: response truncated at max_tokens]`. The skill still returns success, so a turn that ran it ends `COMPLETED` (backlog `L-26`).
2. **A slash skill fails after three consecutive iterations whose tool calls all fail**, whatever the cause: a tool error, an unknown tool, an allow-list refusal, a PermissionRequest/PreTool block, **the side-effect approval gate denying a call (a user declining a mutating call three iterations running)**, or refused cut responses. Before, it ran to `max-iterations` (100 by default), and a slash command cannot be interrupted.
3. **A subagent fork stops after three such iterations and ends `ERROR`**, for the same causes, including the approval gate denying a call because a fork has no channel to ask through. Before, it ran to `maxIterations` (1000 by default; no in-tree caller gives a fork a budget). **This also ends error loops unrelated to truncation.**
4. **The stop message gains a clause** — ` — each of those responses was cut off at max_tokens, and its tool calls were refused` — on the turn, the fork and the skill loop, when every iteration of the streak was a refused cut response. Any other streak's message is byte-identical to today's. The turn's refused-only stall is #113's and still unreleased.
5. **`ReActLlmDeriver` refuses cut tool calls.** No in-tree code constructs it.
6. **The Task tool adds a trailing `Completion reason:` line** for results that are not `COMPLETED`. A `COMPLETED` result is byte-identical.
7. **The `ChunkAggregator` parse WARN text changes:** it gives the exception type, the offset and the length, and no argument text.

Public API: new `at.aimon.core.agent.budget.StalledIterationGuard`. `OrcaAgentExecutor.MAX_CONSECUTIVE_STALLED_ITERATIONS` keeps its name and value (3). No `CompletionReason` value was added, nothing was renamed, and no persisted or wire name changed.

---

## Decisions

The maintainer had not chosen between the options the issues list. Each decision below was settled in the design phase and checked at the design review gate. Each heading gives the option taken, the options rejected, and why.

### D1 — A skill's loop refuses every call of a cut response and marks a cut final answer in the response text; no typed field on the skill result

**Taken.** `LlmSkillExecutor` reads each response with `TruncatedResponses.isTruncated`, as both executors do.
- **Cut response with tool calls.** The assistant message is committed. Neither the bound dispatcher nor the fallback dispatcher is called. Each call is answered with `TruncatedResponses.refusal`, and the loop continues. One WARN names the skill, the 1-based iteration and the tool names (never the arguments).
- **Cut final answer.** It returns `SkillExecutionResult.success(text + TRUNCATION_MARKER)` with a WARN. The marker reaches `CommandExecutionResult.getResponse()`, the turn's final answer and the transcript.

**Rejected — a typed signal on the skill result** (a `CompletionReason`, or `isTruncated()` on the result or its metadata). Nothing would read it:
- The only consumer, `SkillBackedCommandExecutor.toCommandResult`, copies four fields into `CommandExecutionResult`, which has no slot for a reason.
- Carrying the signal to the turn would need public additions in `command/**`, which this run does not own.
- The fork-mode skill path already delivers a cut fork as success plus marker text.

**Rejected — return a failure for a cut final answer.** A failure's response is an error message, so on this path alone the partial text that both executors keep would be lost.

**Consequences, recorded rather than changed:**
- A turn that runs a slash skill whose answer was cut ends `COMPLETED` (registered as `L-26`).
- A single refused skill call shows on no terminal. The command path emits no `ToolUseStarted`/`ToolResultReady` for any skill call, refused or run, and the REPL's tool line comes from a PreTool hook a refused call never reaches. Only the WARN shows it, plus the stop message after a streak.

### D2 — `ReActLlmDeriver` changes now: cut tool calls are refused, and nothing else

**Taken.** A cut response's calls are answered with the refusal, without `invokeTool`, and a WARN names `max_tokens`. A cut text-only response ends the loop as before: `derive` returns observations, not text, so a marker would have no reader. There is no stall guard, because six iterations and the token budget already bound the loop.

**Reachability, measured by search:** zero main-source mentions of the class outside its own file, in every module.

**Rejected — wait for a construction site** (`L-22`'s trigger). The day someone constructs the deriver is a change to some other file, which touches neither this class nor `L-22`. The item would not wake, and the defect would ship with the construction, silently (`docs/backlog/README.md` rule seven). The loop runs unattended and writes to the observation store. The fix is a few lines in a `final` class, pinned with the existing stub harness. The `L-22` closure says plainly that the fix is on a class no deployment constructs.

### D3 — The fork gets the turn's guard through one shared definition, and a trip ends `ERROR`

**Taken.** The new `at.aimon.core.agent.budget.StalledIterationGuard` holds three things: the threshold (3), the predicate (at least one result, all of them errors) and the per-execution streak.
- `OrcaAgentExecutor` uses the guard in place of its local counter, with equivalent semantics: cancelled → reset, otherwise record.
- `DefaultSubagentExecutor` records each tool iteration **after** its iteration-tail cancellation check, so a cancelled iteration is never counted.
- On a trip, the fork returns `createFailureResult(..., ERROR)`: OnStop fires with `success=false`, and the stream ends `[ended: <stop message>]`.

**Rejected — count only consecutive truncated responses.**
- It would be a second definiti

author: stupideity
body:
## What

`pr_opened` read `false` on **every instance of matrix #1 and #2**, including a run that demonstrably opened a PR. Two headline metrics — PR-opened rate and the self-report gap — published a confident `0/2`.

## Root cause

`fetchPrDiff` found the PR from the API, then cloned the repo to compute a diff **its only caller discards**, and returned `pr_opened: true` only after that clone.

The clone could never succeed. Scratch repos are created `private: true` (`seed-github.ts:116`), and the orchestrator process has no git credential helper — the one in `run-task.ts:318` is configured *inside* the container. Verified on the bench host:

```
remote: Repository not found.
fatal: Authentication failed for '.../bench-astropy__astropy-12907-ff74b366.git'
```

`/root/.gitconfig` does not exist. So every call threw, every throw was swallowed by `.catch(() => ({ pr_opened: false }))`, and an unobservable metric rendered as a measured zero.

## The fix

**Not "return `true` before the clone".** The clone has no reason to exist — the diff is deliberately unused (see the comment above the caller on why a PR diff must never be the scoring input). `lookupPrOpened` replaces it: one API call, no git, no temp dir. A source-level invariant pins the clone's absence, for the same reason `check-executor-invariant.test.ts` exists — this was a line that should not have been there, and no happy-path test stops it coming back.

### Tri-state

`pr_opened: boolean | null`. `null` means *the lookup could not find out* — a different claim from *we looked; there is no PR*. Same rule `ticket_fix_overlap` already follows: a measurement never taken leaves the numerator **and** the denominator. `report/render.ts` drops nulls from the rate and names them, with their reason, in the validity panel.

The two paths that reach a record without the lookup running — no `GITHUB_TOKEN`, and a `collect` that threw first — now report `null` instead of guessing `false`.

### Disagreement field

`pr_self_reported` records styre's own claim (terminal outcome `pr-ready`/`done`) beside the forge's ground truth. Ground truth still decides the metric (CLAUDE.md move 5); the claim is what gets checked against it.

Replaying matrix #2's **as-run** data through the new report:

> ⚠ **PR ground-truth vs self-report DISAGREE on 1 instance(s): django__django-12325 (styre: PR, forge: no PR).** One of the two readers is wrong; the PR-opened rate and the self-report gap are both suspect until it is identified.

This defect would have announced itself in matrix #1 rather than being found by hand in #2. Replaying the **corrected** data restores the real numbers: PR-opened rate **50% (1/2)**, self-report gap **50% (1/2)**.

## Testability

The lookup is now an injected seam. The un-injected `fetchPrDiff` was untestable by construction, which is why every existing test stubbed `collect` wholesale and hardcoded `pr_opened: true` — there was no test that *could* have failed here.

## Verification

- 383 tests pass; typecheck and lint clean.
- **All ten mutations killed**, including the two that survived the first pass (`infra`-stage record and absent-token path) and needed tests written for them:

| mutation | result |
|---|---|
| lookup error → `false` not `null` | killed |
| re-introduce a clone | killed |
| PR denominator counts nulls | killed |
| gap predicate loses explicit `===` | killed |
| disagreement drops null guards | killed |
| infra stage guesses `false` | killed |
| no-token path reports `false` | killed |
| `pr_self_reported` never true | killed |
| no-summary self-report → `false` | killed |
| `self_test_passed` swallows null | killed |

## Ticket

[ENG-423](https://linear.app/twinning/issue/ENG-423/bench-pr-opened-is-structurally-always-false-zeroing-two-headline)

author: jrkim-kr
body:
Found while verifying [ERR-230] on production. The deployed stylesheet carried the rule that fix adds — and a rule for the coordinate it removes:

```css
.before\:top-\[44px\]:before { top:44px }   /* the wizard uses this */
.top-\[41px\]                { top:41px }   /* nothing uses this  */
```

`top-[41px]` exists in exactly one file in this repository: **the ERR-230 document**, which quotes the old value twice while explaining why it was wrong. Tailwind v4 finds class names by looking for strings shaped like class names, in every file it can reach, and Markdown is a file it can reach.

## Why it is structural, not a one-off

This repository writes an ERR document for every fix, and most of them name the utility they changed. The mechanism that records a defect was also the mechanism adding weight to every page.

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| static CSS | `136,942 B` | `131,365 B` |

5,577 bytes, 4.1% — the accumulated cost, not one rule's.

## The change

```css
@import "tailwindcss" source(none);
@source "../app";
@source "../lib";
```

Discovery off, the two trees that actually render named.

**`content/` is deliberately absent.** The practice pages and the item screens carry their own semantic classes (`reader-note`, `page-head`) and their own stylesheets. Verified by grepping `content/` for utility-shaped classes and finding none — this was checked before narrowing, not after.

## The guard, and proof it can go red

`test/skeleton.test.ts`, beside the assertion that already reads the **served** stylesheet rather than the markup. The canary is that same quotation: `top-[41px]` stays in ERR-230 for good, appears in no source file, and must not be defined. The test also asserts the wizard's own `before:top-[44px]` **is** defined, so it cannot pass by the stylesheet having lost its arbitrary-value utilities altogether.

Verified red with `source(none)` removed **and the project rebuilt** — the suite runs against a build, so editing the source alone proves nothing. Restored: green.

## One existing test was brittle

`quiz.test.ts` read only the *first* `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block. Tailwind emits its own for the `motion-reduce:` utilities; narrowing the scan reordered the two, and the authored press rule it was looking for was still there, in the second block. It reads every block now. The product rule was never affected — confirmed by finding `:where(button,summary,…)` intact in the build before touching the test.

## Verified

- `next build` — clean
- `vitest run` — 315 passed (one run showed three unrelated failures and re-ran green; the suite's known flakiness under parallelism)

# TL;DR

Render `helm-reval` from its immutable public Git release tag when generating the self-managed stack inventory. This unblocks the inventory asset required by #1760 after the v0.16.0 tag workflow failed to find `helm-reval:1.4.0` in the authenticated release chart source.

## Additional Details

The v0.16.0 tag workflow failed while building the control-plane Helmfile state: https://github.com/NVIDIA/nvcf/actions/runs/34567489568. Every preceding core chart resolved, but the build stopped when Helm could not fetch `helm-reval:1.4.0`.

ReVal is now released independently under `deploy/helm/helm-reval/v*`. Add it to the same `sourceCharts` mapping used by the other independently tagged charts. The inventory renderer checks out that immutable tag, renders the chart from `deploy/helm/helm-reval`, and still records the canonical public NGC chart destination in the published inventory.

The regression test loads the repository configuration and locks both the tag prefix and chart path. Runtime Helmfile values and deployed workloads do not change.

No dependency, license, or NOTICE changes are required.

body:
## Summary

Two independent bugs were making pages scroll sideways on a phone, both found from screenshots of the front page on an actual phone:

- **The nav search popover overflowed the page even while closed.** A closed `<details>`'s content is hidden from view by the browser, but that hiding didn't stop its absolutely positioned child from still contributing to the page's own scrollable width — it was sitting invisibly off past the right edge of the screen. This is very likely the root cause of a pre-existing e2e failure (`test_the_contents_page_fits_the_screen`) that predates this branch; it's fixed by this change too (confirmed by running that test against `main` before and after).
- **The module grid could overflow at phone width.** `.dl-module-grid`'s `auto-fill`/`minmax(13rem, 1fr)` could resolve to two columns that don't actually both fit at this width — one at its 13rem floor, the other squeezed narrower than that same floor, overflowing by the difference. Forced to one column, full width, at phone width instead.
- **Redesigned the nav search's open state at phone width.** It previously opened as a floating card with nowhere to actually float into, clipping itself against the screen edge. It now takes over the nav row in "All tutorials"' place and renders inline instead of floating, so opening it grows the header's own height and pushes the rest of the page down, rather than laying a card over the content beneath it.
- Along the way: gave `.dl-nav-top` its own explicit phone-width layout. `.dl-nav`'s own two-row override (prev/next, then up) never actually reached `.dl-nav-top`, since it carries a second class and so always outranks the plain `.dl-nav` rule on specificity — the single-row desktop shape was silently winning at every width.

- [x] `python3 -m pytest --ignore=tests/e2e` — 508 passed, 28 skipped

author: acefei
body:
`secrets exec` silently corrupted any command containing a newline.

## Symptom

```
$ secrets exec -- bash -c 'echo one
echo two'
bash: line 1: onenecho: command not found
```

The two lines were welded together. Note that it **ran** rather than failed, which is the worse outcome — a mangled command can do something other than what was asked.

## Cause

`sops exec-env` takes a single command string and runs it with `/bin/sh`, so `cmd_exec` had to quote the argv back up. It used `printf '%q '`. For an argument containing a newline, bash's `%q` emits ANSI-C quoting:

```
$'echo one\necho two'
```

That is a bash extension. `sh` does not understand it, so the `\n` never becomes a newline.

## Fix

Quote with POSIX single quotes instead: wrap each argument in `'...'` and replace every embedded quote with `'\''`. A newline inside single quotes survives literally, as does every other metacharacter.

## Test

Against a real store, all five pass:

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Multi-line command | `onenecho: command not found` | `one` / `two` |
| Secrets still injected | — | `GITHUB_USER` and `XENRT_API_KEY` present |
| `$HOME`, backticks, quotes | — | Passed through literally |
| `--pristine` | — | Still works |
| `list` / `get` | — | Unaffected |

Found while wiring the store into a container, where a heredoc-style command hit it.

author: digigang
body:
## What

**The gap under the dock on iPhone.** The composer page was sized with `100svh`. Safari's small viewport is measured against its bottom bar at full height, and on current iOS the bar is compact almost all of the time, so the page stopped about 40px short of the bar and the dock hung above it over nothing. The composer, its search stage, and the page wrapper now use `100dvh`, which is the viewport as it is right now. The page is locked on phones, so the bar never collapses on scroll, which keeps the dynamic unit stable. The gutter under the dock goes from 24px to 16px on a phone.

**App feel on every mobile page.** On phone widths, `html` now takes `touch-action: manipulation` (panning and pinching stay, double-tap zoom and the tap delay go), a transparent tap highlight, and `text-size-adjust: 100%` so Safari does not inflate type in landscape. The anti-zoom viewport tag was already global; this completes the set.

## Files

- `src/app/(app)/new/setup-form.tsx`: `dvh` on the form and the search stage, `pb-4` on phones.
- `src/app/(app)/page.tsx`: `dvh` on the page wrapper.
- `src/app/globals.css`: the mobile `html` rules.

## Checks

- Lint, typecheck, and `next build` pass.
- The `svh` to `dvh` difference only shows on a real iPhone; desktop Chromium renders both the same, so this one needs a look on the phone after the deploy.

## 1. 정산 잠금 — 로켓그로스가 빠진다

매출내역 API 는 **판매자배송(마켓플레이스)만** 반환하고 로켓그로스 정산은 포함하지 않는다.

**실측 2구간 교차검증**

| 구간 | API 옵션 | RG 재고 옵션(494) | RG 정산 엑셀 | MSF 정산 엑셀 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2026-09-01~05 | 16 | 교집합 **0** | — | 교집합 **6** / 52 |
| 2026-07-06~12 | 25 | — | 교집합 **0** / 62 | — |

두 번째 줄이 반증 테스트다 — **로켓그로스 정산이 실제로 존재하는 구간**(`CATEGORY_TR` 엑셀 696행/62옵션)에서도 겹치는 옵션이 하나도 없다.

**우회 경로 없음**
- Rocket Growth 계열 9개 엔드포인트에 정산 없음(주문 2·재고 1·상품 4·카테고리 2)
- 정산 계열은 매출내역·지급내역 2개뿐
- 매출내역 파라미터 = `vendorId` `recognitionDateFrom` `recognitionDateTo` `token` `maxPerPage`(최대 50) — **판매방식 필터 없음**
- 지급내역은 2026-06·07 모두 0건

주력이 로켓그로스인 상황에서 절반만 자동화하면 Wing 수동 엑셀과 병행 운영이 되어 실익이 없다. 재고·판매와 같은 방식으로 UI + 라우트 양쪽에서 잠근다.

## 2. 페이징 토큰 이름 — 정산은 `token`

**정산 API 는 지금 구조로 수집 자체가 불가능했다.**

`paginate()` 가 페이징 토큰을 항상 `nextToken=` 으로 보냈는데 정산 API 는 `token=` 을 요구한다. 이름이 어긋나면 서버가 매번 **첫 페이지와 같은 nextToken** 을 돌려줘 `maxPages` 까지 무한 반복한다 — 12일 조회가 500페이지를 넘겨 죽었다. 3일 조회가 됐던 건 1페이지라 nextToken 이 없었을 뿐이다.

또 첫 페이지에 `token` 을 아예 안 보내면 `400 "token cannot be null"`. 기존 코드는 query 에 `token: ''` 을 박아뒀는데 그 값이 **매 페이지 고정**이라 페이징이 동작하지 않았다.

→ `paginate` 에 `tokenParam` 인자 추가(기본 `nextToken`), 첫 토큰을 빈 문자열로 시작. `nextToken` 계열은 빈 값이 무시되므로 **기존 호출부 동작은 불변**.

수정 후 9/1~9/5 30건 · 7/6~7/12 171건 모두 정상 종료 확인.

타입 에러가 나지 않는 종류라 **회귀 테스트 3건**으로 고정했다 — 기본 이름 / `tokenParam` 지정 시 이름 / 첫 페이지 빈 문자열.

## 검증

lint 0 errors / root·worker tsc 0 errors / build exit 0 / worker 테스트 **23/23**

## ⚠️ 배포 후 필수

**워커 코드 변경이라 main 병합 후 워커 프로세스 kill 이 필요하다**(launchd 자동 재기동).

## 참고 — 스코프 최종 현황

| 스코프 | 상태 |
|---|---|
| 광고 | 🔒 API 계열 없음 |
| 재고 | 🔒 반품 등급 등 12컬럼 손실 |
| 판매·주문 | 🔒 취소 정보 없음 |
| **정산** | 🔒 **로켓그로스 미제공** (이 PR) |
| 상품 | 열림 — 크롤링이 못 주는 것을 주는 유일한 스코프(RG↔마켓플레이스 옵션 연결, skuInfo 치수·무게, 바코드) |

author: shahnuralam
body:
## Problem

On sites running an older **seat plan addon** (below 2.3.x) with a current free plugin, **every add to cart dies with a fatal error** and the customer sees a blank page. No tickets can be bought at all. Reported from a live site (`jugendblasorchester.de`):

```
PHP Fatal error: Uncaught Error: Call to undefined function mep_cart_ticket_type()
 in .../woocommerce-event-manager-addon-seat-plan/frontend/mp_esp_frontend_cart.php:159
Stack trace:
#0 MP_ESP_Frontend_Cart->mp_esp_woocommerce_add_to_cart_validation(true, 11525, 1)
#2 apply_filters('woocommerce_add_to_cart_validation', true, 11525, 1)
```

**Root cause:** the seat-plan rewrite (`ac3074e4`, Nov 2025) deleted `mep_cart_ticket_type()` and moved the work into `MPWEM_Woocommerce::get_cart_ticket_info()` and `::get_cart_ticket_price()`. The old addon still calls the removed function — twice, at lines 82 and 141 of its cart file — from inside `woocommerce_add_to_cart_validation`. An undefined function on that filter is fatal, so the whole request dies.

## Change

`inc/mep_functions.php`: `mep_cart_ticket_type()` is back as a **thin wrapper** over the current pipeline, not a copy of the old body. That way old callers and the plugin itself agree on the tickets, and `mep_cart_ticket_type_data_prepare` still fires — that filter is how the seat addon attaches `seat_name` to each row, which is exactly the field it reads back at the call site.

All three original modes are kept:

| `$type` | Returns |
|---|---|
| `ticket_type` (default) | ticket rows, filtered through `mep_cart_ticket_type_data_prepare` |
| `ticket_price` | the passed-in total plus the cart ticket prices |
| `validation_data` | one `validation_ticket_qty` / `event_id` row per ticket |

The arguments now have defaults and an unknown event id returns an empty array, so a stale caller can no longer fatal here.

## Testing

Plugins are deactivated on my local install, so the files were loaded directly in a CLI process, with two ticket types (VIP 50, Regular 20), quantities 2 and 3, and a filter adding `seat_name` the way the old addon does:

- `ticket_type` → 2 rows: `VIP qty=2 price=50 date=2026-12-01 18:00:00 seat=A1`, `Regular qty=3 price=20 … seat=A2`
- `ticket_price` with a base of 5 → `165` (5 + 50×2 + 20×3)
- `validation_data` → `[{"validation_ticket_qty":2,…},{"validation_ticket_qty":3,…}]`
- event id `0`, and no arguments at all → `[]`, no error
- `php -l` clean

## Note for the customer

This stops the fatal, but the old addon should still be updated to the current seat plan release: it is the version that matches this free plugin, and other calls it makes into removed APIs would not be covered by this one shim.

author: vishnuvardhan122004-boop
body:
## Summary
Found during a full QA sweep: `backend/.env` carries real production Cloudinary and WhatsApp Business API credentials locally (no separate sandbox account exists for either). That means, until this fix, exercising a file upload or any booking-lifecycle action from `manage.py runserver` was a live write to the production media store, or a real WhatsApp text to a real phone — I caught this by checking `settings.py` before testing either surface, but that's session discipline, not a real guard.

- **Cloudinary**: `STORAGES` now only ever selects `MediaCloudinaryStorage` when `DEBUG=False` (Railway/production). Mirrors the `not DEBUG` pattern already used just above for `SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT`, and extends the exact protection the test suite has had since 2026-08-18 (`'test' in sys.argv`) to the dev server too. Local `runserver` always writes to `backend/media/` now, regardless of `.env`.
- **WhatsApp**: `send_template()` now refuses to hit the real Meta API whenever `DEBUG=True`, same as it already does when the token is empty. The one deliberate exception — `manage.py send_test_whatsapp`, an explicit developer-run credential/template check — passes a new `force=True` to bypass the gate; every other caller (the 6 booking-lifecycle notification paths) does not, so no ordinary local QA action can text a real phone anymore.
- **Follow-up (second commit)**: switching local storage to FileSystemStorage exposed a real bug — `FieldFile.url` came back as a bare relative `/media/…`, which 404s the instant the website (port 3000) and the API (port 8000) are different origins (production never showed this because Cloudinary's `.url` is already absolute). Fixed by passing an absolute `base_url` directly to the storage backend via `STORAGES`'s `OPTIONS`, while keeping `MEDIA_URL` itself relative — `django.conf.urls.static.static()` in `urls.py` (what actually serves `/media/*` in dev) is a no-op whenever its prefix is a full URL, so making `MEDIA_URL` itself absolute (my first attempt) broke local serving outright.

## Test plan
- [x] `manage.py test` — 554/554 passed (skipped=2), no test calls `send_template` without mocking the whole function, and none depend on `MEDIA_URL`'s exact format or the storage's `base_url`
- [x] `manage.py makemigrations --check --dry-run` — clean, no migration needed
- [x] Verified live with the real credentials still in `.env`, untouched: `STORAGES['default']['BACKEND']` resolves to `FileSystemStorage`; `send_template()` returns `{'success': False, 'error': 'WhatsApp send skipped in DEBUG mode.'}` without any network call; `force=True` (with `requests.post` mocked) still reaches the real send path, confirming `send_test_whatsapp` is unaffected
- [x] Verified live end-to-end: uploaded a real photo to the hospital gallery via the API, confirmed it landed in `backend/media/` (not Cloudinary), confirmed the API returns an absolute `http://localhost:8000/...` URL, and confirmed it actually renders in the browser

author: payini
body:
## Summary

CS-05 of the Codex Support program (`docs/plans/codex-support/PLAN.md`), [ARC-045](https://github.com/codemagicianhq/arcane/blob/main/DECISIONS.md#arc-045--one-spell-source-thin-client-shims-and-a-user-level-install-tier) decision 4: a repository can now **take its spells from the user tier** instead of carrying its own. `spell_scope: "user"` in `.arcane.json` makes every `spells-*` component install nothing there; `spell update` reports what it no longer manages and `--prune` removes only files that still match the hash Arcane recorded. Minor bump to `1.2.0`. Self-mergeable under the `codex-support-plan` delegation.

**This is the epic that actually removes the duplication the program was opened for** — ten Arcane repositories in one VS Code workspace show one set of `/spell-*` entries instead of ten.

## The two premise corrections, made before the code

1. **There was no prune logic to write.** PLAN.md frames CS-05's risk as "the migration/prune logic must never silently drop an operator-edited file". Measured on a real consumer beside a stubbed-home user tier *before* building: 170 tracked files, **170/170 hash-recorded**, and after one hand edit exactly **169 matched, 1 did not** — and the one it named was the edited file. Opting out turns the repository's spell files into orphans, and `resolveOrphan` already reports every unmanaged file, deletes only under `--prune`, and only while `fileMatchesHash` holds. The epic's real job was making the components install nothing.
2. **The motivation is sharper than clutter.** In the session that designed this epic, with the user tier installed and this repository also carrying its own shims, `/spell-full-cycle` resolved through the **user tier** (the harness expanded the absolute include only the personal command carries) while `/spell-open-session`, minutes earlier, resolved through the **project** copy. Claude Code documents "personal over project"; what was observed is that with both tiers present the answer varied per command in one session. A repository that opts out has no copy of its own, so there is nothing to resolve. That observation is also the first **live** confirmation that a personal command's absolute `@` include loads the canonical body — which CS-04 could only take from documentation.

## Changes

### Features

- **`spell_scope?: "repo" | "user"`** on the repository manifest, absent meaning `"repo"` — every manifest written before `1.2.0` keeps its meaning and nothing migrates. Validated like `scope`: a typo fails loudly instead of silently reinstalling spells. Deliberately distinct from CS-04's `scope` (what a manifest *is*) — this says where a repository takes its spells *from*.
- **`componentForSpellScope`** empties the `spells-*` components under the opt-out and returns every other component untouched (governance, instructions, continuity, hooks, templates never move tier — decision 5). Emptying components rather than filtering by path prefix keeps the client-surface shapes in one place; a test pins that the components named `spells-*` are exactly the ones carrying a canonical or shim path, so a future client cannot drift past the design.
- **`spell init`** asks only when the machine already has a user tier, only interactively, and **defaults to No** — the field is committed and inherited by every clone, so a shared repository must not stop carrying its spells because one contributor's machine had a tier. The question runs before the preview and the copy loop, because it changes what gets installed, not just what gets recorded.
- **`spell update`** honours the field; removal is the orphan path, unchanged in its guarantees, with one added sentence naming the opt-out as the reason.
- **`spell doctor`** gains `checkSpellScope`, the one **blocking** user-tier check: an opted-in repository with no store has no spells in any client. It verifies rather than assumes — counts the store's spells and probes a named one. `spell status` prints `Scope: repo (spells: user tier)`.

### Fixes found by building it

- **A same-version `spell update` short-circuited on "Already up to date."** and never mentioned the newly unmanaged files — so the opt-out looked like a no-op on the very run an operator makes after editing the field. `findUnmanagedTrackedFiles` makes it visible immediately.
- **Switching back to `"repo"` had the mirror problem**: the files are shipped but neither tracked nor on disk, so nothing happened until the next release. `findReadoptedSpellComponents` restores them at the same version, narrowly — only a `spells-*` component whose manifest entry lists zero files, a state nothing but the opt-out produces — so CS-03's rule that an untracked registry file is neither created nor claimed still holds everywhere else.
- **Pruning left the skeleton behind** — 41 empty `.agents/skills/<id>/` directories and the client folders above them. `removeEmptyAncestors` walks up from a pruned file and stops at the first non-empty directory, never at the repository root.
- **An orphan still on disk now stays tracked** (its own commit, `6159ccb`). It used to be reported once and then dropped, which made the `spell update --prune` that same run had just recommended find nothing on the next invocation, left a file Arcane wrote untracked for `spell uninstall` (the hazard `update.ts` already argues for preserved files), and would have let a later re-install overwrite an operator's edits without a word. `test/update.test.ts`'s "reports, but does not delete" assertion encoded the old behaviour and is updated on the record.

## Ship report

| Phase | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| 1 — Plan | reused | PRD R4 / AC6, AC7 (completed in CS-00) |
| 1.5 — Enchant | skipped | PRD already Silver or above |
| 2 — Architect | complete | `features/codex-support/architecture.md`, "CS-05" (D1–D9); 5 stories |
| 3 — Implement | complete | 5/5 stories; `fe6b2a9`, `6159ccb` |
| 4 — Test | complete | full suite 87 files green at push; every gate below |
| 5 — Review | complete | self-review against the architecture, every lens; 0 HIGH |
| 6 — Ship | this PR | self-merge (rebase) under the delegation once the three required checks are green |

### EV-01 — the live two-repository check, built CLI

Two disposable repositories beside one user tier in a stubbed home:

- Both `--profile lite`: **160** spell paths each.
- One set `spell_scope: "user"` and ran `spell update`: `160 tracked files are no longer managed here — reviewing.`, the orphan list, the reason line. **Nothing deleted**, working tree still clean.
- `spell update --prune`: that repository → **0** spell paths, **no empty directories left**; the other → still **160**; governance (3 docs) untouched in both.
- `spell doctor` opted in: `✓ [pass] Spell scope (ARC-045)`, exit **0**. Store removed: `✗ [FAIL]` naming the store and `spell init --user`, exit **1**. `spell status`: `Scope: repo (spells: user tier)` plus the missing-store line.

### Review — every lens

- **Correctness / data loss:** no path deletes a file without a matching recorded hash; the three same-version gaps above were found and closed; switching back is covered by test. **Security:** no new attack surface; the delete paths keep the traversal guard added in `1.1.1`; an escaping manifest entry is still refused and deliberately *not* re-tracked. **Performance:** one extra `readdir` per pruned file's parent chain, bounded by the target directory. **Tests:** five suites new or extended, listed below. **Naming:** `spell_scope` is ARC-045's own name; its overlap with `scope` is documented at both declarations. **Architecture:** D1–D9 implemented as written except D8, dropped on the record.
- **No HIGH findings.** The three defects above were found during Phase 3/4 and fixed in place rather than filed.

## Testing

- **New or extended:** `test/doctor-spell-scope.test.ts` (8 — six states, blocking where it must be); `user-tier` (componentForSpellScope, effectiveSpellScope, the registry invariant

author: franknoh
body:
`ppy.tile`: kernels over tiles, the programming model Triton and Taichi have, so the comparison with them is between like and like. The CUDA example keeps to thread-level kernels.

## The model

```python
@tile.kernel
def block_max(x: native.const_ptr[float], out: native.ptr[float]) -> None:
    pid = tile.program_id()
    values = tile.load(x, pid * 64 + tile.arange(64))
    tile.store(out, pid, tile.max(values))
```

A `@tile.kernel` runs once per program of `tile.launch(kernel, programs, *args)`. `tile.arange(BLOCK)` names the kernel's block size (a power of two, 32 or more) and is the lane index; `tile.load`/`tile.store` gather and scatter through a `native.ptr` with an optional mask (and `other` for masked lanes); arithmetic, comparisons, and `& | ^ ~` are lane by lane with scalars broadcast; `tile.where` chooses per lane; `tile.sum`, `tile.max`, `tile.min` reduce a tile to one number. Under CPython the launch runs the programs in order with a list per lane, the reference the device is held to.

## The lowering

A program becomes a block of up to 256 threads. Each thread holds a slice of every tile as a vector (`BLOCK / threads` lanes, strided across the block so loads coalesce); a gather or scatter is that many lane loads or stores, masked lanes read element 0 and keep `other` rather than branching; a reduction is `simd.reduce` over the thread's lanes, a shuffle tree across the warp, and the warps through shared memory, every thread ending with the same number. Everything is existing gpu- and simd-dialect IR, so PTX and `ppy emit cuda` need nothing new beyond letting the simd dialect into device code and compiling the C backend's vector helpers for both sides. Scalars now broadcast against vectors in the frontend, and `//` and `%` lower lane by lane on integer vectors.

## Checker, staging, runtime

`tile.Tile[T]` is a type; every operation is typed lane by lane and a misuse is `E1644` (`E1631` for a store through a `const_ptr`). A tile kernel is staged like a CUDA kernel with its thread count in the payload, and `tile.launch` picks the device when the build staged the kernel.

## Example and comparison

`examples/44_tile` (saxpy, block max, a row mean and variance) with its outputs recorded, compared with Triton and Taichi through `scripts/compare_docs.py`. On the block max PPY's tile lowering is 0.41 ms against Triton's 0.78 and Taichi's 0.25 (one thread per block looping, no exchange); saxpy is bandwidth on all three. The Triton and Taichi programs moved here from the CUDA example, whose table is now thread-level kernels only.

## The harness, after its first run on the runner

The bench runner's first pass published a PyTorch row of 459 ± 420 ms: PyTorch's default thread count spins on this hybrid CPU some runs. `compare_docs.py` now refuses a row whose spread is half its mean as unstable rather than writing it, rewrites a table only where a kernel drifted beyond the tolerance (so a push does not move every number by noise), and the PyTorch counterpart pins its threads to the performance cores' count, which a program would.

Tests: reference semantics, checker codes, IR shape (thread id, block id, shuffles, shared memory, four lanes per thread for a 1024 tile), `ppy run` parity, and the CUDA unit compiled by nvcc where present.

author: anonpran
body:
## Why Chasing `DISCOVERY-TOOL-SCRIPT-1F` (a `PermissionError` on `/Users/clariadmin/Library/Application Support/JetBrains`, 55 occurrences, escalating) meant I could not tell which customer it came from. The event carries `hostname` and nothing else — no `device_id`, no `domain`, no `app_name`. I had to identify the org by grepping `ai_tool_installation.install_path` in prod for `/Users/clariadmin%` to land on Salesloft. Every detect-phase event has this problem. `detect_all_tools` is a method on the detector (`ai_tools_discovery.py:497`), while `sentry_ctx` is built in `main()` at line 3127, so the handler can only ever send: ```python report_to_sentry(e, {"phase": "detect", "tool_name": detector.tool_name}, level="warning") ``` ## What changed `main()` already builds a single context dict and mutates it for the whole run — its own comment says "Build Sentry context that persists for the whole run", and it adds `device_id` at 3330, `run_id` at 3334 and `system_user` at 3431. Registering that dict by reference once means those later fields land automatically, with no parameter threaded through the detector API: ```python set_sentry_run_context(sentry_ctx) ``` `report_to_sentry` merges it, per-call keys winning: ```python ctx = {**_sentry_run_context, **(context or {})} ``` Reset in `reset_sentry_run_state()` alongside the existing per-run state, so long-lived test processes don't leak context between runs. ## The second hole this closes `_is_ci_or_local_event` (`utils.py:2415`) suppresses events whose report domain is loopback, and it reads that domain **from the context**. Detect-phase events didn't carry one, so the filter never fired for them and local/CI runs reported straight into production Sentry. That is not hypothetical. Over 14 days on `DISCOVERY-TOOL-SCRIPT-1F`, the two loudest hosts are `Nandas-MacBook-Air.local` (16 events, a dev laptop) and `ip-172-31-55-140.us-west-2.compute.internal` (13 events, CI) — roughly half the issue's volume. Both are now suppressed, because the merged context supplies the loopback domain the filter was always looking for. ## Testing New `TestSentryRunContext` in `tests/test_discovery_flow.py`, three cases: - run context reaches an event that never passed it, **including fields added to the dict after registration** (the device_id/run_id case) - a per-call key overrides the run context - a loopback domain now suppresses a detect-phase event Verified they fail without the fix — reverting the one-line merge in `report_to_sentry` turns two of the three red, then green again on restore. 17 tests pass across `TestSentryRunContext`, `TestSentryRunGuards`, `TestParseSentryDsn`, `TestSentryNeverCrashes` and `TestSentryDebugLogging`. Payload capture in the test reads the temp file during the `subprocess.run` call, since `report_to_sentry` passes the event via `-d @file` and unlinks it immediately after. ## Risk Additive. No call site changes its own arguments, and existing per-call keys keep precedence, so nothing that is correctly tagged today changes. The one behavioural difference is intended: events from a loopback domain now get suppressed where they previously escaped. ## Not in scope The `PermissionError` itself is expected — macOS creates `~/Library/Application Support` as `drwx------`, so a non-root scan walking `/Users/*` hits EACCES on every other account. PR #311 already stopped reporting it; that fleet is pinned at a frozen `0.1.24` build and will pick the fix up on its next rebuild. Separately, tracing this surfaced that `clariadmin` is credited with 371 installs it does not own across 150 Salesloft devices, because `macos/claude_code/claude_code.py:38` ignores `self.user_home`. That is live (39 in the last 7 days) and gets its own PR.

Confidence Score: 5/5

The PR appears safe to merge; the previous cross-run Sentry context leak is fully fixed and no new actionable issue remains.

Findings

1.  **Stale context crosses runs** ▶

Summary

- Merges run-level and event-level Sentry context, with event-level values taking precedence. - Allows fields added later in the scan to appear automatically because the registered dictionary is retained by reference. - Applies the existing loopback-domain filter to detector events. - Clears the registered context during `main()` teardown and the canonical reset helper, preventing attribution or suppression state from leaking between runs. - Adds focused coverage for context propagation, override precedence, local-event suppression, and teardown isolation.

Diagram

 ```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'neutral'}}%% flowchart TD A[main builds run context] --> B[Register context by reference] B --> C[Scan adds device ID, run ID, and system user] C --> D[Detector reports an event] D --> E[Merge run context with per-call context] E --> F{Loopback or CI domain?} F -->|Yes| G[Suppress event] F -->|No| H[Send attributed Sentry event] G --> I[main teardown] H --> I I --> J[Clear registered run context] ```
Reviews (4) · Last reviewed commit: ["Clear the run context when the run ends"](https://github.com/websentry-ai/coding-discovery-tool/commit/6fad63bc2b80fe432f853eb52068545685713df9)

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes default control-plane image references (one rollout per edge) and image-refresh rollout logic for fresh vs legacy fleets; mitigated by dual-published digests, rollback knob, and extensive tests.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Chart 1.9.113** switches the default registry for tracebloc control-plane images (jobs-manager, pods-monitor, resource-monitor, requests-proxy) from **Docker Hub to `ghcr.io`** via `images.traceblocRegistry` and `tracebloc.tbRegistry`. Image-refresh’s `IMAGE_REGISTRY` and install docs/egress tables follow that default; **`docker.io` remains the documented per-edge rollback**, and digest pins / `global.imageRegistry` behavior are unchanged.
> 
> The **image-refresh CronJob** (#1008) changes when it re-pins workloads that still run a floating `:tag` while the recorded digest matches latest: it adds **`first-observed` and `digest-applied` deployment annotations** so **genuine fresh installs skip the expensive re-pin rollout** and stay on `:tag` until an upstream digest change, while **established edges with a reverted pin still repair**, and **pre-marker legacy edges get one repair roll** on upgrade so the fleet is not left on a stale tag. Digest annotation reads are **fail-closed** on kubectl/jq errors instead of being treated as “first observation.”
> 
> Helm unit tests and `image-refresh-repin-on-revert.bats` are updated for the new defaults and marker gating.

author: kyle-sexton
body:
Closes #43

## Summary

The dashboard echoed Chromium's profile-directory counter as if it were an order: the picker listed each browser's profiles in whatever order `Local State` wrote them, so `Profile 10` sat before `Profile 2` and every gap from a deleted profile read as meaningful, and the roster card showed only the raw directory name. Research settled that the gaps are the browser's designed output (the counter never decrements), that the app's only coupling to the directory is the persisted string it hands to `--profile-directory`, and that the vendors themselves decouple the display name from the directory. So the fix is order and display in the app, with no browser-side change. The same operand is now fenced to a single path segment, which closes #43.

## Fix

- `ChromiumLocalStateProfileReader` sorts each browser's profiles `Default` first, then `Profile N` by `N`, then any other name ordinal; the browser order stays Chrome, Edge, Brave. New reader test on an out-of-order fixture.
- One rule for a profile directory name, `Core.Accounts.BrowserProfileDirectory.Parse`: a single plain directory name, refusing a path separator or another character no directory name can hold, `.`, `..` or a trailing dot, a control character, a reserved device name, leading/trailing whitespace, and more than 255 characters. `POST /api/accounts` and `PATCH /api/accounts/{email}` apply it with a 400 and store nothing (the POST check runs before the profile folder is created), and `ChromiumFamilyBrowserLauncher` applies it as the last hop before the process, so a name the roster file carries from an older build or a hand edit is refused with the reason rather than emitted as a switch value. Fourteen refused shapes in the endpoint Theory (the superscript-digit device aliases `COM¹` and `LPT².txt` among them, after Codex's review), a PATCH test that the old value survives a refused edit, and a launcher refusal test.
- `GET /api/login-sessions/{id}` carries a comment stating why it is mapped outside the same-origin mutation filter: a read, not readable cross-origin (no CORS, host guards refuse a rebound name), returning what the creating POST already handed the page; guarding reads on the loopback surface is #7's per-instance token, still open.
- `app.js`: the roster card prints `browser / name (directory)` when the discovered catalog resolves the pair and `browser / directory` otherwise.
- `CHANGELOG.md` entries under Unreleased; topic plan `docs/topics/profile-order-and-card-label/PLAN.md`.

## Verification

- `dotnet test -c Release`: total 328, failed 0, skipped 1 (baseline 311 plus 17 new tests); `dotnet build -c Release --no-incremental` with 0 warnings; `dotnet format whitespace --verify-no-changes` clean.
- Review lanes: the code reviewer found no defect (two suggestions, both taken: the changelog categorisation and the Windows-alias question); the security reviewer rated the original fence P4 for Windows alias spellings and noted the launcher trusted the roster file as written; both are addressed in the third commit, and its check of the login-session comment's cross-origin claim (no CORS registered, both host guards) held.
- Isolated instance (temp config, port 48222) built from the final commit, driven with Playwright against the real browsers on the machine: `/api/browser-profiles` came back `Default, Profile 1, Profile 2, Profile 3` for Chrome and `Default, Profile 4, 6, 7, 8, 9` for Edge; the Add form's three `optgroup`s carried the same order read from the DOM; a roster entry mapped to a catalog profile rendered `chrome / <display name> (Profile 1)` and one mapped to a directory the catalog does not carry rendered `chrome / Profile 99`; POSTs carrying `../Profile 1`, `Profile 3.`, `CON`, and `Default::$INDEX_ALLOCATION` each returned 400 with no card, and a PATCH to `Profile 1.` returned 400 and left `Profile 1` in place. Browser console carried only the pre-existing favicon 404. The instance was stopped afterwards.
- Two fresh-context verifiers, one before the review fixes and one on the final diff, confirmed the plan's acceptance criteria (verdicts recorded in the plan's Done note).
- Gates: `markdownlint-cli2`, `typos`, `editorconfig-checker`, and `bash eng/check-no-machine-paths.sh` clean on the changed files.

## Related

- #43 (closed by this PR): both items, the single-segment fence and the documented placement of the login-session status route.
- #7 (open): the per-instance loopback token remains the guard for reads; the comment on the status route points at it rather than claiming it.
- #54 (merged): the docs PR that closes the machine-setup follow-ups plan; this branch is the first follow-up chosen after it.
- Discovery behind the decision lives in the memory tier (`.work/machine-setup-followups/browser-profile-numbering/`), not in the repo.

author: damianpiekarski5-lang
body:
## Problem

Sesje odbyte wczoraj wyświetlają się jako dzisiejsze.

## Przyczyna

`daysSince` w panelu behawiorysty liczyło **upływ 24 godzin**, a nie zmianę daty w kalendarzu:

```js
return Math.floor((Date.now() - d.getTime()) / 86400000);
```

Sesja z wczoraj o 18:00, otwarta dziś o 10:00 → minęło 16 godzin → `floor(0.67)` = **0 dni** → „Trening dziś" na liście psów i „Ostatnia sesja: dziś" na karcie.

Strona spacerów miała ten sam błąd naprawiony już wcześniej (`getCalendarDayDiff` w `utils/dateTime.js`, z komentarzem o zmianie czasu). Panel behawiorysty dostał wtedy własną, uproszczoną wersję i został z wadą.

## Poprawka

Porównywane są początki dni kalendarzowych, tak samo jak po stronie spacerów. **Zaokrąglenie zamiast `floor`**, bo doba przy zmianie czasu ma 23 lub 25 godzin — przy `floor` wczorajsza sesja znów pokazałaby się jako dzisiejsza.

## Zasięg

Ta sama funkcja zasila:

- plakietkę na liście psów („Trening dziś" / „Nie ćwiczy od N dni")
- podsumowanie na karcie psa
- próg pilności „nie ćwiczy od 7 dni" (pomarańczowa krawędź karty)
- pośrednio kolejność listy

Czyli wczorajsze sesje zaniżały też pilność psów.

Sprawdziłem, że ten wzorzec liczenia nie występuje nigdzie indziej — jedyne wystąpienie `86400000` poza `utils/dateTime.js` to właśnie poprawiona funkcja.

## Weryfikacja

```
✔ wczoraj 18:00, teraz 10:00  = 1   (wcześniej 0 — zgłoszony objaw)
✔ wczoraj 23:50               = 1
✔ dziś rano                   = 0
✔ dziś tuż po północy         = 0
✔ tydzień temu                = 7
✔ doba ze zmianą czasu        = 1
```

`react-scripts build` → `Compiled successfully.`

## Wdrożenie

Wyłącznie frontend — bez zmian w Apps Script i regułach Firestore. Dane w bazie były zapisane poprawnie, błąd dotyczył tylko wyświetlania.

## Test plan

- [ ] Pies trenowany wczoraj pokazuje „Nie ćwiczy od 1 dnia", nie „Trening dziś"
- [ ] Pies trenowany dziś nadal pokazuje „Trening dziś"
- [ ] Karta psa zgadza się z listą
- [ ] Kolejność listy uwzględnia poprawione dni

author: jessica12ryan
body:
# fix(docs): exhaustive help for all Settings pages (F1)

## Summary
Pressing **F1** on any **Settings** tab now opens a complete, user-facing reference for exactly what is on that tab. Every visible setting and every dropdown option is documented in plain language with its type, when it appears, what it does, and which values to pick, with restart/reboot/reload effects called out inline. Help dialogs also now navigate between related topics in place — for example the MQTT settings summary links directly to the full MQTT Integration reference and back, without closing and reopening the dialog.

## Coverage
Each help dialog is sourced from `www/settings.json` (`description`/`tip`/`options`/`type`/`children`) and the live grouping in `www/settings-*.php` (`PrintSettingGroup`/`PrintSetting`) and rewritten for non-developers:

`settings.php` gives an overview of all tabs and notes that F1 while a tab is active resolves via `www/js/fpp.js:8183` to `help/settings-{tab}.php`. The tab pages cover `generalPlayback` + `generalScheduler` (11 controls including `MultiSyncEnabled`, `pauseBackgroundEffects`, `blankBetweenSequences`, `screensaver`/`screensaverTimeout`, `openStartDelay`, `remoteOffset`, `DisableScheduler`, `UIStartedPlaylistsProtected`, `ScheduleDistance`, `ScheduleSeconds`), the full A/V matrix (`avModes` `MediaBackend` Simple vs Advanced Full PipeWire, `generalAudio` WLED/IP announcement/volume/offset/aliases, `simplePipeWireAudio` `AudioOutput`/`AudioFormat`/`AudioPeriodSize`/`ForceAudioId`, `pipeWireGeneral`/`pipeWireAudio`/`pipeWireStreams`/`pipeWireVideo` Advanced modals and `simplePipeWireVideo` `VideoOutput`/`ForceHDMI`/`EnableBBBHDMI`/`ForceHDMIResolution`/`HardwareDecoding`/`mediaOffset`/`remoteIgnoreSync`), `input`/`output` (`DisableFakeNetworkBridges`, `BridgeSourcePriority`, `bridgeDataPriority`, `AutoEnableOutputs`, `eFuseRetryCount`/`Interval`, `alwaysTransmit`, `E131BridgingInterval`), `time`/`regionallocation` (live clock, `ClockDate`/`ClockTime`, `piRTC`/`DisablePiRTC`, `ntpServer`, `TimeZone`, `Locale`, `DateFormat`/`TimeFormat`, `temperatureInF`, `Latitude`/`Longitude`), `ui`/`uiColors` and UI Password, `email` (7 SMTP fields plus Configure/Send Test), `mqtt` (11 broker/publish/subscribe fields), `log-levels` (16 dropdowns sharing Errors Only/Warn/Info/Debug/Excessive plus Bulk Change), the privacy table from `www/privacyTable.inc:36` (`stats`, `logos`→`serial`, `crash`→`settings`→`config` + `emailAddress` and the 5-level `ShareCrashData` ladder with Allow/Deny and Preview), `services`/`kiosk`, `StorageDevice`/Grow/New Partition/Flash Create vs Copy/BTRFS/Mounted USB, `system`/`BBBLeds`/`osPassword`/SSH Keys/Reset checklist, and `developer` (`masqUIPlatform`, `gitRemote`/`gitBranch`, `gitHubUser`/`PAT`, `DistributedCompile`/`DistccHosts`).

Within that, the MQTT flow is treated as a connected pair: the **MQTT Settings** summary explains the 11 fields on the tab and links to **MQTT Integration** for the complete publish (`ready`, `version`, `status`, `playlist/*`, `gpio/*`, `command/*`) and subscribe (`/set/command/*`, `/set/playlist/*`, `/light/MODEL/cmd`) topic reference with Home Assistant examples, which now offers a **← Back to MQTT Settings** control at the top to return in place. The dialog itself remembers the last loaded help page (`www/js/fpp.js:8169` `lastHelpPage`) so selecting a different help target while open swaps content instead of dismissing, while pressing F1 again on the same page still closes it, and `ESC` remains handled via `HelpClosed`.

## Why
Every item and dropdown needs a plain-language definition that stays understandable for end users while still being exhaustive. Stale placeholders referenced legacy hardware and omitted settings introduced since PipeWire, privacy consent, and storage-flash flows, leaving Advanced vs Basic visibility undiscoverable and driving repeated support questions.

## How to test
Open each Settings tab and press **F1**; confirm `help/settings-{tab}.php` loads with the section headers above instead of “No help file exists…”. From **Settings → MQTT** press the link to **Help → MQTT Integration** and back — the dialog should stay open and swap content; F1 or `ESC` then closes it. `php -l www/help/settings*.php` and `php -l www/help/mqtt.php` pass, and `php -l www/js/fpp.js` remains clean.

## Checklist
- [x] Help content and the dialog’s in-place navigation updated together (`www/help/` plus `www/js/fpp.js`); no `src/` or config schema changes
- [x] All `settings-*` plus `help/mqtt.php` validated (`php -l` clean, manual F1 spot-checks on playback/av/output/localization/ui/email/mqtt/logs/privacy/services/storage/system/developer and the MQTT ↔ Settings round-trip)
- [x] Language stays user-facing; no new console jargon except the Developer tab where it is gated to UI Level = Developer
- [x] No breaking changes

author: rafaelmedian
body:
This PR gives rounded surfaces continuous corners while preserving round pills and avatars, adds a development-only curve tuner, and keeps project artwork and caption blur correctly clipped.

Changes, in commit order:

1. **Give rounded surfaces continuous corners.** Apply the shared squircle curve with circular-radius fallback, preserve semantic circles and capsules, and document and test the shapes.
2. **Add a live continuous-corner tuner.** Add a development-only DialKit control that stays usable while gallery, booking, and photo dialogs are open.
3. **Show the corner tuner by default in development.** Place it at bottom-left on the normal local preview while preserving explicit edge and photo tuner routes.
4. **Default the corner tuner to exponent 1.2.** Start local previews at the selected curve while retaining the production stylesheet as the source of truth.
5. **Keep caption blur outside the artwork clip.** Separate the media clip from the masked backdrop blur to avoid Chromium's opaque raster, constrain media sizing, and update the documentation and clipping checks.
6. **Extend the dealership preview to the bottom edge.** Remove its bottom inset, document the exception, and verify the artwork edge and updated responsive size.

Verified: lint, production build, 14 design-system Playwright tests, and 374 end-to-end Playwright tests. Browser inspection confirmed the Popparazi artwork fits fully inside its tile.

Kategória porcie (Jasle/Škôlka) mala v `GROUP_CONFIG` natvrdo priradené len Menu A. `OrderService.createEmptyCategory` z toho staval schému `menuCounts`, ktorú `CategoryRow` následne pretínal s prevádzkovým `visible_menus` — takže aj keď mala prevádzka Menu B povolené (a prípadne aj časovo obmedzené cez `menu_day_restrictions`, napr. len v piatok), pre Škôlku/Jasle sa nikde neponúklo.
