author: changs0124
body: 관련 이슈 #151 ## 무엇을 프론트 팔레트를 회사 CI(디인사이트)에서 파생시키고, 로고를 화면 4곳에 올렸다. v1.0 팔레트는 `supanova-premium-aesthetic` 스킬의 Warm Editorial(웜 크림 + 테라코타)에서 왔고 **회사 로고와 아무 관계가 없었다.** 로고를 올리는 순간 시안 로고 위 웜 크림이라는 온도 충돌이 드러나므로 색과 로고를 한 PR 에서 같이 바꿨다 — 원인이 하나인 변경이다. ## 리뷰에서 봐 줄 것 ### 1. accent 값이 어디서 왔는가 로고 원색을 그대로 쓰지 못하는 것이 이 작업의 제약이었다. | 로고 값 | 흰 글자 대비 | 처리 | |---|---|---| | `#41BAE9` (D 마크) | 2.2:1 | 버튼색 불가 → **다크 테마 accent 로만** | | `#F2931D` (오렌지) | 2.3:1 | 글자색 불가 → **배경 칠 전용**(`highlight`) | | `#0070B5` | 5.3:1 | **라이트 테마 accent** | `#0070B5` 는 원색을 임의로 어둡게 깎은 값이 **아니다.** 원본 PNG 를 x 방향으로 0.5 단위씩 훑어 D 마크 접힘면 그라데이션 안에서 찾은 **실재하는 픽셀**이다. 오렌지는 AA 까지 깎으면 `#965D0B` 수준의 갈색이 되어 브랜드 인식이 깨지므로 아예 글자로 쓰지 않는 쪽을 택했다. 라이트·다크 **34쌍을 전부 계산**했고 값은 `design-system.md` 「측정한 대비 (WCAG 2.1 상대휘도)」에 있다. ### 2. 컴포넌트 diff 가 2줄뿐인 이유 색 값이 `index.css` 한 파일에만 있고 화면은 토큰명만 쓰는 구조라 **전면 재도색이 CSS 변수 교체로 끝났다.** 손댄 컴포넌트 둘은 색 교체가 아니라 **의미가 틀렸던 토큰**을 바로잡은 것이다. - `MessageList.tsx` 「자료 없음」 배지 — 동작이 아니라 **주의**인데 `accent`(동작색)를 쓰고 있었다 → `highlight` - `AdminPage.tsx` 오류 배너 — 종전엔 `bg-accent-soft`(테라코타 틴트) 위 `text-danger`(붉은) 라 **우연히** 어울렸다. accent 가 파랑이 되는 순간 연파랑 위 빨간 글씨로 깨진다 → `danger-soft`. **이 PR 이 만든 파손을 메운 것**이라 범위 안이다 ### 3. Logo.tsx 가 인라인 SVG 인 이유 `` 로 두면 워드마크 색을 테마에 맞출 수 없다. 워드마크만 `currentColor` 로 두면 **SVG 하나로 라이트·다크가 다 된다.** 자리는 `icons.tsx` 와 같은 규칙(자체 SVG 는 `components/` 안)이고, `frontend.md` 「폴더 구조」 표에 없는 `src/assets/` 를 새로 만들지 않았다. CI 에 화이트 단색판이 있지만 **다크에서도 D 마크는 브랜드색을 유지한다** — 그 판은 색 재현을 보장 못 하는 인쇄·단색 용도이고, 화면에서 시안·오렌지는 어두운 면에서 오히려 잘 산다. 접힘면 그라데이션은 원본이 18x17 **래스터 마스크**였는데 y 방향 변화가 0 인 완전한 수평 램프라 `linearGradient` 로 갈아끼웠다. 원본 PNG 와 픽셀 대조 시 차이는 **1px 외곽 앤티에일리어싱뿐, 채워진 면의 어긋남은 0건**이다. **경로 좌표는 손으로 고치지 말 것.** 벡터 원본에서 뽑은 값이다. ## 증거 전후 12장을 [이슈 코멘트](https://github.com/changs0124/rag-chatbot/issues/151#issuecomment-5629456010)에 붙였다. 로그인 · 채팅 · 모바일 390x844 · 관리자 오류 배너를 라이트·다크로 찍었고, before·after 모두 같은 URL·상태·뷰포트·셀렉터를 썼다. ## 검증 ``` npm run lint 통과 npm run build 통과 npm run test 16 파일 · 111/111 통과 bash scripts/check-all.sh docs 통과 (참조 232건 · 섹션 24건) ``` 테스트를 늘리지 않았으므로 `case-floors.env` 의 `FRONTEND_MIN` 은 그대로다. ## 일부러 하지 않은 것 - **대비 검사 게이트(`check-contrast.sh`) 신설.** 요청 범위(디자인·테마색) 밖이고 근거도 이 한 번뿐이라, #149 에서 세운 "근거가 한 건뿐일 때 게이트를 만들지 않는다" 기준을 따랐다. **지금은 색을 건드리면 사람이 `design-system.md` 의 대비 표를 다시 재야 한다** — 같은 누락이 한 번 더 나오면 근거가 둘이 된다 - 레이아웃 · 여백 · 타이포 변경. 이번은 색과 로고만 손댔다 - 사이드바 폭이 좁아질 때 로고를 마크로 줄이는 분기. 락업이 `h-7` 에서 121px 이고 사이드바 최소 폭이 200px(패딩 빼고 168px)이라 늘 들어간다 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_017aQYGqujNmSNGNsZR11MFV

author: kevinraffay
body:
## What this delivers

Every race that has a typed board (D232) gains **`Live Win%`, `Δ%`, `Live rank`** beside the existing morning-line columns — plus a read-only `Live` column on the shared `EntriesTable` — and **`STEAM` / `DRIFT` / `NEW FAV`** tags on the horse's name. `Win %` is renamed `ML Win%`.

All of it is one `flagRaceEntries` call in `shared/entry-flags.js`, so `RaceDayView`, `EntriesTable`, `CardView` and `ParsePreview` cannot disagree. The columns are conditional on `comparableCount >= 2`, **derived rather than passed as a prop**: a race with no board, the ingest preview, and the whole static at-track app (no live prices in the payload, ever) keep exactly the table they had, with no call site changed.

### The design decision that matters — and it was a correction mid-build

The first cut printed the raw `1 / (odds + 1)` readings D224 established, and made Δ their plain difference. That is checkable by eye and **wrong**. Driving the real app showed it: a six-horse race whose ML book summed to 126% and whose typed board summed to 136% produced six deltas summing to **+10.4 points** — the gap between the two books, not an opinion anyone formed — so a 4/1 easing to 7/2, which is nothing, printed **`+2.2`** and read as support. A scratch does the same thing harder: two of ten scratching redistributes their share across the survivors and the whole race reads as steaming.

So both books are divided by their own total over a stated **basis** first, and the property pinned in the check script is that **a race's deltas sum to zero**. The basis needs a fallback or the fix breaks the other half — over the comparable set alone, `ML Win%` blanks everywhere no board exists — so it falls back to the ML-priced live runners there. D224's raw reading is not deleted; it moved into each cell's `title`.

### The move rule — two tests, ORed

| | fires on |
|---|---|
| **Proportional** | normalised live ÷ normalised ML ≥ **1.25x** (moderate) / **1.6x** (big), AND ≥ 1 point |
| **Share of book** | \|Δ\| ≥ **5** points (moderate) / **10** points (big) |

A ratio bar alone systematically misses the favourite, which is where the money is — 5/2 bet to 8/5 is a 1.24x ratio while being **+5.5 points of the entire book**. A points bar alone never fires past about 8/1, because nothing out there can move five points. The 1-point floor on the ratio branch keeps tote quantisation out: 99/1 → 60/1 is 1.5x worth 0.7 of a point, and is rounding. Exported as `MOVE_THRESHOLDS` so a findings file can cite the numbers.

**A flag is a LABEL, not a recommendation.** "Follow the steam" and "the drifter is now the value" are both real, contradictory, and unmeasured on this corpus — `docs/requirements/post-time-odds-llm-comparison.md` is what answers that with an `n`, and asserting it in a tag would be concluding it by UI instead.

## How it was tested

**Category: `shared/` + client render + CSS** — so the relevant check scripts, the build, and a real browser.

**Driven in the real app** (Playwright + the bundled Chromium, agent port 8795 against a `VACUUM` copy of the live corpus — never the human's pair). A board typed on Delaware Park race 1:

```
# | Horse                              | M/L | Live | ML Win% | Live Win% |   Δ% | ML rank | Live rank
1 | Stylish Gem  [STEAM 1.2x][NEW FAV] | 5/2 |  8/5 |    23%  |     28%   | +5.5 |    2    |    1
2 | Forget Tomorrow    [DRIFT 2.5x]    | 8/1 | 20/1 |     9%  |      4%   | −5.4 |    5    |    6
3 | Warriors Jewel                     | 4/1 |  7/2 |    16%  |     16%   | +0.4 |    4    |    4
4 | Rules for Three                    | 7/2 |  5/2 |    18%  |     21%   | +3.3 |    3    |    2
5 | Tapwrit Warrior    [STEAM 2.0x]    |12/1 |  5/1 |     6%  |     12%   | +6.1 |    6    |    5
6 | As the Bell Toles  [DRIFT 1.5x]    | 9/5 |  3/1 |    29%  |     18%   |−10.1 |    1    |    3
```

Deltas sum to zero; the tinted cells and the name tags agree because they read the same figures; the saved prices are in their inputs; the raw readings are in the tooltips. Race 2 on the same page, with no board, renders the pre-D236 ten columns. **Both themes, `#root` intact, 0 page errors, 0 failed requests.** Screenshots were read, not just measured — which is how the first cut's `+2.2` was caught.

**`check-entry-flags`: 53 → 85 assertions** (measured, not counted by eye), with **six negative controls**, two of which found real defects rather than confirming the code:

1. comparable set = whole live field → 2 failures
2. no normalisation (raw) → 8 failures
3. AND instead of OR → 2 failures
4. no `minDelta` floor → 1 failure
5. no basis fallback → 3 failures
6. live-rank ties not shared → **passed green**, because no fixture had a tie. A tote prints in buckets, so two horses at 7/2 is ordinary; a tie assertion was added and the control now fires.

The other find: the scratch fixture's comment claimed `5/1, 8/1, 12/1 → 2/1, 3/1, 5/1` was the same shape relative to each other. It is not — that is not a proportional rescale in probability space. The prices are now constructed from the arithmetic (`2/1, 3/1, 5/1 → 5/4, 2/1, 7/2`) and the assertion is zero to twelve decimal places instead of "under a threshold".

**43 of 44 check scripts green, including `check-static-app`** (run from the primary checkout, not a worktree — `client/src/styles.css` and `EntriesTable.jsx` are both in the static import surface). `check-equibase-otr` needs Poppler; **verified it fails identically on `main`**. `npm run build` exits 0.

## Deviations from plan

**Known and not fixed:** at 375px the day-view table overflows and the Live input is not reachable without sideways scrolling. This is not D157's house rule — that binds the phone-reachable static app, and this server is loopback-only (invariant 10) — and it **predates this change**: the pre-D236 table already measured 671px at a 375px viewport. D236 widens a board race to 864px. Flagging it rather than silently widening it further.

## Definition of done

- [x] `DELIVERABLES.md` row added (D236, status, branch, notes).
- [x] The right files reflect the change: **`CLAUDE.md`** gains two gotchas (a raw implied-probability delta carries the difference between the two books' totals; a move flag needs both tests ORed). **`docs/feature-status.md`** gains its row. **`docs/architecture-map.md`** updated for `shared/entry-flags.js`, `EntryFlagTags.jsx`, `EntriesTable.jsx` and `RaceLiveOdds.jsx`. No command added, renamed or retired, so `docs/commands.md` is untouched.
- [x] Verification scaled to what changed — stated above.

author: wildskymaker
body:
## What changed and why

The first release run under the pull-request contract, run 34555409423 for tag `julibrot-1.1.0`, failed at the step "require an annotated tag" with `release: julibrot-1.1.0 is not an annotated tag object`, although GitHub holds `refs/tags/julibrot-1.1.0` as a signed annotated tag object (`84f45978` → merge commit `0999fae7`). The cause is in the checkout action, not in the tag: on a tag-triggered run `actions/checkout@v4` writes the triggering ref into the workspace as its peeled commit, so `git cat-file -t refs/tags/TAG` reports `commit` inside the job whatever the remote stores, and `fetch-tags: true` does not override the ref the action writes for the event's own tag. Because the release workflow runs from the tagged tree, no tag on `0999fae7` can pass, and the fix has to land on `develop` before the tag is cut again. `21881b2c` adds one step to the `validate` job immediately after checkout, "fetch the tag object", which force-fetches the event's tag from origin as an object with `git fetch --no-tags --force origin "+refs/tags/${TAG}:refs/tags/${TAG}"` and proves the local ref is a tag object with `git cat-file -t`; the existing annotated-tag and signature steps follow unchanged. The later jobs check out `needs.validate.outputs.sha` with `fetch-tags: true`, a commit ref rather than the triggering tag, so their tag refs arrive as ordinary objects and `deploy/github-releases.sh` reads the annotation there without a change. `deploy/tests/test-workflows.sh` asserts the step in both parser modes, PyYAML and the awk fallback: exactly one checkout, one fetch step and one annotated-tag check in `validate`, the fetch step directly after checkout and before the annotated-tag check, the `TAG` environment form, and the exact `set -euo pipefail`, refspec and object-type lines; the awk branch records each step's mapping fields independently of key order and counts the fetch step's `env` entries, and the PyYAML branch loads through a `SafeLoader` subclass that rejects duplicate mapping keys, so the two branches judge every fixture identically; four fixtures derived from the live workflow pin that — the step stripped (rejected), an extra `env` entry (rejected), a wrong `TAG:` followed by the correct duplicate (rejected), and a checkout step opening with `name:` before `uses:` (accepted). The eight other `yaml.safe_load` readers in the same file keep their plain loader and are recorded as one line in `docs/plans/backlog.md`. `docs/branching.md` gains one clause in the release-validation paragraph stating why the tag object is re-fetched. body:
Phase 2 of `docs/TERMINAL-DESIGN.md`: the HA SOC panel becomes the only door to the Terminal app.

## Integration

- `terminal.py`: finds the app by slug suffix in the Supervisor's add-on list, reads its info for hostname, state and options, and holds one aiohttp WebSocket to ttyd per session (`ws://<hostname>:7681/ws`, subprotocol `tty`, basic auth). Bytes cross as base64 with ttyd's command byte; one session per user, three per install, eight hours maximum; the browser unsubscribing closes the session; unload closes all.
- `ha_soc.pair_terminal`: accepts only the Supervisor caller (`async_supervisor_call_rejection`), pins the first secret under `terminal_secret`, refuses and audits a mismatch. Described in `services.yaml` and translations.
- Five `ha_soc/terminal/*` commands under `require_soc_access` (owner by default, owner and admins by setting). The open result is repeated as the first `opened` event on the subscription.
- Audit: `terminal_session_open`, `terminal_session_close` (duration, bytes in and out, reason), `terminal_pairing_rejected`; CEF names and severities added.

## App

- `ingress: false`, sidebar entries removed, `homeassistant_api: true` for the pairing call.
- Generates `/data/ha_soc_terminal_secret` once (0600), starts ttyd with `--credential hasoc:<secret>`, and pairs with Core in a background retry loop; the log says "Paired with HA SOC".

## Panel

- New Terminal workspace: xterm.js 6 plus the fit addon, stylesheet generated into `src/generated/xterm-css.ts` by `scripts/gen-xterm-css.mjs` (part of `npm run build`), theme built from HA's CSS variables and rebuilt on theme change, 5,000-line scrollback, session ended on leaving the view. Bundle rebuilt.

## Verified

- `pytest tests -q` in WSL: 804 passed, 13 skipped (12 new in `test_terminal.py`: pairing pin and refusal, status, refusals, tier, byte relay both ways with audit records, ttyd and browser going away, limits, connect failure, unload).
- `tsc --noEmit` clean; shellcheck clean; `check_stale.py` 0 findings.
- In a container: ttyd 1.7.7 with a credential answers 401 to anonymous HTTP, drops an anonymous WebSocket upgrade, and answers 101 with the credential.

## Not verified until installed

- Pairing on the live Supervisor, Core reaching the app's hostname on 7681, a session from the panel, paste and scrollback in xterm.js, theme in light and dark, the close audit record. These are the open items in the design doc.

## Not in this PR (backlog)

- `core` and `addon` targets (need `docker_api` on the app and Protection Mode off), the transcript hash into the audit chain, a palette override.

author: krank3n
body:
## What happened

On 11 Sep the admin inbox got a "💰 New Pro subscriber" email for Tech Flow Electrical, a Play subscriber since 4 Aug. Their sub renewed on 3 Sep, the phone was not opened for three days, and the nightly `expireStaleSubscriptions` sweep flipped them to `isPro:false` on 6 Sep without asking Google (`expiredReason: iap-period-ended-android` is still on the doc). On 11 Sep the launch sweep re-posted the same transaction; `isFirstGrantOfTransaction` treats a non-Pro prior doc as a first grant, so it alerted again and re-ran referral commission.

The email is the symptom. The subscriber was locked out of Pro for five days while paying, and any store subscriber who does not open the app within 3 days of a renewal hits the same thing.

## Changes

- **Sweep asks the store first.** Before expiring a stale sub, the sweep calls Play `purchases.subscriptions.get` or Apple `Get All Subscription Statuses`. A renewal it never heard about extends `currentPeriodEnd` instead of expiring. An unreachable store keeps the sub alive until a 14-day backstop. A doc with nothing to look up expires as before. The decision is a pure helper, `staleSubscriptionAction`, with tests for every branch.
- **A re-grant is not a first grant.** The same sale (transaction id or purchase token) re-validated on a doc carrying an expiry or revoke marker no longer alerts or re-runs commission. The charged-but-never-entitled heal (same id, no marker) still alerts.
- **The admin email fires once per subscriber.** New `isNewSubscriber` gate: an Apple renewal (new transaction id, same `originalTransactionId`) or a Play re-validation on the same purchase token is not a new subscriber. Commission still runs on renewals, as before.
- **A grant clears the expiry markers** (`expiredAt`, `expiredReason`, `revokedAt`, `revokedBy`) so a doc never reads as Pro and expired at once.
- **One Play client.** The Play lookup moved out of `validateGoogleReceipt` into `iapStoreStatus.ts` so the endpoint and the sweep share it. Endpoint behaviour is unchanged.

## Tests

- `receiptValidation.helpers.test.ts`: regression for the Tech Flow shape (expired by sweep, same transaction, no alert), purchase-token match, admin revoke, the heal case still alerting, `isNewSubscriber` for Apple renewals and Play re-validations, and every `staleSubscriptionAction` branch.
- `iapStoreStatus.test.ts`: Play live/lapsed/401/403/5xx/4xx/thrown/no-config; Apple active/grace/expired/revoked/billing-retry, mixed group, stale signed expiry, API errors, no key, sandbox routing.
- Full functions suite: 90 files, 1404 tests green. `tsc` clean.

## Verified against prod (read-only)

- Both lookups answer with the existing keys: Tech Flow's Play token reports live to 3 Oct; a live iOS monthly and a live iOS yearly report their real expiries. The ASC key already has In-App Purchase access.
- Dry run of the new sweep over all 11 live store subs: none stale tonight, so the first run writes nothing.

## Deploy

Functions only: `validateAppleReceipt`, `validateGoogleReceipt`, `expireStaleSubscriptions`, `expireStaleSubscriptionsNow`. No rules, no client change. Note deploy-on-merge only republishes the 1.57 OTA; the functions need a manual deploy.

author: gagahamburger
body:
## Summary

QLI (Quant Lightning Indexer) radix-select TopK — port of CANN `quant_lightning_indexer_v2` (SFA preprocessing), ported to PTO v0.58.4 contracts and placed in the **solution tree** per repo convention (view_copy / gather_v2 / normalization / moe_* / quant style). Rebase/port of #78.

### Content (trimmed per review)

- `kernels/solution/qli/qli_pto_opt_simple.hpp` — static-shape mainline (exact-tile fast path; driver `qli_check_opt`)
- `kernels/solution/qli/qli_pto_opt_dynamic.hpp` — runtime shape + multi-PE token-parallel (driver `qli_check_opt_dynamic`, NPE=1/4)
- `kernels/solution/qli/qli_pto_opt_histogram_radix_design.md` — design doc (algorithm, scheme-A/B evaluation, defence techniques)
- `test/solution/qli/` — Makefile / compile.all / drivers / golden generator / address-fix tooling

Dropped as non-essential: TROWARGMAX baseline and full-defence kernels (no drivers; comparison numbers and defence designs are recorded in the design doc), working-notes and README .md files (non-design docs).

### v0.58.4 port essentials

- `TCOLSUMX` local asm (LB1 = src.ValidRow per upstream f00b928 #101; the b8669ce template binds LB1 to dst.ValidRow=1 and sums only the first source row)
- Row-reduction destinations as physical single-column `[N,1]` (`t1/t1i` `[1,32]` → `[32,1]`)
- Compare results are UINT8 packed predicates: materialize 0/1 masks and candidate sets with `TSEL`; no predicate arithmetic
- `THISTOGRAMX` ByteId encoded in the B.DATR PadValue mnemonic (Zero=0/Max=1/Min=2/Null=3, bits[28:27]) — the canonical decoder ignores bits[19:18]
- `TCMPS` tile-scalar compares (tile-tile TCMP + broadcast tile triggers a LinxV5 backend TMOV size mismatch)
- dynamic driver `tmp16[16*32*numPEs]` (multi-PE path writes per-PE slots at tid*kTm*kTk)

## Validation (gfrun 07e9c661, TileOP b8669ce, llvm 553b08045)

| mode | Sq/Skv/topK | cosine | TopK set |
|---|---|---|---|
| single-PE | 64/128/128, 4/2048/512, 4/8192/512, 4/2080/512 | 1.000000 | 64/64, 4/4, 4/4, 4/4 |
| 4-PE token-parallel (`multiThreadNum=4`) | 4/128/128, 4/2048/512, 4/8192/512, 4/2080/512 | 1.000000 | 4/4 ×4 |

scores max_abs ≈ 3e-08 (FP32 precision); 4-PE partition verified by trace (PE0..3 ↔ token0..3). Re-validated after the solution-tree move and after the trim (both drivers compile clean).

## Build/verify flow (moved from the dropped README)

```bash
cd test/solution/qli
python3 src/gen_qli_golden.py --mode gen --sq 4 --skv 2048 --topk 512 --g 64 --d 128 --outdir <compare_dir>
# point qli_check_data.s .incbin paths at <compare_dir>, then:
$COMPILER_DIR/clang -c -x assembler src/qli_check_data.s -o src/qli_check_data.o
make TESTCASE=qli_check_opt QLI_DTYPE=FP8 Sq=4 Skv=2048 topk=512
# converge SRC*_ADDR with src/fix_cpp_addrs.py until the driver macro equals
# the llvm-nm _binary_srcq_data_start symbol (NOT merely two identical nm reads
# — incremental builds can keep the symbol stable while the macro is off by 8B)
gfrun -f <elf> --dump-memory 0x4000802000:<size>:sim.bin   # NPE=4: -s softcore.multiThreadNum=4
```

Scratch contract (header integration): `indices_gm` must be followed by ≥ `Sq*topK*4 + 8192 + Sq*paddedSkv*4 + 1152 + per-PE hist` writable bytes (see kernel source comments).

## Upstream defects found while porting

1. **TCOLSUM LB1 binding** — fixed upstream by f00b928 (#101); kernels carry TCOLSUMX until toolchains pick it up.
2. **B.DATR ByteId field mismatch** — LinxV5 assembler encodes ByteId at bits[19:18] while the model's canonical decoder reads it from PadValue bits[28:27]; the stock THISTOGRAM template hardcodes Null=3 and mis-rounds Byte0-2 rounds (histograms silently empty → kth=0). No current baseline kernel exercises multi-round THISTOGRAM with a numeric oracle.

## Notes

- NPE=1 ELFs must run with `-s softcore.multiThreadNum=1` (default 4-PE redundant execution shares the single tmp16 slot and races when Sq>1).
- The 4-PE support is token-parallel (per-PE private tiles/scratch, no cooperative instructions); cooperative data-parallel TMATMUL remains an upstream gap as documented in #78.
- `compile_all.sh` registration (`solution/qli`) intentionally not included — this branch predates the solution section of that script; please register on merge.

goldendata 侧修复了 v1 entries API / MCP `list_entries` 的一个翻页 bug：结果按 `created_at` 排序时，`next` 仍回传 `serial_number` 游标，导致翻页漏行、重复。修复后按 `created_at` 排序时 `next` 变为**行偏移**。

- 请求参数与响应字段两处 `next` 的说明同步改成「原样传回」，不再暗示它一定是某条记录的 ID。

author: richlander
body:
This builds robust, reusable Workspace architecture by giving lower layers a
complete immutable ecosystem declaration without coupling them to the
application catalog.

The Queries-owned contract retains exact owner-issued source intent across
exact libraries, Platform populations, and package prefixes. It also keeps
Workspace construction neutral: Ecosystems can later project its evolving
curated composition through this contract, while raw callers remain explicit.

## Product scenario

A discovery-oriented CLI command or Inspect Web Spotlight selection asks
Ecosystems for a fresh curated Workspace. Ecosystems projects Platform,
ASP.NET Core, and Microsoft.Extensions through this lower declaration contract,
then initializes the neutral Workspace API explicitly. The selected package is
added as membership, a Library/type/member becomes focus, and a bounded graph
may use the registered populations under its selected focal length.

The same evidence can support different caller policies:

```text
System.Memory.Data
└─ System.Text.Json
   ├─ package dependency definition: retain the package-authored route
   └─ curated traversal: an exact target-applicable Platform route may prune
      the package edge when ecosystem.platform is registered
      └─ continuation remains available to System.Text.Encodings.Web
```

Package-mode `depends` therefore constructs raw for high-fidelity authored
evidence, while discovery and broad graph experiences may choose curated
construction. Saved Workspaces persist their expanded registrations and restore
raw; they do not persist a `curated` bit whose meaning can drift.

## Demo

The focused test constructs one declaration around the real package asset:

```text
System.Text.Json@11.0.0-preview.7.26381.103
└─ lib/net10.0/System.Text.Json.dll
   └─ exact package Library coordinate

ecosystem.system-text-json
├─ namespace roots
│  ├─ System.Text.Json
│  └─ System.Text
├─ core packages
│  ├─ System.Text.Json
│  └─ System.Text.Encodings.Web
└─ populations
   ├─ exact package Library: System.Text.Json
   ├─ Platform: DotNetRuntime
   └─ package prefix: System.Text.
```

A non-friend consumer observes the same immutable authored order and exact
owner-issued values. Mutating the source arrays after construction does not
change the declaration.

Neighboring cases prove that knowledge-only and scanner-only declarations are
valid, while empty declarations, malformed lower values, duplicate
contributions, null values, and uninitialized immutable arrays are rejected.
Cross-arm overlap remains valid because exact and broad population intent are
distinct.

## Architecture

- Adds canonical `WorkspaceEcosystemRegistrationId`.
- Adds the closed `WorkspaceEcosystemPopulationDeclaration` union:
  `ExactLibrary`, `Platform`, and `PackagePrefix`.
- Adds immutable `WorkspaceEcosystemRegistrationDeclaration` snapshots over
  namespace roots, core packages, populations, and an optional Integration
  scanner.
- Uses Source Selection-owned equality and validation for source declarations;
  Queries validates only its raw namespace and package slots.
- Updates the handoff design and architecture index.

TLA+ is not applicable to this slice: the declaration has no publication,
revision, replacement, scheduling, concurrency, or failure-state transition.
The later Workspace revision and curated-construction owners retain their own
modeling obligations.

## Validation

- `dotnet run --project tests/DotnetInspector.Queries.Tests -c Release -- --filter-class '*WorkspaceEcosystemRegistrationDeclarationTests'` — 30 passed
- `dotnet build dotnet-inspect.slnx -c Release`
- `dotnet run --project eng/DependencyPolicy.Tests -c Release --no-build` — 30 passed
- `dotnet run --project eng/DependencyPolicy -c Release --no-build` — 27 rules, 217 projects, 50 assemblies
- `npx markdownlint-cli docs/architecture.md docs/design/workspace-ecosystem-registration-handoff.md`
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`

Closes #6640.

author: inder
body:
## Summary
- **Bug:** a human could never approve a paper trim or close in a real browser. `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` makes browsers send `Origin: null` on the review form POST, and the exact-origin check refused it. The fetch()-based tests hand-set the Origin header, so they never saw it.
- **Fix:** `Referrer-Policy: same-origin`.
- **New real-browser e2e (Chromium, WebKit, Firefox):**
  - a human reject and approve both work;
  - two cross-site auto-submits that reuse the real cookie and form token (default referrer policy, and no-referrer, which sends `Origin: null`) get 403 and leave the review pending;
  - revisiting says "Review already executed."
- **Docs:**
  - SECURITY.md and ARCHITECTURE.md now state exactly what the review page does and doesn't stop: any local process that can reach loopback and holds the URL, including the MCP client's own agent, can complete it.
  - The agent-facing `instruction` now tells the agent to hand the URL to the user, instead of advertising the bypass.

## Decisions
- **`same-origin` over `strict-origin` or `origin`:** it's the strictest policy that still sends a real Origin; the other two leak the origin to other sites. The page has no outbound links (CSP `default-src 'none'`), so Referer only ever goes to this same server.
- **`playwright-core` over `playwright`:** a user's `npm ci` fetches ~8 MB of JS with no install scripts and never downloads a browser. Browsers are installed only in CI and dev.
- **Rejected for now: moving approval out-of-band** (Telegram or Touch ID). That's a later slice; leaving human approval broken until then is worse. It is required before any real-money approval.

## Verification
- `npm run check`: 62/62, 0 skipped. `npm run test:e2e`: 3/3 (chromium, webkit, firefox), 0 skipped.
- Mutation checks, each caught in every browser:
  - the old `no-referrer` header → the human's own reject/approve gets 403 (the original bug);
  - the origin check deleted → the cross-site attack gets 200;
  - `Origin: null` allowed → the no-referrer attack gets 200.

Refs: Astra S1 "paper-correct strategy" arc, slice 1 of 0–7 (first PR in the arc; the arc spec is kept privately).

author: talaria0101
body:
Foreign arch jobs (riscv64, loongarch64, ppc64le, ppc64) cannot use a job level
`container:`. The binfmt handlers have to be registered from a step before such a
container can start, and a job container is provisioned before any step runs. Those
jobs therefore have to drive the container through `docker run` from a plain step,
and every repository that wants them ends up reimplementing the same plumbing:
binfmt registration, getting `setup.sh` into the container, and the container
invocation itself.

`emulated/action.yml` wraps all of it:

```yaml
- name: Build AppImage (emulated)
  uses: pkgforge-dev/anylinux-setup-action/emulated@<ref>
  with:
    platform: linux/ppc64
```

What it does:

- Runs `emulated/register-binfmt.sh`. `docker/setup-qemu-action` is not used because
  it ships no ppc64 (big endian) handler, and the stock qemu entries require zero ELF
  pad bytes while uruntime stamps `AI` there, so AppImages would fail to exec. The
  entries registered here ignore osabi, pad and e_type.
- Mounts `setup.sh` straight from this repository's own checkout, one level above
  `$GITHUB_ACTION_PATH`, so there is no fetch and no second checkout.
- Runs `get-dependencies.sh` and `make-appimage.sh` inside the container, sourced
  rather than executed so presets like `VERSION` survive between the two.

`DEVEL_RELEASE` flows in from the calling step's `env:` for nightly builds. That is
measured, not assumed: a composite action's steps do see the calling step's `env:`,
and `docker run -e DEVEL_RELEASE` carries it into the container.

Real world use, a six arch matrix with this action driving the emulated four:
https://github.com/talaria0101/Galculator-AppImage/blob/main/.github/workflows/appimage.yml

Validation on that repository, run 34571447236: x86_64, aarch64, riscv64,
loongarch64 and ppc64le all green. ppc64 builds and packs, then fails its runtime
test on pkgforge-dev/Anylinux-sharun#11, which is unrelated to this action and
already open. The same run against the previous hand rolled `docker run` step fails
ppc64 identically, same preload objects and same missing GLIBC_2.3 and 2.4 symbols,
so this introduces no regression on any arch.

author: mgilbir
body:
A parse cannot climb past a step that produces what it reads — `MoveParseUp` stops where `fieldIntersection(node.producedFields(), child.dependentFields())` — and that intersection is taken over path **prefixes**, so a step producing `properties` blocks a parse of `properties.name`.

This engine asked each step only for its `as`. A `lookup` that brings the secondary table's columns in under their own names therefore looked like a step that writes nothing: the flatten formula climbed above the lookup and read a column the source table has never had.

**Seven** specifications in the wild corpus join a table that way and then name a path inside what it brought in — a world map looking up a country's shape and captioning it by `properties.name`.

The names a transform gives itself are upstream's, one per node class:

```js
// LookupNode
public producedFields() {
  return new Set(this.transform.as ? array(this.transform.as) : this.transform.from.fields);
}
```

a lookup's are the secondary table's `values`, a fold's are `key` and `value`, a density's are `value` and `density`, a regression's are the two columns it fits.

## Checks

- 4 tests in `ProducedFieldsTest`, every expectation compiled with upstream rather than reasoned about: the lookup that names nothing, the one that renames, the filter that follows, and the path field of the table's own that still climbs to the source (where upstream writes the empty `parse: {}` this engine already reproduces).

author: koki-develop
body:
Two rationales describe the source their grammar rests on more loosely than the source supports. Neither count or character class moves; what changes is what the prose claims the source says.

## Axiom: one whole token, not two

`builtin_axiom_personal_access_token.go` names two sources for the layout, and only one of them carries a whole value: Axiom's Go SDK writes a personal token as an `X` for each hexadecimal character, which is a mask, and Axiom's documentation prints one whole token of the other kind. A version nibble cannot be read off a mask, so the version 4 reading rests on that single printed value — the API token, which carries the same layout.

The argument the sentence serves is untouched: the version and the variant are declined because nothing of Axiom's states a version, and one printed value is a thinner regularity than two would have been, which if anything makes declining the tightening clearer. `Test_AxiomPersonalAccessToken_anyVersionAndVariant` still pins it, and its comment is corrected alongside.

## Prefect: a boundary widened, not added

`builtin_prefect_api_key.go` says betterleaks reads gitleaks' expression with a closing boundary added. gitleaks builds its Prefect rule through `utils.GenerateUniqueTokenRegex`, whose `secretSuffix` is `` (?:[\x60'"\s;]|\\[nr]|$) ``, so the expression already closes on a quote, whitespace, a semicolon, an escape or the end of the input. betterleaks carries `` (?:\\?['"\x60]|[\s;]|\\[nr]|$) ``, which admits everything that one does and a quote a backslash escapes besides.

What the paragraph rests on is unaffected — betterleaks is still gitleaks' expression rather than a reading of its own, so the count rests on two readings and not four.

Verified against the rules themselves: gitleaks' `cmd/generate/config/rules/prefect.go` and `cmd/generate/config/utils/generate.go`, and betterleaks' resolved config.

`go test ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `golangci-lint run`, `gofmt -l .` and `go fix -diff ./...` are clean.

## Aureus — black & gold screen recorder for Windows, made by Troy

This PR evolves **Aureus** from v1.1.0 to **v1.2.0**.

### v1.2.0 — what's new
- **Browser studio** (`web.go` + embedded `studio.html`): a localhost-only
  (`127.0.0.1:<random port>`) black & gold HTML page served from inside the
  exe. Start/stop recording, watch a live timer, browse every recording with a
  preview, **trim** a clip, and delete it. Nothing to install; not reachable
  off the machine. `-web=false` disables it (console + hotkey only).
- **Choose where recordings go**: `-outdir D:\Clips` (created if missing);
  defaults to your **Videos** folder.
- **Trim** (`trim.go`): GIF trimmed in pure Go (keeps frames whose cumulative
  time falls in `[start,end)`); MP4 via `ffmpeg -ss/-to -c copy`. Backs both
  the `-trim`/`-start`/`-end` flags and the studio's Trim button.
- **One engine** (`engine.go`): a thread-safe recorder with its own frame-pump
  goroutine, shared by the console hotkey loop and the web studio, so neither
  control path can starve capture or drop a keypress.

### Carried over from v1.1.0 / earlier
- **F9 hotkey fix**: `GetAsyncKeyState` is a *level*, previously sampled inside
  the capture loop, so short taps were lost mid-frame. Keys are now polled on
  their own goroutine every 5 ms and handed to the main loop as events.
- **Branding**: app renamed **Aureus**; custom black & gold icon; Windows
  version info ("Made by Troy", product *Aureus*); DPI-aware manifest.
- **Signing**: self-signed code-signing cert (`CN=Aureus, O=Made by Troy`),
  committed at `.signing/`. (Self-signed ≠ trusted — SmartScreen still warns.)

author: themariodiego
body:
Follow-up to #95 (merged as `cc1558a`). Two commits. First pair on `/overview`, which priority 2 names and where all eight states were unproven.

## The obvious window is the wrong one

`status: "parsing"` is opened and closed inside one server request, so it cannot be held from a browser at all — a client-side hold lands *before* the server ever sets it, and `route.fetch()` runs the whole request, so by the time anything can act the status is cleared. Seeding a `parsing` row would reach the panel, and would prove something about the fixture rather than the product.

But `STEP_FOR_STATUS` in the Overview page also maps **`uploaded`** to step 0, and that state is real, server-side and durable: the file is finalized and stored, and preparation has not been asked for yet. Holding the preparation request keeps the account genuinely in it for as long as the test needs.

Nothing is manufactured. The test waits inside a state the product defines, and asserts the row really reads `uploaded` before anything else.

## The timing sentence is the part worth having

The page must state measured p50/p95 durations for the file's tier, or say *"This deployment has not processed enough files to estimate a time yet"* — never a marketing estimate.

So the test does not pick a branch. It reads the same `processing_time_stats` RPC the page reads and follows the data: the registered sentence shape at or above the twenty-file floor, the refusal below it. Those two are the only permitted outputs, so **a page that invented a duration fails, and so does one that withheld a duration it had the evidence for.**

That also makes it correct in both environments rather than tuned to one. This machine's tier 1 has 355 measured files, so the measured branch ran locally; a fresh CI database will usually be below the floor and exercise the refusal instead.

## Second commit: two promises nothing tested

**The panel's own refresh.** `ProcessingPanel` hardcodes `<AutoRefresh active />` and says it "re-fetches every five seconds so the steps advance without a manual reload". Nothing verified that — and the first version of this spec didn't either: it asserted the panel was gone after a *fresh navigation*, which would pass even if the polling were dead. The assertion now runs on the already-open page, never reloaded, so only the panel's own `router.refresh()` can make it go.

**The second form of State A.** `/overview` State A has two forms and `e2e/overview.spec.ts` covers only the first. When a prepared source exists but no report or ancestry does, `needsReportChoice` replaces the Start-here strip with "Choose your reports" and a link to `/genome/me/reports`. That is exactly where the next act is a person's explicit choice of analysis, and it had no browser test at all. Now asserted — including that the strip is **replaced** rather than kept, because telling someone who has just uploaded their genome to "add a file" is the failure worth catching.

Worth recording that I went looking for that as a defect and it was not one: `resolveState()` returns "A" for a prepared file with no purposes, which looked like it would strand the person on the onboarding hub. The page already handles it.

## The heading can only ever say "Processing Genome file"

Pinned deliberately. The canonical finalize RPC stores that literal instead of the person's filename (#95), so State B has no way to name the file they chose — a coherent consequence of that privacy decision rather than a gap, pinned where someone might otherwise "fix" the heading by reaching for the real name.

## Not claimed

`src/copy/overview.ts` defines the product's own **five** overview states, a different vocabulary from the register's eight ids — so the mapping is interpretive, not mechanical. State B → `processing` is the one clean correspondence.

- **`/overview empty` is not claimable**, and this is now settled by reading rather than left open: both absence sentences are gated on `hasReports`, so State A renders domain ledes and contains no statement of absence anywhere. On the standard this repo applies — a page is `empty` when it *says* so — State A does not qualify. That is a decline, not a defect: an onboarding hub telling a new person what the areas are for is a reasonable thing to be, and inventing a requirement that it announce its own emptiness is not this change's to make.
- **State C → `complete` / `partial-coverage`** is arguable in both directions: populated report counts alongside three explicit absences.
- **States D and E** have no browser test at all; D needs two paired accounts, E needs embryo ingest, which is not shipped.

## Ratchet

**234 → 233**, recorded in `docs/route-divergence.json` and compared in both directions. The second commit adds no pair — neither addition is one of the eight state ids, and the value is a branch that runs for real users and had no test.

## Verification

`4 passed (37.6s)` for this spec alongside the existing `e2e/overview.spec.ts`, no skips, no retries. 14 route-gate assertions; route and readability gates clean; typecheck and lint clean.

No acceptance-matrix gate flipped: it stays at 24 YES / 41 NO.

body:
## What is the problem

`applypass/firstmate` had drifted 329 commits behind canonical upstream `kunchenguid/firstmate` while carrying 11 local customizations. The merge base is `a5fe1bcc`. Every upstream fix, backend, and safety change since then was unavailable here, and the gap was growing faster than the fork was.

The customizations were not all worth keeping. Several solved a problem upstream has since solved differently and better, so a straight "merge and preserve everything" would have re-introduced machinery upstream deliberately does not have, on top of a 329-commit conflict resolution nobody could review.

## What was the fix

**Base chosen: current `upstream/main` (`4768e98d`), not the parked branch.** The parked `origin/reconcile/kunchenguid-upstream-20260821` was built for the old "preserve all 11" plan and was already ~173 behind upstream. Because the decided end-state drops five customizations and reduces a sixth, continuing that branch would have meant folding everything in and then deleting it - more work and more ways to leave something behind. Basing on current upstream and re-adding only the kept delta makes the drops self-evident: a dropped customization is simply never re-added, and there is nothing to prove absent by inspection.

**The merge.** `f1f110a2` records `origin/main` as a second parent, so the fork's history is preserved and this lands as an ordinary merge, while the tree is upstream's exactly. The four commits on top are one per kept concern, so this is reviewable a concern at a time rather than as one 329-commit conflict resolution.

**Per customization:**

| # | Customization | How it landed |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `sc-`/type branch convention | **Kept, re-ported inline** (`0cb7ebb8`). The branch and PR-title convention, the `+ticket:<prefix>` registry flag, `fm-merge-local` branch discovery with `--branch` recovery, the same recovery in `fm-review-diff`, `fm-promote`'s ticket-aware ship-branch instruction, and the `fm-bearings.v1` `task` -> `branch` field rename. Two obsolete parts dropped: pre-window fail-closed mode resolution in `fm-spawn.sh` (upstream now requires `--mode`) and the explicit meta-write failure check (upstream publishes meta atomically under lock). |
| 2 | Batched defect-class decision | **Kept, reconciled** (`6a6b9748`). Re-added on top of upstream's 5-step `ask-user-authority` rewrite, cross-reference moved off the retired step 7 onto upstream's step 4. |
| 3 | `cursor-agent` adapter | **Dropped - took upstream's `cursor` adapter**, including `docs/supervision-protocols/cursor.md` and upstream's restructured harness references. |
| 4 | Context-budget guard (180k) | **Dropped entirely.** No `bin/fm-context-budget.sh`, no ceiling stub, no hook slot. |
| 5 | Handover + helm takeover | **Reshaped to its manual core** (`b8c77aba`). Kept: `bin/fm-handover.sh` (prepare / check / release / show / consume / pending, helm-gated, captain-invoked), `bin/fm-lock.sh release` and `clear --pid N`, and one line naming the exact clear command in every live-holder refusal and in `status`. Dropped: the automatic trigger (`fm-session-pulse.sh`), all token and silence measurement (`fm-context-measure-lib.sh`, transcript mtime), automatic helm takeover (`fm-helm-lib.sh`), the `.helm-activity` markers, and the awaiting-the-captain block with its `fm-decided.sh` / `fm-backlog-record-lib.sh` dependencies. |
| 6 | `resolve --no-work` | **Dropped - took upstream** `bin/fm-captain-hold.sh` and both the `decision-hold-lifecycle` and `captain-hold-lifecycle` skills. |
| 7+11 | PR body sections | **Kept, Option A.** Upstream's captain-words-only `--intent` contract taken as-is; the three sections are shaped after the PR opens, in the same post-open edit that sets the `sc-` title prefix. This PR body is that shape. |
| 8 | Trace stand-down failures | **Dropped** (rode inside #4). |
| 9 | Exclude zero-usage entries | **Dropped** (rode inside #5's measurement). |
| 10 | Worktree isolation identity | **Kept, reconciled inline** (`2d99bcd3`). Upstream's `spawn_worktree_isolated` kept as the base, including its git-common-dir check; its three path-text comparisons replaced with device-and-inode identity tests. |

**The six expected conflict files.** `bin/fm-spawn.sh` and `bin/fm-supervision-instructions.sh` stopped being collisions when #3 was dropped and #1's spawn hunks were dropped as obsolete; both are upstream's verbatim, with #10's identity change applied on top of upstream's current predicate in `fm-spawn.sh`. `bin/fm-brief.sh`, `bin/fm-merge-local.sh`, `bin/fm-bearings-snapshot.sh`, and `bin/fm-fleet-sync.sh` are upstream's current versions with #1's changes hand-applied - no textual merge was attempted on any of them.

## Proof of work

**Lint.** `bin/fm-lint.sh` exits 0: ShellCheck 0.11.0 (pinned), actionlint 1.7.12 (pinned), 3 workflow files valid.

**Tests.** `bin/fm-test-run.sh --changed --base f1f110a2` selects 75 files. Three of them drive real Herdr lifecycle behaviour, which this task is not scaffolded to run, so 72 were run: **63 pass, 9 fail, and every one of the 9 is an environment limit on this machine, not a regression.**

| Failing test | Why |
|---|---|
| `fm-captain-hold-lifecycle`, `fm-pr-merge`, `fm-bearings-board`, `fm-teardown`, `fm-backlog-atomicity`, `fm-bearings-snapshot`, `fm-backend`, `fm-control-relaunch` | `bin/fm-tasks-axi-lib.sh` sets `FM_TASKS_AXI_MIN=0.2.4`; the installed `tasks-axi` is 0.2.3. Each stops on the same refusal, `fm-captain-hold: compatible tasks-axi is required` or `automatic backlog transitions require tasks-axi 0.2.4 or newer`. body:
## Scope

Adds defense-in-depth before no-vig / EV / Kelly economics for canonical `doctore.market-snapshot.v1` inputs.

The current decision core models one win probability and one decimal price. It cannot correctly price explicit push, Asian quarter-line half-win/half-loss, KBO/NPB tie, or tennis retirement/void states without additional outcome probabilities.

This PR:
- keeps generic research price-vector no-vig API behavior unchanged
- allows currently representable canonical domains (e.g. MLB moneyline, half-line baseball/basketball totals/spreads, soccer 1X2 and half-goal totals)
- blocks integer/quarter push-capable line economics
- blocks KBO/NPB moneylines until tie probability is modeled
- blocks tennis match moneyline economics until retirement/void probability is modeled
- adds a direct decision-core regression proving an unsupported integer total returns `BLOCKED` before EV/Kelly/stake fields are populated

No probability is modified or negotiated. No bet is placed automatically.

author: shjwudp
body:
## Why

Follow-up to [guihong-nv's review comment on PR #6486](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/6486#discussion_r3979226842):

> Enabling PP introduces duplicate embedding/output weights, but `FullyShardedOptimizer.get_grad_norm()` counts both copies in its WORLD reduction. Its replication correction only covers DP. A four-rank reproduction returned 7.071 instead of 5, causing excessive gradient clipping. Preserve the shared-parameter marker and exclude duplicate copies from gradient statistics.

`FullyShardedOptimizer.get_grad_norm()` and `FullyShardedOptimizer.count_zeros()` each run their own loop over `self.get_parameters()` and divide only by `count_replication(grad)` — the product of the replicated **DTensor mesh** axes, i.e. DP. So with `PP > 1` the tied embedding/output weight is counted twice.

`megatron/core/models/common/language_module/language_module.py` builds that tie as two *distinct parameter objects* on two different pipeline stages:

* the **first** stage (`pre_process`, not `post_process`) gets `shared_embedding = True` only (line 276) — this is the canonical copy;
* the **last** stage (`post_process and share_embeddings_and_output_weights`, or `mtp_process`, and not `pre_process`) gets `shared = True` **and** `shared_embedding = True` (lines 289–290) — this is the duplicate.

Both copies hold the same weight and the same gradient, so the sum over the grad-stats group counts every element twice and the reported norm is inflated by `sqrt(2)` — exactly the `7.071 / 5 = 1.4142` in the report. The over-reported norm then over-clips gradients. `count_zeros()` has the identical defect, so the `num-zeros` metric was inflated the same way.

## What changed

**This revision narrows the change to a single production file.** `megatron/core/optimizer/optimizer.py` is now **byte-identical to the base** (zero diff), and the base version of `tests/unit_tests/test_optimizer.py` is restored (zero diff). An earlier draft of this PR refactored `MegatronOptimizer._filter_grads_for_norm` into a shared `_filter_params_for_norm`; that refactor is reverted, so the classic optimizer path is untouched by this PR.

`git diff --stat 8f4fa598d..HEAD`:

```
 megatron/core/optimizer/fully_sharded_optimizer.py | 47 ++++++++++++++++++++--
 .../distributed/mfsdp_v2/test_optimizer.py         | 27 +++++++++++++
 2 files changed, 71 insertions(+), 3 deletions(-)
```

**`megatron/core/optimizer/fully_sharded_optimizer.py`**

* New module-level `_filter_params_for_norm(params)` — keeps a parameter only when `param_is_not_shared(param)` holds, i.e. drops exactly the `shared = True` duplicate. `param_is_not_shared` is imported by extending the existing `from ..transformer.module import MegatronModule` line.
* `get_grad_norm()` and `count_zeros()` both iterate `_filter_params_for_norm(self.get_parameters())` instead of `self.get_parameters()`. Both had the same bug; fixing only the norm would have left `num-zeros` inflated.
* **The loop bodies are unchanged**: each surviving parameter still contributes `||local||^2 / count_replication(grad)` (resp. zero counts) into the reduction over `self.get_grad_stats_parallel_group()`, and each loop keeps its own `if grad is None: continue`.
* Both docstrings gained a paragraph stating that the statistic counts one copy of a tied parameter across PP ranks, and that mesh-replicated axes are handled by `count_replication` instead.

### Why only the shared-parameter duplicate, and not TP/GTP replicas

The earlier draft also applied `param_is_not_tensor_parallel_duplicate` and `param_is_not_gtp_duplicate` here. That is wrong for this code path, and it is dropped:

* TP and GTP replicas are copies **of the same parameter**. They are therefore expressed as **replicated axes of the gradient's DTensor mesh**, and `count_replication(grad)` already divides each rank's contribution by the number of ranks holding that shard — the correction these statistics are built around. Filtering them out again would double-correct.
* The PP-tied embedding/output duplicate is different **in kind**: it is a *separate parameter object* living on a *different pipeline stage*, so no mesh layout of either gradient describes the relationship and `count_replication` cannot see it. That is the only double count this filter has to remove.
* Dropping the predicates also keeps this file off the global process-group reads those predicates need. With `tp_group`/`expert_tp_group` unset (as they are for `FullyShardedOptimizer` — nothing in that class or its bases assigns them), `param_is_not_tensor_parallel_duplicate` falls back to `get_tensor_model_parallel_rank()`/`get_tensor_model_parallel_group()` global MPU state, and `param_is_not_gtp_duplicate` to the GTP remat global ranks. `AGENTS.md` explicitly asks `megatron/core` code to avoid new direct reads of global process groups, and there is no reason to take on that dependency for a correction `count_replication` already performs.

### Why the filter does not test `param.grad`

The `grad is not None` check deliberately stays in the callers:

* which attribute holds the gradient depends on the optimizer (`decoupled_grad` for precision-aware runs, `grad` otherwise), so a parameter-level predicate must not look at it; and
* MFSDP v2 needs the gradient **DTensor object** itself, not an extracted tensor, to read the replicated mesh axes `count_replication` divides by. Filtering parameters and reading the gradient in the caller keeps both the layout and the replication factor.

## Tests

* Added `test_filter_params_for_norm_drops_shared_duplicate` to **`tests/unit_tests/distributed/mfsdp_v2/test_optimizer.py`** (the MFSDP v2 unit-test bucket, glob `tests/unit_tests/distributed/mfsdp_v2/**/*.py` in `tests/test_utils/recipes/h100/unit-tests.yaml`). It marks one of two parameters `shared = True` and asserts the filter keeps exactly the unmarked one, that an unmarked parameter is never dropped, and that an empty input stays empty. It is pure parameter bookkeeping — no CUDA, no multi-rank setup, and it does not request the `distributed_setup` fixture.
* The assertions compare by identity (`kept[0] is embedding`) rather than `==`, because comparing `Parameter` objects elementwise would be a tensor op.
* `tests/unit_tests/test_optimizer.py` is back to the base version, so the tests added by the previous draft of this PR (and the `MockOptimizer` changes they required) are gone.

## Verification done — and what was *not* run

Run on the final commit:

* `python -m py_compile` on both changed files: OK.
* `uv run --no-sync ruff check --select F821,F811 --isolated <files>`: `All checks passed!`
* `uv run --no-sync ruff check <files>` with repo config: `All checks passed!`
* `uv run --no-sync isort --check-only <files>`: no changes needed (run because the `transformer.module` import line changed).
* All added lines are ≤ 90 characters (repo limit 100).
* `git diff --name-status 8f4fa598d..HEAD`: only `megatron/core/optimizer/fully_sharded_optimizer.py` and `tests/unit_tests/distributed/mfsdp_v2/test_optimizer.py`, both `M`.

**No pytest run, and no GPU/multi-rank run.** On this machine `import megatron.core.optimizer` fails at `megatron/core/inference/quantization/mxfp8_tensor.py:50` with `AttributeError: module 'torch' has no attribute 'float8_e8m0fnu'` (system torch 2.4.0); the same failure reproduces on the pristine base commit, so it is environmental and pre-existing. There is also no CUDA device here, and the MFSDP v2 bucket runs under `torchrun` on GPUs. **The added test has therefore never been executed.**

As a partial substitute, the *actual source text* of `_filter_params_for_norm` was extracted from the changed file with `ast`, `param_is_not_shared` was taken verbatim from `megatron/core/transformer/module.py`, and the result was executed on CPU: a `shared = True` parameter is dropped, an unmarked one is kept, an input without the attribute is kept, an empty input stays empty, and summing both copies vs. one copy

author: fkras
body:
The sleep system was purely idle-timeout based, so an always-on deck could only be achieved by setting huge timeouts, which also disabled any night dimming. Add time-of-day brightness windows and fix several hot-path costs that matter on a low-power SBC.

Night schedule:
- Add sleep.schedule: a list of {from, to, brightness} windows in local time (honoring TIMEZONE). Windows may wrap midnight; the first match wins.
- Allow sleep_timeout/dim_timeout of 0 to mean "never" (the schema previously required >= 1, so "never sleep" was not expressible).
- Outside every window the deck stays at full brightness rather than idling down, so a wall-mounted deck no longer dims in the middle of the day.
- Pressing a button inside a window restores normal brightness for readability.
- De-duplicate brightness writes so the device isn't told the same value twice.

Performance:
- Cache compiled Jinja templates instead of recompiling on every redraw (~79x).
- Replace DeepDiff with plain equality for button comparison; it was building a full diff report just to answer "did this change?" (~1500x).
- Give generated icons a stable SHA-1 based name. They were named from Python's hash(), which is randomized per process, so the cache never hit after a restart. The cache now survives restarts and is pruned by age instead of wiped, with entries touched on use.
- Debounce Home Assistant state_changed events (100ms) so a scene touching several entities causes one redraw instead of several.
- Disable optipng by default (ENABLE_OPTIPNG=1 re-enables); it cost hundreds of ms per icon for a little disk space.
- Log a broken template's traceback once instead of on every redraw.
- Wake the backlight before repainting so the deck feels responsive.

Also:
- Add GET /v1/status to the server, reusing the existing is_script_running().
- Add homedeck.service for start-on-boot and recovery after USB/HA loss.
- Add assets/configuration.wall-mount.yml.example.
- Add tests for the schedule and brightness state machine (40 tests).
- Document all of the above in the README.

## Summary
PR1 of CM-1438's split plan: adds the `fetchAndSaveStarSnapshot` Temporal activity in a new, dedicated `star_snapshot_worker` service (not folded into `security_best_practices_worker` — separate feature, separate worker).

## Changes
- New `services/apps/star_snapshot_worker` package: `main.ts` (`ServiceWorker` boot), `activities/index.ts` + `activities.ts` barrel, `workflows.ts` placeholder (required by Temporal's workflow bundler even with no workflow defined yet, plus sibling `workflows/` dir since the bundler `fs.statSync`s that literal path before webpack resolves the barrel file).
- `fetchAndSaveStarSnapshot`: fetches GitHub GraphQL `stargazerCount` for a repo and upserts a row via the CM-1436 DAL function (`upsertStarSnapshot`), modeled on `packages_worker`'s `fetchLightRepo.ts` fetch/error-classification pattern, including its retry classification for GraphQL error types and rate-limit-message detection.
- Retry classification: 401 is retryable (requester/platform-side auth hiccup — token rotation, GitHub auth incident — not a per-repo signal). 403 inspects the response body for "rate limit" and only treats it as non-retryable auth failure if that's not the cause, so GitHub rate-limiting retries with backoff instead of permanently dropping the fetch. GraphQL errors of type `NOT_FOUND`/`FORBIDDEN`/`INSUFFICIENT_SCOPES` are non-retryable unless the message indicates rate-limiting, which stays retryable regardless of type. Fetch is bounded by a 30s AbortController timeout covering the full response (headers + body).
- `capturedAt` is passed in by the caller rather than computed inside the activity, so retries stay idempotent against the `(repositoryId, capturedAt)` unique constraint.

## Type of change
- [x] New feature

## JIRA ticket
https://linuxfoundation.atlassian.net/browse/CM-1438

PR1 of 3 for this ticket (see ticket comment for full split: PR2 workflow+schedule, PR3 docker/builder tooling).

author: kopancek
body:
First slice of [WAN-1074](https://linear.app/waniwani/issue/WAN-1074). SDK only. The app, template and kit changes land separately, and this has to go out first because the template depends on a published `@waniwani/sdk`.

## What changes

**The browser bundles stop leaking Node.** The three browser-facing tsup entries build on `platform: "browser"`. On the node platform `nanoid` and the streamdown → unified → vfile chain resolved to their Node entries, so `dist/chat/index.js` and its chunks shipped bare `crypto`, `path`, `process` and `url` imports that every customer bundler had to shim. Nothing needed promoting to a peer dependency.

**The stop button works.** `useChatEngine` exposes `stop`, `chat-embed` passes it to `PromptInputSubmit`, and after the local abort it POSTs `{ sessionId }` to `{api}/cancel` so the runtime stops the turn rather than generating into a dropped stream.

**Endpoint hygiene off the platform.** `use-call-tool` and `export-session` build their URLs with `buildApiUrl`, so a base carrying a query string stops producing a broken route. The document module and the event ingest resolve through a new `platformEndpoint`, which returns `null` off the `/api/mcp/` mount: a customer-hosted runtime serves the chat siblings and nothing else, so uploads refuse up front and page-view, suggestion and host-page tracking stay quiet instead of 404ing against the customer's own origin.

**A build-time guard for the above.** `platform: "browser"` also opts packages into DOM-only builds. `decode-named-character-reference` answers the browser condition with `index.dom.js`, which runs `document.createElement` at module load, so the first commit here made every SSR import of `@waniwani/sdk/chat` throw `document is not defined` — the first render of any Next.js page carrying the widget. The chat entry now aliases that package onto its isomorphic entry, and `bun run build` ends on `check:browser-bundles`, which imports each browser entry with no DOM and walks the chunks each one reaches looking for bare Node builtins. CI runs `bun run build` and nothing else, which is why the check lives there rather than in the test suite.

## Verification

```
bun run build        green, ending on "Browser bundles OK"
bun test             910 pass, 5 fail — the same five fail on main, untouched by this branch
```

Server-rendering `ChatEmbed` through `react-dom/server`, against the built bundle:

| build | result |
| --- | --- |
| `main` | imports fine, ships a bare `crypto` import |
| this branch without the alias | `ReferenceError: document is not defined` |
| this branch | renders, no Node builtins in the browser output |

The guard was checked in both directions: reverting the alias fails it on the DOM half, dropping `platform: "browser"` fails it on the `crypto`/`path`/`process`/`url` half.

## Worth knowing before merge

- **`POST {api}/cancel` is not served by app.waniwani.ai yet.** Only the self-hosted runtime in the template answers it. On hosted chat the stop click aborts the stream locally, which is the visible fix, and the cancel POST 404s harmlessly. The server keeps generating until the app grows the route, so that wants to follow soon.
- **`platform: "browser"` on `mcp/react` and `mcp/react/skybridge` is a no-op today** — byte-identical output either way. Kept for intent, and both are covered by the new guard.
- **Uploads and tracking now refuse off the `/api/mcp/` mount.** That includes `ChatEmbed`'s default `api` of `/api/waniwani`, where they resolved to a URL nothing served anyway. A host proxying the chat somewhere other than `/api/mcp/…` loses document upload, which is the one real narrowing here.
- **No version bump**, per the release rule. The bump is its own branch once this lands.
- The docs delta this implies (the `/cancel` route in the bring-your-own-backend contract, and the upload/tracking narrowing) is not in this PR.

> **Medium Risk**
> Changes default chat bundle output, SSR import behavior, and narrows uploads/tracking off `/api/mcp/`; stop also depends on runtimes implementing `/cancel` for server-side turn cancellation.
> 
> **Overview**
> This PR hardens **browser-facing SDK bundles** and fixes **chat stop** plus **URL routing** when the chat `api` is not on the Waniwani platform mount.
> 
> **Build & SSR:** Chat and MCP React entries now build with `platform: "browser"` so dependencies stop resolving Node paths that leaked bare `crypto`/`url`/`process` imports. The chat bundle aliases `decode-named-character-reference` to its isomorphic entry so SSR (e.g. Next.js) does not crash on `document` at import time. **`bun run build`** runs a new **`check:browser-bundles`** step that imports entries without a DOM and scans reachable chunks for Node builtins.
> 
> **Stop:** `useChatEngine` exposes **`stop`**: it aborts the local stream, then **POSTs `{ sessionId }` to `{api}/cancel`** via `buildApiUrl` (404/network errors are ignored after abort). **`ChatEmbed`** passes this to **`PromptInputSubmit`**.
> 
> **Endpoints:** **`buildApiUrl`** is used for tool calls, scenario export, and cancel so query strings on the base stay valid. New **`platformEndpoint`** returns **`null`** when `api` is not under `/api/mcp/`—document uploads fail fast with `upload_disabled`, and page-view, suggestion analytics, and **`chat.track`** noop instead of hitting bogus URLs on customer-hosted runtimes. Chat sibling routes (`/config`, `/tools`, `/cancel`) still use **`buildApiUrl`** on any mount.

body:
## Summary

The spine's stacked (one-figure-per-line) container arm moves from `14em` to `18em`, so it takes over before the five-column arm has less room than one figure. Follow-up to #274, where this was found and measured but left out of scope.

## Problem

At a 320px viewport at the default text size — the width SC 1.4.10 reflow names — the km cell was 16px wide: `30.15` on three lines, `AHEAD` as five single letters, on every row. The five-column arm's four set tracks (30.5ch ≈ 18.8em of the row's type) plus four 0.6em gaps cost more than the container had, `minmax(0, 1fr)` let the km track go to nothing, and `overflow-wrap: anywhere` did what it promises. Same band at 375–414px/125% text, 480px/150%, 600px/200%.

The root cause is one this repo has recorded before: a container query's `em` is the **container's** type (`.spine` inherits 1rem), while the row is set at 0.6875rem. `14em` of container is 20.4em of row — well inside the broken band.

## Solution

- `@container (max-width: 18em)` — 30.5ch × 0.617em + 2.4em gaps + a 4.1em figure = 25.3em of row type = 17.4em of container. The comment in `WeekRow.astro` carries the derivation and the sweep.
- A gate in `tests/training-page.test.ts` holds the **relationship**, read from the shipped sheet: the row's rem size, the arm's `ch` tracks and the gap, plus one figure, must be covered by the stacked arm's threshold. The two measured constants (0.617em per `0`, 4.1em widest figure) are stated as measurements with the re-sweep recipe.

author: xylar
body:
Write every units attribute in the udunits/CF plain form (m s-1, m-2 s-1, N m-2, 1), replacing the three strings udunits cannot parse; drop standard names that are not in the CF standard name table and use the three valid CF names that exist; omit empty units and standard_name attributes; stop writing the non-CF duplicate attributes (Name, name, Description, Units, StdName, ValidMin, ValidMax); add the Conventions global attribute; fix valid_min on 26 signed fields that used numeric_limits::min() and on the Cartesian mesh coordinates; fix the dimension order of the VertFlux fields, which made writing the VertAdv group segfault; and add CF_METADATA_TEST to keep all of this true. cfchecks now reports no errors or warnings on Omega history output.

Fixes #544. Fixes #529.

## Units

All units strings now use the CF plain form already used in `TracerDefs.inc` and `Eos.cpp`: factors separated by spaces with signed integer exponents and no caret, slash or braces (`m s-1`, `m-2 s-1`, `N m-2`, `kg m-2 s-1`, `W m-2`, `1` for dimensionless). The three invalid strings (`N m^{-2}`, `dimensionless`, `tracer units`) are gone; arrays that hold several tracers with different units (`TracersMonthlySurfClimoCell`, `Del2TracersCell`, `VertFlux`, `TracerTend`) now carry no units attribute, as do the debug tracers that had `"none"`. Long names that quoted units as `(m^2)` or `(radians s^-1)` now use the same spelling as the attribute.

**Please review specifically:** `SpecVolDCt` changed from `m3 kg-1 degC-1` to `m3 kg-1 K-1` (its own commit, ff8e664620). A derivative with respect to temperature is per temperature difference, for which the SI unit is the kelvin; the numerical value is unchanged. If the team prefers to keep the derivative in the same spelling as the `degree_C` tracer, that commit can be dropped without affecting anything else.

## Standard names

The CF checker rejects any `standard_name` not in the standard name table. Three had CF equivalents and were replaced (`square_of_brunt_vaisala_frequency_in_sea_water`, `ocean_vertical_tracer_diffusivity`, `ocean_vertical_momentum_diffusivity`). The rest (`sea_water_velocity` for an edge-normal component, `barotropic_*`, `*_tendency`, the specific-volume family, the Richardson numbers, `x`/`y`/`z`) are removed; their meaning stays in `long_name`.

## Attributes and global metadata

`Field::create` now stores only the CF attributes `long_name`, `units`, `standard_name`, `valid_min` and `valid_max` (plus `_FillValue` when data is attached). The capitalized duplicates and both `Name` and `name` are gone (#529); nothing in Omega read them, and the field name is the netCDF variable name itself. `units` and `standard_name` are omitted when empty, since an empty `standard_name` is a CF error. `Field::init` adds `Conventions = "CF-1.8"` to the code metadata; 1.8 is the newest version the current `cfchecker` release validates and Omega uses nothing newer.

## valid_min

Twenty-six fields passed `std::numeric_limits<Real>::min()` (the smallest *positive* double) as `valid_min`, declaring every negative value of surface stress, SSH, geometric height, vorticity, etc. invalid; they now use `lowest()`. `XCell`/`YCell`/`ZCell` and the edge and vertex counterparts had `valid_min = 0`, wrong on a sphere; they now use `-7.0E+6` to mirror the existing maximum.

## VertFlux dimension order

`VertFlux` and `LowOrderVertFlux` are allocated `(NTracers, NCells, NVertLayersP1)` but their Fields declared `(NCells, NVertLayersP1, NTracers)`, so any stream containing the `VertAdv` group segfaulted in `IOStream::writeFieldData`. Found by the new test.

## Testing

New `CF_METADATA_TEST` initializes all modules, checks every field's units form, standard-name form, valid range and absence of the retired attributes, checks `Conventions`, and writes a stream with the State, Tracers, AuxiliaryState, VertAdv, VertMix, Eos, Tendencies and Forcing groups and inspects its attributes with netCDF. Whether a standard name exists in the CF table is left to an external checker. `Field::getAllFieldNames()` was added for the test and documented in the Field developer guide.

- Machine: `chrysalis`
- Compiler: `intel`
- Build type: `Release`

`cfchecks ocn.cfmeta.nc` on the file written by the test: 0 errors, 0 warnings, 5 INFO (fields intentionally without units).

## What

Iteration 64 — new rule HCR088 (TypedClients, Warning).

`AddHttpClient<T>` registers `T` with a factory that injects the configured `HttpClient` into the typed client's constructor. When no constructor parameter accepts `HttpClient`, the registration silently produces a client that never receives it.

Flags `AddHttpClient<T>` and `AddHttpClient<TClient, TImpl>` on `Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection` receivers when the constructed type lacks an `HttpClient` ctor parameter. Skips factory/configure lambdas, abstract types, unresolved symbols, and non-framework lookalikes.

author: frankie567
body:
Add persistent identity sessions for authenticated access through opaque bearer tokens, with issuance, validation, and family revocation backed by abstract storage methods. Tokens are stored as hashes.

Optional refresh tokens rotate on use: refreshing invalidates both previous tokens, preserves an absolute family deadline, and revokes the family when a consumed refresh token is reused. Callers can disable further refresh issuance; revoke accepts either token type. Storage contracts specify atomic replacement and durable family revocation.

Rename AuthenticationSessionService.get_by_token to validate for consistent lifecycle naming. Include Google-style docstrings, focused tests grouped by method, and the RFC 9700 reference skill.

Validation: just lint passed; just test passed (275 tests). Concurrency guarantees remain the storage adapter's responsibility and are not exercised by the simplified test adapter. Access tokens default to 24 hours, refreshable families to 30 days; inactivity expiry is not implemented.

author: muras3
body:
## 何を入れたか

- `Row.recommended` / `Row.equivalent` を追加。下端の昇順で1位（同額タイ含む）を枠に入れ、1位の区間と重なる社を最大2社まで枠に追加する（確定仕様2・3）。3社目以降で重なる社には枠に入れず「同等」の印だけを付ける（確定仕様4）。
- 順位・差額・`cheapest`・`tied` は元から `total.low` で決まっていた（P1-1 のまま、挙動を変えていない）。

## 「重なる」の定義

候補行が1位の区間 `[low, high ?? +Infinity]` と重なるかを、**候補行自身の下端 `low` だけ**で判定する（候補行の `high` は一切見ない — 確定仕様6「下端のみで比較する」）。

## `high === null`（上限不明）の扱い（コーディネーター判断1、2026-09-11）

+Infinity として扱う。上限不明は「上端が無い」のではなく「差が不確かさに埋もれている最も強い状態」で、これを有限に丸めたり判定から除いたりすると不確かさを隠すことになる。「枠が全社を飲み込む」懸念は、枠に最大2社という上限があるので成立しない。

## `rankStable` の新定義（コーディネーター判断2、2026-09-11）

最初の実装は「基準の枠のうち1社でも両端の枠に残れば安定」だったが、枠は最大3社なので5社中3社が枠に入る局面でこれがほぼ自明に成立し、判定として機能しなかった — 実測で既定カート・7カ国すべて `rankStable=true` になる欠陥として発見した。

新しい定義: **おすすめ枠の集合が ×⅓・×3 の両端で基準と完全に一致するかどうか**（`Set` で比較するので枠の中の順序は見ない。顔ぶれが1社でも変われば `false`）。`weightSensitivity.decisive` も同じ規則に変えた。

## US でおすすめ枠に Neokyo が入っていなかった件

バグではない。Neokyo は米国宛に日本郵便を売っておらず（自社の見積画面が3方式すべてに "Not available or suspended in your country."）、米国では `comparable: false`。おすすめ枠の判定は比較可能な行だけが対象なので、これは既存仕様どおり（`docs/ROADMAP.md` の `WEIGHT_SHIFT_COUNTRY` の説明と同じ理由）。

## 実カート7カ国の測定（5点・¥3,000・600g・ヤフオク）

| 国 | おすすめ枠 | 同等 | rankStable |
|---|---|---|---|
| US | FROM JAPAN, ZenMarket, Buyee(consolidated) | Jauce, Buyee(default) | true |
| GB | Neokyo（単独） | — | false |
| DE | Neokyo（単独） | — | false |
| FR | Neokyo（単独） | — | false |
| AU | Neokyo（単独） | — | true |
| CA | Neokyo（単独） | — | false |
| SG | Neokyo（単独） | — | true |

US は比較可能な5社全員がおすすめ枠か同等に入っており（1位が上限不明のため +Infinity 扱いで全社重なる）、`docs/ROADMAP.md` に追記した「全社が重なったときの表示」の実例になる。`rankStable` の新旧比較: 新しい値は US/AU/SG=true・GB/DE/FR/CA=false で、**P1-1 時点の値と一致**した（`measured.ts` の `RANK_STABILITY` は変更不要、`render-docs.py --check` も通過）。

## e2e への影響（落ちたので直した。緩めていない）

`rankStabilityNote` の文言変更（「stays cheapest」→「stays in the recommended range」）と、`rankStable`/`decisive` の判定基準変更で、e2e の2ケースが実際に挙動を変えた:
- test17（DE、既定2点+PLUSH）: 既定2点の時点で枠が拮抗しており、以前は「安定」だったが新定義では既に不安定（枠の顔ぶれが動く）。実測して正しい値に更新した。PLUSH追加で個別品が decisive になる、という後半の主張は変わらない。
- test18（単一品、US）: FROM JAPAN が全域で1位のまま変わらないが、おすすめ枠の顔ぶれ（Jauce↔Buyee）は動くため、新定義では正しく不安定・nag する。タイトルも実態に合わせて書き直した。

## 変更していないもの

UI（RankBoard/CostTable/DiffBar/RowBreakdown）は変更していない（P1-3の範囲）。`recommended`/`equivalent` は型に追加しただけで、既存の `cheapest`/`tied` を使う画面の見た目は変わらない。

## テスト・検証

- `npm test`（vitest）: 679 tests, 全件 green
- `npm run lint` / `npx tsc --noEmit`: クリーン
- `npx playwright test`（desktop + mobile）: 213 passed, 11 skipped（既存の skip）
- `python3 master/validate.py` / `python3 master/render-docs.py --check`: OK
- `docs/ROADMAP.md` の P1 に「全社が重なったときの表示」（オーナー判断 2026-09-11）と、今回のコーディネーター判断1・2を理由つきで追記

author: sunilkumar-nvidia
body:
## Summary

This is PR3 of the pluggable Machine Validation framework described in [the design PR](https://github.com/NVIDIA/infra-controller/pull/5092).

PR1 (#5455) introduced the safe OCI plugin-runner and contract foundation. PR2 (#5576) added the plugin control plane. This PR connects approved plugin definitions to Scout's existing Machine Validation execution lifecycle.

## What is included

- Selects the already-approved, enabled plugin tests as part of normal Machine Validation selection.
- Executes plugin-backed tests sequentially through the safe OCI runner.
- Writes the versioned `input.json` contract with run, run-item, attempt, machine, context, deadline, plugin, and non-secret parameters.
- Maps plugin `pass`, `fail`, and `error` results into existing Machine Validation results and attempt status.
- Uses the NICo registry credential flow for plugin pulls; plugin execution does not depend on the legacy `container_auth` external configuration.
- Rejects an unapproved full-host plugin again at execution time.
- Records the selected plugin definition and full-host approval on the run item for auditability.
- Fails a plugin attempt when an image pull fails and retains bounded diagnostics when a plugin exits unsuccessfully.

## Example flow

1. A site admin creates, verifies, approves as needed, and enables a digest-pinned GPU validation plugin through the PR2 control plane.
2. A matching Discovery run selects that enabled plugin alongside any legacy tests.
3. Scout materializes the run item, pulls the configured image using the stored registry credential, and starts the configured entrypoint.
4. The plugin reads `/opt/forge/mv/input/input.json` and writes `/opt/forge/mvoutput/result.json`.
5. Scout validates the result contract and records the result through the existing Machine Validation run and attempt lifecycle.

## Compatibility

- Existing Machine Validation definitions and legacy execution are unchanged.
- A test without a plugin continues through the existing command/container path, including legacy `container_auth` setup.
- Only plugin-backed tests use the OCI runner and plugin credential flow.
- Execution remains sequential; this PR does not enable parallel execution.

## Bigger picture

1. PR1 (#5455): Safe OCI runner and plugin-contract foundation. Merged.
2. PR2 (#5576): Plugin definitions, site policy, verification/enablement, registry credentials, and full-host approval. Merged.
3. PR3 — this PR: Scout execution, plugin input/output contract, result mapping, and run-plan snapshotting.
4. Follow-up work: streamed execution logs and the remaining observability and operational features from the design.

## Related issues

- https://github.com/NVIDIA/infra-controller/pull/5092
- https://github.com/NVIDIA/infra-controller/issues/3655
- https://github.com/NVIDIA/infra-controller/issues/2962
- https://github.com/NVIDIA/infra-controller/issues/5577

- [ ] Change - Changes in existing functionality
- [ ] Fix - Bug fixes
- [ ] Remove - Removed features or deprecated functionality
- [ ] Internal - Internal changes (refactoring, tests, docs, etc.)

## Breaking Changes

None.
