author: im10furry
body:
### Description

`ui.spec.ts > suite report navigation` is flaky. On `windows-latest` it failed in [run 34358157064](https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/actions/runs/34358157064/job/102488118436), and each retry failed at a *different* step: the report pane kept the previous suite after a row click, then an "Expand" click did nothing, then a "Collapse" click did nothing.

**Root cause.** The explorer renders its rows in a `RecycleScroller` (`packages/ui/client/components/explorer/Explorer.vue:264`). The `child failure suite` / `nested failure suite` rows sit at or just below the bottom of the test viewport, so `locator.click()` first has to scroll them into view. Playwright verifies the element under the cursor and *then* dispatches a real mouse event at those coordinates - and the virtual list recycles rows in between, so the click is delivered to whichever row moved into those coordinates.

I instrumented a capture-phase `click` listener and looped the interactions from the test (viewport from the Playwright config, 800x1300):

```
PROBE-FAIL round 1 "child failure suite": clicks=[{"row":"successful suite","tag":"SPAN","cls":""}] report=" All tests passed in this suite"
PROBE-FAIL round 3: expand had no effect, clicks=[{"row":"successful suite","button":"Collapse successful suite"}] (child not visible)
```

The first line is the CI failure verbatim: the click aimed at `child failure suite` was received by `successful suite`, so the report stayed on the previous suite (`Expected substring: "failing child"` / `Received string: " All tests passed in this suite"`). The second line shows the same thing happening to the expand/collapse buttons - the click meant for `Expand successful suite` hit the `Collapse successful suite` button that was rendered before the state flipped, because the whole row moved.

### Fix

- Selecting an item now uses the existing `openExplorerItem()` helper (scroll into view, then dispatch the click **on the located element**), which the trace tests already use. I added a comment there explaining that dispatching is deliberate, since `locator.click()` looks like the obvious choice.
- Toggling gets the equivalent `toggleExplorerItem(page, name, 'expand' | 'collapse')`.

Neither can be redirected to a neighbouring row, because no coordinates are involved.

### Verification

This test is intermittent rather than reliably broken, so the probe above is the actual evidence; these numbers only confirm it is reproducible. `--workers=1 --retries=0`, both the `ui` and the `html report` variant of `suite report navigation`:

| version | command | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `main` | `--repeat-each=25` | 3 failed / 50 runs |
| `main` | `--repeat-each=60` | 1 failed / 120 runs |
| `main` | `--repeat-each=30` | 0 failed / 60 runs (clean sample) |
| this branch | `--repeat-each=30` | 0 failed / 60 runs |

### Scope

I left the other `getExplorerItem(...).click()` call sites alone (`testError`, `testVisualRegression`, `add`, `watch-updates.spec.ts`). They use the same pattern and are probably worth converting too, but this PR only changes the test whose failure I could reproduce and verify - happy to extend it if you prefer.

author: addycooks
body:
## Description
Closes a critical security vulnerability where `nanocoder daemon start` could execute untrusted code without user confirmation. The daemon fast path went straight to `runDaemonCli` → `startDaemon` → `bootSkillPipeline` without checking directory trust, loading every `.nanocoder/agents|commands|tools/*.md` and `skills/<name>/skill.yaml` unconditionally.

**Security Impact:**
1. **Unattended code execution**: The daemon loads skills in headless mode with NO confirmation prompts for `execute_bash`, `write_file`, `string_replace`, `diff_edit`, and MCP tools
2. **Attack vector**: A malicious repo with `.nanocoder/skills/evil/skill.yaml` containing a `file.changed` subscription could execute arbitrary commands when ANY file is touched
3. **Bypass of all safeguards**: Headless mode is strictly more permissive than auto-accept - even bash execution runs without prompts

**Fix:** `daemon start` now checks `preferences.trustedDirectories` before spawning the daemon process and refuses with exit code 1 if the directory isn't trusted. The trust-check logic was refactored into a shared `ensureDirectoryTrust()` helper in `@/config/preferences` (eliminating code duplication from plain/shell.ts). Users must either:
- Run `nanocoder` interactively once to accept the trust disclaimer, OR
- Pass `--trust-directory` flag (one-shot bypass), OR
- Set `NANOCODER_TRUST_DIRECTORY=1` (persists trust)

## Type of Change
- [x] Bug fix (security vulnerability)
- [ ] New feature
- [x] Breaking change (security-critical fix - previously unprotected daemon now requires trust)
- [ ] Documentation update

## Changeset
- [x] Added a changeset (`pnpm changeset`) describing this change for the changelog

## Testing

### Automated Tests
- [x] New features include passing tests in `.spec.ts/tsx` files
- [x] All existing tests pass (`pnpm test:all` completes successfully)
- [x] Tests cover both success and error scenarios

### Manual Testing

author: egurucharri
body:
Cierra #147. Rebasado sobre `main` y **verificado con el motor del proyecto (Godot 4.7-stable)**.

## El problema

Cada sistema sorteaba por su cuenta: los compañeros con `randi()` global, el combate con un `randomize()` en `_ready`, el sueño con un hash del día. Todo funciona hasta que algo sale raro: un informe que dice «me salió mal el careo» no es reproducible si la tirada salió del reloj.

## Qué hace

No añade azar: le pone una raíz. Una partida tiene **una semilla** y todo lo jugable se deriva de ella por dominio, así que la misma semilla con las mismas acciones da la misma partida, y **recargar no vuelve a tirar los dados** — que es lo que permitía repetir un turno del combate hasta que saliera bien.

- **`guion/azar.gd`** (nuevo): `raiz_nueva()`, `derivar(raiz, dominio, indices)` y `derivar_texto(...)` como funciones puras. Mezcla FNV-1a a mano y no `hash()`, que es un detalle del motor y puede cambiar al actualizarlo — una semilla que cambia al actualizar Godot no es una semilla. Los dominios son una lista cerrada (`Azar.DOMINIOS`).
- **`Partida`** guarda `semilla`. Una partida anterior a este cambio recibe una al cargarse y desde ahí ya es reproducible.
- **`Jornada`** lleva `raiz` y `vuelta`. La plantilla de compañeros se **deriva** en vez de sortearse: cambia cuando te reasignan y solo entonces. `reiniciar_vuelta` conserva la raíz y avanza la vuelta. Una jornada guardada antigua hereda la raíz de su partida pero **conserva su plantilla**: a quien va por el día quince no se le vacía la oficina porque haya actualizado.
- **`Sueno`** entra la semilla en `semilla()` y `noche()`, para que la noche sea de su partida y no del calendario.
- **Combate**: la Ventanilla siembra sus tiradas desde semilla + vuelta + día. El careo acepta `semilla_tiradas`; hoy la escena solo la abre la herramienta de capturas, así que cae al reloj cuando vale 0.
- **`Azar.manifiesto()` / `manifiesto_en_texto()`**: semilla, vuelta, día, versión de guardado y huella de los catálogos, para pegar en un informe de bug. **No se enseña al jugador** — va en las herramientas de depuración (#116).

Cada dominio deriva por su lado a propósito: que el sueño de la noche 3 no cambie porque el combate haya tirado una vez más.

## Un bug real que encontró la prueba

Las semillas de 63 bits **no sobreviven al guardado**: JSON no tiene enteros, un entero así vuelve redondeado y la partida recargada sorteaba otra cosa — recargar te cambiaba media oficina. Todo lo que se persiste pasa ahora por `derivar_guardable()`, a 32 bits, y hay una prueba de ida y vuelta por JSON de verdad (no por copia del diccionario, que es donde el fallo se escondía).

## La guarda

La presentación —el tono de una pisada, hacia dónde mira el gato, el grano de una textura— sigue con azar global porque no decide nada. Para que eso no se deshaga solo, la suite recorre `guion/*.gd` y falla si aparece un `randi()`/`randf()`/`randomize()` suelto fuera de esa lista corta.

## Criterios de aceptación del issue

- [x] Dos partidas con la misma semilla y las mismas acciones producen el mismo estado
- [x] Guardar, recargar y continuar no cambia ninguna decisión determinista
- [x] Dos semillas distintas producen variaciones, sin tocar reglas ni dificultad
- [x] El sueño y los compañeros se reproducen individualmente en tests
- [x] Un informe de bug puede incluir semilla, día, vuelta y versión de datos
- [x] Las partidas antiguas siguen cargando
- [x] No se añade telemetría ni se expone la semilla al jugador

El clima (#143) todavía no existe; su dominio queda declarado para cuando llegue.

## Gates

Con Godot **4.7-stable**, el que fija `.godot-version`:

```
$ python3 scripts/verificar_godot.py
Godot: importación / suite / recorrido / arranque
454 pasadas, 0 fallos
34 pasadas, 0 fallos
$ gdlint godot && gdformat --check godot
Success: no problems found
43 files would be left unchanged
```

63 aserciones nuevas, en `pruebas/pruebas_semilla.gd` — siguiendo el troceado de la suite que trajo #144, con `comprobar` como `Callable`. `minimo.txt` sube de 376 a 450.

author: authen27
body:
## v10.28.0 — forms get a page of their own

The add and edit forms that opened as a sheet over the screen are now dedicated, focused full-screen pages.
**No money, data or permission rule changes**: the fields, validation and saves are the same form components;
only their container and the way you reach them changed.

### Scope (as requested)
| Form | Routes |
|---|---|
| Transaction | `/transactions/new` · `/transactions/:id/edit` |
| Split | `/splits/new` · `/splits/:txnId/edit` |
| Debt | `/debts/new` · `/debts/:id/edit` |
| Budget | `/budgets/new` · `/budgets/:id/edit` |
| Account | `/accounts/new` · `/accounts/:id/edit` |
| Asset | `/networth/assets/new` · `/networth/assets/:id/edit` |
| Reconcile Account | `/accounts/:id/reconcile` |

The three decisions behind this:
- **Add and Edit** both became pages.
- **After save or cancel, you go back to where you came from**, via history back. A form reached directly falls back to its list screen, and "Save & add another" stays on the form.
- **Focused full-screen layout:** no banner, section tabs, tab bar or FAB; just Close, the title, the form and a pinned Save bar.

### How
- **`lib/formRoutes.ts`** owns every form path. App.tsx renders form routes outside `<Layout>`, like onboarding.
- **`pages/FormPages.tsx`** resolves each route:
  - an edit route reads its entity **once** when the page opens, so a sync refresh cannot wipe what was typed;
  - an unknown id redirects to the list;
  - Add/Edit Budget keeps the Budgets screen's `manage_budgets` gate.
- **`components/ui/FormPage.tsx`** replaces `HalfSheet` for these seven forms and takes the same props.
  - It renders a `main` landmark named by the title, with the title as the `h1`.
  - Escape closes the form unless a sheet opened from it is showing (the delete-account guard); that sheet keeps the key.
- **Store:** the `openAdd*` / `openEdit*` actions keep their names and signatures but now navigate.
  - All ~80 callers are unchanged: FAB, N/B/D/A shortcuts, command palette, Ask Vyact and notification seeds.
  - `lib/appNavigation.ts` binds the router for the store, and a seed travels as router state.
  - The six `{entity}ModalOpen` / `editing{Entity}` / `close{Entity}Modal` slots and `seedTxn` are removed; nothing else read them.
- **`components/layout/HistoryRestoration.tsx`** replaces `ScrollToTop`.
  - Moving forward to a new path still starts at the top.
  - **Back** restores scroll position and focus on the opener, which a modal used to give for free.
- **Reconcile:**
  - The account edit page and the Accounts list open the reconcile page rather than a nested sheet.
  - "Let me find what's missing" *replaces* the reconcile page, so Back from those transactions skips the page.
- **Still sheets (out of scope):** recurring schedule, household, notifications, filters, the delete-account guard.
- **CLAUDE.md:** the binding "Global modals via store slots" convention is replaced by "Entity forms are routed pages".

### Validation
- **Full gate** `node scripts/automation-run.mjs`: **13/13 steps, 238/238 scenarios** (ESLint, app + e2e type-check, unit tests, build, admin, catalog reconciler, migrations, version drift).
- **Unit inventory:** **1,058 passing cases in 67 files, zero skipped**. That includes 3 new `formRoutes` cases: every path round-trips, screens and non-form sub-paths are not form routes, and a reserved-character id stays in one segment.
- **Browser (Chromium, local-only test build)** — a temporary probe spec, removed before commit:
  - **All 7 forms are pages:** each has its `main` landmark and `h1`; no banner or section tabs; Close and the Save bar are in view; no horizontal scroll at 1280 and 390.
  - **Close and Escape** return to the opener with focus on it (`+ Add Budget`; `N` → Escape).
  - **Direct links:** a directly loaded `/debts/new` closes to `/debts`; unknown edit ids redirect to the list.
  - **Scroll:** a scrolled Dashboard keeps its scroll position across a form.
  - **Ask Vyact seed** pre-fills Add Income. "Save & add another" stays on `/transactions/new` and saves the row.
  - **Accounts:**
    - Cash reconcile → Confirm → back on Accounts with the toast.
    - Bank edit → Reconcile → Not now → back on the edit page.
    - Escape in the delete-account sheet closes only the sheet.
- **Affected e2e specs** (14 files that open these forms), run against this build: **30 passed, 19 failed, 2 skipped**.
  - The 19 failures are all in TD-29 files: debts-payment, networth-assets, privacy, transactions-create and transactions-edit-delete.
  - **The same five files at their origin/main versions, against a build of origin/main (f060cce), fail the identical 19 tests, compared by test ID.** No new failures.
  - Causes include stale seed text matches, the "All details" POM path, the old two-account investment destination (TD-36) and loan-payment toast copy.
  - These pass: budget-editor, category-picker, dialog-correction, finance-guidance, help-guide, keyboard-accessibility, permissions-local, budgets and networth-impact.
- **Help guide:** HELP-FC-001 recaptured the five form screenshots from the new pages at a 600px column. For the capture only, the sticky Save bar and the viewport min-height are neutralised so each image shows the whole form. Reviewed visually.
- Lane A remains parked under TD-29.

body:
I have investigated and successfully resolved the issue where a raw API test of the WMS Scanner endpoint in the browser was failing with ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED on port 5000.

Root Cause
Wrong Port Configuration: Despite the documentation and earlier configurations pointing to 5000, the backend was defaulting to port 3000. Therefore, trying to hit port 5000 naturally resulted in an ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED since the Node process was not listening there.
Method Not Allowed: A "raw API test in the browser" performs an HTTP GET request. The /api/drivers/scan-inventory route was defined exclusively as router.post(). Thus, even on the right port, it would have returned a 404 Not Found to a browser.
Minimal Fix Applied
Updated Port Binding:
Edited 

server.js
 to set the fallback port to 5000.
Updated the PORT variable in the backend 

\.env
 to 5000 to align the local dev environment with documentation.
Updated Route Methods:
Modified the mock scanning endpoint in 

driverRoutes.js
 from router.post to router.all.
It now gracefully extracts barcode parameters from either req.body or req.query, meaning testers can now hit http://localhost:5000/api/drivers/scan-inventory?barcode=123 right from their browser address bar without errors.

author: jkitchin
body:
## Why

The two-clock discipline of `examples/29_model_updating.ipynb` — monitor with parameters frozen, re-estimate only as a deliberate campaign — is something a *person* applies. A model kept current against a running plant has nobody to apply it, and the discipline does not survive being automated naively.

Two gaps show up the moment you try:

- **The verdict is advisory.** `MonitorResult.diagnose()` already decides whether a sensor or the model is at fault, but nothing in `src/` consumes the answer — it is a report to a human. Left that way, a scheduled re-estimation happily runs on a day whose honest verdict was "go calibrate the dp meter".
- **The update has no memory.** `reconcile_multi` pools a window, which is a *rectangular* filter: hard in/out edges, a ten-day-old period weighted like this morning's, recomputed from scratch each time. Run it on a schedule and the estimate lurches as periods fall off the back.

This adds `difflow.reconciliation.tracking`, which writes the discipline as an update law.

## What changed

Four public, stateless steps plus an offline driver. **No new estimator** — one period's reconciliation already returns both halves of a Kalman measurement update (the estimate, and its block of `reconciled_covariance`), so all the physics stays inside `reconcile()`.

| | |
|---|---|
| `update_gate` | reads a `MonitorDiagnosis`, permits an update only on `model drift` |
| `time_update` | advances the random walk `θ⁺ = θ + w`, `cov(w) = Q·Δt` |
| `parameter_measurement` | one period's estimate of the parameters, with covariance |
| `measurement_update` | combines prior and measurement, full covariance, Joseph form |
| `track_parameters` | drives all four over a campaign |

```python
run = track_parameters(
    F, daily_measurements, sigma, names=layout.names,
    state=TrackerState.initial(["eta"], [1.0], std=[0.02]),
    drift_std=drift_std_from_time_constant(0.05, 30.0),   # 5% over a month
)
run.final.as_params()      # {'eta': 0.71} -- the shape a Block takes as theta
```

`drift_std` is the same knob as `process_std` in `difflow.mhe`, with the same warning (too large and the parameter absorbs sensor noise; too small and a real drift is rejected) and the same refusal to default it. `drift_std_from_time_constant(spread, tau)` lets you state it as "5% over a month" rather than as a rate.

## Does it work — on the notebook's own gas network

Section 7 of `examples/29_model_updating.ipynb` runs the loop over both campaigns the notebook already builds: a pipe fouling from η = 1.00 to 1.30 over 45 days, and a **clean** pipe whose `p2` meter picks up a 6σ bias on day 30.

|  | fouling campaign | meter-bias campaign |
|---|---|---|
| **gated** (default policy) | 1.257 (true 1.300) — lags | **1.000 — correct, never moved** |
| **gate wired open** | 1.288 (true 1.300) — tracks | **1.165 — fouling invented** |

Opening the gate buys about **0.03 in η** where the model really had drifted, and costs a confident **16% fouling claim on a pipe that is clean**. The gated loop makes zero updates on the meter-bias campaign: every day reads `consistent` or `instrument fault`, and neither entitles the model to move. What it reports instead is a widening error bar and a named suspect to go calibrate.

The χ² panel shows the loop closing — frozen at η = 1 the same data rejects for the whole back half of the campaign; tracked, it drops back under the threshold after each update. The section also says what a statistic that *failed* to come down would mean.

The lag is drawn rather than argued: fouling starts on day 12, the gate does not open until day 33, and the error bar visibly widens while the parameter is held.

## Design decisions worth a reviewer's attention

- **The verdict gates, it does not advise.** No filter gain prevents the failure above — a slow filter just reaches the wrong answer gracefully, and the χ² statistic *falls* while it happens, so the twin looks healthier as it gets wronger.
- **The gate is a statistical rule, not a guarantee** — and writing section 7 proved it. At the default window a couple of days early in the meter bias read as diffuse, slip through as `model drift`, and drag η to 1.13 before the rule settles. `diagnose()` already takes `rejection_threshold` and `concentration_threshold` for exactly this, but `track_parameters` forwarded only `window`, so the tunable rule was unreachable from the loop. **Both are forwarded now**, and the notebook tunes them rather than widening `allow`, which would remove the rule instead of sharpening it. Two tests cover the pass-through.
- **Holding on `consistent` is the deadband**, making the loop event-triggered. A parameter re-estimated every period tracks that period's noise and the twin stops being a model.
- **The time update runs on held periods too.** Holding is not knowing: a held parameter widens its error bar at the drift rate, so the next permitted update steps further. `max_std` caps it.
- **Full covariance, Joseph form.** Correlated parameters have a *difference* variance a diagonal gets wrong by a factor of a few (the warning CLAUDE.md already gives for `ScenarioSet.from_covariance`). `(I-K)P` loses symmetry over a long run and a twin is a long run — a 300-step test asserts symmetry and PSD to 1e-18.
- **The prior stays outside `reconcile`.** `parameter_measurement` leaves the parameters at `sigma = inf` (free, not regularised). Smuggling the prior in through `sigma` would make it diagonal and would inflate the objective that is supposed to test data against *model*. Cost: each period must identify the parameter alone, else `ReconciliationStructureError` — loud, not a NaN — and the docs point at `reconcile_multi` for pooling.
- **A weakly informative period needs no special case:** large `R`, zero gain, estimate does not move.

## Out of scope, and said so

This filters *parameters*, not model **form**. Under structural mismatch the parameter converges to something that is not the physical quantity and shifts with operating point, so the twin's gradients are wrong even where its values match — fatal for a differentiable flowsheet, where everything downstream is a derivative. The symptom is `run.monitor.statistic` never coming back down after an update; the answer is `difflow.planning.modifiers`, not a faster filter. The module docstring, the docs and the notebook all say this.

## One bug found in self-review

A caller-supplied `unmeasured_scale` is plant-length, but the augmented problem is `n + p` — it is now extended rather than passed through at the wrong length. `dg.reconcile_network` fills that in from the layout, so this would have hit the gas path immediately (and did, in section 7). Covered by `test_a_caller_supplied_scale_describes_the_plant_block_only`.

## Testing

- `tests/test_tracking.py` — 49 tests, all passing. The load-bearing ones are linear, where a Kalman update is the exact two-Gaussian combination and can be checked against the closed form rather than a tolerance.
- **Full suite: 3137 passed, 42 skipped, exit 0** (before the notebook commit; `tests/test_tracking.py`, `test_reconciliation.py`, `test_context.py`, `test_doclinks.py` re-run green after it).
- `examples/29_model_updating.ipynb` executes end-to-end under nbconvert with no errors; every number in the section's prose is quoted from the committed cell output.

## Docs

New `## Tracking a drifting parameter` section in `docs/data-reconciliation.md`, continuing directly from the two-clock material, plus section 7 of the notebook. Invariants also recorded in CLAUDE.md, and `src/difflow/gui/static/docs-index.json` rebuilt (`test_context.py` asserts its freshness).

author: livinglikekrillin
body:
저장소 밖에 이 프로젝트의 그림 아홉이 **더 넓은 폭**으로 그려져 있었고 저장소에는 없었다. 그중 **여섯**을 들인다.

## 복사가 아니다

README 열이 **837**, `docs/*.md` 가 **1012** 라 1180 을 그대로 넣으면 글자가 바닥(9.5px) 밑으로 내려간다. **폭을 인자로 받는 생성기**(`tools/diagram-gen/`)로 다시 그렸다 — 넓은 판이 다시 필요하면 같은 파일에서 뽑으면 되고, 손으로 두 벌 두면 어느 날 한쪽만 고쳐진다.

## 옮기기 전에 주장을 코드에 댔다

오늘 `change-plan.svg` 가 사실관계가 틀린 채로 공개 문서에 걸려 있던 것을 봤기 때문이다. **여섯 중 둘이 틀렸다.**

| 그림 | 판정 |
|---|---|
| `gate` | ✅ `RevisionValidator` 가 `gate.GateRunner` 를 실제로 부른다. 검사 8 + 음성 |
| `startup` | ✅ `Main.kt` 의 문장과 **글자까지 같았다** |
| `four-axes` | ✅ `BindingService` 가 `SUPERSEDED` 재활성화를 든다 |
| `task-states` | ✅ 상태 열 열 개와 `Resolution` 셋이 계약과 일치 |
| **`three-layers`** | ⚠️ **기체를 셋만 그렸다** — Orbit 이 생기기 전 판. 넷으로 고쳤고, Orbit 은 로봇이 아니라 **플릿 관리자**라고 적었다 |
| **`capability-projection`** | ⚠️ **「나머지 넷」이라 적었는데 다섯이다.** 프로파일 최상위 **열셋**, `Capability` **여덟** → 남는 것 **다섯**. 빠진 것은 `derived_from` 이고 **스키마 첫 커밋부터 있었다** |

## 자리

| 그림 | 간 곳 | 주장 |
|---|---|---|
| `three-layers` | `docs/architecture.md` §0 | 경계는 두 곳뿐이다 |
| `four-axes` | `docs/commissioning.md` | 되돌릴 수 없는 축은 하나뿐이다 |
| `gate` | `docs/contract.md` | 구현은 하나이고 호출 지점이 둘이다 |
| `capability-projection` | `docs/contract.md` | 능력만 나가고 설정은 남는다 |
| `task-states` | `docs/architecture.md` | 종착은 래치된다 |
| `startup` | `mimic/README.md` | 부분 기동은 없다 |

**README 히어로는 `seam.svg` 가 그대로 지킨다.** README 첫 문단이 그 그림의 주장을 그대로 풀어 쓰고 있어 글과 그림이 붙어 있다. `three-layers` 와는 **다른 질문에 답한다** — 하나는 *무엇이 붙는가*, 하나는 *왜 계약 하나로 붙는가*.

★그러면서 `architecture.md` 안의 낱말 충돌을 끊었다. 새 §0 이 「경계 셋」을, §1 이 「층 넷」을 말한다 — 같은 낱말로 다른 것을 센다. 한 줄로 갈랐다: **§0 은 누가 무엇을 구현하는가(배치), §1 은 어휘가 어디서 갈리는가(ADR 36).**

## 내가 낸 결함 — 검증기가 못 잡는 것

`task-states` 를 그리면서 **부제가 설명하는 노란 선을 안 그렸고**, `cross` 배열의 라벨 넷을 **정의만 하고 안 그렸다.** 선이 무엇이었는지가 그림의 절반인데 없었다. 둘 다 **렌더를 눈으로 보고서야** 잡혔다 — 생성기 README 에 그 사실을 적었다.

검증기가 잡은 것은 셋이다: 칩 폭을 `label.length * 10.5` 로 어림해 옆 지대를 침범한 것 둘, 라벨 위로 화살표가 지나간 것 하나.

## 남은 셋

`disconnect-buffer` · `direction-rule` · `injection-point` — 좁은 주제라 해당 문서가 생길 때 같이 간다.

## 검사

`:gate:test` **256 개 초록**.

body:
## Done

Adds a Relay source and a local store for saved views to `@canonical/dataviews-core`.

**`createRelaySource`** runs the collection's queries over a forward-paginating Relay connection.
- It talks to Relay through a structural environment (`retain`, `lookup`, `subscribe`, `execute`). Relay's own `Environment` satisfies it, so nothing imports `relay-runtime` at runtime. It is typed by the compiled query type.
- Relay's store stays the only cache. Each request retains its operation, delivers a stored page at once, fetches it, and follows later store changes. Releasing cancels the fetch, stops following and releases the retention.
- Capabilities are declared by the application, never inferred.
- Pages go forward from each page's end cursor, kept per query and page size for the 32 most recently used queries. A page with no known cursor is refused, not guessed.
- A query reading through `@connection` is refused, since Relay merges those pages into one list.
- A null total stays unknown, never zero. A page missing a record, edge or field fails instead of arriving shorter.

**`createIndexedDBViewStore`**, imported only from `@canonical/dataviews-core/views`, keeps saved views in the browser.
- The application passes `indexedDB`, a database name, the collection and an account partition (`string | null`); partitions never see each other.
- `update` and `remove` succeed only at the revision last read; otherwise they return a conflict, so two tabs never silently overwrite each other. `create` takes a caller-minted id, so a retry finds the view rather than duplicating it.
- Pins and arrangements are preferences stored one record per key, so different keys written from two tabs are both kept.
- Unknown-version or malformed records are reported unreadable and never overwritten.
- Blocked, full or missing storage rejects with the platform error; nothing falls back to memory.
- Other tabs hear real writes through a `BroadcastChannel`; a throwing listener cannot fail a committed write.

No REST store ships; the README shows an application's own.

**Also:** `encodeQuery` accepts `window: null` to write a query alone, as a saved view stores it. The provider no longer builds a row model for a completion that cannot publish; a followed store change used to build one and drop it.

**Test-only devDependencies, pinned exactly:** `relay-runtime` 21.0.1 and `@types/relay-runtime` 20.1.1 (the versions the repo already resolves for the Relay Storybook addon), and `fake-indexeddb` 6.2.5.

Merge order: #1232 must land first — this is based on it, so the diff here is only this change.

## QA

- `bun run check` green at the root (68 projects).
- `@canonical/dataviews-core`: 654 tests at 100% branch/function/line/statement coverage; build emits both entry points.
- `@canonical/dataviews-react`: unchanged, 178 tests pass.
- The Relay tests run the real `relay-runtime` store and executor against a hand-answered network; a type test proves Relay's `Environment` fits the structural surface.
- The view store tests run on `fake-indexeddb`: conflicts, retries, partitions, version refusal, blocked upgrades, cross-tab notification.

- [x] PR title follows the Conventional Commits format.
- [x] The code follows the appropriate code standards.
- [x] The package defines `check`, `check:fix`, `test`, `build`, `build:all`.

author: automatosai
body:
## Summary

Production runs several uvicorn workers; one holds the scheduler lock and hosts APScheduler. A scheduled task created / paused / resumed / cancelled, or a heartbeat toggled or re-configured, is written by whichever worker served the request and only touches **that** worker's (absent) scheduler — so the leader learned of the change at its next restart. The calendar's own "Schedule for later" and "Pause routine" actions (#712/#713) hit this on every request that didn't land on the leader.

- **`services/schedule_reconcile.py`** — an interval job on the leader (every 60 s, and once at boot) that diffs the DB against the registered jobs for both sources.
- **`ScheduledTaskService.reconcile_with_scheduler`** — active rows without a `scheduled_task_<id>` job are registered; jobs whose row is no longer active are removed; a present row is left alone (re-adding a cron job would reset its next fire time). The non-leader register path now logs that the tick will pick the task up, instead of "on restart".
- **`HeartbeatService.reconcile_agent_heartbeats`** — enabled blocks get a job, disabled ones lose theirs, a changed block is re-added. A per-agent config signature means an unchanged job is never churned.
- **`main.py`** — started right after the boot load of scheduled tasks.

### Feed alignment (the WATCHTOWER-style "hourly routine that never fires")

`ActivityService._heartbeat_items` treated a heartbeat block as a routine unless `enabled` was literally `False`; the scheduler only fires blocks whose `enabled` is truthy. A block without the flag showed hourly on the calendar and never ran. The feed now uses the scheduler's rule.

## Test plan

- [ ] `tests/test_schedule_reconcile.py` — fake scheduler/session coverage: adds missing, removes stale, leaves present, no-op second pass, skipped off the leader, non-leader wording, heartbeat add/change/remove, boot-loader signatures, tick composition + session close, boot order guard.
- [ ] `tests/test_schedule_endpoint.py` — helper now builds enabled blocks; new test: block without the flag (or `null`) is excluded.
- [ ] CI orchestrator lanes green.

## Review fixes (second commit)

- **Tick job carries no scheduler argument** — job stores pickle job args and a scheduler instance refuses to be serialized; under RedisJobStore the tick would have died at registration. The job resolves the live scheduler at call time. Prod logs show `[Scheduler] Using memory job store` (the Redis path never engages: `RedisJobStore(url=…)` is not a valid kwarg — flagged, not fixed here), so this was latent.
- **One-shot misfire grace** — APScheduler's default grace is 1 s, so a one-shot registered late was dropped as "missed" and would have been re-added and missed again every tick. One-shots register with a 3-minute grace; older ones are left alone (the calendar shows them as missed).
- **No double firing** — `execute_task` claims the row with `SELECT … FOR UPDATE`, so a one-shot re-registered while its completion commit is in flight waits and then finds the row inactive.
- `unschedule_heartbeat` forgets the config signature.

  * Added recovery for missing, changed, stale, or disabled scheduled jobs across scheduler workers.
  * Added handling for overdue one-time schedules to prevent unintended duplicate execution.

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Heartbeats without an explicitly enabled configuration are no longer scheduled.
  * Improved protection against concurrent duplicate task execution.
  * Reconciliation failures no longer stop recurring scheduler activity.

author: brightears
body:
Concurrent DJ image requests could pass the same credit check and incur provider usage before a debit was recorded. Requests now reserve one credit and create a pending generation in a short database transaction before contacting Gemini. Settlement consumes or refunds that reservation once; ambiguous provider outcomes retain the reservation for review. Admission also enforces one pending request per user, 12 attempts per user and 24 globally in a rolling 24-hour window, with a 45-second provider deadline and bounded request bodies. The existing additive monthly credit allowance is preserved.

The unused public Listening Room endpoint now returns 410 without parsing input or contacting a provider. The operations runtime is updated to Next 15.5.25, React 19.1.9, Clerk 6.39.6 and Sharp 0.35.4. Unreferenced Auth.js components and dependencies are removed; current Clerk authentication remains in use.

Validation: 28 agency tests and 29 AI tests passed, including real PostgreSQL concurrency, duplicate settlement, month rollover, provider configuration failures and a persistence failure after provider success. An ordinary AVIF decode/resize test verifies the patched native image runtime. Type checking and the production build passed. CI runs the same checks against a disposable PostgreSQL service. No production schema migration is required.

Live limitations: metadata-only checks of both existing Gemini keys returned API_KEY_INVALID. No live generation or new provider billing was activated. The patch protects this feature but does not repair its credential configuration. The production dependency audit now reports zero critical findings; 15 high and 5 moderate findings remain, including inherited/tooling findings, and are separate follow-up work. This is not a claim that the whole application has been security audited.

body:
**Ctrl+S ukládá na GitHub, a když není nastavená cesta i token, do souboru** — to platilo a platí, je to tentýž `smartSave()` jako u Alt+S a jako tlačítko Uložit. Ověřeno: bez GitHubu → soubor, s cestou i tokenem → GitHub, a funguje i uvnitř textového pole.

Při ověřování ale vypadly dvě díry:

- **Caps Lock.** `Ctrl+S`, `Ctrl+F` a `Ctrl+K` se porovnávaly jen proti malému písmenu, takže se zapnutým Caps Lockem (`ev.key` je `S`) neudělaly nic.
- **Cizí rozložení.** Na rozložení, kde ta klávesa píše jiné písmeno (ruské `ы`), neplatila ani jedna z Ctrl-zkratek.

Nově je pozná `ctrlKlavesa()` **podle znaku i podle fyzické klávesy** — znak proto, že to tak lidé mají naučené, fyzická klávesa kvůli Caps Locku a cizím rozložením. Týká se všech: Ctrl+S, Ctrl+F, Ctrl+K, Ctrl+T, Ctrl+W, Ctrl+Shift+O, Ctrl+Shift+S, Ctrl+Shift+P i Ctrl+Shift+F.

Je to táž třída chyby jako u Alt-zkratek v [PR #100](https://github.com/egdilna/nastroje/pull/100), jen z druhé strany: tam se četl znak, kde měla být fyzická klávesa, tady se četl jen jeden tvar znaku.

## Ověření

Playwright + Chromium s událostmi, jak je pošle anglická klávesnice, Caps Lock, ruské rozložení a macOS (Cmd místo Ctrl): všech pět variant Ctrl+S uloží, ostatní Ctrl-zkratky s Caps Lockem taky (schránka, paleta, hledání, filtry, panel). Plus regrese Alt-zkratek, i18n a přístupnostní audit — bez chyby v konzoli.

Dokumentace: tabulka zkratek upřesňuje, že Ctrl+S je totéž co Alt+S (GitHub, jinak soubor), a poznámka o fyzické klávese teď platí i pro Ctrl — česky i anglicky. `dkm/CLAUDE.md` má pravidlo „nikdy neporovnávej jen `ev.key==='s'`".

author: ronaldo-f-dev
body:
## Résumé

Aboutissement du chantier PHP embed SAPI amorcé par les jobs CI
`ios-php-embed-step1..4` : iOS peut désormais exécuter un vrai
interpréteur PHP 8.3.15 **en process** (plus besoin d'un `phpx serve`
tournant sur la machine du développeur pour tester le rendu réel).

- `bin/phpx bundle:ios` copie `public/` + `lib/` + `packages/*/src` +
  `vendor/` (composer install avec `--ignore-platform-req=php`, le
  plancher `>=8.4.1` de Symfony ne concerne que le PHP système de la
  machine de build, pas le runtime 8.3.15 réellement embarqué) dans
  `Resources/www` de `PhpNitroNativeEngine`.
- `phpx_embed_handle_request()` fait maintenant tourner un vrai cycle
  requête (`php_request_shutdown` + `php_request_startup`) pour
  pouvoir servir plusieurs écrans dans le même process.
- Bug réel trouvé et corrigé : `zend_eval_string_ex()` renvoie
  `FAILURE` quand le script fait `exit`/`die` (ce que fait le vrai
  `public/index.php` après avoir émis son JSON), même si toute la
  sortie a déjà été capturée — confirmé par un harnais C brut reproduisant
  fidèlement le vrai `index.php`. `phpx_embed_eval()` ne renvoie
  `NULL` que si le buffer de sortie est réellement vide.
- `libphp.xcframework` recompilé avec les correctifs runtime
  nécessaires au vrai code de l'app (chacun découvert via une
  vraie erreur/crash reproduits, jamais deviné) :
  `--without-pcre-jit` (PCRE2 JIT interdit sur iOS, Bus error confirmé
  via lldb), `--enable-session=static`, `--enable-pdo=static
  --with-pdo-sqlite=static --with-sqlite3=static` (Doctrine DBAL).
- README + CI (`ios-php-embed-step1..4`) mis à jour pour documenter
  ces mêmes flags.

## Test plan

- [x] `xcodebuild ... test -only-testing:PhpNitroNativeEngineTests/PhpEmbedRuntimeTests`
      — 5/5 tests passent sur iOS Simulator, dont
      `testHandleRequestServesTheRealHomeScreenAsJson` qui sert le
      vrai `public/index.php` (screen=home) via le runtime PHP
      embarqué et vérifie un JSON de commandes de dessin valide.
- [x] Reproduction du bug exit/FAILURE via un harnais C brut
      (`simctl spawn`) contre le `libphp.a` simulateur fraîchement
      recompilé, avant et après le fix.

Hors scope (décision architecturale séparée à venir) : brancher
`PhpEmbedRuntime` dans le vrai chemin de requête de
`NativeScreenViewController`/`ScreenClient` pour basculer entre mode
réseau (`phpx serve`) et mode embarqué.

author: aarontaylor-dev
body:
Stacked on #7 — base is that branch, so this diff is just the new work. GitHub will retarget it to `main` when #7 merges.

`spec-first.com` redirects to `/spec`, and the page it lands on said nothing about why. Spec First was a development method — problem, scope, domain, behaviour, tests, then code, with the behaviour written as Gherkin `.feature` files — and it is retired. Following that redirect meant arriving at a skill with no account of what became of the thing you were looking for.

`/spec` gains a short unnumbered section after the source, driven by a new optional `provenance` block in `skill.json`. It says what the method was, what the skill kept from it, and gives two places to check the claim: year.tools, where the full method is still practised and its `spec/` directory is public, and the note explaining why Spec First was retired rather than renamed. The header's jump links gain a fifth entry on this page only — the segmented control still fits one row on desktop and stacks on mobile, both checked.

It is an appendix rather than a step: the reading order of a skill page ends at owning the file, and history belongs after that. It is on the page rather than in the file for the same kind of reason — a downloaded `SKILL.md` should not have to carry the history of a method it no longer belongs to. The skill is unchanged at v0.2, so no entry names it.

`partOf` stays unset, which is now a decision rather than a wait. That field names a method a reader can go and check, and this one has no public artefact left, so setting it would be exactly the unverifiable claim the README already refuses. The README said the method "had nowhere public to point at", which described the symptom rather than the fact; it says retired now. Its opening sentence also still called this a workbench for practical AI work, which is the claim the site dropped in #7, so it now says four skills.

The `provenance` block is validated like everything else in `skill.json` — at least one non-empty paragraph, and links carrying all three parts — and that check is listed in the README beside the others. A section that exists has to say something.

`node build.js` has been run. Only `spec.html` gains content; the other three skill pages and the rest of the site differ by the footer version alone.

body:
Fixes the `backend-tests (iluvatar)` and `backend-tests (metax-maca3810)` failures.
**Changes**

1. flash_attention_backward: make `triton.knobs` import optional
- The module-level `from triton.knobs import autotuning` added in #6077 breaks `import flag_gems` on vendor/older Triton builds that do not provide the `triton.knobs` module (e.g. iluvatar's CoreX Triton).
- Wrap the import in `try/except ImportError` and make `_disable_aabs_for_small_seqlen` a no-op when the knob API is unavailable. On builds that have the knob, behavior is unchanged.（#6176）

2. metax special_hermite_polynomial_he: cast n to int64 in the scalar-x path
- The scalar-x + tensor-n path reused the tensor-tensor kernel directly. When `n` arrives as a float tensor (e.g. float32 from the scalar-x test), the resulting float-n kernel specialization triggers an internal mlir-opt error in the MetaX Triton compiler.
- Cast `n` to an int64 tensor on the host before launching the kernel, so the integer-n specialization (already verified by the other test cases) is used. Output dtype is unaffected (promotion follows arg0), and `n` is a small integer in [0, 10] so the cast is lossless.

Fixes #3618

body:
#410 added the router data source so the subgraph indexes all five Aqua events — the number 1inch's own documentation asks for. It merged with the README already saying *"the data source lands with 340 fills nobody could otherwise query."* Studio was still serving v0.2.0, which has no `fills` at all. This is the deploy that closes that gap.

```
version    v0.3.0
build      QmbhmRoR9C7Eo6RGRdM4kCd6iBhWvRWcLXXAx4SSd5WSfe
```

Read back from Studio at `version/latest` after sync:

```
deployment         QmbhmRoR9C…    ← latest now serves v0.3.0
block              504,018,404    against a head of 504,018,412
hasIndexingErrors  false
fills              340            ← the README's number, measured
unique takers      3
accounts           1              ← the account opened today, still there
```

Before deploy: `graph codegen`, `graph build`, and the subgraph's 12 tests — four of them new for the router handler.

One thing worth knowing about how Studio behaved: `version/latest` kept serving v0.2.0 until v0.3.0 had caught up, then switched. `config.production.json` and the app both name `latest`, so the enclave never read a half-built index. The catch-up was 18.5 million blocks in under two minutes, because the router source filters on a single event signature.

author: tyler-dane
body:
No issue: scheduled technical-debt sweep over the 50 commits merged since 2026-09-04.

## What and why

Three behavior-preserving cleanups, one per commit, all from code that landed in the last seven days.

**1. `chore(web): drop the committed bun test junit dump`**

`packages/web/test-results.xml` is a 2,034-line JUnit report from somebody's local `bun test` run (995 tests, 383 failures, a laptop hostname in every `testsuite` element). It landed by accident in #3579 and nothing reads it: no reporter configured in this repo writes that path, and no script or workflow consumes it. It only churns unrelated diffs. The ignore rule covered the `test-results/` directory but not the sibling file, so this adds it.

**2. `refactor(web): derive connect statuses from one list`**

`ConnectStatus` and `STATUS_VALUES` in `connect-status.util.ts` spelled out the same seven statuses twice. The file's own comment explains why that hurts: a status present in the type but missing from the runtime list makes `readConnectStatus` return null, and the user lands on the calendar after a failed connect with no explanation at all. The type now derives from the list, so the two cannot drift, and the `as ConnectStatus` cast in `readConnectStatus` becomes a type guard.

Same commit deletes `refreshUserMetadataAfterConnect`. It took a `ConnectStatus` it ignored, no caller remained after `applyConnectRedirect` absorbed the refresh, and only its own test kept it alive.

**3. `refactor(web): share the oauth callback shell between both views`**

`ProviderAuthCallbackView` and `AppleAuthCallbackView` each carried the same one-shot effect (a `didRun` ref guarding the StrictMode double-invoke) and a byte-identical spinner `OverlayPanel`, copied down to the `aria-hidden` border classes. Two copies of a one-shot OAuth exchange drift quietly: a fix to one callback's mount semantics silently misses the other.

`useOneShotAuthCallback` and `AuthCallbackOverlay` now hold the shared parts. Each view keeps its own exchange and its own catch, because the failure copy and the funnel method genuinely differ; only the mount guard and the panel are shared. New unit tests cover the hook's once-per-mount contract and the overlay's status announcement.

The three are separate commits rather than separate PRs because this session is pinned to a single branch.

## Verify

`bun run verify --strict`

```
Selected packages: web
Checks run: test:web, type-check, lint, knip, test:a11y
Checks skipped: (none)
Failed: test:e2e
VERDICT: FAIL
```

`test:web` (888 pass, 0 fail), `type-check`, `lint`, `knip`, and `test:a11y` all pass locally. `test:e2e` fails locally on two specs, both sandbox-bound and neither reachable from this diff:

- `e2e/auth/sign-in-providers.spec.ts:99` "starts Microsoft sign-in with the M shortcut" — `page.waitForURL: net::ERR_CONNECTION_RESET`. The spec navigates the real browser to `login.microsoftonline.com`; this sandbox's egress proxy resets that hop. The diff touches the OAuth *return* views, which the spec never reaches.
- `e2e/calendars/calendar-experience.spec.ts:523` "day view separates visible calendars into distinct columns" — `page.waitForURL: Timeout 10000ms exceeded`, with the Playwright log showing it did navigate to `/day` and simply missed the 10s `load` budget on a slow sandbox.

CI confirms both are environmental: all 18 checks on this head are green, including `e2e-shard (2, ... e2e/auth ...)` and `e2e-shard (4, ... e2e/calendars ...)`, the shards that own those two specs.

author: reyesnick54
body:
## Summary

Completes Phase 4 (slice 4H) by delivering the canonical HeartStone Authority & Policy Engine on top of the Phase 4A register foundation.

The server now computes authority for a specific institutional actor, function, and action. Authentication, MFA, OIDC claims, and technical access alone never confer government authority.

## Architecture

- **Identity** answers WHO
- **Institutional structure** answers WHERE THEY SIT
- **Appointment/Delegation** establish institutional relationships
- **Governing sources** establish the source basis
- **FunctionAuthorityRecord** defines WHAT FUNCTION is being evaluated
- **AuthorityAction** defines WHAT THEY ARE TRYING TO DO
- **Conditions/dependencies** define WHAT ELSE MUST BE TRUE
- **AuthorityEvaluationService** determines WHETHER THAT SPECIFIC ACTION MAY PROCEED

Evaluation results do not create authority; they evaluate recorded authority.

## Key components (`src/authority/`)

- `FunctionAuthorityRecord` with eight `AuthorityClassification` values
- `GoverningSource` registry with version history and relationships
- `FunctionGoverningSource`, `FunctionAuthorityAssignment`, `AuthorityActionRight`
- `InstitutionalActorResolver` (appointment/delegation validation)
- `AuthorityConditionEvaluator`, `AuthorityDependencyEvaluator`, `SegregationOfDutyEvaluator`
- `AuthorityEvaluationService` + immutable `AuthorityEvaluationRecord`
- `AuthorityExplanationService` with safe-halt semantics
- Separate audited function activation (`FunctionActivationAudit`)

## API surface (`/api/v1/authority/...`)

- `POST /authority/governing-sources` (+ authenticate/revoke)
- `POST /authority/functions` (+ activate/suspend — not via ordinary create)
- `POST /authority/evaluate` (session-protected; server computes outcome)
- `GET /authority/evaluate/records/:id` (immutable replay)

## Testing

- Eight-classification `NON_PRODUCTION_SAMPLE_TEST_ONLY` fixtures
- Positive E2E: authenticated human → institutional chain → ALLOW
- E2E delegated, retained-national, professional, technology-assisted, prohibited paths
- Phase 4H must-fail suite (40+ invariants)
- Unit, integration, and e2e suites all green locally

## Migrations

- `20260911140000_phase_4_authority_engine` — full Phase 4 schema

## Documentation

- `docs/architecture/phase-4-authority-policy-engine.md`

## Notes

- Reconciles prior Phase 4A register and Phase 4B governing-source work into one canonical engine implementation
- `AuthorityBoundaryService` remains identity-side only; evaluation is exclusively via `AuthorityEvaluationService`
- Software readiness ≠ institutional acceptance

body:
#213 triage onayındaki dar kapsam: önce mevcut main'de başarısız karakterizasyon, sonra **yalnız sol aday** için geometri kontrolü, `VERSION` v11 → v12.

## Kök neden

#261'de (`8891461`) eklediğim sol yan çubuk adayı, "sol kenarda ve dar" satırlardan toplanıyor. `pickSidebar`/`sidebarScore` yalnız satır sayısını ve genişlik oranını sınıyor; aday ile geri kalan ana akışın **yatay ayrışması** doğrulanmıyordu. Tek sütunlu bir CV'nin kısa bölüm başlıkları (`EGITIM`, `BECERILER`, `NOT`) da tam böyle görünür. `MIN_SIDEBAR_LINES` dolunca bu başlıklar ayrı akışa çekiliyor, içerikleri de ana akışta açık kalan deneyim bölümüne yapışıyordu. Ölçümler: https://github.com/Halildeu/ats/issues/213#issuecomment-5631839678

## Değişiklik

- `restStartsRightOf`: sol aday yalnız geri kalan satırların başlangıç **x ortancası**, adayın sağ sınırından büyükse geçerli. Koordinatlar sayfadan okunuyor, fixture'a özel sabit x yok. Sağ aday değişmedi.
- Ortanca, en küçük değer değil. Bu ölçüldü: en küçük x ile mevcut `columns_sharing_the_same_baseline_do_not_bleed_into_each_other` kırmızıya dönüyor.
- `VERSION` `pdfbox-3.0.5-rules-v11` → `pdfbox-3.0.5-rules-v12` (zorunlu bump sözleşmesi): aynı PDF v11'de `EDUCATION`'ı `EXPERIENCE`'a karıştırıyor, v12'de ayrı bölüm veriyor. Testteki üç sürüm referansı güncellendi.

## Kanıt: önce kırmızı, sonra yeşil

| commit | içerik | sonuç |
|---|---|---|
| `1227754` | yalnız karakterizasyon testi | CI [34588674759](https://github.com/Halildeu/ats/actions/runs/34588674759): app-boot 261 test, **yalnız yeni test kırmızı** (`alinan alanlar: [SUMMARY, FULL_NAME, EXPERIENCE]`) |
| `1c6f4d4` | kural + v12 | yerel `PdfBoxResumeDocumentParserTest` tests=47 failures=0 errors=0 (surefire XML); CI [34589078213](https://github.com/Halildeu/ats/actions/runs/34589078213): **success**, `PdfBoxResumeDocumentParserTest` 47/0/0/0. Tek atlanan `LiveSttLiveConformanceTest`, `main`'de de aynı şekilde atlanıyor. |

**Negatif doğrulama:** sol yol tamamen kapatılınca `a_left_hand_narrow_column_is_treated_as_the_sidebar` ve `columns_sharing_the_same_baseline_do_not_bleed_into_each_other` kırmızıya dönüyor. Yani gerçek sol yan çubuk mevcut testlerde gerçekten sınanıyor ve kural onu koruyarak geçiyor. Sağ yan çubuk, aynı-baseline iki sütun, başlık/hiyerarşi ve korumalı alan regresyonları aynı sınıftaki mevcut testlerle kapsanıyor ve yeşil.

**Kendi kodumu yoklarken sildiğim test:** ortanca seçimini "sayfa genişliğinde tek başlık satırı" düzeniyle gerekçelendiren bir test yazmıştım. En küçük x kuralıyla da geçtiğini ölçtüm, yani iddiayı ölçmüyordu. Testi sildim; gerekçeyi yukarıdaki ölçülen testle değiştirdim.

## Kapsam dışı (triage gereği)

- `NOT` sözlüğü: `NOT` içeriği #208 kuralıyla `SKILLS` sonuna ekleniyor; yeni testte bilerek assert edilmiyor.
- Mixed-case gevşetmesi, endpoint/şema/policy değişikliği yok.
- TEST okuyucu sürümü/digest'i ve normal kullanıcı gruplu satır düzeltme → gönderim → İK okuma kabulü ayrı kapıdır. Bu kaynak/CI sonucu kullanıcı kabulünün yerine geçmez; merge/deploy yapılmadı.

Refs: Halildeu/ats#213

body:
🤖 Reclaim expired query-graph runtime state as one batch. Previously, removing each node rescanned every operator-state, arrangement and memo entry. Removing K nodes from M retained entries could therefore perform K full scans. The new path collects removed IDs once and visits each state map once.

For example, when a temporary query releases a chain of nodes while another subscription remains active, only the expired IDs are removed from runtime state; shared or suspended graph nodes remain protected by the existing retention calculation. The retention rules, graph-node removal and point-index cleanup are unchanged. Empty removal batches do not scan the state maps.

author: niconoe
body:
## Problem

Reported as "publishing a template can leak a private area", but the root cause sits lower. `_save_alert` set whatever area ids the payload carried, with no visibility check. Area ids are sequential, so user B could attach user A's private area to their own alert by guessing its id. Reproduced: the create request returned 201 while the same area was absent from B's area list and its GeoJSON returned 403. The geometry stays hidden, but the filtering effect leaks.

The same path let `alert_create_from_template` copy a private area out of a template into any user's alert, and `alert_publish_as_template` copied areas into templates verbatim, exposing the id to every user through the templates list.

## Fix

- `_save_alert` rejects, as a validation error on `areas`, any id that is neither public nor owned by the alert's user (`Area.objects.available_to`). This covers direct create and update, and the from-template path.
- `alert_publish_as_template` refuses with 422 an alert that uses a private area, so the operator finds out at publish time rather than users at copy time. Dropping the area silently was rejected: a template with a different filter than the alert it came from is a surprise.
- Both new error strings are translated in fr, nl and nb. The generated TypeScript types are unchanged.

Visible behaviour change: editing an existing alert whose area was made private after the fact is now refused until another area is picked. That is the intended outcome.

## Tests

- Create and update with another user's private area return 422 and change nothing (failed before).
- Create with a public area and with the user's own area still returns 201.
- Publishing an alert with a private area is refused with 422 (failed before); with a public area it still works.
- A template that references a private area, built through the ORM, cannot be copied into another user's alert (failed before).

Full suite: 904 passed. mypy clean.

## Summary

Adds an explicit goal logit has been assuming but never written down: `statsd_in -> statsd_out`,
`otlp_in -> otlp_out`, and `syslog_in -> syslog_out` should each be a transparent relay. No code
changes -- this is scoping and documentation only.

- **[ADR `lossless-transit`](docs/adr/lossless-transit.md)** states the goal, a named list of
  permitted normalizations (batching, tag reordering, a sink-configured dialect change, counter
  sample-rate folding), and the fields-vs-attributes convention new codec work should follow.

  protocol in `OVERVIEW.md`'s scope (statsd, DogStatsD, OTLP, syslog 3164/5424, Prometheus,
  Prometheus remote-write, InfluxDB line protocol, collectd, Graphite) actually expresses per
  signal, checked against each protocol's own spec, with comparison matrices and a numbered
  superset-requirements list.
- **[`docs/plans/lossless-transit.md`](docs/plans/lossless-transit.md)** assesses today's model and
  codecs against that survey (file:line cited), proposes a target model reshaping

author: srbino
body:
Closes #2496. Found while completing the §9 acceptance for #2473.

## Correction first

The issue as I filed it says "the server validates no typed run or preset
input". **That headline is wrong**, and the fix work is what showed it.
`pipeline.ValidateFormInputs` exists and is wired on the run path twice — the
`Run` handler before dispatch, and the executor again before the first step —
and the decision-form and fixture paths use the same function.

My original probe passed everything because of `hasInputForm`:

```go
func hasInputForm(in InputSpec) bool { return in.Widget != "" || len(in.Options) > 0 || in.AllowCustom }
```

An input carries a form contract only if it declares a `widget`, `options`, or
`allow_custom`. The probe declared `type` and `required` but no `widget`, so
every input was legacy by that rule and every check was skipped. The observed
matrix was accurate; my explanation of it was not.
`TestPresetValidation_RunPathAlreadyRejects` pins the real behaviour so the
next reader does not "fix" it twice. The acceptance report's finding N3 is
rewritten in #2494 for the same reason.

## The actual defect

A plan's preset is validated only when the *routine* later changes (that is
the #2495 gate). Nothing validates it when the **plan itself** is written. A
plan can therefore be stored carrying values its target routine already
rejects, sit enabled in the calendar looking healthy, and fail for the first
time at its next firing — with no run row to inspect, because the executor
refuses before one exists.

Against a routine whose inputs DO carry a form contract:

| `POST /pipeline-schedules` inputs | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `{}` — required `region` (select) missing | **201** | 400 naming `region` |
| `{"region":null}` | **201** | 400 |
| `{"region":"antarctica"}` — outside `options` | **201** | 400 |
| `{"region":"eu","dry_run":"yes"}` — string for boolean | **201** | 400 |
| `{"retries":9}` — above declared `max` | **201** | 400 |
| `PATCH` onto `{"region":"antarctica"}` | **200** | 400, stored preset unchanged |
| routine save whose `trigger.inputs` the recipe rejects | **200**, plan stored | 422, whole save rolled back |

## Three doors, one rule

`CreateSchedule` and `UpdateSchedule` call `gateSchedulePreset`;
`createTriggerTx` validates the preset a routine save's `trigger` block
carries against the very definition that save is publishing, so a recipe and
the trigger created beside it cannot be born disagreeing. All three call
`pipeline.ValidateFormInputs` — the same function the run path calls, not a
second opinion. A preset this accepted and the executor then rejected would be
worse than no check.

The wake gate's own preset is checked against the wake routine for the same
reason: it fails the same way at the same 02:30.

## Compatibility

Pinned by tests rather than asserted in prose:

- `false`, `0` and an empty list are **answers**, not absences.
- An input the recipe does not declare is still passed through.
- An input with no `widget`/`options`/`allow_custom` is **not** validated here,
  because it is not validated at execution either. Most existing routines are
  that shape, and tightening it is a separate decision about the legacy
  contract — not something a preset fix should smuggle in.
- A pinned plan is checked against the version it names.
- A definition that no longer parses is left to the executor to surface rather
  than blamed on the plan being edited.

Response codes: 400 on the schedule doors (already declared in their OpenAPI
entries — `gen-openapi` produces no diff), 422 on the save doors via the
existing `ErrInvalidTrigger` mapping.

## Verification

- Red first: every row of the table above returns 201/200 on the parent commit.
- `go test ./internal/... ./cmd/...` — running, will report before merge.
- `go vet ./...` clean, `go run ./scripts/docs-inventory -strict` clean,
  `go run ./scripts/docs-surface-check` clean, `gen-openapi` no diff.
- `internal/api/pipeline_schedule_preset_validation_test.go` covers all three
  doors, the compatibility cases, and the run path that was already right.
- Depends on nothing in #2495, but both touch `internal/pipeline/store.go`; if
  #2495 lands first this will want a rebase.

author: torztomasz
body:
`@l2beat/config` is consumed through `ProjectService` and type imports; deep imports of `build/` files are not allowed. The package root had grown a block of CROPS runtime exports (`resolveProjectCrops`, `qualifiesForGarden`, `CROP_ATTESTATIONS`, the EAS constants) that the frontend and l2b called at request time. This PR moves that work into the config build, so config exports only types for CROPS again and every reader sees the same data. Reverts the runtime half of #12796.

## Config

- `getProjects` resolves `crops` into a new `gardenInfo` field: every default applied, the OSI license looked up, and `inGarden` decided once, in the build. `crops` stays as what the reviewer wrote. `canonicalCrops.ts` becomes `crops/getGardenInfo.ts` and nothing from it is exported.
- `eas.ts` folds into `crops/attestations.ts`. The build stores one `CropAttestations` row (network, schema, networks, ledgers and the current attestation) in a new `crop_attestations` table; `ProjectService.getCropAttestations()` reads it.
- The schema uid drift check moves from l2b into `attestations.test.ts`, next to the hardcoded value.
- The crops types (`CropKey`, `ResolvedCrops`, `ProjectGardenInfo`, the attestation and network types, `HexString`) live in `types.ts`. The root index is back to its previous shape.

## Frontend

- The garden page, the project pages, the address index and the garden API read `gardenInfo` and `ps.getCropAttestations()` instead of resolving at request time. `getAttestationsMeta` and `getGardenAttestation` are async now; the explorer URL is built in `getCropsProjects`, the one place that needs it.
- Client components are untouched: they only ever imported types.

## l2b

- The crops commands load the attestation state through `ProjectService`, pick the network from it (`--network` is a plain name; the default is the network config reads) and pass an `EasTarget` (network + schema) through `easClient`, `state`, `execute` and `plan` instead of reading constants.
- `crops.test.ts` uses local schema and network fixtures.

## Testing

- `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format` in config, frontend and l2b.
- `pnpm test` in config (24702 passing, including new tests for `getGardenInfo`, the attestations row and the schema uid), frontend (474 passing) and l2b (71 passing).
- Built config and read `build/db.sqlite` through `ProjectService`: all five reviewed projects carry `gardenInfo` with the expected `inGarden` and license, and `getCropAttestations()` returns the sepolia revision 3 attestation over five projects.

## Follow-ups

- #12804 (crops-api) and #12809 restack on this: crops-api reads `gardenInfo` and `getCropAttestations()` the same way, and the "copied from the frontend" garden helpers shrink accordingly.

author: milind-soni
body:
## What changes

Make Stop finish reliably when a provider or its helper processes do not exit promptly.

- Track only process groups created by our CLI launcher; never group-signal an unrelated child.
- Send graceful termination, then bounded force-stop, and confirm that the owned group is gone before reporting success.
- Deduplicate concurrent stops and allow retry after an uncertain result.
- Make Claude and Codex preserve turn ownership until shutdown is confirmed; a later successful Stop can finish cleanup without leaving the thread permanently busy.
- Make npm install timeouts settle visibly and let Antigravity verification wait for the complete shutdown budget before removing its files.

No new dependencies. Windows taskkill behavior is preserved. Deliberately detached descendants outside the owned POSIX group are not covered.

## Verification

- Initial compatibility run: 398 tests passed, 1 Windows-specific skip across 14 files.
- Review corrections: 105 Claude/isolated Stop tests passed (1 Windows-specific skip), and 63 Antigravity tests passed.
- Real isolated server Stop workflows: root exits before helper; root and helper ignore TERM. Both retain busy state during shutdown, confirm the recorded PIDs are gone, and accept a subsequent message.
- Real TERM-ignoring Antigravity fixture validates successfully after forced shutdown.
- False-then-true stop regressions cover fresh and retained Claude sessions, exactly one completion, and a working replacement turn.
- Server typecheck, focused lint, and whitespace checks passed. No live user app or data used.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

- **Bug Fixes**
  - Improved task interruption so stubborn processes are fully stopped before a task is marked complete.
  - Preserved session and task ownership when shutdown cannot be confirmed, allowing safe retries.
  - Prevented premature completion events and ensured subsequent turns work after successful interruption.
  - Improved timeout handling for engine installation, including clearer errors when termination cannot be confirmed.
  - Reduced the risk of accidentally terminating unrelated processes during shutdown.

author: eifrah-aws
body:
The unit tests replace some C functions with gmock mocks. Every call to such a function must go to `__wrap_<name>`, and the real function must stay reachable as `__real_<name>`. On Linux the linker does this with `--wrap`. The macOS linker has no such option.

The Makefile build already solves this: it renames the symbols inside the object files with llvm-objcopy. The CMake build only had the Linux path, so linking the tests on macOS failed with undefined `___real_*` symbols.

Add the same step to the CMake build:

* wrap-objects.py asks `llvm-nm` which functions an object file defines. In the file that defines the function the symbol is renamed to `___real_<name>`, in every other file the call is renamed to `___wrap_<name>`. The changed objects are collected into a static library.
* On macOS the test sources are built as an object library, so that their objects can be renamed too. generated_wrappers.cpp stays out of it, because it defines the `__wrap_` functions itself. Its archive is force loaded, so all gtest cases are still registered.
* Linux and the other systems keep the `--wrap` path unchanged.

Also stop the configure step when a Makefile build left generated_wrappers.{cpp,hpp} in src/unit. The header is found before the generated one, because the test files include it with quotes, so the test objects would be built against an out of date header.

Tested on macOS arm64: `make test-unit` runs 784 tests, none failing.

author: rohitkf
body: Four things, in one batch. ### The app logo is the owner's The mark in the top-left has been a hard-coded "RIM" tile since the shell was built — fine for this church, wrong for the app. It is a setting now, in **Settings → App logo**, and it belongs to the owner rather than to every Admin. Every other row of `app_settings` is a number an Admin may tune; the mark at the top of every page is the church's identity, not one of its clocks. RLS cannot say "except this column", so migration **0089** does it with a trigger firing before anything records a change: an Admin editing the clocks never meets it, an Admin reaching for the logo is stopped whether they come through the app, the API, or psql. The file lives in a new private `branding` bucket that only the owner may write to and any signed-in person may read. The drawn tile is the fallback, exactly as asked: no logo, a logo taken down, or a signed URL that could not be had all draw the app's own mark. Both are the same 36px square with the same corner radius, so nothing in the header moves when a logo arrives or goes, and the logo is fitted rather than cropped so a wordmark survives. ### Search: the right key, and the middle of the screen - **The key.** ⌘K was printed for everybody, including the people on Windows and Linux who do not have that key — a hint naming a key your keyboard lacks reads as "not for you". The label follows the platform now. Both shortcuts always worked and still do; only the label changed. - **The middle.** The shortcut used to put the cursor in a quarter-width field in the corner with a dropdown under it, on a page that carried on scrolling behind. It opens over the page now, centred, scroll held, Escape or the backdrop to leave. The header keeps a button that looks like the old field, for anyone who never learned the shortcut. - **Anything.** Six more sources: events, songs, running-order sessions, team chat, alerts, and service templates, alongside the teams, people, kit, services, roles, messages and pages it already had. RLS still decides every row, so nobody is shown the existence of something they could not open. ### The header lost two duplicates Appearance and team colours are in the account menu under their own headings, and were in the header as well. One switch, one home. ### Ages on the Teams page Every member's age, core and guest alike. It comes off `profiles`, which any signed-in person could already read — **nothing was widened for this**, and the sensitive row (visas, DBS) is untouched. The page shows the number rather than the date: the year is the part that changes how you speak to somebody. ### Verified - Migration 0089 was run against production inside a self-rolling-back transaction first, impersonating both principals: owner sets the logo ✓, a non-owner Admin is blocked with "Only the owner can change the app logo" ✓, that same Admin can still change `rota_window_days` ✓, owner clears it ✓, bucket private with a 2 MB cap ✓, four policies ✓. Then applied, and the column, trigger, bucket and policies re-checked live. - Rendered the open palette in Chromium against the built CSS, light and dark: centred card, results across six kinds, each labelled. - 16 new tests — the platform label (Mac/Windows/Linux/iPhone/Android, and not reading "mac" out of a substring), the palette (opens and closes on the shortcut, opens from the header, navigates, is modal), the mark's three fallback cases, the logo card (uploads under a fresh name, takes the old file down, asks before removing, tells an Admin whose decision it is), the owner-only Settings room, and ages for core and guest against a frozen clock. - `npx tsc --noEmit` on both projects, `npx vitest run` (154 files, 1205 tests), `npm run build` — clean; `npm run lint` holds at the 41-warning baseline. **Worth knowing:** SVG is an allowed logo format. author: kawanet-bot
body:
## Summary

What a named file may be is decided up front by two rules, the same in every mode, instead of by where it happened to fail.

| extension | suite, Node mode | suite, browser modes | `--script`, browser modes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `.js` `.mjs` | runs | runs | runs |
| `.cjs` | refused: CommonJS | refused: CommonJS | **runs** (was a 403) |
| `.cts` | refused: CommonJS | refused: CommonJS | refused: TypeScript |
| `.ts` `.mts` | runs, on Node's type stripping | refused: TypeScript (was a 403) | refused: TypeScript (was a 403) |

- **CommonJS suites are refused in every mode.** Under Node a `require("node:test")` bypasses the resolve hook and registers with Node's own runner: this package reports no tests and success, Node's runner prints a second report, and a passing suite passes for nothing. A browser has no `require` at all. Before, the browser modes served such a suite and the run ended on a load error with `[object Event]` on stderr.
- **TypeScript is refused in the browser modes**, for a suite and for a `--script`, since a browser strips no types. Before, it was a 403 from the static server, seen only in the access log.
- **`.cjs` is served**, so a `--script` may be one: a classic script is one whatever its name, and a `.js` CommonJS file was served all along. `.ts`, `.cts` and `.mts` stay 403 as the last line for a relative import a suite makes.
- **`--port` takes decimal digits.** `Number()` also read `0x50`, `1e3` and the empty string; the usage says `<number>` and the error says `0 to 65535`, so those are refused now.

## Also

`importMapOf` and the `Alias`/`Import` types move out of `options.ts` into `src/extras/import-map.ts`, with their tests in `import-map.test.ts`; the reader throws plain `Error`s and `options.ts` puts `--import-map <file>:` in front. `options.ts` is down to the flags and the rules. No behavior change in that part.

## Checked

`make -C builder test`; through the CLI on chromium, a `.cjs` `--script` sets its global and the suite sees it; the three refusals print their reason and the usage; a `.ts` suite still runs in Node mode.

author: jonbj
body:
## Ripresa dopo la review

Il rilievo bloccante era corretto: il report usava `fill_price` per entrambe
le uscite, ma `_fetch_policy_rows()` non lo selezionava dalla vista di
produzione. Di conseguenza i prezzi P0/P1 arrivavano come ignoti e le metriche
di false exit, recovery e giveback restavano vuote. Questa revisione aggiunge
`fill_price` alla query e una regressione TDD sul confine SQL; inoltre il
fixture end-to-end ora ha la stessa forma delle righe di produzione, senza
iniettare i prezzi manualmente nel solo test della qualita'.

## Cosa

Issue #299 chiedeva il valutatore statistico appaiato del trial exit S4. La
parte inferenziale era gia' in tree dalle PR #380 (valutatore puro: block
bootstrap event-day, intervalli unilaterali, gerarchia P1→P0 prima di
P2→P1, boundary golden PROMOTE/REJECT/INCONCLUSIVE, guardie su early stop
e sulle 213 sedute), #382 (ponte dalle viste appaiate) e #542 (N_cluster =
5816 dal contratto congelato). Il controllo fatto ora mostra pero' che di
quel valutatore non esisteva nessun consumatore di produzione: le metriche
§8.3 e il trial ledger erano codice testato ma mai eseguito.

Questa PR collega il valutatore al report che il cron esegue ogni 6 sedute
(`scripts/check_s4_trial_milestones.py` lancia
`scripts/report_s4_replacement.py`). Il verdetto porta un blocco `metrics`
calcolato sulla stessa coorte D0 dell'intervallo: delta e costi con copertura
dichiarata, capital-days, overnight share, downside deviation, expected
shortfall, max drawdown, worst trade, false-exit rate, recovery entro
l'orizzonte e giveback da MFE. Il costo d'uscita esce dal `net_pnl` e arriva
come delta esplicito; i costi d'ingresso sono condivisi per contratto. Un
costo o prezzo mancante resta ignoto, mai zero.

Il verdetto espone anche il `ledger` di ogni variante vista, con ruolo e note.
Il report lo persiste nella tabella append-only `s4_trial_ledger` (migrazione
066); il `ledger_id` e' il fingerprint uuid5 di finestra e variante, quindi
rieseguire la stessa finestra non aggiunge righe o molteplicita'. I ruoli
ammessi separano `confirmatory` e `diagnostic`, cosi' D+1, D+3, term structure
e sottoperiodi non possono rientrare come confirmatory.

La qualita' dell'uscita nasce dal path di prezzo: fill d'ingresso da
`s4_lifecycle_current`, fill d'uscita P0/P1 da
`s4_exit_policy_current`, e barre al minuto Alpaca. La correzione della review
garantisce che i fill d'uscita raggiungano davvero questo calcolo in
produzione.

## Criteri di accettazione

1. Metriche con denominatori congelati: blocco `metrics` di questa PR.
2. Block bootstrap, intervalli unilaterali e coverage sintetica: #380.
3. N_cluster derivato e guardia contro le 213 sedute: #542, #380 e #382.
4. Gerarchia P1→P0 prima di P2→P1: #380.
5. Trial ledger append-only e diagnostici separati: migrazione 066 e persistenza nel report.
6. Boundary golden e INCONCLUSIVE distinto dall'equivalenza: #380.
7. Nessuna promozione anticipata; safety halt distinto: #380.

## Come verificare

Dal worktree dedicato:

```
../../.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/strategies/ tests/scripts/
```

Atteso: `1030 passed, 2 warnings`; i warning sono preesistenti (deprecazione
`websockets.legacy` e scipy su input costante).

```
../../.venv/bin/python -m ruff check scripts/report_s4_replacement.py src/strategies/s4/counterfactual.py src/strategies/s4/counterfactual_runtime.py src/strategies/s4/evaluator_bridge.py src/strategies/s4/exit_quality.py src/strategies/s4/paired_evaluator.py tests/scripts/test_report_s4_replacement.py tests/strategies/test_s4_counterfactual.py tests/strategies/test_s4_evaluator_bridge.py tests/strategies/test_s4_exit_quality.py tests/strategies/test_s4_paired_evaluator.py
```

Atteso: `All checks passed!`.

La regressione specifica e' osservabile isolatamente con:

```
../../.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/scripts/test_report_s4_replacement.py::test_query_legge_costi_e_prezzi_di_uscita
```

Sul commit precedente fallisce perche' `fill_price` non e' nella query; su
questa revisione passa.

## Freeze e perimetro

Nessun parametro di taratura e' stato toccato: il lavoro e' interamente di
correttezza, strumentazione e misura. Il contratto
`config/s4_exit_trial.yaml` resta letto ma non modificato; nessuno dei file
vietati e' stato toccato.

Il dossier §8.3 nomina due definizioni operative senza formalizzarle. Questa
PR le dichiara, senza cambiare tarature: overnight e' il movimento attraverso
i gap di seduta della gamba challenger ancorato al fill d'ingresso; false exit
e' P0 che esce prima dell'orizzonte con prezzo P1 superiore al prezzo P0;
recovery e' il ritorno almeno al prezzo d'ingresso entro l'orizzonte residuo;
giveback e' `(MFE high - uscita P1) / ingresso` in bps. `d0` resta dichiarato
nel report come proxy conservativo dell'event-day (`cluster_caveat`).

Closes #299.
