author: henglicam
body:
H, the moment he saw the stars in the list: *"In die Learn karte Muss es auch."*

## What changes

**☆ Star / ★ Starred** joins ⚑ Flag for review and ✎ Edit on the Learn back, **first in the row** — the learner's own mark before the app's, then the edit. Same field, same `setStar`, **no new translation key** (v425's "Star" and "Starred" serve both screens). The on-state is the label, as the flag's is, not a colour — every `.del` in that row is already tint.

The **front** is deliberately left alone: it is one tap-to-reveal surface with the v417 swipe over it, and a target there would compete with both.

## The measurement was wrong before it was right

The first cut kept the row's `gap:22px` and no wrap, and the probe asked `scrollWidth > clientWidth` on the row and on each button — **all ten languages came back clean.** They were not: a flex item *shrinks* rather than overflows, so the German labels wrapped **inside** their buttons and the row rendered as three ragged two-line columns with the glyph stranded above its word. The screenshot showed it; the numbers could not.

**A fit check must ask whether the text broke, not whether the box overflowed** — `range.selectNodeContents(el).getClientRects().length > 1` is the question, and it is the one the suite asks now.

The row wraps as whole buttons since (`flex-wrap:wrap`, `gap:2px 22px`, `white-space:nowrap` on the labels). Measured over ten languages × 390 and 360 px: **0 labels broken anywhere** — one row in English, Thai, Japanese and Korean, two in German, French, Spanish, Russian and Indonesian.

## The release note moves 425 → 427

v425's number was burned three times (see #494), so no phone would ever have been told about the star. A phone that took the *first* v425 saw the note for a feature that was not in that build; showing it once more now, when the star is actually there, is the better of the two errors.

## Verified

`verify-star` gains the Learn back: the three labels with no label broken, the tap writing memory and IndexedDB, the Cards list agreeing on the same card, and the tap back off. `detail`, `link`, `guide`, `flag`, `order`, `resume`, `whatsnew` and `swipe` pass; `cards` and `english` fail **exactly as on the v424 baseline** (the context-word search v424 removed, and the harness's own service-worker line). Checked by screenshot in English and German dark.

**Field-confirmed on the way:** the v425 star in the list, H at v426 — *"Jetzt sehe ich die Sterne."*

author: safiqsindha
body:
Five fixes, all found by asking one question — **can we prove which model answered each call?** — and then by trying to start a real core run. Every one of them produces a plausible-looking wrong number rather than a crash.

## 1. We could not prove the model version, and I said we could

`canonical_slug` on every record is read from **config** and echoed back, never from the response. I previously reported those dated slugs as "read back from 1,989 calls", as empirical confirmation. **That was wrong** — they were our own config reflected at us.

The gap is invisible by construction: the response body carries only the **moving pointer** (`qwen/qwen3.8-flash`), never the dated snapshot; `served_provider` is unchanged by a version roll, so the existing pin assertion can't see it. A mid-study repoint would split the run across two models.

The catalog does expose it, and all four currently match config:

| model_id | canonical_slug |
|---|---|
| `openai/gpt-5.6-luna` | `openai/gpt-5.6-luna-20260709` |
| `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash` | `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash-20260826` |
| `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash` | `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-20260910` |
| `qwen/qwen3.8-flash` | `qwen/qwen3.8-flash-20260826` |

`assert_canonical_slugs()` runs from **`resolve_models`** — the one chokepoint every live run passes through — and **fails closed** if the catalog can't be read. Live:

```
[version-check] gpt-luna -> openai/gpt-5.6-luna-20260709
```

## 2. Per call: the model that answered is the model requested

Across **2,075 real calls** this field was the requested slug every time, so a mismatch is an anomaly. It immediately caught a test fixture pairing a real captured `nex-n2.5-pro` response with an unrelated `model_id` — a shape that cannot occur live.

## 3. The core phase drew from a different pool than everything else

`core` loaded the full **909-task** dataset while the gate, pilot and frontier all used the **200-task sample**. Two things break at that boundary:

- `free_tasks.json`, the no-op manifest `select_gate_tasks` subtracts, was measured on the sample only — drawing from 909 selects tasks whose no-op status was never established, reintroducing the floor the discriminating draw exists to remove.
- Every `--expected-accuracy` and every neutral baseline lives in the sample.

Measured live as a Luna core run started: its draw of 50 from 909 overlapped the n=100 gate sample by **2 tasks**; only 6 of 50 were in the sample at all. **48 of 50 tone comparisons would have had no baseline.** Caught 48 seconds in because the startup line read `50 of 909`; the run was stopped after 7 calls and $0.0074.

Drawn from the sample, the same seed gives a 50-task draw sitting **entirely inside** the gate's 100 — every task already has a measured neutral baseline. `--full-dataset` is now an explicit opt-in that warns what it forfeits.

## 4. Dry runs wrote into live files

`--dry-run` mocks every model but used the same filenames. A mock `core` invocation left **48 fabricated rows** in `study2_core_gpt-luna.jsonl`; the next live run announced it was resuming its budget from them and would have analysed them as real. Caught by that resume line on a file that should have been empty.

Dry runs now get their own tag across every artifact. One mock model marks the whole run. The unnamespaced "most recent gate" alias is never written from a dry run.

## 5. A stray run can no longer destroy a report

Self-inflicted: a `--n-tasks 1` smoke run overwrote the completed **100-task GLM report**, which survived only because a compact copy had been committed minutes earlier in #28. The gate now refuses to replace a larger run's report with a smaller one's — **checked before the run**, so a refusal costs no spend — with `--force-overwrite` as the escape hatch. The GLM report is restored and its 3 stray calls trimmed; per-turn diagnostics for that run are not recoverable, every reported number is.

Also: `.gitignore` covered `results/analysis/*.json` but never gained the `.jsonl` line the crash-durability work added, so every live run left an untracked file changing every few seconds.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest -q` — **223 passed** (up from 209)
- [x] 14 new tests: version match/drift/vanished/unreadable-catalog, response served as a different model, core sample nests inside the gate sample, a bigger pool gives a different draw, every phase defaults to the sample, dry-run tags don't collide with live ones, report-shrink guard and its escape hatch
- [x] Verified live: version check prints the observed slug, the shrink guard refuses before any task runs, the relaunched core run reports `50 of 200` and writes only `openai_compatible` rows

author: utkudenizaltiok
body:
## What this PR does

The app on top of #2098: a gym log book you tap through between sets, with the phone face-down on a bench.

**Built and used in four real gym sessions on a WHOOP 5.0, and every one of them changed the design.** Three of the four findings were *silent wrong data* rather than anything that looked broken — those are described below, because they are the part of this work worth reviewing.

### Why this belongs in NOOP rather than in a standalone lifting app

NOOP already knows what a session **cost** you: it measures heart rate throughout and derives strain from it. What it has never known is what you **did** — which movement, how heavy, how many, how long you actually rested. Those halves only mean anything together, and they only come together in an app that owns both the strap and the log.

Three things follow that a standalone tracker cannot do:

1. **A logged session becomes a real `workout` row**, so it lands in Workouts, Today and Effort like any other training — and the engine then fills its strain from the heart rate the strap **measured** over that window. No lifting app that isn't talking to the band has that measurement.
2. **The strap is an input device.** A double-tap on the band advances the set, so the phone can stay face-down between sets. One buzz confirms the tap registered — with the phone face-down there is otherwise no way to know it did — and three buzzes mean the rest is nearly up. **A whole session can be run without looking at the phone at all.** That only works if the app is already paired to the strap.
3. **It stays offline and on-device**, like everything else here. No account, no server, no sync.

### What it is

**Programs.** Build one once ("Upper A") and reuse it: a name plus an ordered list of exercise lines carrying targets — exercise, working sets, reps, weight, rest, and a free-text technique cue.

**Custom exercises, no catalogue.** NOOP ships **no** exercise list and **no** exercise→muscle mapping. You type whatever you call a movement and it is remembered with the muscle group *you* gave it. A shipped catalogue silently mis-attributes everything it fails to recognise, and per-exercise weightings ("bench = 0.7 triceps") have no published table behind them — inventing one makes every downstream figure fiction wearing the costume of precision.

**The session is a sheet, not a wizard.** Every set of every exercise is a row, and any pending set can be started at any time. The first version walked the plan strictly in order, and a real gym killed it: when a machine is occupied you move on and come back.

### The three silent-data findings, because they are the interesting part

**Finishing a set moves to the next set of the SAME exercise**, falling back to plan order only once that exercise is done. Plan order alone sent the user back to the machine they had just walked away from, after every single set.

**A completed set records the numbers it was showing.** The grey values on a pending row are a plan — this exercise earlier in the session, then last session, then the program's target — and completing the set commits exactly those. The first version recorded nothing unless you typed: 19 sets were completed against visible "50 kg × 10" placeholders and every one saved with weight and reps NIL. Silence is not the conservative choice when the alternative is losing the measurement. **RPE is never carried** — it is knowable only after a set, and inventing it would make the coverage card report every set as rated.

**Typing into a set you are not currently doing was silently discarded**, because the write path could only edit a set that already had a record. The field looked like it accepted the value until focus left. Numbers are now held and applied when the set is recorded — but typing still never *creates* a set, or a set nobody performed becomes data.

**The session outlives its screen.** Swiping the sheet down minimises it to a bar above the tab bar; the clock, the strap gesture and the buzzes keep running, and it is on the Lock Screen as a Live Activity.

### Six figures, no invented score

Volume load, Foster session load (sRPE × duration), work-vs-rest measured from the taps, Epley 1RM, RPE coverage, and fractional sets per muscle against the reference band. Every one is arithmetic the user can redo by hand from the sets on the same screen. There is deliberately **no composite "workout score"** — one invented number feels satisfying and tells you nothing about what to change. **Effort is never modified:** a session saves `strain: nil` and the engine fills it from measured HR.

### Relationship to `MuscleGroups` (#1968)

#1968 landed a name-derived matcher over a 13-group vocabulary, and its own header records the open seam: *"published attribution wins where a source provides it and this matcher is the fallback for the sources that do not."*

**This feature is a source that provides it.** The classification here is not derived from a name — the user assigns it once per exercise, and it is snapshotted onto every set at log time. So by #1968's own stated reconciliation these two do not compete: stored attribution wins for sets logged in NOOP, and the matcher remains the fallback for Hevy and Liftosaur imports, which carry no classification of their own.

The two vocabularies are different granularities on purpose — 20 groups here because the reference doses are measured at that resolution, 13 there because that is what a name can honestly support. The lossy 20→13 bridge #1968 says "waits for a consumer" is a judgement call rather than a transcription, and I would rather write it as its own PR with the mapping argued than smuggle it into this one.

### Deliberately absent

No acute:chronic workload ratio and no injury-risk or overtraining warning (disputed construct, and NOOP is not a medical device). No frequency score (negligible independent effect on hypertrophy). Nothing renders as COMPLETE — the evidence gives a hypertrophy floor of about 4 sets/week and **no** ceiling, so a full bar or a success-green would claim something the science does not support.

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / cleanup
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] CI / tooling

## How it was tested

**On real hardware — a WHOOP 5.0, across four gym sessions.** That is the only way the strap gesture, the Live Activity, and the values carried between sessions could be tested at all. Everything strap-dependent is confirmed working: the double-tap advancing a set with its confirming buzz, the three-buzz rest warning, the Lock Screen activity showing live HR and reps × weight with ticking seconds, and ghost values carrying across sessions.

**One commit touches shared BLE code**, and it is read-side only. `FrameRouter` now de-duplicates `DOUBLE_TAP` on the event's own `event_timestamp`: one physical gesture reached the app twice — live, and again when the strap offloaded its banked event log, because `dispatchLiveGestureIfFresh` accepts any event inside the 45-second live window, and `AppModel.handleDoubleTap`'s 1.2 s debounce cannot catch a replay landing seconds later. With the Lift Log claiming the gesture, the phantom silently advanced the session and cost a logged set. **No new writes, no change to the connection path or the window**, and it benefits every double-tap consumer rather than only this feature. Verified over two full sessions on hardware: previously frequent enough to be reported as a defect, now one ambiguous occurrence in the first session and none clearly attributable in the second. 4 unit tests cover the replay case.

**Automated:** `swift test` — WhoopStore 579, StrandAnalytics 2000, StrandImport 317, WhoopProtocol 704, all 0 failures. `xcodebuild … test` on macOS — 1823 tests; the only failures are two pre-existing `TodayCarryOverTests` that compare a US date format and fail identically on a clean checkout of `main` on this machine (English language, German region). **Both app targe

author: snkmcb
body:
The start of `v0.7.0`, ahead of `v0.6.0` for the reason `v0.5.0` was: this is
code, and the consumer integration is waiting on a gigabyte fixture and a host.
Three of phase 7's rows — the bounds §10 of the design policy names and the tree
did not enforce, and the per-stage configuration surface that lets a host state
them for one stage rather than for the whole process.

## What it does

**A bound on the response header block** (`660925b`). 64 KiB per exchange,
summed across interim `1xx` responses and counted in the transport before a line
is stored. With the caller's buffer already bounding the body, that is the whole
of §10.1's "bound the response header block and the total response size". A
response abandoned at the bound is refused whole, as `InvalidResponse`, whatever
its status — its status line arrived intact, and an open that took
`Content-Length` and `Accept-Ranges` from the prefix that fit would be acting on a
response nobody finished receiving. The corpus gains a nineteenth row,
`OversizedHeaders`, and the redirect-hop scheme allowlist gets the explicit case
implementation-status.md said it was owed.

**A destination policy** (`856ff4e`, `e6e8768`), `USD_HTTP_RESOLVER_DESTINATIONS`:
a set of address classes — `public`, `private`, `loopback`, `link-local`,
`metadata` — a connection may reach. The default is `public,private,loopback`:
loopback and intranet hosts are what `http` is registered for, and link-local
and the well-known instance-metadata endpoints are refused — the latter a class
of its own, by value, because AWS's IPv6 endpoint is unique-local and Alibaba's
is in the shared address space. It is judged three times — at connect time, in
`CURLOPT_OPENSOCKETFUNCTION`, against the address a name actually resolved to;
before each request, against the host as libcurl's own URL parser will send it,
which is what holds through a proxy; and at every redirect hop against a
canonical literal. IPv4-mapped, -compatible, and NAT64 addresses are the class
of the IPv4 address they carry. A refusal is `AccessDenied` naming the class,
unsent and unretried. libcurl is also told `http,https` and nothing else.

**Per-stage configuration through `ArResolverContext`** (`9bf6459`, `e6e8768`):

```python
ctx = Ar.GetResolver().CreateContextFromString(
    "https", "USD_HTTP_RESOLVER_DESTINATIONS=public; USD_HTTP_RESOLVER_MAX_RETRIES=0")
stage = Usd.Stage.Open("https://example.org/scenes/main.usda", ctx)
```

The environment's own names and parser, so a value in a context is refused or
adjusted for exactly the reasons it would be in the environment, and kept as
the parser read it so that equivalent spellings are one context. The
environment is snapshot at the resolver's first use and a context resolves
against it: context, then environment, then default. No header of this
repository reaches a host that configures it this way.

## What the review found (`e6e8768`)

A `/code-review` pass over the first three commits found the same shape of
defect four times: a guarantee that held in the case written for it and not the
one beside it. Each is closed, and each fix has a case that fails without it.

- **Through a proxy, a non-canonical spelling walked past the policy.** The
  connect is the proxy's, and libcurl normalizes `2852039166` to
  `169.254.169.254` before the proxy reads it. The host is now judged as
  libcurl will send it; `usdAssetHttp_destination_policy` uses the fixture
  server as the proxy, and with the check removed four of five spellings reach
  it.
- **Refusing link-local did not refuse the metadata endpoints outside it**, so
  those became the `metadata` class.
- **OpenUSD's scoped cache keyed `Resolve` by path**, walking past a per-stage
  policy the way the layer registry had. The bundle declares
  `implementsScopedCaches` and keys the scope's cache by configuration. Asset
  info had the same gap and now answers from memory only for a caller whose
  policy could have reached the asset.
- **Implementing contexts means being constructed in every process that opens
  any stage.** The constructor had configured the persistent tier, creating its
  directory for local-only hosts. Construction now does nothing and
  configuration happens at first use; a local-only child process is asserted to
  leave no directory behind.

Smaller, in the same pass: no retry of an abandoned header block behind a
`503`; line breaks trimmed from a destination list instead of falling back to
the wider default; context adjustments judged over the environment; the Python
conversion under the GIL and no other lock; the context type out of OpenUSD's
namespace; close-on-exec sockets; dead getenv entry points removed.

## Things worth reviewing

**The header bound was not optional.** With it removed, libcurl 8.7.1 opens an
asset behind a megabyte of ordinary header fields; the library's ceilings are on
a single line, and a block of kilobyte lines never reaches them. With libcurl's
own `CURLE_TOO_LARGE` reclassified as something else, the row still passes, so
the refusal is this code's.

**Only the connect-time check stops a name.** Removing it leaves every literal
case passing and lets `localhost` through a policy that refuses loopback.
`usdAssetHttp_destination_policy`'s name case is the one test that fails, which
is what it is there for.

**Every identifier this resolver owns is now context-dependent.** Not because it
resolves to a different path under two contexts, but because whether it resolves
at all can — and OpenUSD's layer registry acts on the answer. For a path that is
not context-dependent, `SdfLayer::FindOrOpen` finds an already-loaded layer by
identifier whatever `Resolve` has just said, so a stage whose context refuses a
destination would be handed the layer by any stage that opened the URL first.
Answering `false` fails exactly the `stillRefused` case in `httpResolver_stage`.
The only other reader of that answer in OpenUSD is `usdUtils` packaging, which
sends URI paths down its remap path either way.

**The retained opens are keyed by transport options as well as identifier.**
Correct keyed by identifier while one process had one configuration; a reader
keeps the options it was opened with, and keyed by identifier alone the refusing
context in `TestRetainedOpenIsNotHandedAcrossContexts` got a reader a permissive
resolve had left behind.

**The metadata list is a list.** Eight addresses, by value, documented in
CONFIGURATION.md §2.1. It is the one piece of provider-specific knowledge in
the policy, and the alternative — calling link-local "the metadata endpoint" —
was true of one address out of eight.

**Four variables are not settable per stage.** The block size, the two budgets,
and the persistent directory stay the environment's, although the roadmap's
v0.7.0 scope lists block size and budgets among what a context resolves. Every
stage shares the store they configure, and the store's stripes are sized for one
block size — eight blocks to a stripe, 2 MiB at the defaults — so a stage asking
for larger blocks would fetch each one and watch it evicted on arrival. A context
naming one is told so when it is created. This is a judgement call and the place
to disagree with it.

**A Python conversion in the bundle.** Without one, `ctx.Get()` raised
`TypeError: No to_python (by-value) converter found`, and `Usd.Stage.__repr__`
printed `pathResolverContext=<invalid repr>`. The context converts to its
canonical string, registered once Python is running. It uses the vendored
`pxr_boost::python` that `tf` already links, under `PXR_PYTHON_SUPPORT_ENABLED`.

## Tests

- `usdAssetHttp_destination` — address classification as a table: every class
  boundary from both sides, the metadata endpoints and their neighbours, the
  mapped/compatible/NAT64 spellings, and the non-canonical forms left to the
  transport.
- `usdAssetHttp_destination_policy` — the client-side and connect-time halves
  over a real socket, through `localhost`, `127.1`, and a proxy.
- `usdAssetHttp_protoco

author: baslack
body:
### Problem

Deleting a node that is wired into a wildcard-typed `Switch (Any)` (`ImpactSwitch`) throws in the browser and aborts the delete partway through:

```
TypeError: target_node.findInputSlot is not a function
    at ComfyNode.connect
    at nodeType.onConnectionsChange (impact-pack.js:639)
    at ComfyNode.onConnectionsChange
    at ComfyNode.disconnectInput
    at LGraph.remove
    at LGraphCanvas.deleteSelected
```

Reproduced on ComfyUI 0.34.0 with `comfyui-frontend-package` 1.49.6.

### Cause

`js/impact-pack.js:639` calls:

```js
node.connect(link_info.origin_slot, node.id, 'input1');
```

This was valid when litegraph node ids were numbers: `connect()` resolves a legacy id form via `getNodeById()`.

In current ComfyUI_frontend, `NodeId` is a string-branded type and `LGraphNode.id` is always a string. `connect()` still guards that legacy path with `typeof target_node === 'number'`, so a string id falls through unresolved and is then used as if it were a node, producing the `TypeError`.

### Fix

Pass the node object directly. This restores the previous behaviour exactly, since the numeric id resolved to this same node.

### Why it is worth fixing promptly

The throw is not contained by the caller. It escapes `LGraph.remove()` and `LGraphCanvas.deleteSelected()`, which emits its `before-change` / `after-change` pair without a `try`/`finally`. The closing event never fires, so the editor's change-transaction counter stays raised. From that point on, for the rest of the browser session, the frontend silently stops recording undo history, stops persisting drafts, and stops flushing canvas state before a workflow tab switch or save. The visible result is lost work with no error beyond the initial toast.

I am filing that containment gap separately against ComfyUI_frontend. This PR only addresses the call that throws.

### Note for the maintainer

I kept this minimal and behaviour-preserving. It is possible the intended target was the switch node (`this`) rather than the origin node, which would make this branch actually reconnect the link to `input1` instead of being an effective no-op. I did not change that, since you would know the intent. Happy to adjust if so.

author: sphamandla-designer
body:
## Summary

Home page follow-up to #45. Adds the uploaded GEMIS logo, introduces a **Products** mega menu, and removes the "Our Team" section. Scoped to `index.html`, `home.css` and `home.js` — every other page is untouched.

## Changes

### Our Team — removed
Section, its stylesheet block, and the footer link to it. The freed footer slot became a **Products** column (ManaGem / Gemis Tech / Design Studio).

### Years figure
`12+` confirmed correct and left unchanged — consistent with "trusted since 2014" and "over a decade" in `about.html`.

### Products mega menu
A new top-level item that expands a full-width panel beneath the header.

| Product | Links to |
|---|---|
| ManaGem | `managem.html` |
| Gemis Tech | `services.html` |
| Design Studio | `brand-studio.html` |

Each entry carries an image, heading, description and a pill CTA.

- Opens on hover (pointer devices only), click, or keyboard focus; closes on Escape, outside click, focus-out, or scroll.
- A close delay lets the cursor travel diagonally from the trigger into the panel.
- The header leaves its transparent state while the panel is open — otherwise the logo and links sit navy-on-blue.
- The panel is nested inside its own `<li>` so it resolves full-bleed against the fixed header on desktop, and expands inline under "Products" in the mobile drawer.
- New menu imagery cropped to a consistent 16:10 from existing project shots.

### Logo
The upload (`Link (1).png`) is 187×34 — the gem mark is roughly 17px across, too small to scale cleanly. It is vectorised to `assets/img/logos/gemis-logo.svg`: the gem silhouette, its inner ring and the type are each traced from the source and emitted as paths.

The paths fill with `currentColor` and ship as a single inlined `<symbol>`, so the logo inherits whatever its context sets — white over the hero and photographic bands, navy on paper and in the footer, with a drop-shadow only where it sits over imagery.

## Notes for review

Two bugs surfaced and were fixed while building this, both worth knowing about:

- **Focus/click conflict** — a pointer press focuses the trigger *before* the click event, so the focus handler opened the panel just in time for the click handler to toggle it shut. Opening on focus is now gated on `:focus-visible`, wrapped in try/catch for older engines.
- **Selector leakage** — with the panel nested inside a `.nav__links` item, the mobile nav-link rules (19px, ink) were reaching the product links inside it. Those rules are now scoped to direct children.

## Verification

Rendered and driven in Chromium at 1440 / 768 / 390px:

- No console or page errors; no failed requests
- Logo legible in all four header states (over hero, scrolled on paper, over the blue band, panel open) and in the footer
- Menu verified on desktop hover, desktop click, touch tap and keyboard, plus Escape and outside-click dismissal
- Mobile drawer accordion expands under "Products" with Work/Contact following below
- 40/40 scroll reveals fire; stat counters reach 12+ / 50+ / 5+
- All internal links and image paths resolve; no horizontal overflow at any width

body:
## Summary

Enforces a strict offline runtime without deleting existing app files or modifying `glance.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj`. Existing camera capture, Vision/Core ML, Keychain, Accessibility/keystroke, onboarding, and face-recognition behavior is preserved.

## Network-related code / external links removed

- `glance/Updater/UpdaterController.swift`
  - Removed Sparkle runtime updater behavior by replacing the updater with a source-compatible local no-op shim.
  - `start()` and `checkForUpdates()` cannot initiate network traffic.
- `glance/Info.plist`
  - Removed `SUFeedURL = https://tryglance.app/appcast.xml`, Sparkle public key, and update configuration.
- `glance/Settings/Pages/AboutSettingsPage.swift`
  - Removed `https://tryglance.app/feedback` external link.
  - Removed manual and automatic update controls; replaced with static `Strict offline mode` text.

## Final offline audit

The CI workflow now contains a permanent runtime-source audit. It fails if Swift runtime sources introduce common networking/update/telemetry mechanisms including `URLSession`, `URLRequest`, `NSURLConnection`, Network.framework/NW* APIs, CFNetwork/socket host APIs, WebKit, Sparkle imports, common telemetry/network SDKs, curl/wget execution, or HTTP(S) string literals. It also fails if network client/server entitlements or Sparkle network plist keys are reintroduced.

One audit hit was reviewed and determined to be comment-only: an MIT attribution URL in `NotchSkyLight.swift`. The guard was narrowed to HTTP(S) Swift string literals so source-license comments do not create false positives.

Final macOS 15 CI result for head `a45197dff08ee5e9f49fbe714e5064cab8595b6d`:

- Offline runtime audit: **passed**
- Xcode version check: **passed**
- Unsigned Debug `xcodebuild`: **passed**
- `CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO`
- `CODE_SIGNING_REQUIRED=NO`

## Files changed

1. `.github/workflows/build-check.yml` — macOS 15 unsigned build validation plus persistent offline-source audit.
2. `glance/Updater/UpdaterController.swift` — runtime updater replaced by no-op implementation.
3. `glance/Settings/Pages/AboutSettingsPage.swift` — removed update and external feedback entry points.
4. `glance/Info.plist` — removed Sparkle endpoint/update configuration.
5. `glance/glanceApp.swift` — `AppDelegate` marked `@MainActor` for Xcode 16.4 actor-isolation correctness.
6. `glance/CameraDeviceCatalog.swift` — `resolvedDevice()` marked `@MainActor` for camera-settings actor isolation.

## Entitlements / project-file verification

- `glance/glance.entitlements` retains only the existing Keychain access group and camera entitlement; it contains neither `com.apple.security.network.client` nor `com.apple.security.network.server`.
- `glance.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj` was **not modified**.
- No existing app file was deleted.
- Branch is based on `main` and is 0 commits behind.

## Build-time dependency note

The Xcode project still contains the pre-existing Sparkle Swift Package reference because `project.pbxproj` was explicitly out of scope. `Package.resolved` pins Sparkle 2.9.6, so a clean Xcode/CI build may access GitHub to resolve that dependency. The compiled application does not start Sparkle, check for updates, declare a Sparkle feed URL, or expose update/feedback network entry points. This is a build/supply-chain dependency, not an application runtime communication path.

body:
Studio was mixing three font-size scales (DS `ui-*`/`header-*` tokens, Tailwind `text-xs…4xl`, arbitrary `text-[10px]`/`text-[11px]`) with line-heights that didn't match the sizes. The same 12px text could render with a different rhythm depending on which class a component happened to use, and headings at the same semantic level ranged from 12px to 30px across pages. This moves everything onto the existing DS tokens. In `theme.css` the Tailwind utilities are now aliased to the token sizes, and every token carries its paired line-height, so `text-ui-md` alone gives the right leading. All `text-xs/sm/…` and `text-[Npx]` classes in both packages are migrated to `text-ui-*`/`text-header-*`, redundant `leading-*` overrides are dropped, and headings follow one convention (h1 → `header-md`, hero → `header-xl`, section h2 → `header-sm`, panel h3 → `ui-md`). Chart tick sizes and inline `rem` values in code views/dialogs now read from tokens too. Before: ```tsx

Skills

meta ``` After: ```tsx

Skills

meta ``` An eslint `no-restricted-syntax` rule in both packages now rejects non-token sizes so this doesn't drift back. `ee/signals/*` still uses `text-[10px]` and is excluded from the rule for a separate follow-up. Test plan: build, typecheck, lint and tests pass on `@mastra/playground-ui` and `@internal/playground`; control greps for Tailwind sizes and arbitrary px are empty outside `ee/`. A visual pass is still worth doing on dense areas whose height depends on line-height (sidebar, table rows, command palette) since ex-`text-xs` blocks go from 16px to 18px leading.

author: scottdraves
body:
Depends on **e-dream-ai/python-api#56** for `find_keyframe_by_name` and `link_keyframe_to_playlist`.

## The "horrible" bit

`assure_keyframe` scanned the playlist's keyframe list once per name, under a comment that said so:

```python
# i would love to have a query API to find by name. it should exist
# because the feed UI does this, but since that's not obvious, i'm
# going to just search the keyframes in this playlist sequentially
# which is horrible but should work.
```

On Meditations that is 279 sheep × 2 names × 399 keyframes ≈ 220k comparisons, growing with the square of the playlist. Now the list is indexed by name once.

The query API does exist — `GET /keyframe?search=&userUUID=` — it just was not in the SDK. It is now.

## Stray keyframes

The lookup only ever consulted *the playlist*, so a keyframe that existed but was not linked to it was invisible and the script minted another. Runs that died between creating a keyframe and linking it left exactly those — Meditations currently has three strays named `00248=42856` from the run that hit the backend 500.

Resolution is now cheapest-first: playlist index → backend name query → create. A dry run on Meditations reports `would_link: 1` for that stray instead of making a fourth copy.

## Structure

Three passes — parse, resolve keyframes, update dreams — so the two that touch the network run on a small thread pool (`--jobs`, default 4) instead of one blocking roundtrip per dream. Each call retries with backoff; a failure is reported and counted rather than killing the run and leaving the playlist half-linked, and the exit status is non-zero if anything failed.

## Also

- `--dry-run`
- `--flock-begin` to override `FLOCK_BEGIN_INDEX`
- errors out when no playlist uuid is given, instead of requesting `/playlist/None`
- a run summary rather than a line per dream
- guards for dreams with unparseable or non-numeric sheep ids
- the dead `if False:` delete-everything block is gone

## Verification

Dry run against alpha's Meditations playlist:

```
playlist Generation 248: Meditations: 2260 items, 399 named keyframes
279 sheep in range, 1 keyframes to resolve

would change:
  would_link: 1
  would_update: 5
  already_linked: 274
  below_flock_begin: 1981
```

The write path is exercised against `api-stage` in the SDK PR (`link_keyframe_to_playlist` reuses a keyframe across playlists; `add_keyframe_to_playlist` no longer strands one when the link fails). A full write run against alpha is still blocked on e-dream-ai/backend#492 reaching that environment — the endpoint this script needs is the one that regressed.

README and AGENTS.md are left alone here to stay clear of the unpushed `export_genomes.py` commit on `main`; happy to document the new flags in a follow-up.

author: dennisonbertram
body:
First slice of #158. Part of #152. Builds on #176.

**#158 stays open** — this is steps 1–2 (approval identity). Cancellation truthfulness and the channel bridge seams are not here; see "What remains" below.

## The problem

An approval can be answered long after it was asked. Eve's docs are explicit that a structured response may resume an older request after intervening turns, and that plain follow-up text starts an ordinary new turn while approvals stay pending. So two things must be impossible: a stale answer authorising a *different* action than the one a person saw, and a plain new turn silently spending a parked approval.

## What landed

`agent/lib/approval-identity.ts` reduces the authorised action to a fingerprint and decides whether an answer authorises what is now in hand. A resume is honoured only when the request id, the task, and the terms all still match; otherwise it is `terms_changed`, `wrong_task`, or `unknown`. A material change needs a fresh native approval — nothing here widens what can be approved.

The fingerprint derives from the approved fields only: `action`, `terms`, `origin`, `target_ref`, `target_token`.

**Payment and vault exclusion is structural, not a convention.** The declared contract has no place to put them, so a caller cannot route secret-adjacent material into a stored value even by accident. That is a change from my first draft, which used a generic `unknown` walker — the repo's lint rejected it, and it was right to: a typed contract over the known flat terms is both safer and simpler than a recursive canonicaliser.

`commit_browser_action.ts` puts that fingerprint in its commit receipt, so the root learns what was authorised from the tool that owns the approval rather than from prose.

## Verification

| | |
| --- | --- |
| `tests/agent/lib/approval-identity.test.ts` | `7 passed` (AP-01 … AP-07) |
| `tests/agent/subagents/browser-agent/tools/commit-browser-action.test.ts` | `20 passed` |
| `pnpm check` | `Tasks: 6 successful, 6 total` |
| `pnpm build` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm eval:contract` | `Results: 4 passed (4 total)` · `Gates: 98 passed` |
| `pnpm eval:square` | `Results: 13 passed (13 total)` · `Gates: 113 passed` |
| `git diff --check` | clean |

Square applies because the worker tool is in the diff, and it came back green first time.

Mutation checks, each applied alone then reverted:

| Mutation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| canonical key ordering removed | 1 failed |
| terms excluded from the fingerprint | 2 failed |
| origin excluded from the fingerprint | 1 failed |
| resume stops comparing terms | 1 failed |
| resume stops checking the task | 1 failed |
| resume accepts any request id | 1 failed |
| receipt drops the fingerprint | 1 failed |

One process note worth recording: two of these *initially* reported as survivors, because my perl patterns still targeted the pre-rewrite code shape and so never applied. I corrected the script and re-ran rather than reporting coverage I had not actually tested. A mutation that silently fails to apply looks exactly like a mutation that was caught.

AP-03 also changed honestly: it originally probed payment exclusion by passing an undeclared extra property, which the lint flagged as a useless spread. With exclusion now structural, there is nothing for a test to probe there, so AP-03 asserts what is still provable — the digest is opaque and carries no substantial term material back out. Short values like a quantity of `2` are excluded from that check, since any hex digest contains them by chance.

## What remains on #158

- **Step 3, cancellation and steering truthfulness.** Composing "cancelled after dispatch" versus "cancelled without dispatch" versus "outcome uncertain" from retained evidence, and never asserting rollback. That reads the #176 attempt record, so it belongs with the channel binding rather than ahead of it.
- **The channel bridge seams** in `agent/channels/linq.ts` and `agent/channels/sendblue.ts`, carrying identity metadata through their existing `input.requested` gates. Deliberately untouched: there is nothing to carry until the binding exists, and I am not creating a second approval engine.
- **Step 4, duplicate prose removal.** The plan requires first demonstrating with a RED that an authored instruction asks an equivalent prose confirmation before the native gate. I have not demonstrated that, so I have not edited any instruction. If the questions cover distinct terms, the plan says stop — and that determination has not been made.

author: lilred92
body:
# Update API models and improve error observability in commit generator

## Focus on the "Why"
This change updates the AI models used for automated commit message generation to ensure reliability and cost-efficiency, swapping the explicit Gemini model version to `gemini-flash-latest` and updating the fallback model to `openai/gpt-oss-120b`. 

Additionally, error handling and system observability have been heavily improved. Previously, API failures swallowed specific error codes or statuses, making debugging difficult. We now explicitly log HTTP response statuses and construct detailed error messages using API-specific error structures (`status`, `code`, `type`), speeding up the diagnosis of integration failures during local execution or CI/CD runs.

## The Big Picture
This change lives in the local tooling and development pipeline (`generate-commit.mjs`). It does not interact with the React frontend or PostgreSQL database, but ensures robust, self-healing, and highly observable developer tooling when generating automated commit messages prior to code submission.

## Related Issues
Closes #<issue_number>

## Testing Instructions
1. Pull this branch to your local environment.
2. Ensure you have your environment variables configured with valid Gemini and Groq API keys.
3. Run the commit generation script:
   ```bash
   node generate-commit.mjs
   ```
4. Verify that the output logs the status code (e.g., `Gemini responded with status 200`) and successfully generates the commit.
5. To test the error handling and fallback mechanics:
   * Temporarily invalidate your Gemini API Key.
   * Run `node generate-commit.mjs` again.
   * Verify that the terminal outputs a clear, detailed warning showing the Gemini API error status and message, followed by a successful fallback to the Groq model.

## Visual Proof
No frontend UI components were modified in this pull request.

## Risk Assessment
* **Model Availability**: The model `openai/gpt-oss-120b` is specified on the Groq endpoint. Ensure this model is fully supported on your Groq plan/routing layer to prevent fallback failures.
* No other major breaking changes or new external dependencies were introduced.

body:
## Context

**Related Ticket** [watchborne/charge-points-frontend#394](https://github.com/watchborne/charge-points-frontend/issues/394)

- `ChargePointDetailPanel` exposes several tabs (main/actions/consumption/sessions/alerts/security), and users tend to consistently open the same one for their workflow. Today every click into a station — or every fresh session — resets to a fixed default tab regardless of what a given user actually uses the panel for.

## Solution

- Persist the last-used tab in `localStorage` (`cp-detail-last-tab`) and apply it as the default when: (a) a user opens a different charge point, and (b) on a fresh mount when the tab wasn't otherwise deep-linked from the URL.
- A URL-deep-linked tab (`initialTab`, set from the `?tab=` query param) still always wins over the stored preference — a shared link keeps working exactly as before.
- No backend change: this is a client-only, per-browser preference (Phase 1 of the personalization plan — see the issue for the optional Phase 2 cross-device persistence).

## Testing strategy

### Unit tests
Added to `ChargePointDetailPanel.test.tsx`:
- persists the clicked tab to `localStorage`
- defaults to the stored tab when no `initialTab` is given
- `initialTab` still wins over a stored preference
- switching to a different charge point falls back to the stored tab instead of always "main"

All existing tests in the suite (16 total) still pass, including the Strict Mode regression test for `initialTab`.

### Local testing
- [ ] Open a station, switch to e.g. "Consumption", open a different station — confirm it also opens on "Consumption"
- [ ] Reload the page — confirm the last-used tab is still applied

body:
## Build Plan v2 — M2.6

Exercise interrupted bundle recovery with a real child process rather than a synthetic pre-written tail.

The fixture writes one complete record, replaces the active segment stream with a wrapper that durably writes only the first half of the next record, signals the parent, then blocks. The parent kills the child process at that boundary and verifies `DiagnosticBundleRecovery` returns only sequence 1 and reports a non-zero discarded partial tail.

This keeps production code unchanged and proves the existing recovery contract against an actual process interruption. Merge only after the exact head passes the full existing CI matrix.

author: arthurhughes27
body:
## Summary
Extends the same fallback already in place for the influenza timepoint and Ebola supplementary applications to `application_supplementary_FE.R` and `application_supplementary_geneset.R`: if screening on the split training data finds no significant markers, an evaluation stage on held-out test data isn't run. Instead, screening is re-run on the full (unsplit) data and interpreted as the final output.

- `application_supplementary_FE.R`: outputs `risemeta_tiv_screening_FE_fulldata.pdf` in the no-significant-markers case.
- `application_supplementary_geneset.R`: outputs `risemeta_screening_{BG3M,none}_fulldata.pdf`, evaluated independently per grid value (`BG3M`/`none`) inside the existing `for (val in grid)` loop.

Both scripts factor the duplicated `rise.screen.meta` call (split vs. full data) into a `run_screen()` helper, matching the pattern already used in `application_supplementary_ebola.R` and `R/run_influenza_timepoint_supplementary.R`.

## Test plan
- [ ] Run both scripts against real data and confirm each takes the correct branch (evaluation vs. full-data re-screen) based on `length(rise_screen_result$significant.markers)`.
- [ ] For the geneset script, confirm both grid values (`BG3M`, `none`) are handled independently — one could take the evaluation branch while the other falls back to full-data screening.

body:
## Description

Adds the two Phase 1/2 roadmap gaps flagged in the verification issue, on top of the already-merged implementation (PR #1).

author: veraspabienhoa
body:
The iPhone recording shows focus remaining on the service search after a service is selected, requiring another tap to open room selection.

Booking selections now advance through employee, customer/combo, service, room, request and notes. The next searchable dropdown opens on focus. Quantity controls are skipped, disabled or absent fields are skipped, and conflicting rooms retain focus for correction. Users can return to add further services. Typing alone never advances or submits the form.

Selection updates are committed before focus moves, within the original gesture for mobile keyboard access. Native selects attempt showPicker where supported and otherwise receive focus.

Validation: all 20 mounted UI/helper tests passed, including click/Enter advancement, room conflicts, and adding another service. ESLint has zero errors and three existing warnings. Production build passed. Actual iPhone keyboard/picker behavior has not been verified on a physical device.

Draft for review: direct publication to main was blocked by automatic approval review pending explicit authorization. This PR has not been merged or deployed.

author: selim-create
body:
## Amaç
Content Engine’in ilk AI üretim fazını ekler: `ready` candidate → kaynak metni zenginleştirme → OpenAI editoryal dönüşüm → WordPress `draft` post.

## Kapsam
- Yeni `Sektorel_Content_Detail_Extractor`
  - TOBB için resmi RSS özetini kullanır; başarısız detail-page zincirini geri getirmez.
  - TCMB için strict host allowlist ile güvenli detail fetch yapar.
  - timeout, redirect ve response-size limitleri vardır.
  - çıkarılan metni candidate `extracted_text` + evidence alanına kaydeder.
- Yeni `Sektorel_Content_AI_Draft_Processor`
  - yalnız `ready`, `draft_post_id=0`, `ai_status=pending|error` candidate işler.
  - tek manuel batch en fazla 5 candidate.
  - varsayılan günlük limit 20; `SEKTOREL_CONTENT_AI_DAILY_LIMIT` ile değiştirilebilir.
  - mevcut `SEKTOREL_OPENAI_API_KEY` ve `SEKTOREL_OPENAI_MODEL` sabitlerini kullanır.
  - OpenAI Responses API üzerinden yalnız verilen kaynak metniyle JSON editoryal çıktı ister.
  - çıktı başlık, excerpt, HTML içerik, kategori, tag ve SEO description içerir.
  - kategori yalnız deterministic triage’in izin verdiği slug listesinden seçilebilir.
  - post her zaman `draft`; otomatik publish yoktur.
  - candidate→post idempotency için `_sektorel_content_candidate_id` meta kullanır.
  - candidate üzerinde model/token/draft/evidence/lifecycle kaydı tutulur.
- Yeni `Sektorel_Content_AI_Draft_Admin`
  - Kaynak Merkezi’ne `5 Hazır Candidate'dan Taslak Üret` paneli ekler.
  - batch sonucu, draft/hata/atlanan/kalan ve günlük kullanım gösterilir.
- Bootstrap yalnız mevcut Content Engine facade içinde yapılır.

## Güvenlik / guardrails
- admin-only + nonce
- otomatik publish yok
- AI duplicate karar mekanizması değildir
- source text dışı bilgi üretmesi prompt ile yasaklanır
- TCMB fetch host allowlistlidir
- TOBB detail-page fetch geri getirilmez
- Event Engine’e dokunulmaz

## Production kabul testi
1. Merge + Core deploy.
2. Kaynak Merkezi’nde yeni AI panelinin görünmesini doğrula.
3. İlk testte yalnız 5 candidate çalıştır.
4. 5 candidate için draft oluşturulursa:
   - candidate `processed`
   - `ai_status=done`
   - `draft_post_id` dolu
   - WP yazısı `draft`
   - kategori/tag/meta/evidence mevcut
5. Aynı batch tekrar çalıştırıldığında aynı candidate için ikinci draft oluşmamalı.
6. Bir detail/OpenAI hatası olursa AI status/error alanında görünmeli; otomatik publish olmamalı.

author: vknotts-coder
body:
Lift the reportable-object + list-view catalog out of fcr-dispatch into the
shared package so every app shares one fcr_core-coupled source of truth instead
of copy-pasting it. New subpaths:

- @fcr/core/catalog/truck    truckObject(opts) + truckFields
- @fcr/core/catalog/trailer  trailerObject(opts) + trailerFields
- @fcr/core/catalog/listviews  LIST_VIEWS + helpers (pure data/logic)
- @fcr/core/catalog          barrel

The object factories inject the app-specific half — `capability` (the object
gate, REQUIRED and never defaulted since the permission model is Module 1 /
unscoped) and `link`/`linkEnabled` (app routing) — while baking the schema half
(table/join/baseWhere/fields). Field tables copied verbatim from dispatch for
byte-identical behavior. 10 faithfulness tests pin the schema coupling.

Rebased onto v0.4.2 (includes the #103 reports-engine fixes). Minor bump to
0.5.0 (additive). Part of #107 (sibling of #59).

author: alexedmon1
body:
## Summary

- **A failed or timed-out R statistics step now fails the run** (`RStepFailed`, exit 1). A paradigm-wide run finishes its other modules first, then lists what failed.
- **No default R time limit.** Limits were hard-coded at 3600 s, or 600 s for the electrode and evoked modules. `r_timeout_sec` in a module's config block sets one.
- **`roi_cross_freq`** attempts PAC and AAC/PPC before failing, so one tier failing no longer costs the other its tables.
- **PAC mosaics are drawn.** The call named columns the native table doesn't have, so none was ever drawn. The figures pass now draws them.

## Why

On the FORGE treatment re-run (v0.7.0), four R steps were killed at exactly 3600 s, logged, and **exited 0**:

| step | arm(s) | effect |
|---|---|---|
| `roi_directed` | cartesian MC, shell MC, ROI-based | region tier left at the pre-fix 8 categories (or never written) |
| `roi_cross_freq` AAC/PPC | cartesian MC | `…_aac_region_hypotheses.csv` left at 8 categories |

author: reif-y
body:
## What this does
When the automated bug-filer checked GitHub to see if a problem was already reported and that
check itself failed (a busy moment, a rate limit), it used to shrug and assume "nothing's
there" — then file a brand-new duplicate report. That happened for real today: two duplicate
issues (#911, #912) had to be found and closed by hand. Now, when that check can't run, the
filer skips that item and says so, instead of guessing and cluttering the board.

## How fits the number
Guardrail: the backlog board has to say what's really there — a filer that turns a transient
API error into a duplicate issue corrupts the one artifact gru, marie and a human all rank
from. (Marie's PRD comment on #914.)

## How verified
- `python3 -m unittest scripts.test_journey_issue_filer` — 33/33 pass, including 6 new tests
  covering every acceptance criterion (sentinel distinguishability, no-file-on-lookup-failure,
  the working no-match/has-match paths unchanged, one failed key not aborting the rest).
- `python3 scripts/selftest.py` — new check `journey_issue_filer never files a duplicate when
  the dedup lookup itself fails (gh#914)` passes; confirmed it FAILS against the pre-fix code
  on `main` (files issue #999 in the test's stub) before this change, and passes after.
- The other 10 selftest failures in this run (`ZoneInfoNotFoundError` on `control_plane`
  checks, an unrelated `ask.py` NTFY rate-limit test) are pre-existing and untouched by this
  diff — confirmed by `git diff --stat`, which shows only `journey_issue_filer.py`,
  `selftest.py`, and `test_journey_issue_filer.py` changed.

## What changed
`scripts/journey_issue_filer.py`:
- Added `LOOKUP_FAILED`, a sentinel `find_open_issue()` now returns when `gh issue list` exits
  non-zero or returns unparsable JSON — distinct from the `None` a genuine no-match returns.
- `process()` checks for `LOOKUP_FAILED` in both the fail-branch (file/comment) and pass-branch
  (close) paths; on it, files/comments/closes nothing for that key and appends
  `{"key": ..., "reason": "lookup_failed"}` to a new `summary["skipped"]` list, then continues
  to the next key.
- `main()` prints a stderr line naming how many keys were skipped when the board couldn't be
  read, so a sentry-pass report shows the run was degraded rather than clean.

`scripts/test_journey_issue_filer.py`: new `LookupFailureTest` class, 6 tests, one per
acceptance criterion.

`scripts/selftest.py`: new regression check `_filer_lookup_failure_never_files_a_duplicate_gh914`.

Non-goals kept out of scope per marie's PRD: no retry/backoff against rate limits, no change to
the dedup key scheme, no touch to `ensure_label()`'s `--repo` handling (that's #922), and no
auto-closing of #911/#912 (already done by hand).

See it: (internal)

Fixes #914

author: atomantic
body:
Unreadable media and sprite JSON now stops durable state mutations instead of replacing stored records with empty defaults. Existing initialization, compatibility normalization, backend routing, and write queues remain intact.

## Storage classification

| Owned module / path | Classification and decision |
| --- | --- |
| `imageTo3d/sourceKeying.js`: prepared metadata | Rebuildable cache. Source bytes plus the explicit keying/framing request regenerate the image and metadata; non-strict fallback remains documented beside the read. |
| `mediaAnnotations.js`: annotation state | Durable write-back. Local edits and peer merges preserve existing author entries; strict read before persistence. |
| `mediaSketches.js`: per-key sketch JSON | No write-back cycle. The read only projects the canvas; save replaces the complete canvas from explicit input, and erase explicitly removes it. Non-strict read is documented. |
| `sprites/atlas.js`: runtime pointer | Durable geometry/provenance. Strict pointer reads preserve the geometry the user compiled and publish reuses. Surviving version manifests also read strictly before immutable output recovery. |
| `sprites/localAnimationJobHook.js`: animation run record | Durable write-back. Retry stamps the new job ID while preserving the run; unreadable records reject before staging or attachment. |
| `sprites/publish.js`: publications and pointer | Durable write-back. Strict history read preserves prior destinations and code-binding baselines; strict pointer read stops a fallback compile from losing custom geometry. |
| `sprites/recordsFile.js`: sprite catalog | Durable file adapter. Strict read protects create/update/delete/import; PostgreSQL routing is unchanged. |
| `sprites/reference.js`: candidate generation sidecars | No same-record write-back cycle: generation writes a new candidate name. Read-only listing retains documented fallback. Approval reads existing provenance strictly so unreadable data cannot bypass the target guard. The related reference manifest is durable and now reads strictly before edits. Catalog-only projections isolate unreadable manifests without passing their fallback into any write. |
| `sprites/walk.js`: walk set and selection | Durable approval/finalization and per-track targets; strict reads prevent reseeding or bypassing frozen evidence. Related mutable run records also read strictly. Redraw/source-frame projections and validated immutable postprocess evidence have documented no-write-back fallbacks. |
| `youtubeIngest.js`: ingest index | Durable write-back. Strict shared loader protects index additions, updates, and deletion while retaining other video entries. |

## Validation

- 385 tests pass across 12 focused server suites: annotations, sketches, media write-back boundaries, YouTube ingest, source keying, sprite records, reference, walk, atlas, publish, local animation hook and its persistence boundary.
- Temporary-file regressions cover malformed, empty and whitespace JSON, injected EACCES, byte preservation, absent-file behavior, valid prior records, and retry after repair. Sprite workflow regressions cover geometry pointers, publication history, finalized walk sets, sibling animation targets, reference evidence, and local-render retries.
- No real database, live records, provider generation or external media tools used by the new tests.
- Release notes derive from the conventional commit; no per-branch changelog file is required.

## Optional review

Claude reviewed the branch diff with medium effort, tools disabled, plan permission mode, safe mode and no MCP servers. Its confirmed catalog-availability finding was fixed and covered by a focused regression; the repaired reference suite passes. The shared JSON reader already rejects non-array roots for array-backed stores, so that reported gap does not apply. Existing object compatibility normalizers remain unchanged as required by this issue. Atlas fixtures use file-level hooks; candidate listing versus strict approval is intentional and documented.

Closes #6976

author: jonmmease
body:
## Why

Core scenes need a vector export format for browsers and documents. This PR adds SVG export directly from `SceneGraph`.

## What

`avenger-svg` exports vector marks, gradients, clipping paths, layered patterns, native text, outlined math, and embedded images. Export can share the text engine used for layout and embeds its resolved font faces, preserving shaping tables and font collection indices. Text limits follow the core policy, including rotated Typst labels. Warped images retain the complete texture when raster resolution reaches its size cap.

Typographic scripts use the font-provided size and baseline. SVG uses the text engine’s outlines for runs that require explicit OpenType features or variable-font coordinates. This preserves their glyphs and spacing across viewers. Ordinary text and synthesized scripts remain native text.

Orange guides mark the expected clipping boundaries: a solid outline for the group clip and dashed lines for the text limits.

![SVG export gallery](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jonmmease/avenger/77c0c4889c49745e48446ccc15e4b165c0de5be2/docs/images/svg-gallery.png)

[Open the SVG](https://github.com/jonmmease/avenger/blob/77c0c4889c49745e48446ccc15e4b165c0de5be2/docs/images/svg-gallery.svg)

## Tour

`SvgRenderer::render_scene_graph` follows the shared display list and emits SVG paint, clipping, and text in draw order. The renderer requires image resources to be resolved before export. The gallery and regression tests cover font selection, text clipping, image resources, and geometry. Focused glyph tests check script sizing, feature fallback, and separation from adjacent letters. The affected SVG, text, and scenegraph suites pass, as do formatting and strict Clippy checks. The gallery was also inspected in Chrome and compared with WGPU output.

author: gesslar
body:
`object "/std/living/player"*` never produced an array of named objects. The path of a named object type is parsed with the general expression parser, so the trailing `*` bound as a multiply operator, the parser went looking for a right operand, and found the `}` that closes the doc type:

```
 * @returns {object STD_PLAYER*} An array of player objects in the room.
                              ^ Expression expected.
```

The type that came back was plain `object*` — the path discarded, the array marker spent on a multiplication that never happened. So the annotation was accepted and did nothing, which is why this went unnoticed: `present_players()` in a mudlib simul_efun has been typed `object*` since the feature shipped.

## Not a regression

Two dates matter and they are not the same one.

The parse has been wrong since #230 introduced named objects for FluffOS lpcdoc and switched the path from `parseLiteralNode()` to `parseExpression()`.

The *diagnostic* is four days old. #374 began rolling an include's parse errors up onto its `#include` directive, and that is what made an 18-month-old silent bug suddenly report four errors on a simul_efun whose own files are clean when compiled directly. The error is invisible in the file that owns the doc comment; it only ever surfaces through a directive.

## The fix

This is the third operator in the same family. #270 fixed the identical shape for `|` and `&` in union types with named object members by adding `disallowPipe`; `*` is what was left. `disallowAsterisk` sits next to it and breaks the same loop in `parseBinaryExpressionRest`, so the marker is left for `parsePostfixTypeOrHigher` to consume as the array it is.

## Verification

Against the mudlib that reported it, not only against fixtures — `present_players`, `present_npcs` and `get_players` resolve to `object "/std/living/player"*` and `object "/std/living/npc"*` where they previously resolved to `object*`.

The spec covers the literal, spaced and macro-sourced spellings, plus the include path. A test that checked only the owning file would pass against the bug.

author: claude[bot]
body:
## What this changes

Three things on the restore path: restored accounts can no longer carry an older session marker forward, both restore paths now bound how far an archive may *unpack*, and the portable-backup passphrase floor goes from 8 to 12 characters.

## Why

A full restore rebuilt the accounts table and wrote each row's `sessionEpoch` straight out of the archive — typically a *lower* value than the live one it replaced. That counter is the session-revocation lever, and restoring was the one operation that wound it backwards. Every restored row now takes one global floor, `min(max(live max read before the deleteMany, archived max) + 1, 2147483647)`.

The 512 MB cap bounded only the *compressed* upload, so a small crafted archive could still exhaust memory during a restore; and the saved-file restore path had no size cap at all — it read the whole file into memory before anything checked it.

### Two things the reviewer corrected, which changed what this PR claims

- **This does not end pre-restore sessions, and the docs no longer say it does.** The mechanism originally described — a session inheriting a reused account id — is unreachable: `users_id_seq` is never reset, so ids only advance on a given database and a pre-restore token is *orphaned* rather than re-pointed. Verified on a simulated fresh install with the sequence restarted. The floor is what keeps the reused-id case safe (a database rebuilt from a dump, or an archive restored onto another install sharing the JWT secret) and what stops the counter moving backwards. Revoking orphaned sessions is what the preceding release does.
- **An archived `sessionEpoch` at the integer ceiling turned a working restore into an unhandled 500** (`P2020`, transaction rolled back). Now clamped, with a comment noting that at the clamp the guarantee degrades from "above" to "equal".

`BACKUP_MAX_EXPANDED_MB` defaults to 1024 — measured against a real credential-bearing backup of 500 students / 4,750 records, which came to 0.96 MB. JSZip writes these archives uncompressed, so compressed and expanded are the same number for honest data and the upload cap binds first.

Independently reviewed. Verified: the floor read happens before the `deleteMany` (proven behaviourally, not structurally); hostile archived values never reach Postgres; a credential-free restore leaves epochs untouched and signs nobody out; the bomb is refused on both paths; and a TT02 archive created under the old 8-character floor still restores, because the floor is encrypt-only.

body:
## Scope
User requested a smartphone-accessible, minimal-cost web console using the existing development method. This PR implements a clearly labeled **initial local registry**, not full ChatGPT-account integration. The account-wide live session list and direct sending to existing WORK sessions remain unavailable/unimplemented; the UI must not be described as completing those requirements.

## Changes
- Adds an independent static page under `apps/rinne/public/work-desk/` plus manifest/icon.
- Local-only task/session registry, project filters, source/time labels, stale-running reports, draft preparation and explicit manual ChatGPT handoff.
- JSON backup, metadata-only conversation export import, explicit WORK report import.
- Read-only public GitHub PR and `integration/develop` status display; separate from session counts.
- Restrictive hash-based CSP, URL allowlist/escaping, storage-failure and concurrent-tab protection.
- Adds ten fast node:test checks and scope/privacy/verification documentation.

Affected app: rinne (new static page only).
Shared packages: none.
No existing game runtime, main, Production, workflow, Integration rules, or external paid service changes.

## Validation actually performed
- `node --check` on the exact inline JavaScript: PASS.
- `node --test apps/rinne/tests/work-desk.test.mjs`: 10 PASS.
- Chromium rendered-HTML functional checks: 30 PASS, covering editing, draft vs sent state, reports, import/dedup, escaping, stale data, storage failures, mocked GitHub, and 360/412/844/1280px widths.
- Browser navigation is blocked by this working environment's policy. It was not bypassed. Chromium checks used set_content with storage/clipboard/download/network mocks; they are NOT a public-URL or real Pixel Fold verification.
- Exact tested HTML blob SHA: `112fb9d136983ea3fb46b4edc73d6be773410477`, matching GitHub.
- Normal repo clone/dependency install was unavailable locally. Full repo fast validation and normal Integration must be run by existing CI; do not bypass or synthesize success. All added text files are small (largest 40,714 bytes), no binary transport fallback needed.

## Integration / delivery
User's request includes reaching a smartphone-usable web state. Proceed through the existing normal develop Integration after exact-head checks and review, with no main/Production changes. Expected URL only after successful deployment: `https://charukun.github.io/soul-lineage/dev/rinne/work-desk/`.
The existing game browser gate does not by itself establish interaction correctness of this independent page. Public availability and relevant verification scope must be reported honestly.

## Remaining product limitations
No account-wide auto-discovery, live WORK heartbeat/state, direct task dispatch/start/stop, or cross-device sync. First use is an empty registry, not a claim that the user's account has zero sessions. No private conversation metadata embedded in public source. Browser storage is not an encrypted or same-origin-isolated vault.

author: agustinrhcp
body:
```
def limit -> Int
  [1]
end

NoMethodError: undefined method 'call' for nil
  jade/frontend/type_checking/state.rb:25:in 'unify'
  jade/frontend/type_checking/inference/list.rb:32:in 'infer'
```

This is the crash #266 fixed for `RecordUpdate`, at the three other call sites that close with a blockless `unify_result` against the expected type: `List` (both the empty and non-empty paths), `ConstructorReference`, and `Assign`. The failure needs an authoritative expected type, which a signature supplies. These all crashed:

| Signature | Body | Now |
|---|---|---|
| `-> Int` | `[1]` | `Expected Int but got List(Int)` |
| `-> List(String)` | `[1]` | `Expected List(String) but got List(Int)` |
| `-> a` | `[1]` | `Expected a but got List(Int)` |
| `-> a` | `[]` | `Expected a but got List(a)` |
| `-> Int` | `Nothing` | `Expected Int but got Maybe(a)` |
| `-> Int` | `x = "s"` | `Expected Int but got String` |

#266 noted it couldn't build a failure through `Assign`; a binding in last position is one.

All three sites share one `type_mismatch` helper in `Inference::Helpers`. Each shape reports exactly one error; `FunctionDeclaration`'s own body check doesn't pile a second one on.

Not fixed here, and not a crash: `def foo -> a` returning `Nothing`, and `def foo -> Maybe(a)` returning `Just(1)`, are both accepted. That's the roadmap's "declared type variables aren't rigid" item.

The CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` section conflicts trivially with #271, whichever merges second.

Full suite: 2669 examples, 0 failures.

author: virtuelethuiszorg
body:
## ⚠️ Draft on purpose — enable the ruleset first, then merge this

Merging it now would turn main red, **because the gate really is off.** That is the point of it.

## What I could not do, and what I could

I can't switch the branch ruleset on: the REST write is refused by the agent proxy, and the GitHub MCP server has no repository-administration tool. That remains your two minutes in Settings → Rules → Rulesets (`PENDING_FOR_LEE` §2 **S16**).

**But the gate being off was never the deepest problem — the silence was.** Ruleset `main` was created **2026-07-16** and left `enforcement: disabled`. It stayed off through the outages of 23 and 25 July and the broken main of 11 September, every one of them a red guard merged past, and **no check anywhere went red**, because an unprotected branch behaves exactly like a branch nobody has got round to protecting yet. Two months of false safety.

This adds `scripts/ci/check-merge-gate.mjs` and a `Merge gate is enforced` job that reads `/rules/branches/main` on every push and **fails when the gate is not on**.

That endpoint matters more than it looks: it answers *"what applies to this branch right now"*, not *"does a ruleset exist"*. A ruleset that is disabled — **or whose target list is empty** — returns `[]`, and **both were true of 19055263**. A checker that read the ruleset *definition* would have seen a well-formed object and said nothing.

It also **refuses `Manifest matches production`** as a required check: it's `push`-only, reports `skipped` on every PR, and a required check that never reports leaves every PR pending for ever. Adding it looks helpful and would lock the repository solid.

## Proof

- **18 unit tests** over a pure `evaluateMergeGate`, no network: each of the six required checks dropped in turn, each of the three rules removed in turn, the push-only check added, both the string and object forms of a context, a non-array error body, and the empty array that actually happened.
- **Driven against the live repository as it stands today** — exits 1 with *"Nothing applies to this branch"*. It has been seen to refuse the real defect, not just fixtures.
- **`ciJobIsolation.test.ts` caught this very job** for mapping a secret into `env` without calling `require-secrets` first — my own guard from earlier today, working on me. Fixed rather than excepted.
- 231 files, **4458 tests, 1 skipped — green.** Typecheck clean, lint warnings unchanged at 60.

## The order

1. Settings → Rules → Rulesets → `main`: Active · target default branch · the six checks · add `merge` to allowed methods · both bypass actors from the dropdowns.
2. Run the three verifications in S16.
3. **Then** mark this ready and merge. After that, a ruleset silently disabled, narrowed, or missing a check goes red on the next push instead of going unnoticed until the next outage.
4. Delete the caveat paragraph in CLAUDE.md — your original wording becomes true.

author: giri-aayush
body:
## What & why
22 has been in Maintenance since 2025-10-21 (EOL 2027-04-30). 24 is the LTS line today: Active until 2026-10-20, then Maintenance to 2028-04-30. Dependabot opened the same bump to 26 (#483); that is closed, because 26 is Current until it becomes LTS on 2026-10-28, and because it changed the Dockerfile alone while five workflow pins stayed on 22, which the repo suite reds on purpose. Revisit for 26 after 2026-10-28.

Every place the repo names a runtime moves together: both Dockerfile stages, the five pins in ci.yml, the one in live-smoke.yml, `NODE_VERSION` in the legacy render.yaml, and the prose in CONTRIBUTING, DEPLOY and the PR template that still said "Node 23+" from before #257. The ci.yml comment says why 24 and when to look again.

## Testing
- `npm ci` + `npm test` inside `node:24-slim` on a clean copy: 767 tests, 767 pass, 0 fail on 24.21.0. (The slim image has no openssl, and the live-probe suite fails loudly rather than skipping without it, which is correct and cost me one confusing run.) CI's `app` job repeated this on 24.20.0.
- Linux harness `SUITES=repo`: 92 passed, 0 failed, and the agreement check reads "matches the Dockerfile's node 24". Reviewer re-ran it and baselined main (also 92/0).
- Mutations: one ci.yml pin left at 22 reds the check and names it (`mismatched: ci.yml:22`); the run stage alone left at 22 reds the "every stage agrees on ONE major" check.
- `docker build` of the Dockerfile on 24 builds (CI's `image` job repeats the build and runs `node -e` in it; it does not start the app). I started the image by hand with a zallet config: `/api/health` 200, `/api/status` served, `/api/ready` 503 with no wallet behind it as it should be, `node -v` inside 24.21.0.

## Risks / follow-ups
- Deploy rebuilds the image on merge (Dockerfile changed). The health gate rolls back if the 24 build fails to serve; I will watch `buildCommit` through the swap.
- render.yaml is a leftover from the Render era and nothing reads it. Deleting it is a separate, easy PR.
- `@types/node` is on 26 while the runtime is 24, unchanged here; whether to pin the types major to the runtime is a separate decision.
- The "LTS only" policy for the node image lives in a closed PR rather than in dependabot.yml; an `ignore` on semver-major for `node` would encode it.

author: copilot
body:
This adds a G-code-first workflow to `Robot8DoF` so precomputed conformal trajectories can be loaded and executed directly, instead of relying on the existing vision-reactive loop in `junto2.m`. The new path preserves the current hardware stack and reuses the existing XY serial / MyCobot integration model.

- **G-code parsing**
  - Adds `Robot8DoF/gcode_parser.m`
  - Parses `G0/G1`, `G28`, `G92`, `G90/G91`, common `M` codes, inline comments, and slicer-style metadata
  - Normalizes motion into absolute `waypoints` as `[X Y Z E F]`
  - Handles:
    - absolute vs relative positioning
    - feedrate inheritance
    - omitted axes inheriting prior state
    - multiline / continuation commands
    - extrusion-only and Z-hop style moves

- **Trajectory execution**
  - Adds `Robot8DoF/gcode_executor.m`
  - Executes parsed waypoints across:
    - XY platform via serial G-code commands
    - MyCobot Z motion via the existing `mc_bridge.py`
  - Includes:
    - XY feedback polling using the existing GRBL/Marlin/Klipper query pattern
    - hardware limit / safe-radius clamping
    - placeholder extrusion accounting from `E`
    - telemetry capture for `r_log`, `ref_log`, `e_log`, RMSE, distance traveled, and material usage
    - pause/resume and abort handling from keyboard input

- **New entry points**
  - Adds `Robot8DoF/junto2_gcode.m`
  - Adds `Robot8DoF/exec_gcode.m`
  - Loads existing calibration assets, initializes hardware, previews the trajectory, executes the job, and prints a compact completion report
  - Keeps `junto2.m` unchanged

- **Documentation and focused coverage**
  - Updates `Robot8DoF/README.md` with the G-code workflow
  - Adds `Robot8DoF/test_gcode_workflow.m` covering parser state handling and dry-run execution output

```matlab
[traj, meta] = gcode_parser('C:/absolute/path/conformal_print.gcode');
[logData, report] = gcode_executor(traj, s, mc, struct('plotTelemetry', true));

% or use the one-shot entry point
[logData, report, traj] = exec_gcode('C:/absolute/path/conformal_print.gcode');
```

System 7 rendering now has an independent acceptance oracle: 84 genuine System 7.5.3 Revision 2 captures at 1-bit and 8-bit depth, a coordinate-based metric sheet, and an original 191-glyph title atlas. Sparse goldens come directly from those screenshots; no ChonkStep renderer generated them.

- Reproducible classic-Mac fixture and capture driver exercise document/zoom windows, focus, held controls, WindowShade, four titles, screen-edge shadows and character/advance charts. Source/settings/toolchain hashes and rights notes are included.

- Classic monochrome is the exact target. Genuine 8-bit focus also changes the outline; those captures remain comparison evidence, preserving the title-only focus damage contract. Palette roles and exact integer/faithful fractional scale policies are specified.
- Also fixes the foundation's x86 Arch packaging test failure: strace proved glibc's secondary-arena shrink queried `/proc/sys/vm/overcommit_memory` after the I/O gate. The disposable child now uses one allocator arena. All syscall prohibitions and the SIGSYS negative control remain enabled. Reproduced failure and verified the fix in the updated native Arch environment.

- Repairs the existing memory E2E gate exposed by CI: preserve the cold 4 MiB heap-extent limit, then check extent/size/RSS across three repeated workloads against one exercised baseline. This separates first-use residency from continuing retention. The real negative control with allocator policy disabled still fails on 8.2 MiB cold heap growth; the fixed binary's three repeats stabilize within 40 KiB RSS growth.

Validation: 115 Python harness tests pass; `cargo test -p wm-theme` and strict all-target wm-theme Clippy pass; the unchanged I/O denial test passes on the host and updated Arch container; all 84 capture-derived cases verify. Main's foundation Wayland E2E, workspace tests, lint, SDK, audit and aarch64 package checks passed; the x86 allocator-test failure is addressed here.
