ラウンド結果パネルの `className` が **won / lost / Trischaken のどの分岐でも一律 `text-ds-success`（緑）** に固定されており、デクレアラーが契約を落として `roundResult.lost` が出る場面でも勝利時と同じ緑だった。

## 色は文言と同じ視点に揃えた

`TappTarockBreakdown.won` は **declarer 側の成否**（型定義の doc が `teamPoints` を "Declarer side's card points"、`threshold` を "Points needed to succeed" と書いている）。文言 `roundResult.won` / `lost` も declarer 視点。

したがって色も declarer 視点にしている。**人間プレイヤーの損得（`breakdown.seats` の自分の増減）に読み替えていない** — 文言が declarer 視点なのに色だけ人間視点だと、隣り合う 2 つの表示が矛盾する。

**Trischaken は契約の成否ではない。** 最も多く取った席を名指しするだけなので、成功色も失敗色も付けず中立のままにした。

結果の種別を**一度だけ**求め、そこから class と `data-result` の両方を導いている（同じ 3 分岐を 2 か所に書くと、片方だけ直されて色と属性が食い違う）。

`data-testid="zw-round-result"` は変更していない。これは Zwanzigerrufen からクローンした名残の名前だが、改名はこの issue の範囲外。

## テスト

`TappTarockPage.test.tsx`（18 passed）:

- `won: true` で成功色が付く
- **`won: false` で失敗色が付き、`text-ds-success` を含まないこと** — **これが本体。両方の色を付ける実装を排除する**
- **負の対照:** Trischaken（`loser >= 0`）では成功色も失敗色も付かない
- 文言自体は従来どおり（解決後の文言で検査）

- [x] `bun run check` — exit 0
- [x] `bun run typecheck` — exit 0

author: ilbertt
body:
## Why

Bringing a fresh host up was nine steps with a loop in the middle:

```
curl … | sh                                   → starter config, laid out
systemctl daemon-reload
systemctl enable --now nibrunnerd             → a host with no [proxy.http], serving nothing
edit /etc/nibrunner/config.toml
nibrunnerd install                            → two new units on a zerofs host
fill /etc/nibrunner/host.env
systemctl daemon-reload
systemctl enable --now nibrunner-zerofs nibrunner-zerofs-mount
systemctl restart nibrunnerd                  → its drop-in had no ordering on the mount
```

`install` wrote into `/etc/systemd/system`, set sysctls, `modprobe`d and created accounts, then stopped short of `systemctl` and handed back three incantations — the same three whether this was a first run or an edit, so the restart an edit needs was never said, and `what_is_still_yours` said *"It is running"* before anything ran. Every step printed a line, so the re-run case was a dozen `unchanged`s before the part that mattered.

## What

Two verbs with one meaning each:

| | does | never does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nibrunnerd install` | puts files where `config.toml` says: guest image, kernel settings, ZeroFS, directories, units, `host.env`. Prints only what changed, then what is left — numbered. | touch systemd |
| `nibrunnerd start` | lays the host out again, checks what a start would otherwise find out too late, `daemon-reload`, `enable`, starts or restarts the units this host has, reports each. | render differently from `install` |

A fresh host:

```
$ curl … | sh
…
==> nibrunnerd install
  /etc/nibrunner/config.toml written, because this host had none
  guest image 2026.9.11 laid down
  /etc/sysctl.d/99-nibrunner.conf written
  /etc/modules-load.d/nibrunner.conf written
  /etc/systemd/system/nibrunnerd.service written
  /etc/systemd/system/nibrunnerd.service.d/install.conf written
  /etc/nibrunner/host.env created

Laid out; nothing started. What is left:

  1. edit /etc/nibrunner/config.toml
     written just now: volumes as files on this disk, plain HTTP on :80, nothing in an
     object store. Every key: https://github.com/ilbertt/nibrunner/blob/main/docs/config.md
  2. edit /etc/nibrunner/host.env
     the secrets that configuration needs, each named in the file
  3. nibrunnerd start
```

A host given its own configuration is asked only for what is missing (`1. set ZEROFS_ENCRYPTION_PASSWORD, AWS_REGION, … in /etc/nibrunner/host.env`, `2. nibrunnerd start`), or just for `nibrunnerd start`. The order stops mattering: write the config before or after the script, `start` re-renders either way. Every later change, and every new release, is `nibrunnerd start`.

```
$ nibrunnerd start
this host cannot be started:
  ZEROFS_ENCRYPTION_PASSWORD is not set in /etc/nibrunner/host.env
  [proxy.http.tls] key /etc/nibrunner/tls/origin.key is not there
nothing was started

$ nibrunnerd start
  /etc/systemd/system/nibrunner-zerofs.service written
  nibrunner-zerofs.service         restarted
  nibrunner-zerofs-mount.service   restarted
  nibrunnerd.service               restarted

Up. It serves what /var/lib/nibrunner/desired.json says; `journalctl -u nibrunnerd -f` follows it.
```

**`start`'s rules**, each with one reason:

- `nibrunnerd` is always restarted. It reads `config.toml` itself, so an edit there changes no rendered file — and its restart takes no tenant with it (`KillMode=process`).
- `nibrunner-zerofs` is restarted only when its binary, config or unit was rewritten this run: a restart drops every NBD device under every live guest. The mount follows it, or is restarted alone when only its unit changed.
- Refuses before touching systemd when a variable the configuration needs is empty in `host.env`, or a path in `[proxy.http.tls]` is not a file. A start that then fails is one the configuration got wrong.

**`host.env`** now names every variable this host could read — `ZEROFS_ENCRYPTION_PASSWORD`, `AWS_REGION`, `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` — the ones the configuration needs uncommented and empty, the rest `# NAME=`. Still written once and never again, so a configuration that changes to need one finds the line already there to uncomment. `start` reads it the way systemd does: comments, empty values and quotes.

**`deploy/config.toml`** gains `[proxy.http]` on `:80`. A host with no listener refuses the README's own example document, which is not a starting point. The README paragraph apologising for that is gone.

`Laid` records what changed (`done`) and which files (`written`) instead of narrating every step, so the printout and `start`'s restart decision come from the same list. `install.sh` is unchanged.

## Decisions

- AWS keys are *required* whenever any URL is `s3://`. A machine with an instance role would legitimately have none in `host.env`; that host does not exist today, and a `start` that cannot fail on a Hetzner box was the ask.
- Bare `nibrunnerd` still serves in the foreground. Rendering the unit as `… serve` would fix the "typed `nibrunnerd` to start it" trap but touches the unit every existing host runs under — separate change if wanted.
- Not done: the binary fetching its own guest image the way it fetches ZeroFS (would drop `--from` and shrink `install.sh` to packages + binary), because the binary would need to know its release tag and versions are `0.1.0` against CalVer tags.

## Verification

`just test` (742 lib tests, including new ones for the secrets file, the next-steps block, and `start`'s plan and refusals), `just lint`, `just fmt --check`. Not run against a live host: `systemctl` calls are exercised only by their plan.

body: ## Summary External strategy producers (LOATS, per its ADR-006 Amendment 5) route every TradeDecision to `/api/v1/analyze` (`ANALYZER_INTAKE_PATH=analyze`). The producer side shipped on 11 Sep, but the gateway never had the endpoint — every routed decision resolved as HTTP 404 and was honestly counted as a routing error. This PR adds the endpoint so that error class becomes real decisional telemetry, without touching the producer. ## Changes - `restx_api/analyze.py` — new `/api/v1/analyze` endpoint: receive-and-record only; apikey-authenticated, rate-limited, schema-validated (`decision_id`/`symbol`/`decision_type`/`timestamp` required; unknown fields retained so producers can evolve); acknowledges `200 {"status": "success"}`. No orders, no broker calls, no analyzer-mode changes — the read-only ANALYZE-mode semantic is intact. - `services/analyze_intake_service.py` — records into `analyzer_logs` under `api_type=analyze_intake` with the credential stripped. - `restx_api/__init__.py`, `restx_api/account_schema.py` — namespace registration + request schema. - `test/test_analyze_intake.py` — 15 contract cases, including the historical defect class: the namespace registered under `/analyze` is asserted, because an implemented-but-unregistered route is indistinguishable from a missing one for the producer. - `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — `test_analyze_intake.py` added to the CI-safe backend test job. ## Companion note: upstream test env defect (separate from this change) `tests/test_python_editor.py` binds a server to port 5000 (the platform's default dev port). On machines where a foreign OpenAlgo instance is already listening on 5000, the suite's assertions evaluate against the **wrong server** — independent of this PR (locally A/B-proven against a live :5000 instance; the failures follow the foreign server, not the diff). Candidate upstream fix: bind to an explicit ephemeral test port, or skip when a foreign server answers. Flagging here because it produces false local/CI failures that look like regressions. ## Test plan - [x] `pytest test/test_analyze_intake.py` → **15 passed** (Windows 11, Python 3.11, repo venv; against this exact tree, post-rebase onto current main) - [x] Live probe: `POST /api/v1/analyze` → 400 on empty payload; unknown route → 404 (registration proven on a running instance) - [x] Working tree clean on `main` = `a51822b4`, rebased onto upstream tip `c1bc96c9` Base-branch note: rebased onto current upstream `main`; the only conflict vs main was `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (both sides appended one test line — union-resolved). --- ## Summary by cubic Adds the `/api/v1/analyze` decision-telemetry intake endpoint. LOATS producers have routed every TradeDecision to this path since 11 Sep, but the gateway returned a 404 for each one, counted as a routing error. The new endpoint turns that error class into real decisional telemetry without touching the producer. **Changes** - Receive-and-record only: apikey-authenticated, rate-limited, schema-validated. `decision_id`, `symbol`, `decision_type`, and `timestamp` are required; unknown fields are retained so the producer can evolve. Acknowledges `200 {"status": "success"}`. - No orders, no broker calls, no analyzer-mode changes; the read-only ANALYZE-mode semantic is intact. - Records into `analyzer_logs` under `api_type=analyze_intake` with the apikey stripped before storage. - Registers the namespace under `/analyze` and adds the request schema. - Adds 15 contract tests covering the producer wire shape, namespace registration, and credential handling; wired into the CI backend job. - Separate upstream issue, not from this PR: `tests/test_python_editor.py` binds port 5000 and can false-fail against a foreign instance. Written for commit a51822b4c47aa80b7680f44706aeb92c4db26fe1. Summary will update on new commits.

author: ali-ulu
body:
## The problem

The nightly alarm filed a single issue titled `Nightly full-suite run is red` and
reused it while open. That meant:

- Closing it after a fix left nothing open, so the next red night opened a **new**
  issue. #2030, #2088 and #2101 were three unrelated defects under one title in
  three days — each needing its own fix.
- A night with two broken files put two separate fixes in one thread.

## The change

`planAlarmActions()` returns one action per failing file, titled
`Nightly red: <file>`, and the workflow step loops over them instead of reading
only the first.

Decisions worth naming:

- **Grouped by file, not by (file, shard).** The same file failing on two shards
  is one defect reported twice; both shards go in one body.
- **Already-open file issue → comment.** A file that stays broken keeps
  collecting evidence in one thread; a fixed file simply stops appearing.
- **Empty failure list → the shared title is kept.** A run that died in the
  impact plan, `npm ci`, or a killed shard has no file to key a title on, and
  silence there is the exact blindness the alarm exists to remove.
- **Unreadable sidecar → one stable title.** Its "file" is an error message whose
  text varies, so keying on it would file a fresh issue every night for the same
  broken shard.

## Verification

- `test/nightly-failure-alarm.test.js` — 12/12 pass (5 new tests)
- `test/ci-change-classifier.test.js`, `test/ci-runtime-classifier.test.js`,
  `test/test-impact-plan.test.js` — 17/17 pass
- Mutation-checked, both caught (2 failures each):
  - `alarmTitleForFile()` returning the shared title
  - the plan returning only its first action

author: matt-roe
body:
Continues the Sets/Triples refactor: sets now enter the graph the same way facts do — extracted, reviewed, serialized — and the cost of that was measured rather than assumed.

## The bug that was sitting there

**Every set a user made in the app was invisible to the sets layer.** F65 shipped `ktype:EntitySet` + `kpred:has-member` and the canvas still writes it; F187 chose `skos:Collection` + `skos:member` and `sets.ts` read only that. Each half passed its own tests, so nothing failed — including for the two sets that ship in `static/knowledge.ttl` and `static/starter-everyday.ttl`, which `set-integrity` and `set-pages` never saw.

`readSets` reads both dialects now; `buildEntitySet` writes SKOS. Found by grepping both vocabularies, not by a test — there is now a test that crosses the seam.

## What sets cost — measured

`scripts/offline/set-complexity.ts`, a new script-tier gate, over 17,163 quads in 31 graphs:

| | Measured | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Storage | 184 quads, **1.07%** | not the interesting cost |
| Compute | `readSets` 3.8ms vs plain scan 2.0ms | **1.9x**, both O(n), one pass |
| Order | **3.0 extra quads per ordered member** | 4x multiplier, used by 6 of 19 sets |
| Terms | 6 for a plain set (4 standard SKOS); +6 for page blocks (**0 standard**) | blocks are the part to scrutinize |
| **Search** | **11 of 25** member queries had a membership row in the top 10; **5 of 25** lost a real result | **the real cost, and nobody had looked** |

BM25 makes one document per statement, so a membership row competed with facts while repeating a name every real fact about that member already carries. Structural rows are now downweighted in **both** search implementations — downweighted, not dropped, because dropping them makes "what is in the shortlist" unanswerable.

`0.2` is a swept plateau, not a guess: `0.5 / 0.3 / 0.2 / 0.15 / 0.05` displace `3 / 2 / 1 / 1 / 1`. **5 → 1.** The survivor is genuinely the strongest lexical match for its query and is reported rather than tuned away.

## Sets in extraction — deterministic, arm (c)

A `group` stage between `type` and `archive`, the fifth of the nine stages `kb:staged-extraction` names and the first of the three with nothing behind them. It recognizes groupings the graph **already states** rather than asking a model — the work-tiering ladder and the 2026-09-09 bench both said to do this first (best local model: 10 of 15 sets at 0.44 precision; **overlap 0 of 5 across every model and every run**).

**A derived set costs two quads, not N+2.** A graph usually states its grouping already (`dam-shortlist includes aprimo, opentext, bynder`), so the proposal declares the type and *names the carrying predicate* (`kpred:member-predicate`) instead of restating N edges. No duplicated facts, no new rows in the search index, and it keeps the author's own word for membership rather than overwriting it.

### It scored 0% on the first real graph, and that was the valuable part

Four sets proposed over `personal-notes`, four wrong; three grouped by `kpred:extracted-from`. That predicate sits under `urn:kbase:predicate/` like every claim does, so F194's layer reader fell through to the `claim` fail-safe — **every MCP tool response had been filing provenance alongside what the graph knows.** `captured-notes.ts` already called it "a RECORD the extractor derived and can re-derive"; nothing had said so where a script could read it.

Now declared in `reckons-vocabulary.ttl` and in both layer readers. **A bug in one feature found a misclassification affecting three, and the fix was one classification rather than one more exclusion list.**

After it: `personal-notes` proposes 0 and refuses 4 (correct — it states no groupings); `reckons-roadmap` proposes 23 and they are real (`integrations has-integration`, 8 members; `stabilization-trust-boundaries has-part`, 9; `has-phase`, `has-dimension`, `has-tier`).

Refusals are reported as loudly as finds — in the stage detail, the ingest log and the chain report. The bench showed refusing is most of the skill: the two models that never over-grouped managed it by never grouping anything.

## The round-trip claim is no longer untested

`kb:set-substrate` asserted that a set "round-trips exactly like any other fact" on the strength of the reasoning that produced it. Eight cases check it now. **The ordered case is the one that mattered**: the skolemised membership node chosen over `rdf:List` survives byte-identical across two parses in one process — the exact condition that broke `rdf:List`. Overlap survives too.

Two of the eight were my own bugs and both are recorded rather than quietly fixed: an id containing `|` reaches an IRI unescaped via `urn:kbase:stmt/<id>` (not reachable in the app, worth knowing), and a *pending* proposal is correctly not exported — now pinned by its own test, because "a proposal is not a fact" is worth failing loudly on.

## Documentation

Six entities under a new **"The Set"** section in `docs-triples-rdf.ttl`, placed *beside* the triple rather than under it. Written for a first-time reader per `kb:journey-docs`. The lead argument is the honest one — **triples cannot separate a fact about a group from the same fact about each member** ("the team weighs 800 kilos" vs "each person does"), which is why sets are substrate rather than page layout. Carries the unflattering numbers too: no model in the benchmark ever put one thing into two sets.

Roadmap updated in the same branch: F187.2 and F187.3 `planned` → `scaffolded`, with what shipped, what it cost, and what is still open.

## Still open

- **Review is the unsolved half** — a set is confirmed row by row, not as one decision. Smaller than it was (two rows, folded into an existing entity card) but it bootstraps on `kb:loop-job-grouping`.
- Stages 6 (set attributes) and 7 (order) untouched; the corpus carries no set expectations, so model arms (b)/(d) stay unmeasurable.
- Two principle decisions are with Matt — see HANDOFF.

## Verification

Full suite **3023/3023 across 209 files** · mcp-server **150 + 10** · svelte-check **4213 files, 0 errors** · `offline:all --tier=script` **36/36** · graph-lint **0 errors** · set-integrity **0** · md-align **149/149 match** · kb-align **no discrepancies** (fixed a stale claim — production.ttl said 2997 tests / 208 files).

body:
## Summary

Retires the C++ ProteoWizard tree from this repository and makes the C# port (`pwiz-sharp/`) the native layout, with each project where its C++ ancestor lived. This is the **content** cutover of the C++ retirement; the history rewrite that purges the C++ commits (and the `ProteoWizard/pwiz-cpp` archive that keeps them) is a separate, later operation — runbook in `ai/docs/cpp-retirement-runbook.md`, tracking TODO `ai/todos/active/TODO-20260910_retire_cpp_tree.md`.

Stacked on `Skyline/work/20260612_net8_port` (#4619).

## Layout

| Was | Now |
|---|---|
| `pwiz-sharp/pwiz/src/Util` | `pwiz/utility/` (tests in `test/`; bindings in `bindings/{Hosted,NativeAot,timstof_prm_scheduler}`) |
| `pwiz-sharp/pwiz/src/{Common,MsData,IdentData,TraData}` | `pwiz/data/{common,msdata,identdata,tradata}/` (`Common` beside the `.obo` files it embeds) |
| `pwiz-sharp/pwiz/src/Analysis` | `pwiz/analysis/` (beside `spectrum_processing/*.data`) |
| `pwiz-sharp/pwiz/src/Vendor/<V>` | `pwiz/data/vendor_readers/<V>/` beside `Reader_<V>_Test.data`; the cpp `ABI` dir + fixtures renamed `Sciex`; `Vendor/Common`, `TestHarness` → `vendor_readers/{Common,TestHarness}` |
| `pwiz-sharp/pwiz/src/StlContainers` | `pwiz_tools/Shared/StlContainers/` |
| `pwiz-sharp/pwiz/src/{ZedGraph,MSGraph}` | dropped — SeeMS uses Skyline's SDK-style `pwiz_tools/Shared/{zedgraph,MSGraph}` |
| `pwiz-sharp/Tools/{BiblioSpec,Commandline,BullseyeSharp}` | `pwiz_tools/…` |
| `pwiz-sharp/Tools/{SeeMS,MsConvertGUI}` | landed *into* the legacy `pwiz_tools/{SeeMS,MSConvertGUI}` (C# since 2008; same file names, so their history continues) |
| `pwiz-sharp/{Pwiz.sln,Directory.Build.*,build.*,tcbuild.*,clean.*,build/,vendor-archives/,examples/,scripts/}` | repo root; the installer under `scripts/installer/` |
| `pwiz_aux/msrc/utility/vendor_api_*.7z` | `vendor-archives/` (full Windows Bruker SDK as `vendor_api_Bruker_full.7z` beside the trimmed runtime subset) |

Deleted: `pwiz/` sources, `pwiz_aux`, `libraries` (except 7za/7zz/bsdtar+DLLs, msparser, zlib/expat for Hardklor), `doc`, `scripts` (except the TeamCity trigger scripts), the Jam/VS/quickbuild files, Bumbershoot, the C++ commandline/BiblioSpec, the net472 MSConvertGUI/SeeMS projects, Crawdad, TestDiagnostics, the dead BullseyeSharp submodule, every Jamfile, the C++ GitHub workflow. Kept in place: CV ontologies + `unimod.xml`, vendor fixtures + reference mzMLs, spectrum_processing test data, BiblioSpec test corpus + `modifications.xml`, generator inputs (`cv.hpp`, `ChemistryData.cpp`). Hardklor and the Thermo method builders remain the only C++ Skyline compiles.

Other changes: root `Directory.Build.props` anchors (`PwizRepoRoot/PwizRoot/PwizToolsRoot/…`) and a global `DefaultItemExcludes` (`test/**;Test/**;**/*.data/**`); one-line `Directory.Build.props/.targets` shims in the hoisted `pwiz_tools/<tool>/` dirs so Skyline's props never apply to them; `Pwiz.sln` regenerated with folders mirroring the tree; `VendorSdkLoader` falls back to `ProteoWizard/pwiz-cpp` so SDK pins in shipped installers survive the history rewrite; TeamCity trigger configs drop the C++ builds (commented out for reference); README/.cursorrules/copilot rules/.gitignore/.editorconfig/clean scripts updated. The mechanics are scripted in `ai/scripts/Repo/{retire_cpp_tree.py,relayout_pwiz_projects.py}`.

## ⚠️ Do not merge before (Stage 0 of the runbook)

1. `ProteoWizard/pwiz-cpp` exists as a `--mirror` of this repo and the C++ TeamCity configs (Core bt83/bt17/…, Bumbershoot, BiblioSpec, Docker Wine, Sourceforge, website, net472 Skyline/release-branch configs) point at it.
2. `ProteoWizard_CoreWindowsNet` / `_CoreLinuxNet` build steps call the root `tcbuild.bat|sh` instead of `pwiz-sharp/tcbuild.*` — until then this branch's Core CI cannot run.
3. `master` required checks switched to the .NET configs.

## Verification

- `dotnet build Pwiz.sln -c Release` clean; `build.bat Release --i-agree-to-the-vendor-licenses` builds, produces both Setup.exe variants, and passes every test project. On the local branch tip 3 tests (2 Bruker CompassXtract, Installer per-user) 404'd downloading their pinned SDK archive because the pinned commit wasn't on GitHub yet — now that it is pushed they should pass on CI.
- `pwiz_tools\Skyline\build.bat` builds (incl. Hardklor), stages, and 14 targeted TestRunner tests pass (Thermo/Agilent/Shimadzu/Waters/Wiff/Wiff2 formats, TestInstrumentInfo, TestQcTraces, TestScanDescription, TestInstrumentSerialNumbers, FileTypeTest, TestLibraryBuild, TestDiaSearch, CodeInspection). body: # Description This PR fixes a bug where `PullImage` blocked for up to 2 minutes during cold pulls, frequently tripping the 30-second Temporal `HeartbeatTimeout` and causing silent sync failures in Docker mode. It threads `req.HeartbeatFunc` down into `DockerExecutor.PullImage` and replaces the synchronous `io.Discard` copy with a custom `heartbeatWriter`. This pulses a heartbeat every 5 seconds synchronously from the pull stream, safely bypassing the Temporal timeout. Heartbeat return values are intentionally ignored since Temporal handles cancellations natively by aborting the context. Fixes #203 ## Type of change - [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [ ] This change requires a documentation update # How Has This Been Tested? - [x] Ran a local test script by pulling `tensorflow/tensorflow:latest-gpu` (which takes >2 mins) and observed the custom `heartbeatWriter` successfully pulsing heartbeats every 5 seconds for the entire duration without triggering a context timeout. # Screenshots or Recordings ## Documentation - [ ] Documentation Link: [link to README, olake.io/docs, or olake-docs] - [x] N/A (bug fix, refactor, or test changes only)

author: siegelingsgame
body:
Two changes, plus the `progress.md` record for the previous deploy.

## 1. The Deception lesson is now a four-step chapter that plays the card

It was a single passive tip ("check their pool to see which Deceptions you can play") with the whole hand locked — sitting underneath Ashfall's still-open preview on a phone. Replaced by:

1. **`t3-strategy-close`** — swipe the card preview down (same targets and copy shape as the existing `preview-close` step; skipped on desktop, which has no drawer).
2. **`t3-deception`** — tap the Deception itself, marked and locked to that card, with copy saying the printed number is the **opponent's** energy, not yours.
3. **`t3-deception-energy`** — spotlights the opponent's energy readout (`#mobileEnemyElements` on the phone strip, `#enemyEnergy` on the desktop rail) and reads the live numbers back — "needs 3 ice, they have N" — saying plainly whether the condition is met.
4. **`t3-deception-set`** — set the trap.

New helpers `trapCardInHand()`, `trapTarget()`, `enemyPoolFor()` and `trapTriggerMet()` back it. `trapTriggerMet()` deliberately mirrors the server — `EnergyService.canTriggerTrap` is `canAfford` on the *other* side, and `GameService` refuses the set with "Opponent bucket does not meet the trigger" — so the set step is **skipped, not stalled**, when their pool is short. That's the "if the energy is available" half of the request.

The set step is also the one step before the claim that deliberately leaves a card playable: it locks the rest of the hand but not the trap and not the Set control. Ashfall therefore still can't be cast before the claim lesson that pays for it, and the player ends up casting **both** — the Deception here, the Strategy at `t3-wipe`.

`style.css` raises `.tut-layer` to 1390 for the three new steps that run with a drawer open, or their tips would be buried under it (510) exactly as the `badge-*` tips once were. Pin `arena-tutorial.js` 46 → 47.

## 2. Hand cost badge hangs off the card name

`.hand-cost-badge` used one card-level offset, but the header sits at **10.6%** of card height on a Siegeling frame and **19.6%** on a spell/trap frame — so the badge landed *on* one name and *above* the other. It now renders inside `.hand-card-header` at `top: 100%`. Holo full-art faces keep the old corner (no header); the containing-block rule is scoped with `:has(> .hand-cost-badge)`; the tutorial cost highlight was repointed off its now-broken child combinator. Pins `style.css` 263 → 264, `game.js` 292 → 293.

## Verification

- `trapTriggerMet()`/`enemyPoolFor()` lifted **verbatim from source** and run against stub state: enemy ice 3 / needs 3 → true; ice 2 → false; ice 9 → true; nine Fire but no ice → false; no trap in hand → false.
- Headless Chromium at 390x844 and 1920x1080 on the real `play.html`: at the set step, `Ashfall=LOCKED, Shatter Seal=live, Draco=LOCKED, Set=live`. Layer resolves to **z-index 1390** for `t3-strategy-close`, `t3-deception-energy` and `t3-deception-set` (clearing the 510 drawer), while `t3-deception` stays at the default 200 — correct, the drawer is closed by then.
- Cost badge: badge tops moved from 12.4% (both frames) to 23.4% / 32.1%, each tracking its own title; overlap sweep at 390x844, 375x812, 360x800, 320x568 and 1920x1080 over five costed cards shows a consistent 2px gap and no overlap with any title, stat pill or card edge. Screenshots read back.
- `./mvnw -Dtest=TutorialRuleParityTest,TutorialScriptedDrawTest test` — 13/13 green. New assertions pin the chapter's order against `ashfall-pages` and `t3-claim`, the opponent-pool trigger rule, the skip-when-short rule, and the lock shape. The existing "nothing playable before the claim" assertion was **refined rather than dropped**: the always-shut list now covers the new reading steps, and the two Deception steps are asserted separately to mark the trap and lock the rest of the hand.
- Full `./mvnw test`: 681 tests, the same 3 pre-existing adventure/keep cache-pin failures, no new ones.

## Tóm tắt

Việc số 2 trong "Việc còn lại của P2 phần (b)" ở ROADMAP. **Không đụng Engine** — `so_don` đã nằm sẵn cạnh `doanh_so` ở mọi ô `gopSucKhoeCongTy()` trả về, nên không có chuyện bẫy số 4 ở lượt này.

- Hai biểu đồ dùng chung **một** dải tab đơn vị, **một** dải nút phụ và **một** chú giải — chúng luôn nói về cùng một kỳ, lặp lại ba lần chỉ tổ rối. Đơn vị trục dọc ghi ở tiêu đề từng biểu đồ.
- Rê chuột vào chấm nào cũng đọc được **cả hai** con số của điểm đó.
- Hạ chiều cao mỗi biểu đồ (230 → 200) vì giờ xếp dọc hai cái; giữ nguyên là phải cuộn mới thấy dải nút tháng nằm dưới.

**Kèm sửa trục dọc** (áp cho cả hai biểu đồ): trước lấy thẳng giá trị lớn nhất làm đỉnh nên mốc chia ra `6.667` và `13.333` — đọc biểu đồ mà phải nhẩm. Giờ làm tròn bước chia về 1/2/5 × 10ⁿ:

| | trước | sau |
|---|---|---|
| doanh số (nghìn đ) | 0 · 6.667 · 13.333 · 20.000 | 0 · 5.000 · 10.000 · 15.000 |
| số đơn | 0 · 1 · 1 · 2 | 0 · 2 · 4 · 6 |

Số đơn bị ép bước **nguyên** — đơn hàng không có nửa đơn, không thì hai mốc lẻ cùng làm tròn về 1 và trục hiện "1, 1, 2". Trục tiền có thêm sàn 3.000 đ: cả kỳ dưới 3.000 đ thì bốn mốc cùng ra "0" sau khi chia nghìn — ca này **có thật**, sổ 09/2026 có đơn bị chiết khấu hết thành 0 đ.

- [x] Ghim rằng hai biểu đồ **vẽ hai chuỗi khác nhau** chứ không cùng một chuỗi: đỉnh trục Doanh số là số lớn (6.000 nghìn đ), đỉnh trục Số đơn là số nhỏ (6 đơn).
- [x] Ghim trục chia chẵn: bốn mốc số đơn đều nguyên và **không mốc nào trùng nhau**.
- [x] Phép canh hình học đổi cho hợp đỉnh trục giờ có khoảng dư: **chấm giá trị 0 phải nằm đúng trên đường đáy** (lệch 0.0px). Đây vẫn là phép bắt đúng lỗi cũ "quên cộng lề trên" — nếu quên, cả chuỗi trôi lên 12px.

body:
Adds a generic follower ledger verifier for repositories where phone/tablet work may lead other maintained environments.

The verifier distinguishes build/runtime/artifact/physical-device/publication evidence, requires exact source binding for accepted followers, rejects stale receipts and unexplained N/A, and keeps unsupported targets unresolved rather than green.

Commands:
- `aici-followers verify JOBS RECEIPTS`
- `aici-followers pending JOBS RECEIPTS [TRIGGER]`
- `aici-followers matrix JOBS RECEIPTS [TRIGGER]`

Includes strict C17 self-tests and shared agent policy. Consumer-specific target inference remains in the consumer repository rather than hard-coding Cat Food architecture knowledge into AICI.

body:
> ベースは PR #40（要件3）です。#40 のマージ後に main へ向け直します。パイプラインの記録係（`recorder.ts`）に相乗りするためです。

AI Company OS v3.1 の実装を段階に分け、その第1段階（§25 Observability）です。

## 要件書と実装の照合結果

先に、要件書の前提と実際の差分をお伝えします。

| 要件書の前提 | 実際 |
|---|---|
| Department | ✅ `DEPARTMENTS`（静的config。ハードコード） |
| Skill | ⚠️ 14件あるが**大半が `status: "planned"`（未実装）** |
| Workflow | ❌ **エンティティとして存在しません** |
| Employee Agent | ⚠️ 概念が2つに割れています（`Secretary` と `AgentRole`） |
| Agent権限（§24） | ❌ `memoryScope` はあるが `permissions` / `risk_level` は**ありません** |
| Observability（§25） | ⚠️ 部分的。**処理時間とタスク単位のコストは未記録** |
| CEO Feedback（§14） | ✅ `ReviewFeedback` として実装済み |

## なぜ §25 を最初にやるか

**Pattern Analyzer（§4）も Proposal Score（§8）も、この層が無いと成立しません。**

§8 は Time Saving（20点）と Cost Reduction（10点）に配点していますが、**その元データが存在しませんでした**。記録は6箇所以上に散らばり、形式もバラバラで、処理時間は一切測っていません。

反復検出は数週間の蓄積が前提なので、**土台を先に動かして貯め始めることに意味があります。**

## 設計上の判断

**既存の記録は消していません。** 横断で数えるための薄い層として併存させます。移行を伴う統合は、途中で失敗すると履歴を失うためです。

**Observer は観測だけを担当します。** §3の「会社構造を変更する権限を持たない」に従い、`events.md` 以外には触りません。

### signature の正規化が反復検出の精度を決めます

「同じ依頼が3回以上で Skill 候補」（§4）を判定するため、日付・数値・括弧の揺れを落として仕事の種類だけを残します。**ここが揺れると反復がすり抜け、落としすぎると別の仕事が混ざります。** 両方向をテストで固定しました。

### CEO介入率の定義（§13）

**承認そのものは介入に数えていません。** 承認は設計上の関門であって手戻りではないためです。差し戻しと「編集して承認」だけを分子にします。

§13自身が「人間介入率0%を目指してはいけない」としています。承認を介入に数えると、**指標を改善しようとする力が安全弁を外す方向に働きます**。ここは定義の時点で分けておく必要があります。

### 測れないものを0で埋めていません

処理時間・コストは測定できたイベントだけで集計します。0で埋めると「速くなった」「安くなった」と誤検出され、**Proposal Score が実態と逆を向きます**。テストで固定しました。

## 次の段階（参考）

```
Phase 1  観測の土台                    ← 本PR
Phase 2  組織モデルのデータ化（Agent統一・権限・Workflow）
Phase 3  Observer + Pattern Analyzer + Proposal Engine + Score
Phase 4  Daily/Weekly/Monthly Review + Health Score
Phase 5  Implementation Spec + CEO承認UI
Phase 6  自動実装・自動PR（Protected Core強制）   ← 最後
Phase 7  RPG UI
```

|---|---|
| `npx tsc --noEmit` | エラーなし |
| `npm run build` | ✓ Compiled successfully |
| `test:qa` | 134 pass（うち新規13件） |
| `test:architecture` | 20 pass |

author: kareemsakr
body:
## Why

The RADR remote cannot talk to our servers while its Bluetooth is on: once Bluetooth is running there is not enough contiguous memory left for a secure connection, and every attempt to squeeze it in has broken again with the next feature. The OSSM does have working secure connections, so pairing and firmware update now run on the OSSM. The remote sends one Bluetooth command and shows what the OSSM reports.

While testing on the bench we found two problems that were already hitting OSSMs in the field, and fixed them here:

- The OSSM rebooted every ~66 s and crashed whenever a remote connected. The firmware fingerprint was recomputed on every Bluetooth read and that allocation failed under load. It is now computed once at boot.
- The OSSM could not open a secure connection at all once MQTT was up, so the once-a-minute pairing check failed every time. The MQTT connection parked 20 KB of fixed TLS buffers forever and fragmented the heap. TLS buffers are now allocated per record. Free memory with MQTT up went from 19.6 KB (largest block 9 KB) to 50 KB (largest block 24 KB).

## What changed

- Bluetooth accepts `go:pairing`, `go:update` and `go:restart` from any screen.
- One code path for every secure request: pause MQTT, check that enough memory is free, do the request, resume MQTT. If memory is short it says so instead of hanging.
- The OSSM reports progress in its state (checking, update available, installing, paired, failed with a reason) so the remote can follow along.
- New screens: update available, update failed, pairing failed, each with the reason.
- The state message is built with a JSON library; the old string concatenation sometimes produced invalid JSON.

Why so many files: the state machine, the pages, the Bluetooth command handling, the update code and the pairing code all had to learn the new states, and the memory settings live in the four sdkconfig files.

## Safeguards so this does not come back

- Every secure request checks the largest free memory block first and logs free/largest before and after, plus a line when MQTT is resumed. A regression shows up in the serial log on the bench, not at a customer.
- The update and pairing tasks are created only after MQTT is paused, and creation is checked. A failure shows an error screen.
- Native tests cover the Bluetooth command grammar and the state JSON (220 cases).
- Bench: 20 update checks and 3 pairings in a row with a remote attached, largest free block unchanged at 31.7 KB, MQTT resumed every time, 45 h uptime without a reset.

Companion RADR PR: https://github.com/researchanddesire/radr-wireless-remote/pull/140. Ship this one first; old remotes keep working with it.

author: mrandreyisachenko
body:
The stores occupy **778 MB** and contain **238**.

| store | contains | occupies | files | per record |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| event archive | 96.7 MB | 315 MB | 80,624 | 1,258 B |
| journal, root | 50.5 MB | 165 MB | 42,220 | 1,254 B |
| journal, user | 90.6 MB | 298 MB | 76,170 | 1,247 B |

One file per record at ~1.25 KB against a 4 KB allocation unit. The archive is bounded at 256 MB, held 96.7 and occupied 315 — **over a bound it had not reached**. At that bound it would occupy ~840 MB, and the journals another ~660: a gigabyte and a half where the configuration says 456 MB.

A bound is a promise about a disk. This one was not.

## What changed

- **Stored records are measured, not estimated.** `st_blocks` is what the filesystem charged and it is exact; rounding a record's length would be a guess a compressed or inlined record makes wrong.
- **A record not yet written is rounded up.** It is the one number the filesystem cannot be asked for, and counting it at its length admits one record more than the bound meant to, on every append.
- **What the archive reports is what it counts.** Two numbers differing threefold — one called "size", one enforcing the bound — is how this stayed invisible.
- **The age window is 7 days.** Thirty was configured and never applied: at ~12 MB/day the byte bound arrives in about twenty-one, so the window an operator read off the configuration was a number nothing ever used. The two bounds now arrive together.

## Both paths, because they are different code

The archive learns a record's size when it **publishes** one and when it **reads its directory**. If those disagreed, what the bound counts would depend on whether the archive had been restarted.

A mutation of the directory path **survived** the first version of the regression, because the published path answered first from the cache. The test now reads a size both ways and requires them equal. Five mutations, all caught.

## Installing this evicts

The archive holds eight days and 315 MB occupied; it will trim to seven and 256, dropping about **fifteen thousand** of the oldest records and writing overflow records that say so. That is the change doing what it was asked to, stated here so it is not discovered.

## Not in scope

The spool and the journals carry the same defect. Their bound is the one that was left alone deliberately, and correcting their accounting means restating every size assertion in their tests — mechanical, and not safe to do quickly. It is named in the roadmap.

Closes the largest product gap found this session: a one-time purchase (10 products, up to $1,500) recorded an audit row and delivered **nothing** — no buyer confirmation, no signal to anyone that a sale happened.

author: obvious-autobuild-staging[bot]
body:
## Why

The retrospective review of PR #22 (right-click snooze, merged as `bdb6577`) verified seven findings. The two majors are user-facing bugs: in the docked/user-hidden state, clicking a snooze menu item never arms the snooze — the dock's capture-phase click handler swallows the click and wipes the standing "hidden" preference instead. This PR fixes all seven, fix-forward from `main`.

## Findings → Fixes

| # | Severity | Finding (at bdb6577) | Fix in this PR |
|---|----------|----------------------|----------------|
| F1 | MAJOR | `handleDockClick` (src/widget/feedback-toolbar.ts:695-715): while `restingMode === "docked"`, the capture-phase handler `preventDefault` + `stopPropagation` + `revealFully()` on every click that isn't a `[data-toolbar-action]` — and snooze menu items are not toolbar actions. Clicking "Hide for 1 hour" in the docked/user-hidden state never armed the snooze; `revealFully()` persisted `userHidden=false`, wiping the standing preference. | `handleDockClick` now returns early when `event.composedPath().includes(this.snoozeMenu)` — menu clicks belong to the menu, never to dock/undock logic. Two unit regressions (user-hidden `"false"` survives; drag-docked `"true"` survives). |
| F2 | MAJOR | `closeSnoozeMenu` (:773-785) never restored focus on close — Escape stranded the keyboard user on `<body>` (menu a11y spec, art_Z020DA0s). | `openSnoozeMenu` captures the previously-focused element (resolved against the shadow root); `closeSnoozeMenu` restores it on every close path: Escape, outside pointerdown, drag start, and item selection. After a selection the bar hides, so focus returning into the hidden bar is the accepted choice — documented in the field comment. When nothing held focus, the bar's drag handle is the fallback (a real focusable element). Three unit tests. |
| F3 | MAJOR | The composedPath unit regression (tests/unit/feedback-toolbar.test.ts:864-888) was vacuous: happy-dom does not retarget shadow-internal events, so an event dispatched directly on a menu item carries `target` = item — a shape real browsers never produce. Reverting the F1 fix would not fail it. | New Playwright e2e witness (`tests/e2e/specs/snooze-docked-state.spec.ts`) in real Chromium: seeds `toolbarVisible: "false"`, hovers the docked bar's peek sliver, right-clicks it, performs a real mouse click on the "Hide for 1 hour" item, and asserts the snooze arms while the standing preference survives. **Proven to bite** (see Bite-proof below). |
| F4 | MINOR | Two `JSON.parse(...) as {...}` casts in tests (:938/:956). | `readActiveSnooze()` is now exported from the module (typed); assertions run on its inferred return value — no casts. |
| F5 | MINOR | Storage event with `key === null` (`localStorage.clear()`) handled in code but untested. | Unit test: dispatch `StorageEvent` with `key: null` → snooze clears and the bar restores without throwing. |
| F6 | NIT | Stale comment ":883-885" claimed popover suppression was "the only state that returns opacity 0" — snoozed now does too. | Comment updated to name both opacity-zero states. |
| F7 | MINOR | The storage listener (:355) accepted any event with a matching key, regardless of `storageArea`. | Guard: events whose `storageArea` is not this tab's `localStorage` (sessionStorage area, synthetic events without one, environments where storage access throws — via the new `tabLocalStorage()` helper) are ignored. Two new unit tests; existing storage-event tests now present `storageArea: window.localStorage` like real browsers do. |

## Commit map

- `99aaa47` fix: guard dock click handler against snooze menu targets (F1)
- `5b5d37e` fix: restore focus when the snooze menu closes (F2)
- `af2bbba` chore: stale comment + storageArea guard (F6, F7)
- `ad6d72b` test: retargeting e2e witness, storage-clear path, cast removal (F3, F5, F4)

Commit 3 (F6/F7) precedes the test commit so every commit tip stays green: the F7 tests require the F7 source guard.

## F3 bite-proof (revert-the-guard, observe red, restore, observe green)

With the `composedPath()` guard temporarily reverted and the bundle rebuilt, in real Chromium:

- The e2e witness fails exactly as diagnosed — the bar undocks (`data-presentation="open"`) instead of arming the snooze: [tc-2-error.txt (e2e failure)](https://stage.obvious.ai/p/allow-user-to-hide-the-feedback-floating-bar-i-thi-BLHwUfzb/f/tc-2-errortxt-WU3cLKmG)
- Both F1 unit regressions fail as well: [tc-2-error.txt (unit failures)](https://stage.obvious.ai/p/allow-user-to-hide-the-feedback-floating-bar-i-thi-BLHwUfzb/f/tc-2-errortxt-tcMDjhxQ)

With the guard restored: witness passes (1.6s) and the full e2e suite is green (14 passed, 1 pre-existing skip). Output recorded in the tc-2 QA evidence.

## Test evidence (QA runs recorded against head ad6d72b)

- **tc-1 — docked/user-hidden interaction, dogfooded in real Chromium** (seed `toolbarVisible: "false"` → reload → docked/hidden at rest → hover peek sliver → right-click → menu opens → real click "Hide for 1 hour" → bar fully hides → `toolbarVisible` still `"false"`):
  - [tc-1-recording.webm](https://stage.obvious.ai/p/allow-user-to-hide-the-feedback-floating-bar-i-thi-BLHwUfzb/f/tc-1-recordingwebm-OkmDfDgY) — the full flow
  - [Menu open over the peeked sliver](https://stage.obvious.ai/p/allow-user-to-hide-the-feedback-floating-bar-i-thi-BLHwUfzb/f/tc-1-resultpng-n5iz18qy)
  - [After: bar fully removed, snooze armed](https://stage.obvious.ai/p/allow-user-to-hide-the-feedback-floating-bar-i-thi-BLHwUfzb/f/tc-1-afterpng-FpQCkXI9)
  - Plus before/peek screenshots and the DOM-state assertion log in the tc-1 QA run.
- **tc-2 — witness bite-proof** (failure logs above + restored-green outputs) in the tc-2 QA run.

## Verification

- `bun run test:typecheck` — clean (tsc --noEmit; Bun strips types, so the compiler run is required evidence)
- `bun run test:unit` — 175 pass, 0 fail (baseline 168 + 7 new: 2×F1, 3×F2, 1×F5, 2×F7)
- `bun run build` — ESM + DTS success
- `bun run test:e2e` — 14 passed, 1 skipped (pre-existing skip)
- No linter in this repo.

## Notes

- The remote `feat/toolbar-snooze` branch is untouched and remains.
- AC impact: AC1 (complete visual removal + restoration) and AC7 (standing-preference preservation) are re-evidenced by tc-1/tc-2 against the tested head; AC6 (a11y/focus) is re-evidenced by the F2 tests. Full AC re-verification belongs to the retrospective follow-up.

🔗 [Obvious Project](https://stage.obvious.ai/p/allow-user-to-hide-the-feedback-floating-bar-i-thi-BLHwUfzb) · 🧵 [Obvious Thread](https://stage.obvious.ai/p/allow-user-to-hide-the-feedback-floating-bar-i-thi-BLHwUfzb?thread=th_i7zRKrs9)

## Why this matters
host.network-peer accepts a named private peer, including an mDNS name resolving to link-local IPv6. getaddrinfo supplies the interface in sockaddr[3], but the observer discarded it and connected with scope 0. This reported reachable services as closed and collapsed identical link-local addresses on distinct interfaces.
Carry the resolver's numeric scope in the address, pass it to TCP endpoints and retain it in ICMP probes and the content-free receipt.

All 502 tool-loop-guard tests pass; a new receipt test verifies the existing consumer accepts scoped IPv6 and retains its evidence.
Linux/WSL tests use resolver/socket fixtures. No real remote IPv6 host was probed. Kept draft for independent network-boundary review; this does not expand allowed peers or ports.

Developed with AI assistance.

body:
## Summary
- `infra/docker-compose.pc-gamer-workers.yml`'s worker services ran `npm run build --workspace=@intcloudsysops/orchestrator` — this builds only that one package, not its workspace dependencies.
- `apps/orchestrator` depends on `@intcloudsysops/universe` (via `content-studio`'s `universe-bridge.ts`), `@intcloudsysops/prompt-guard`, `@intcloudsysops/ml`, and several others whose `main`/`types` point to `dist/` — none of that gets built first, so the worker crash-looped with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` on `@intcloudsysops/universe` (same bug class as #1178, different container).
- Fix: `npx turbo build --filter=@intcloudsysops/orchestrator` instead — turbo's `dependsOn: ["^build"]` pipeline (already configured in `turbo.json`) builds the full dependency graph automatically, in order. This is more robust than any manually-maintained list (which is exactly what caused #1178 and #1181 earlier today).

## Verification
- Applied directly on the PC-gamer host (SSH) to unblock immediately: worker now reports `{"status":"ok","service":"orchestrator","role":"worker","mode":"worker-enabled"}` on `:3011/health`.
- Verified locally: `node_modules/turbo/bin/turbo build --filter=@intcloudsysops/orchestrator` → 15/15 tasks successful, correctly builds `universe`, `content-studio`, `ml`, `llm-gateway`, `prompt-guard`, etc. before `orchestrator`.
- Also had to install the NVIDIA Container Toolkit on the gamer's WSL host (was never configured — `nvidia-ctk: command not found`, `docker: could not select device driver "nvidia"`) so the `ollama` container could actually get GPU access. Not a code change; documented here for anyone else who reconnects this host from scratch.

## Risk
Low — worker-only compose change, verified against a real running worker.

body:
Summary

Begins Phase 9 Caribbean country coverage with the first bounded Jamaica increment.
This change extends the existing river-name artifact pipeline using a country-specific profile, independently sourced target rivers, content-addressed artifacts, provenance metadata, and explicit partial-coverage semantics.

Jamaica coverage
The initial target set is based on the Jamaica Water Resources Authority’s A National Water Resources Master Plan for Jamaica 2022:
- Great River
- Montego River
- Rio Grande
- Rio Cobre
- Black River

The resulting artifact is classified as partial:
- 4 of 5 targets passed the source-to-source evaluation
- Montego River remains explicitly unverified
- 14 OSM display features captured
- 31 HydroRIVERS reaches indexed
- Artifact size: 122,971 bytes
- SHA-256: da8057032e63852a3cbd81a635ab0e329aae6b50709168e1f2e7c7e6a33afaca

The implementation does not fabricate a Montego River match or promote source-name agreement to surveyed positional accuracy.

Implementation details

- Added the Jamaica build profile and production geography ID.
- Generated the immutable Jamaica artifact, manifest, evaluation, and source record.
- Added Jamaica-specific regression coverage.
- Updated RIVER_NAME_COVERAGE.md with the target scope, result, limitations, and authoritative reference.
- Recorded Phase 9 state, approved baseline, verification commands, and verification evidence.
- Corrected phase scope metadata so the generated Jamaica artifacts are explicitly recognized as in-scope.

Verification

The approved baseline at 863d52b passed:
- Backend baseline: 240 passed, 3 skipped
- TypeScript: passed
- Frontend lint: passed

Post-edit verification passed:

- Backend: 244 test cases, no failures
- TypeScript: passed
- Frontend lint: passed
- Baseline comparison and changed-file scope: passed
- Targeted river-name tests: 6 passed

Scope exclusions

This PR does not:

- Add runtime Nominatim or other scraping.
- Commit raw geospatial source datasets.
- Modify the GeoParquet schema or delivery architecture.
- Add Central or South American country coverage.
- Perform database migrations, production writes, deployment, or secret changes.

Follow-up

After review, Phase 9 can continue with the next independently scoped Caribbean country increment. Jamaica remains partial unless additional evidence supports revisiting the Montego River result.

Independent reference: [Jamaica Water Resources Authority — A National Water Resources Master Plan for Jamaica 2022](https://www.wra.gov.jm/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/A-National-Water-Resources-Master-Plan-for-Jamaica-2022.pdf)

author: eastcountyaquatics
body:
## Summary
Two real issues found during a codebase audit:

- `dashboard.html`'s Purchases table rendered `description` unescaped (self-XSS via a crafted athlete name); the same block escaped `profile.phone` but not `profile.full_name`/`user.email` right next to it — an inconsistency that gave away the oversight. All three now go through `escapeHtml`.
- `sponsorships.website_url`/`logo_url` only had a length cap. Anyone can submit a sponsorship inquiry anonymously, and admin-sponsors.html renders both as clickable links for the owner. `<input type="url">` doesn't restrict scheme (`javascript:...` passes browser validation) and RLS doesn't check format, so a malicious submission's link would run arbitrary JS in the owner's session on click. Fixed with a DB check constraint requiring `http(s)://` or null — already applied to production and confirmed no existing rows violated it. `sponsor.html` now normalizes a bare `www.co.com` entry to `https://` instead of bouncing a legitimate sponsor with a raw DB error, and `admin-sponsors.html` only renders the link if it's still http(s), as a second layer.

## Test plan
- [ ] Confirm the `sponsorship_url_scheme_check` migration is applied (already done directly against production and verified)
- [ ] Submit the sponsor form with a bare domain (no `https://`) and confirm it's accepted and normalized
- [ ] View a purchase whose description contains special characters and confirm it renders as text, not markup

author: devops-igor
body:
## Issue #86 — capacity invariant undocumented
**Problem:** the `MaxPeersPerBackend` serialization contract (who holds which lock, when) lived only in reviewers' heads; nothing asserted it under load.
**Fix:** serialization contract documented on `Pool.IncrementConnections/DecrementConnections/SetConnectionCount`, `Service.mu`, `HandleIncomingPeer`, `FilterHealthy`, and the `ReplacementHook` path (fixed `s.mu` -> `sm.mu` lock order, no gap). 200-goroutine stress test through `HandleIncomingPeer` asserts `MaxPeersPerBackend` is never exceeded, passing under `-race`. No reservation counter in this change (future PR).

## Issue #89 — forwarder srcIP rebind hijack
**Problem:** the srcIP self-heal rebind path would rebind a forwarder to any claimed inner source IP, letting a spoofed peer hijack an existing session.
**Fix:** rebind now requires the claimed inner source IP to be inside the portal client subnet AND currently unassigned, checked atomically under the forwarder write lock. Spoofed rebinds are dropped, never forwarded, and counted (`SpoofedRebinds` / `ErrSpoofedSourceIP`). Legitimate NAT self-heal preserved. `NewForwarder` plumbed with the portal subnet CIDR.

## API-visible change
`NewForwarder` gained a `portalSubnetCIDR` parameter; all call sites updated.

## Verification
- 7 smoke gates: build, vet, `go test -race` (30/30 packages), stress test, rebind guard tests re-run PASS, guard verified in source, contract docs present at all sites
- pm_bot independent re-verification: `go test -race` 30/30 packages; stress + 3 rebind guard tests re-run individually PASS

## Tests
- `internal/vpn/capacity_stress_test.go` — capacity stress, 200 goroutines, cap=6
- `internal/vpn/forwarder/rebind_guard_test.go` — two-peer hijack blocked; legit rebind preserved; out-of-subnet claim fail-closed

Fixes #86

author: danirv
body:
## Summary

Prepares Ypsilon 2.5.0 as a semantic-accuracy release without widening the mechanical write surface.

### Home Assistant state-class corrections

The current Home Assistant sensor model defines `measurement` for present-time measurements and explicitly excludes historical aggregations. It defines `total_increasing` for positive cumulative totals which can periodically start a new meter cycle.

Accordingly this PR:
- keeps instantaneous `flowRate` as `measurement`;
- keeps `dailyWaterConsumption` as `total_increasing`;
- keeps current remaining treatment capacity as `measurement`;
- removes `measurement` from `averageWeeklyWaterConsumption`, because the device already reports a historical weekly average;
- removes `measurement` from `periodicWaterProduction`, because the observed field is not established as a present-time measurement or a cumulative meter.

Regression tests pin these choices.

### F79D semantics

- Adds a read-only `Work pattern` enum for field 9 using the exact 0..9 labels recovered from the legacy WaterDevice application.
- Keeps existing `flow` / `time` regeneration entity state keys for backward compatibility while improving their translated labels.
- Centralizes F79D semantic mappings in the transport-neutral `runxin/` layer.
- Marks field 9 as observed on real F79D hardware.
- Adds semantic protocol information to diagnostics while retaining raw codes/state.
- Documents verified cubic-metre volume/service-flow interpretation.
- Documents cloud-only `regenerationTimes` as intentionally unmapped because no local F79D field correspondence has been proven.

### Safety / compatibility

- No new writes are enabled.
- Fields 9 (`workPattern`) and 46 (`regenerationPattern`) remain outside the safe Home Assistant write whitelist.
- Existing entity IDs and stable regeneration state keys are preserved.
- Existing strict SET -> read-back reconciliation is unchanged.

Version: `2.5.0`.

author: zx8086
body:
https://linear.app/siobytes/issue/SIO-1694

Prerequisite for verifying [SIO-1369](https://linear.app/siobytes/issue/SIO-1369): until the eval can see what the agent actually queried, a gate-8 run cannot tell whether the elastic prompt rule worked.

## The bug

`datasourcesCovered` read only `targetDataSources` — the dispatch list `entityExtractor` writes once. The correlation layer's Sends (`enforce-node.ts`) spread `...state` and override only `currentDataSource`, so a reactively fetched datasource lands in `dataSourceResults` and **never** in `targetDataSources`.

With 15+ rules declaring `requiredAgent: "elastic-agent"`, the metric under-reported evidence the agent genuinely gathered. Part of SIO-1369's reported 3-of-5 failure was a measurement artifact, not missing evidence.

## The fix reads `firstAttempts`, not `dataSourceResults`

The obvious fix is dead on arrival: the raw array is **deliberately never returned** by the eval run function. `data` is `z.unknown()` and `toolOutputs[].rawJson` would ship full tool payloads to LangSmith, breaking the privacy invariant documented at `run-function.ts`.

`firstAttempts` is an existing projection of the same array — already in the returned output, already in `FrozenOutputSchema`. So: no run-function change, no fixture re-record, no new egress.

**Only a successful fetch counts.** `firstStatus: "error"` includes the "no tools available, MCP server may not be connected" case — a dispatch that obtained nothing; counting it would swap an under-report for an over-report. `recovered: true` counts, since a failed first attempt with a later success did produce evidence. Mirrors the precedent in `toolDataUtilization`.

## Also adds `datasources_precision`

The recall metric computes only `expected \ actual`, so extras have always been free — a run querying all seven datasources scored 1 on every example. Over-fan-out was invisible in both the score and the comment, despite an elastic dispatch costing a 60 super-step ReAct loop under a 360s timeout.

Kept as a **separate key** rather than folded into the existing score: they answer different questions (did we get the evidence / did we pay too much for it), and silently turning a recall metric into an F-score would break comparability with historical runs. Emits nothing when the example declares no expectation, so it cannot dilute the dataset.

Registered in `run-eval.ts` (gate 8) only — `run-mcp-tool-eval` scores tool selection, not datasource scope, so precision there would be noise.

## Verification

- 61 pass / 0 fail in `evaluators.test.ts`, including **9 new tests**. This evaluator had **no test coverage at all** before, so the recall-only behaviour was never pinned either.
- Full agent package: 4501 pass / 24 fail. The same 24 fail on the untouched base tree (proven by stashing this diff in the previous session's run); pass count rises 4492 → 4501, exactly the 9 added.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean in the worktree.
- Biome: **0 errors**. The 4 `noUnusedFunctionParameters` warnings are pre-existing — confirmed by checking the base file in-tree, where they sit at 548/565/625/651 versus 610/627/687/713 here, a uniform +62 shift from this diff, on four `tool*` functions this change never touches.

## Behavioural note for reviewers

This shifts `datasources_covered` for the two other runners that already import it (`run-incident-replay-eval`, `run-mcp-tool-eval`). A LangSmith A/B against a pre-fix baseline is **not comparable on that key**. That is inherent to fixing the metric rather than a reason to defer, but worth knowing before reading any cross-run comparison.

## Not verified

No live `eval:agent` run was performed — that is SIO-1369's remaining step, and is now interpretable because of this change.

author: danielsmith960416
body:
The first connector a customer can actually switch on, end to end: read the
gateway's documentation, hold the credential somewhere safe, put a page in
front of it.

## What is here

| | |
|---|---|
| `lib/connectors/paystack/api.ts` | Paystack's HTTP API, GET only |
| `lib/connectors/paystack/reads.ts` | those answers in Amryn's words |
| `lib/connectors/paystack/provider.ts` | Paystack behind ConnectorProvider |
| `lib/connectors/native.ts` | which connectors have an implementation |
| `features/connectors/` | the connect and disconnect actions, and the key field |
| `data/integrations/[connector]` | the page where a key is typed |
| migration 43 | Supabase Vault as the credential store |

## Written from the documentation, not from memory

Every path, parameter and response field comes from Paystack's own reference.
Where the reference is silent this is silent too, and says so in a comment
rather than filling the gap — the page cursor and the key format are the two
places that happens.

Confirming the catalogue row cost four of its six claimed reads. `refunds` and
`payouts` are real and unread; `customers` arrives inside a transaction rather
than from the list endpoint the row implied; `fees` is a field, not a fetch.
A shorter honest list is worth more than a long one nobody can cite.

## Read-only is structural, not promised

A Paystack secret key can initialise a transaction, charge a stored
authorisation and take a partial debit — the same key, the same header, and the
gateway offers no narrower scope. So the narrowing is in the code: GET only, no
method that takes a body, and a test over the client's own source that fails if
a write path ever appears in it.

## Where the credential lives

`data_connections` has carried this comment since migration 02: *"Credentials
live in the secret manager and are referenced by handle, never stored in the
tenant database."* There was no secret manager. Migration 43 names one —
Supabase Vault, already installed — and the grants are the point:

- `store_connection_credential` — signed in, needs `manage_integrations`
- `forget_connection_credential` — same, and quiet when already gone
- `connection_credential` — **`service_role` only**

The web application cannot read a credential back. Not even its own
organisation's. The worker can. `native.ts` builds two different providers so
that is structural rather than conventional: the page gets one with no
credential store and physically cannot read one, and a test asserts it.

Checked against the live database rather than assumed — the extension version,
the function signatures, that `anon` and `authenticated` have no grant on
`vault.secrets` — and the create/read/delete round trip was proved inside a
transaction that was rolled back.

## Two honest corrections recorded rather than hidden

`Invitation.expiresAt` becomes `Date | null`. A key is typed into a page inside
Amryn, behind the same sign-in as every other page; an invented thirty-minute
expiry would be a deadline the interface announces and nothing enforces.

`adopt()` assumes a stored credential readable by handle, which is exactly
wrong for a key typed in — it would have needed the one grant this design
withholds. `KeyAuthorisedProvider.checkKey()` is the shape that fits, and
checking before storing is better anyway: a typo leaves no connection row, no
secret in the Vault and nothing to clean up.

## Also

Paystack moves from Growth to **Starter**, so every plan reaches it. A tier
sold with two connection slots and nothing to spend them on was selling an
empty slot. The ceilings are unchanged — 2 / 8 / 20 / unlimited, confirmed
against the live plan table — so this widens who may connect, not how much.

The integrations page compared `data_source_id` (a uuid) to a catalogue id, so
a connected system would have shown as unconnected. Nobody noticed because
nothing could connect.

## Not in this change

The sync. A connection made today is a verified, stored credential and nothing
more, and the page says that in those words rather than letting a green badge
imply figures are arriving.

## Checks

- 1,103 unit tests, 6 skipped
- 459 schema assertions, all 43 migrations applied from scratch
- typecheck, lint, production build clean
- no secrets in 356 bundled files
- migration 43 is additive: two functions, one partial index, no table altered

author: jposluns
body:
Found by a tri-family QA scan of the whole corpus (Claude Fable 5, Codex GPT-6 Astra, Gemini 3.1 Pro, one identical brief, read-only). Every claim here was then checked against the vendor's own page or source during this change, not recalled and not taken from a worker's report.

## The one that matters most

**vLLM.** `model-servers.md` recommended an API key and verified only `/v1/models`. vLLM's security page states the key authenticates only the `/v1`, `/v2` and `/inference` prefixes, lists `/invocations` as requiring no key while reaching the same inference capability as the protected routes, and says plainly not to rely on the key alone. A reader who followed the guide exactly, and whose Verify step passed, was left with an unauthenticated inference endpoint. The guide now states the limitation and Verify probes `/invocations` for a refusal at the proxy.

## Wrong setting

**Airflow.** `[core] auth_manager` selects the auth manager. `[fab] auth_backends` selects API authentication backends and the FAB provider documents it as independent of the auth manager. The guide named the latter for a job only the former does, so a reader could follow it and leave the dev-only Simple Auth Manager active.

## Stale defaults and plan claims

**OpenTelemetry Collector.** `localhost` has been the default host for every server in Collector components since v0.110.0. The guide called the all-interfaces listener the default.

**Vercel.** The 9 September 2026 changelog makes All Deployments protection free on every plan including Hobby, where production protection previously required the USD 150 per month add-on. `nextjs.md` and `paas.md` still required Pro or Enterprise, contradicting `cloud-identity-proxies.md`, which was already current. Three guides, three different answers, all flagged September 2026.

## Verify steps that could not discriminate

**Prefect.** The server exempts `/health` and `/ready` from the auth string on GET so container probes keep working. Verify expected a 401 there, which would fail a *correctly* configured server and push the reader to change something that was right. Now probes `POST /api/flows/filter`.

**Langfuse.** `/api/public/health` returns health status by design, not a login response. Verify now checks the dashboard root.

**MinIO.** Anonymous policies are set per bucket, so a denial at the service root does not prove any bucket is private. Verify now checks a bucket listing and a known private object.

**OTLP probe.** It sent `{}` with curl's default form encoding, which the Collector rejects with 415 on content type before authentication is reached, so the rejection proved nothing. Now sends OTLP JSON with the content type set.

## Notes

Sources added for every claim. `site/llms-full.txt` regenerated through `scripts/build-llms-full.sh`. Whole-corpus gate suite run once before push: all pass.

One finding from the same scan was **refuted** on checking and is deliberately not here: the `gpu-clouds.md` RunPod "port above 70000" wording tracks RunPod's own documentation faithfully.

author: jharcey-flexion
body:
# Purpose

Bootstraps a new `dora-metrics` workspace for reporting DORA metrics from this repo's GitHub Actions history, starting with Deployment Frequency, and wires it into a scheduled GitHub Actions workflow so the report runs automatically without a local checkout. Addresses GH #262 (CAMS-72). Additional DORA metrics (lead time, change failure rate, MTTR) will be added to this same PR as follow-up commits rather than as separate PRs.

# Major Changes

* New `dora-metrics` workspace (added to root `package.json`), scaffolded to match `dev-tools` conventions (tsx, vitest, shared eslint config)
* `@octokit/rest` fetch layer (`src/github/fetch-workflow-runs.ts`) that paginates `continuous-deployment.yml` workflow runs, filtered to `main`-branch/`completed` runs, stopping once past a `since` cutoff
* Pure compute layer (`src/metrics/deployment-frequency.ts`) that buckets successful runs into fixed-width periods and computes deployments/day — no I/O, easy to unit test, and the shape future metrics will extend
* CSV output layer (`src/output/write-csv.ts`) and CLI entrypoint (`src/report-deployment-frequency.ts`, run via `npm run report:deployment-frequency`) that writes `data/deployment-frequency.csv` and logs a one-line summary
* New `.github/workflows/dora-metrics.yml` workflow (weekly cron + `workflow_dispatch`) that installs dependencies, runs the report, and uploads `deployment-frequency.csv` as the `dora-metrics-deployment-frequency` build artifact — read-only permissions (`contents: read`, `actions: read`), no new secrets beyond the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`

# Testing/Validation

Implemented using TDD — unit tests for the fetch layer (mocked Octokit; pagination boundary, branch/status filtering, request-shape assertions), compute layer (bucketing, bucket-edge behavior, success-only filtering, deploymentsPerDay math, empty-input handling), and CSV writer (header/row formatting, parent-directory creation). All pass, along with `typecheck` and `lint`.

Also ran the CLI live against this repo (`GITHUB_TOKEN=$(gh auth token) npm run report:deployment-frequency`), producing a correct CSV: 212 successful `main` deployments over the trailing 90 days across 13 weekly buckets.

The new workflow file passes this repo's pre-commit workflow checks (`check-github-workflows` schema validation, `update-workflow-diagrams` guard). `workflow_dispatch` can only be tested live once this lands on `main` (GitHub requires the workflow file to exist on the default branch before it can be dispatched via API/CLI, even against a different `--ref`) — the `workflow_dispatch` and `upload-artifact` steps should be re-verified with a manual run shortly after merge.

Ran `/cams-spec-review` against all three test files (fetch layer, compute layer, CSV writer): 0 CRITICAL/HIGH findings. The two MEDIUM findings have since been fixed: (1) `computeDeploymentFrequency` now throws on a non-positive/non-finite `periodDays` (0, negative, `NaN`, `Infinity`), guarding the pure compute layer directly rather than only its one caller, plus new tests for the guard and for a genuine non-exact-multiple period count (10-day range over 7-day periods) that actually exercises the `Math.ceil` rounding-up behavior; (2) the pagination early-stop test's fixture now sets `total_count: 100` (rather than coincidentally matching the mocked run total), which I verified by temporarily removing the `since`-boundary break and confirming the test fails. All 14 tests, `typecheck`, and `lint` pass.

# Notes

No other workspace is touched — this is additive only. `data/` is gitignored within `dora-metrics/`, so report output never gets committed.

# Definition of Done:

- [ ] Code refactored for clarity: Developers can understand the work simply by reviewing the code
- [ ] Dependency rule followed: More important code doesn't directly depend on less important code
- [ ] Development debt eliminated: UX and code aligns to the team's latest understanding of the domain
- [ ] No regressions: Changes do not cause regression in related or unrelated areas of the application

## Summary by Sourcery

Introduce automated deployment-frequency reporting from GitHub Actions history through a new dora-metrics workspace and scheduled workflow.

New Features:
- Add a DORA metrics workspace that reports successful deployment frequency from GitHub Actions workflow history and exports period-based CSV data.
- Schedule the deployment-frequency report weekly and make it manually dispatchable, with the generated CSV uploaded as a workflow artifact.

Enhancements:
- Separate workflow-run retrieval, deployment-frequency computation, and CSV output into testable components with configurable repository, workflow, date range, and period settings.

Build:
- Add the dora-metrics workspace and its dependencies, scripts, TypeScript, ESLint, and Vitest configuration.

Tests:
- Add unit coverage for workflow filtering and pagination, deployment bucketing and validation, and CSV generation.

body:
TLDR:
Per-user installations now use ~/.local/bin so the Settings update button can replace the executable without sudo.

Problem:
The installer selected /usr/local/bin whenever sudo was available, even though macOS LaunchAgents and Linux user services run without that permission. Updates then failed with an executable-directory permission error.

Solution that was arrived at:
Use ~/.local/bin by default on macOS and for Linux --user installations. Preserve --bin-dir and PLANS_BIN_DIR overrides and the existing Linux system-service selection. Regenerate install.sh and update help and migration documentation. Existing installations still require the documented one-time migration.

Validation:
Passed 14 temporary directory-selection checks across the source and generated installer, shell syntax checks, generated-artifact checks, and git diff --check. No real installation or service restart was performed.

Closes #5.

author: jplock
body:
Closes #69.

## What changes

`waiting.js` polled `/status` and `/queue_num` every 5 s regardless of queue position, so a
visitor 900,000 back polled as often as one about to be admitted.

`/status` now publishes a poll policy — `floor_ms`, `ceiling_ms`, `divisor`, set as Terraform
variables on the `read` Lambda — and the client polls at
`clamp(wait_seconds * 1000 / divisor, floor, ceiling)`. Defaults are 5,000 / 30,000 / 10.
Visitors near the front converge on the floor, which **equals the previous fixed interval**, so
time-to-admission cannot regress; the long tail backs off to the ceiling. Jitter becomes
proportional to the interval rather than a fixed window.

A hidden tab stops polling and catches up on return, guarded two ways: a floor-elapsed rate check
so tab-flapping cannot beat the floor, and an `inFlight` flag so a visibility-triggered poll
cannot race a chain already running and claim two positions for one visitor. A paused event keeps
the interval bounded by the visitor's own distance to the front, so operator actions — including
`fail_open` — still reach near-front visitors promptly.

The policy is parsed all-or-nothing at the client boundary, and a client that has already adopted
one keeps it if a later poll omits it. No per-visitor input enters `/status`, so the path-only
cache key and the request collapsing the design rests on are unchanged.

## Measurements

Origin load is unchanged and was never the target — origin request counts are identical between
polling modes in every run (`/v1/status` 462-482, `/v1/queue_num` exactly 1,000,000). This is a
client-request-count property only.

All figures below are at 1,000,000 visitors against the built-in stub, on a build verified
byte-identical to the source.

| configuration | baseline | adaptive | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--countdown 180 --arrival uniform --target-rate 833 --seconds 480` | 68,757,884 | 23,878,829 | **2.88x** |
| `--countdown 180 --arrival late --target-rate 833 --seconds 480` | 58,323,285 | 21,916,029 | **2.66x** |
| `make load VISITORS=1000000 SECONDS=90` (the reference command) | 16,625,940 | 9,098,894 | **1.83x** |

**The saving is real and smaller than the design originally modelled.** The two 833/s runs are
the ones that genuinely exercise the countdown phase, and both land below the 3.9x blended model
and well below the 6.0x that model attributes to the countdown alone. `DESIGN.md` §12 now says so
directly and restates the CloudFront allowance headroom as roughly 35-40% rather than 56%.

An earlier revision of this PR quoted a 3.83x run as the closest empirical match to the model.
That was withdrawn: at a 200/s drain the queue barely moves, so the run is dominated by
deep-queue visitors at the ceiling and its closeness to 3.9x is a coincidence of the queue
component, not corroboration of the countdown one.

The 1.83x row is documented deliberately. A 90-second run is dominated by the ~60-second
first-ask spread window, during which no position is known and both modes poll identically at the
floor — so most of that run compares the adaptive client against itself. Anyone following the
issue's own measurement guidance would otherwise conclude the change barely works.

Arrival shape moved the ratio opposite to intuition for the second time in this project (#84 was
the first): uniform arrival saves *more* than late arrival, because late arrivers reach the
countdown near its end and see only a short slice of `closed` whatever interval they picked.

`DESIGN.md` §12 is recomputed against the shipped client and the client-request column, states
the pricing model it assumes, separates measured ratios from modelled ones, and carries a
hidden-share sensitivity table scoped to the desktop Chrome throttle with the iOS suspension case
alongside. Dollar figures are recomputed rather than relabelled. The `target_rate` unit is
corrected to visitors per second, which `DESIGN.md` alone had wrong.

## Testing

Client logic is tested by loading the shipped `waiting.js` under `node:vm`, so the tests run
against the artifact that ships rather than a copy — 26 tests, a new `client-ci.yml` workflow,
and a prek hook. No `package.json`, no lockfile, no npm dependencies.

The client suite was mutation-verified twice independently: seven fixes were reintroduced one at
a time and all seven mutants were killed. A drift test ties the harness's interval constants to
the Terraform defaults and was confirmed to fail closed against a changed default, a renamed
variable, and a reformatted declaration.

## Known limits

- The harness models all-foreground visitors and has no Page Visibility model, so every figure
  above is the hidden-share-0 row. It says nothing about the Chrome-throttle or iOS-suspension
  rows in §12's table.
- The ~215M full-event baseline in that table has not been re-derived from measurement. An
  80-100 minute event is impractical to simulate; these runs are 8-9 minute slices.
- The harness always polls at the fixed `--target-rate`, while the real client prefers a locally
  measured rate after 30 s of samples, so it cannot model controller-driven rate variance.
- The harness counts requests only and has no admission timestamps, so "near-front cadence does
  not regress" is an argument from the code — the floor is an unconditional lower bound identical
  to the previous fixed interval — rather than a measured result.
- A visitor hidden longer than the admission grace loses their place. Pre-existing, sharpened but
  not created by this change, tracked in #97.
