author: jacksonqueenking
body:
## Summary

PR #412 wired `episteme/github-token` in as a plain bearer, but the credential we actually have is the **minerval-agents GitHub App's private key**, which cannot be sent as a bearer. This adds GitHub App auth to the issue-filing path and stores the key.

- **`src/services/github-app-auth.ts`** (new): signs an RS256 JWT with the App key (`iss` = app id, backdated 60s, 10 min max), exchanges it at `POST /app/installations/{id}/access_tokens` for an hourly installation token, caches it until five minutes before expiry, shares one in-flight exchange between concurrent callers, and drops the cache on a 401 so a rotated key or reinstalled App recovers without a restart.
- **`github-issue-service.ts`**: `githubIssuesConfigured()` accepts either credential; every request asks `getGithubBearer()` for the header. A plain `GITHUB_TOKEN` still works (local runs); the App wins when both are set.
- **Config**: `GITHUB_APP_ID`, `GITHUB_APP_INSTALLATION_ID`, `GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`. The key is normalised so a raw PEM, a `\n`-escaped one-liner, or a base64 blob all work.
- **Infra**: `episteme/github-app-private-key` is **imported** with `fromSecretNameV2`, not created, because it was populated by hand today (see below) and CloudFormation must not try to create the name. The API task gets the two ids as plain env and the key as an ECS secret. The existing `episteme/github-token` placeholder secret stays as the PAT alternative and is ignored while the App is configured.
- **`.gitignore`**: `*.private-key.pem`.
- Docs paragraph updated in `docs/architecture.md` and its `web/content` mirror.

## Already done outside the repo

- Secret `episteme/github-app-private-key` created in us-east-1 with the key; verified byte-for-byte against the .pem.
- Verified the key end to end before storing it: JWT → `GET /app` returns `minerval-agents`; installation 160924398 mints a token with `issues: write, metadata: read` scoped to exactly `minerval-ai/minerval`.

Merging deploys the new task definition, which picks the secret up on its own. No force-new-deployment needed.

## Test plan

- [x] `tests/unit/services/github-app-auth.test.ts`: JWT shape and signature verify against the public key; plain-token passthrough; single exchange shared by concurrent callers; re-mint inside the 5 min margin; re-mint after reset; exchange failure throws with status and retries next call.
- [x] `github-issue-service.test.ts`: App auth wins over the plain token, exchanges once per process, and re-mints after a 401.
- [x] Full unit suite: 171 files, 1585 tests pass. `tsc --noEmit` clean in root and `infra/`.
- [x] `cdk synth EpistemeApi` renders `GITHUB_APP_ID`, `GITHUB_APP_INSTALLATION_ID`, the `GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` secret ref, and the read grant on the imported secret.

body:
## Overview
Implements the static dashboard web app overview and anchor directory listing in `dashboard/`, delivering an accessible, neutral trust signal that reads `data/summary.json` to monitor anchor SEP compliance without running the CLI.

## Problem
With `data/summary.json` being produced by automated crawls, users and integrators need a public entry point to discover tracked Stellar anchors, inspect their compliance rate at a glance, filter by status/network, and see 7-day historical trends.

### Scenarios
| Scenario | Previous Behavior | New Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| User visits dashboard root | No web UI existed | Displays overview metrics, real-time search, filters, and anchor directory |
| Operator searches for domain | Required CLI execution | Instant filtering by domain name and registered anchor name |
| Filtering by network / status | Not available | Responsive pill filters for network (`testnet`/`mainnet`) and status (`pass`/`fail`/`warn`) |
| Greyscale / Screen-reader user | No visual indicator | Status badges use distinct shapes, icons, ARIA labels, and text |
| `summary.json` is missing / empty | Blank crash | Graceful error/empty state with retry action and informative message |

## Solution
1. Built a static frontend web app in `dashboard/` (HTML5, Vanilla CSS with custom properties, ESM JavaScript).
2. Computed summary metrics: Tracked Anchors, Compliance Rate %, Passing Anchors, Failing count, and Last Crawl timestamp.
3. Implemented real-time search and multi-criteria filters with active filter status bar and reset capability.
4. Rendered anchor cards/rows with direct links to `stellar.toml`, network badges, check ratios, and 7-day historical sparklines with tooltips.
5. Created `.github/workflows/dashboard-deploy.yml` for automated GitHub Pages deployment.

## Changes by File
- `dashboard/index.html`: Accessible, semantic HTML5 structure with Google Fonts (Inter, JetBrains Mono), search/filter controls, metrics cards, table directory, and state views.
- `dashboard/style.css`: Modern styling system supporting dark/light mode toggle, glassmorphism, responsive table/card layouts, and distinct status shapes for greyscale accessibility.
- `dashboard/dashboard-lib.mjs`: Pure data functions for metrics calculation, multi-criteria filtering, 7-day sparkline extraction, and relative timestamp formatting.
- `dashboard/app.js`: Dynamic client script managing UI state, data loading from `data/summary.json`, DOM events, and table rendering.
- `dashboard/data/summary.json`: Fallback/sample summary data for local preview and development.
- `.github/workflows/dashboard-deploy.yml`: GitHub Actions workflow assembling static assets and published data to deploy to GitHub Pages.
- `test/dashboard.test.mjs`: Unit tests verifying metrics calculations, filter permutations, sparkline extraction, and relative time formatting.

## Regression Tests
| Acceptance Criterion | Test Case | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Static site reading `data/summary.json` | `computeMetrics > calculates correct summary counts and compliance rate` | PASS |
| Header metrics (total, rate, last updated) | `computeMetrics > calculates correct summary counts and compliance rate` | PASS |
| Real-time domain search | `filterEntries > filters by domain search case-insensitively` | PASS |
| Network and status filters | `filterEntries > filters by network / status / combined` | PASS |
| 7-day sparkline history | `getLast7Runs > extracts the last 7 daily runs ordered chronologically` | PASS |
| Empty & error states | `computeMetrics > handles an empty entries array gracefully`, `filterEntries > returns empty array when no match` | PASS |
| Relative timestamp formatting | `formatRelativeTime > formats relative times accurately` | PASS |

## Testing
```text
> sep-compliance-validator@0.1.0 test
> vitest run

Test Files  19 passed (19)
Tests       450 passed (450)

> sep-compliance-validator@0.1.0 lint
> eslint . --max-warnings=0

> sep-compliance-validator@0.1.0 validate:registry
> node scripts/validate-registry.mjs
registry OK: 1 entry, 1 enabled, 0 opted out
```

## Notes for Reviewers
- The dashboard is fully static and decoupling from the crawler ensures fast, zero-server hosting on GitHub Pages.
- `package.json` published npm files (`"files": ["dist"]`) remain unchanged, so the CLI install package size is completely unaffected.

Closes #89

author: jkapcar
body:
## Why the watchdog is red

`survivor pipeline watch` failed closed, not because of a Bozo bug: `nfl-data.yml` had **no successful scheduled/dispatch/chained run within 30 hours** (issue #96). Last success was 2026-09-09T14:35Z; the Sep 10 and Sep 11 runs both died in 31s at `refresh` → *Accept only verified new finals*. No `automation/nfl-results` branch and no results PR were ever created.

## The real failure

`scripts/nfl_results_automation.py` did its job — both Week 1 finals were accepted, the review list was empty, receipts stayed append-only. The in-worktree test gate then rejected the tree:

```
tests.test_elo_538_classic
  test_input_and_schedule_snapshots_are_distinct_contracts
  AssertionError:
    receipt schedule_snapshot_id  sha256:d8b1f35cea30ff0a26278b04232f536e8d733a6e06b61c8bf56e409a28b8a80f
    current schedule snapshot     sha256:b87940b523b3059ffbe88b832ceb4a8b9af784ae09c89d4a150db217e6d4c362
```

Reproduced locally, byte-for-byte on those two SHAs.

That assertion contradicted the test's own docstring. Receipts are pinned to the snapshot they were written against, and landing a final necessarily moves `data/nfl-schedule.json` forward — so the check turned every result into a receipt rewrite, which the append-only ledger forbids. Wednesday's job never hit this path (zero eligible finals, early return); Thursday and Friday did, because scores existed.

## What changed

**`tests/test_elo_538_classic.py`** — the test now matches its docstring. It still checks both snapshot IDs are `sha256:…`, that `forecast_id` carries the input-snapshot prefix, that the receipt's game still exists on the published schedule, and that input and schedule snapshots stay distinct contracts. It no longer requires the receipt to carry today's published schedule snapshot. The test was fixed, not deleted or skipped.

**The two finals**, landed through the existing results-only path (`result_candidate()` projection, then the same `elo_538_classic.py refresh` / `tools/build-data.js` / `tools/data-manifest.js` regenerate steps the automation runs):

| Game | Result |
|---|---|
| `2026_01_NE_SEA` | NE 10 @ SEA 13 |
| `2026_01_SF_LAR` | SF 27 @ LAR 7 |

Only `status` / `home_score` / `away_score` differ on existing games. No kickoff, rest, site, ID or provenance-policy edits. `model-receipts.json` `data[]` rows are byte-identical (1088 rows, 272 per model); only its envelope moved.

Published state after this PR: 2 games final, 270 games scheduled, 538 Classic current forecasts = 270.

## Verification

```
python -m unittest tests.test_nfl_data_backbone tests.test_elo_538_classic tests.test_nfl_results_automation
  → Ran 45 tests — OK
python scripts/nfl_data_backbone.py validate
  → validated 272 games and 1088 model receipts
python scripts/elo_538_classic.py validate
  → validated 538 Classic (270 current forecasts), normalized receipts
    {'nfelo': 272, '538-classic': 272, 'ddpr-nfl': 272, 'ddpr-nfl-linear': 272}
python scripts/nfl_data_backbone.py verify-history --base-ref origin/main
  → append-only history preserved for 1088 existing receipts
node tools/validate-data.js
  → all checks passed
```

Diff is limited to `tests/test_elo_538_classic.py`, `data/nfl-schedule.json`, `data/538-classic.json`, `data/model-receipts.json` (envelope only), `data/receipts-inventory.json`, `data/index.json`.

PR #32 (`automation/nfl-data-refresh`) is untouched — that is the full-source refresh and stays manual.

## After merge — manual step required

Go to **Actions → NFL data backbone → Run workflow** on `main`. The watchdog only counts `schedule`, `workflow_dispatch` and `workflow_run` events; the PR `validate` job does not clear it. Until a dispatch run succeeds, issue #96 keeps growing and the 12:35 / 18:35 / 23:35 UTC mails keep coming.

If that dispatch run still fails after the tests pass, the next candidate is the bot push to `main` (branch protection). That has not been reached yet — no run has gotten that far.

author: adrianviniciuscs
body:
## Resumo

Centraliza em `apps/sgp/services/access.py` a regra de escopo territorial ("super-admin/ugp → global; articulador-estadual → seus estados; adt-acr → seus territórios") que estava reimplementada em pelo menos 7 lugares — mais do que os 5 mapeados originalmente: as duas cópias dentro de `views/activity.py` (uma delas já admitia no próprio comentário ser cópia da outra) e `services/workplan_access.py` também reimplementavam a regra à mão.

### Regra de negócio corrigida

Confirmei ao vivo, num ambiente Docker real (dados sempre revertidos por rollback de transação), que um usuário `adt-acr` cujo `UserProfile.territorio` é `None` recebia acesso **global** em vez de vazio, em **todos os pontos** — inclusive na implementação que a issue aponta como "canônica" (`workplan_access.py`). Isso acontecia porque a regra herdava, sem querer, o fallback de `apps.core.services.permissions.user_territories()` ("sem território → acesso global"), que é intencional para papéis globais (ugp/super-admin) mas não fazia sentido pra adt-acr.

Corrigido dentro desta issue via `_territorios_do_papel()` em `services/access.py` — que ignora perfis sem território em vez de tratá-los como concessão global. Mesmo padrão que `services/budget.py::_territorios_do_adt()` já usava, sem crédito da issue. Não toquei em `apps/core/services/permissions.py` — o fix fica isolado na camada sgp.

### Pontos migrados

|Local|Antes|
|---|---|
|`views/upf.py`|`upfs_acessiveis_ao_usuario()` reimplementava a regra|
|`views/activity.py`|`get_queryset()` **e** `calendario()` — duas cópias no mesmo arquivo|
|`views/tecnico.py`|`articulador-estadual` resolvido por loop Python sobre `Territory.objects.all()` — trocado por `territorio__estados__overlap` (equivalência testada em 6 cenários antes de mexer)|
|`views/upf_documentos.py` + `views/production.py`|Método `_accessible_upf_queryset` idêntico byte a byte nos dois arquivos|
|`views/form_responses.py`|Função solta com a mesma lógica|
|`services/workplan_access.py`|Delega via `resolver_escopo()`, mantendo a API pública (`is_global_workplan_user`, `activity_scope_for_user`, `filter_workplan_actions_for_user`, `filter_workplan_metas_for_user`) e o `Q(pk__in=[])` que já usava|


### Regras de negócio / permissões

|Perfil|Escopo|
|---|---|
|super-admin / ugp|Global|
|articulador-estadual|Estados do usuário (`user_states()`, com fallback global intencional se sem território)|
|adt-acr|Territórios do usuário — perfil sem território atribuído agora resulta em **conjunto vazio**, nunca global (o achado corrigido acima)|
|Nenhum papel com escopo|`403 PermissionDenied` nos endpoints que já levantavam antes|

### Testes

|Suite|Testes|
|---|---|
|`test_access_service.py` (novo)|15 — `resolver_escopo()`/`scope_queryset()` isolados, incluindo o caso do gap corrigido|
|`test_escopo_territorial.py` (novo)|18 (6 casos × 3 endpoints: UPF, Atividade, Técnico) — a matriz de regressão que a issue pede|

`test_upf.py`, `test_membro.py`, `test_activity.py`, `test_workplan.py`, `test_tecnico.py`, `test_upf_documentos.py`, `test_production.py` — diff zero, critério de aceite.

### Comportamentos especiais

Nenhum endpoint muda de resposta, exceto o caso do gap corrigido (adt-acr sem território: antes via lista completa/global nos 7 pontos, agora vê lista vazia — no Plano de Trabalho, antes via tudo, agora `Q(pk__in=[])`).

### Breaking changes

- Comportamento de adt-acr sem território mudou de "acesso global" pra "conjunto vazio" em todos os endpoints territorialmente escopados do SGP, incluindo Plano de Trabalho. É a correção de um gap de segurança, não uma mudança de contrato de API (mesmos formatos de resposta, resultado diferente só nesse cenário específico e hoje não coberto por nenhum teste existente).

### Observações

- Achado fora do escopo desta PR, não corrigido: `apps/sgp/services/forms.py::get_available_upf_forms` tem o mesmo formato de risco (`user_territories().exists()`), mas filtra um model de outro app (`apps.sgf`) e não estava nos locais mapeados pela issue. Vale virar issue própria.

---

Closes #263

body:
## 概要

背景地図の下地に使っていた国土地理院の「淡色地図」をやめ、拡大したときに道路網や道路番号の標識が見えないようにします。

## 原因

ズーム8以上では陸の色を出すために淡色地図を薄めて重ねていました。淡色地図は道路・道路番号・鉄道・地名・記号を画像に含むため、薄めても平野部の道路網や道路番号（「20」「52」など）が見えていました。

## 変更内容

- 陸の下地を、道路も地名も含まない**色別標高図**を大きく色あせさせたもの（彩度 -0.85、明度下限 0.78）に変更
- 国土地理院のベクトルタイルはズーム8以上で海を水域の面（`vt_code 5101` ほか）として配信するため、海はその上から正確に塗る
- 外洋でベクトルタイルが配信されない範囲（ズーム11以上の沖合など）も、色別標高図が海底地形として塗るため陸の色にならない
- ズーム7までのタイルには全国で陸地の面（`AdmArea`）があることを確認し、下地の重ね始めを 6〜7.5 から **7.5〜8** へ遅らせた。全国表示の見た目は変わらない
- 取得エラーの判定から、なくした淡色地図のソースを外した

## 検討して採らなかった案

- **下地を陸の色にして海だけを塗る**：東シナ海、ロシア寄り、外洋ではズーム8以上でもタイルが404になり、そこが陸の色になるため不採用
- **白地図タイル**：道路はないが海も白く、地名も重複するため不採用
- **淡色地図を低い倍率で引き伸ばす**：ズーム5〜6でも地名や鉄道が描かれており、ぼやけた染みとして残るため不採用

## レビューで見てほしい点

- 「標高の色分け」を切っても、陸の下地として淡くした色別標高図が残るため、地形の色味が少し残る
- 残る細い灰色の線は鉄道（パネルの「地図」で切り替え可能）

## 検証

- lint、typecheck、単体テスト97件（新規1件：道路入りのラスター地図を使っていないこと）、ブラウザ統合テスト17件（3件は従来どおりスキップ）、production build に成功
- ズーム7.5・9.5・11.5で、道路と道路番号が消えたことを修正前後の画像で確認

## What kind of change does this PR introduce?

Docs fix.

## What is the current behavior?

The README badge, the README install section, and `docs/api.md` all say Python 3.7+.

`setup.py` disagrees:

```python
MINIMUM_PYTHON_VERSION = (3, 8, 0, "", 0)
```

and the classifiers list 3.8 through 3.12. So someone on 3.7 follows the install instructions and gets `At least Python 3.8.0 is required.`

Looks like the floor was raised at some point and the docs were left behind.

## What is the new behavior?

Three occurrences of 3.7 changed to 3.8. No code touched.

## Additional context

While reading `docs/api.md` I also noticed a few smaller things: two typos (`sucessfully`, `incldues`), a sentence that repeats itself ("expect sub-minute a response in under a minute"), and the warning text quoted in the Query section says `cosine_similarity`, which isn't a value of `IndexMeasure` — the code emits `Query does not have a covering index for {measure}`. Kept them out of this PR to keep the diff on one topic; happy to send a follow-up if you want them fixed.

Used Claude (Anthropic) to cross-check the docs against setup.py.

author: forkwright
body:
## Summary

A live instance agent (syn) hit repeated `ls`/`find` failures reported only as "Tool error: input preparation failed", plus a `git_log` failure logged as a bare "tool execution failed". The agent concluded "the ls tool is having issues with absolute paths" — wrong, and impossible to self-correct from, because the typed error never reached it.

Changes:

- **nous** (`execute/dispatch.rs`): `prepare_input` failures now surface the typed reason to the model-facing tool result and the persisted call record (`Tool error: input preparation failed: <reason>`), matching the executor-error path's existing `Tool error: {error}` behavior in the same file. The message is scrubbed of vault-resolved secret values first, since preparation runs on post-substitution arguments.
- **organon** (`builtins/workspace.rs`): the "path outside allowed roots" rejection now names the configured allowed roots, so an agent can retry under a root it may touch.
- **organon** (`builtins/git_ops.rs`): git's `fatal: not a git repository` exit is translated to an explicit "workspace is not a git repository" error (nous workspace dirs are plain directories, not work trees), instead of forwarding git's raw fatal line.
- **hermeneus** (`secret.rs`): new `redact_vault_values_in_str` helper used by the dispatch change above.

## Root cause

- **ls / find**: in-scope absolute paths were never broken — registry `prepare_input` → `validate_path` canonicalizes and admits them (now covered by regression tests). The live failures were `prepare_input` rejections (e.g. an absolute path outside the agent's allowed roots, such as sibling instance directories the workspace convention points agents at), but dispatch collapsed every preparation error to the fixed string `Tool error: input preparation failed` (`map_err(|_error| ...)`), so the agent could not see the "path outside allowed roots" reason.
- **git_log**: invoked with the nous workspace as cwd, which is not a git repository. The tool forwarded git's raw `fatal: not a git repository (or any of the parent directories): .git` as a generic execution failure; the dispatch log line (`tool execution failed`, target `nous::execute::dispatch`) carries no stderr, so the failure looked opaque.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — clean
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --features test-core -- -D warnings` — clean (the PR gate's exact invocation)
- `cargo nextest run -p organon --features test-support` — 703/703
- `cargo nextest run -p nous` — 1327/1327
- `cargo nextest run -p hermeneus` — 570/570
- New regression tests: in-scope absolute-path `ls`/`find` prepare+execute through the registry; out-of-scope `ls` error names the allowed roots; `git_log`/`git_status` outside a git repo return the translated typed error; dispatch surfaces the typed preparation reason; dispatch scrubs a vault-resolved secret out of the surfaced reason.

Note: `cargo test -p organon` under plain libtest can flake in `metrics::tests::register_and_record_sandbox_unconfigured` — pre-existing process-global metrics race documented in the code (#6931); reproduces on an unmodified tree, green under nextest (which the gate uses).

author: koala73
body:
## Summary

Public-site session holders could rotate country/date queries to trigger ACLED calls and create per-query Redis entries. The RPC now filters the Railway seed only, so neither cold requests nor seed outages can consume provider quota or create query caches. Country names and ISO2 codes are supported; explicit date bounds are inclusive milliseconds. An unset start includes midnight UTC 30 days ago. Only history available in the seed is returned (the producer targets 30 days), and seed failures retain the empty response with caching disabled. Composed embeds mark the conflict layer unavailable and disable frame caching on a failed seed read.

Related: #8051. DeepSec finding 43.

## Integration

Targets `main`, which now includes the raw seed reader and shared ACLED query normalization fixes. The normal base merge preserves this PR's seed-only caller behavior and embed recovery.

The scanner's credentialless-RPC and dynamic embed-window claims were outdated: direct no-credential requests get 401; public-site sessions retain access; the composed embed uses zero/default parameters. The reachable live-fetch/cache-growth path was confirmed. The provider-specific DRC spelling is normalized locally. No shared ACLED helper, rate registry, gateway, generated code, or producer changes.

## Validation

- 137 focused tests passed across generated ACLED routing, real Redis helpers with synthetic storage, producer normalization, date windows, Country Brief coverage, and existing session/no-auth gateway contracts.
- An original-handler witness made three mocked ACLED calls with configured synthetic credentials; the corrected handler made zero. Rotating cold/filtered queries read only the fixed seed and create no Redis entries.
- Default seed/envelope and preview-prefix behavior, GDELT geographic exclusion, ISO/name filtering, inclusive boundaries, no-op pagination, seed failure and recovery passed, including the real composed embed handler.
- 487 full sidecar tests, API typecheck, boundary lint and exact-head sequential ce-code-review passed with no actionable findings at `ac56fdfd999753d7b201dd71ed6ba76340cbd166`. No live provider freshness, deployed CDN, browser, or native runtime acceptance claimed.

## Post-Deploy Monitoring & Validation

Owner: repository operator after separately authorized deployment. During the first seed cycle, compare default and country-filtered RPC rows against the geographic rows in `conflict:acled:v1:all:0:0`; inspect `seed-meta:conflict:acled:v1:all:0:0` and conflict worker logs. Observe route errors, empty-response rate and ACLED request volume: varying RPC queries must not produce ACLED requests or new `conflict:acled:v1:<query>` keys. Missing-seed responses must be no-store. Investigate a sustained empty response with a populated geographic seed or any request-triggered ACLED traffic before accepting rollout. GDELT-only seeds intentionally have no geographic RPC rows; empty data alone is not proof of quiet conditions.

author: qoega
body:
The x86-64 bit-manipulation helpers modify the condition-code register, but their inline assembly declarations do not list the `cc` clobber. Compilers can consequently assume that flags survive these blocks. FilC rejects the incomplete assembly contract at runtime when ClickHouse builds a text-index posting list.

Declare the clobber for all three macros that execute `bts`/`btr`/`bt` followed by `sbb`. With this change, the ClickHouse functional test `05059_text_index_lazy_multi_block_windows` passes under FilC; before it, FilC stops at `bitset_container_from_array` with `assembly sets flags but "cc" clobber is missing`.

body:
## Tóm tắt

Việc cuối của P2(b) trước khi dọn Engine. Thuần giao diện — **không đụng Engine**, số đã có sẵn trong khối `line` mà `/api/bao-cao/suc-khoe` đang trả.

Mỗi line một biểu đồ đường nhỏ (12 tháng của năm đang xem — `trangThai.nam`, không ăn theo tab Ngày/Tháng/Quý vì xu hướng cả năm là khái niệm riêng), cạnh nhau để so **hình dạng**: đang lên, đang xuống, đứt gãy đột ngột (nhân viên nghỉ), hay chỉ mới xuất hiện — thứ vòng cơ cấu ở PR trước không nói được (vòng cơ cấu chỉ trả lời "ai to ai nhỏ ở một kỳ"). Mỗi ô dùng trục dọc **RIÊNG** theo giá trị lớn nhất của chính line đó nên hình dạng luôn đọc được dù line to hay nhỏ.

**Nút chuyển Doanh số/Số đơn** áp cho **CẢ LƯỚI**, không phải mỗi ô tự chọn — 10 line × 2 chỉ số cùng lúc là 20 ô, không ai đọc hết được. Đổi nút thì thứ tự sắp xếp (giảm dần, "Khác" luôn cuối — cùng luật vòng cơ cấu) cũng **tính lại theo đúng chỉ số đang xem**, không kẹt theo thứ hạng lúc mở màn.

Tháng nào line không có dòng nào là **ngắt đoạn**, không vẽ liền một đường phẳng ở đáy như thể vẫn bán với giá 0 — dùng chung nguyên tắc "khoảng trống thật" với mọi biểu đồ khác trong file. Nhãn duy nhất là giá trị tháng cuối cùng có số ("Lines → value at the end", không ghi số lên từng tháng — dataviz).

**Sửa kèm hai lỗi thật phát hiện lúc viết bài kiểm:**
- Đọc `L.thu_tu` không bọc `|| []` như `veKhoiCoCau()` bên cạnh đã làm — bảng line méo (thiếu `thu_tu`, đúng ca "Engine chưa trả khối `line`" giữa hai lượt deploy) làm **sập cả `veLai()`**, kéo luôn hai biểu đồ chính vừa vẽ xong bị dọn trắng theo qua nhánh lỗi.
- Thiếu dọn `innerHTML` trước khi thêm nút chuyển chỉ số — không nhất quán với `veTabDonVi()`/`veDaiPhu()` bên cạnh, khiến nút cũ còn nằm lại nếu trình duyệt không coi id lặp trong `innerHTML` mới là một phần tử khác hẳn.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm test` xanh — 19 bộ, 877 đạt, 0 hỏng.
- [x] Chạy thật qua DOM giả (`kiem/dashboard-ve.js`), dựng ca "có lỗ hổng giữa năm" (đường tách 3 đoạn), ca "đủ tháng không lỗ hổng" (đường 1 đoạn), ca "chưa có số năm nào" (câu thông báo, không SVG rỗng), ca "chỉ một tháng" (vẫn có chấm + nhãn).

## Qué arregla

Auditoría `familia-libra-que-mejorar-2026-09`, sección 2.8: uvicorn corre con **un solo proceso**, así que una ruta `async def` que toca la base frena la instancia entera mientras dura. Mismo arreglo que Contalibra #298, Restolibra #283 y libracore #251.

| Dónde | Qué bloqueaba | Qué se hizo |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /comprobantes` (`facturar`) | muchas consultas a la `Session` y `await emision_arca.numero_que_sigue` / `pedir_cae`, que mezclan la base y la firma del TRA con `openssl` con WSAA/WSFE | Pasa a `def`; las dos corrutinas corren con `asyncio.run` en un loop propio del hilo. Sus firmas no cambian. **El pedido de CAE sigue dentro de la misma transacción** (misma sesión, mismo hilo): si ARCA rechaza, 502 y no queda comprobante |
| `POST /configuracion/logo` (`subir_logo`) | `Session`, auditoría y commit | Pasa a `def`; el archivo se lee con `archivo.file.read()`, mismos topes y mensajes |
| `spa` (`app/asgi.py`) y `SecurityHeadersMiddleware` | sólo archivos / cabeceras | **Sin cambios** |

⚠️ Las rutas de libracore que monta LibraCargo (`/api/arca/*` y el restore) siguen bloqueando hasta el bump a libracore **v1.95.0** (libracore #251), que va en un PR aparte cuando cierre la tanda de v1.94.0.

## Cómo se probó

`tests/test_rutas_no_bloquean_el_loop.py`: `facturar` parametrizado en tres puntos lentos —`registra` (`emite_por_arca`), `numera` (adentro de `autenticar`) y `pide-cae` (adentro de `solicitar_cae`)—, el logo, y un control de que el rechazo de ARCA sigue sin dejar comprobante. Mientras duerme, un `/health` por el mismo loop tiene que terminar antes.

| | Resultado |
|---|---|
| Test contra `origin/develop`, antes del arreglo | 4/4 rojos, los cuatro por bloqueo; el control pasa |
| Con el arreglo | 5/5 verdes |
| Mutación: ruta `def` pero la numeración vuelve al loop con `anyio.from_thread.run` | sólo `[numera]` rojo, por bloqueo. Restaurado con sha256 igual a `HEAD` |

Suite completa como el CI (PostgreSQL 16, TZ Argentina): **358 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**, cobertura 97,06 % (piso 95). Ruff limpio.

author: mateusevangelista-nic
body:
## Resumo

Implementa a issue #769: o composer deixa de descartar texto, anexos, gravação de voz e contexto de resposta ao trocar de conversa. Cada conversa passa a ter seu próprio "draft" independente.

Também inclui, na mesma branch (a pedido do solicitante, para evitar overhead de uma branch separada):
- correção dos testes E2E que quebraram após a feature de drafts;
- correção de dois gaps de broadcast em tempo real no backend, encontrados durante a verificação manual desta PR: eventos de chamada (iniciada/encerrada) e de membro adicionado não chegavam via WebSocket, exigindo reload para aparecer na timeline.

## Mudanças principais — drafts (#769)

- `useConversationDrafts.ts` (novo): store por conversa (`kind:targetId`), mantido em `AppShell` — sobrevive a troca de conversa (channel↔dm) e a navegação para `/profile` e volta. Inclui revisão monotônica por draft, usada para não apagar texto novo quando o ACK de um envio anterior chega atrasado.
- `chatDraftPersistence.ts` (novo): espelho em `sessionStorage`, escopado por usuário — **só** texto do editor e id da mensagem respondida, nunca anexos/blobs/áudio. Sobrevive a F5 na mesma aba. Inclui hidratação eager para a sidebar mostrar "Rascunho" logo após o F5, sem precisar reabrir a conversa.
- `useAttachmentUpload.ts` / `useVoiceRecorder.ts`: passam a escrever no draft por identidade (draftKey + localId/attachment), em vez de depender só do estado local do componente — um upload ou gravação em andamento sobrevive à troca de conversa e é atribuído corretamente à conversa de origem, nunca à nova.
- `ChatComposer.tsx` / `useChatEditor.ts`: o editor é semeado a partir do draft ao montar, escreve de volta a cada edição, e só limpa o texto após um envio confirmado se nada mudou desde o envio (proteção contra ACK atrasado).
- `ChatSidebar.tsx` / `.css`: indicador "Rascunho" numa segunda linha sob o nome da conversa, independente de unread/menções.
- `chatTargetNavigation.test.tsx`: o teste que provava que um draft nunca sobrevive a uma volta à mesma conversa foi invertido (com justificativa no código) — é exatamente o comportamento que esta issue pede. Os testes de isolamento entre conversas **diferentes** continuam intactos e passando.

## Mudanças principais — fix de CI (E2E)

- `message-interactions.spec.ts`: seletor `getByText("oi😀")` era ambíguo em strict mode após a badge de rascunho ser adicionada à sidebar; escopado para `getByTestId("chat-msg-bubble").getByText(...)`.
- `channel-message-flows.spec.ts` acusava texto acumulando entre envios (`"uma"` → `"umaduas"` → `"umaduastrês"`). Causa raiz: `handleSend` limpava o reply do draft incondicionalmente a cada envio, o que incrementava a revisão do draft mesmo sem reply ativo e derrubava a proteção de ACK atrasado. Corrigido para só limpar o reply quando de fato havia um `replyToMessageId` no draft.

## Mudanças principais — fix de broadcast em tempo real (encontrado na verificação manual)

Descoberto ao validar #769 manualmente: adicionar um membro a um canal, ou iniciar/encerrar uma chamada, gerava corretamente o evento de sistema no banco (`chat.messages`, `kind='system'`), mas o WebSocket nunca publicava o `conversation.event` correspondente — só reload trazia a mensagem para a timeline de quem já estava com a conversa aberta.

- `call_store.go` / `call_service.go` / `app.go`: `CreateResourceCall`/`TransitionCall` passam a retornar o id da mensagem de evento criada; `CallService.Start`/`transition` (Accept/Decline/Cancel/End) publicam `conversation.event` com esse id.
- `member_store.go` (canal) / `dm_store.go` (DM) / `channel_handler.go` / `dm_handler.go`: `AddChannelMembers`/`AddGroupParticipants` passam a retornar o id do evento de sistema já persistido; os handlers HTTP publicam `conversation.event` após adicionar membros.
- Cobertura: testes unitários novos para os dois caminhos (`call_service_test.go`, `add_members_handler_test.go`, `add_participants_handler_test.go`) e verificação manual ponta a ponta via WebSocket real (login real, subscribe real, add-member real via API) confirmando o `conversation.event` chegando ao cliente subscrito, sem reload.

## Como testar

1. Digitar um rascunho numa conversa, trocar para outra, voltar — o texto deve estar lá.
2. Anexar um arquivo, trocar de conversa antes do upload terminar, voltar — o anexo deve aparecer concluído na conversa original.
3. Começar uma gravação de voz, trocar de conversa — a gravação finaliza (mic desliga) e fica disponível para revisar/enviar ao voltar (comportamento confirmado com o solicitante: sem manter o microfone ativo em segundo plano).
4. Enviar uma mensagem e, antes do ACK, digitar algo novo — o texto novo não pode ser apagado quando o ACK chegar.
5. F5 no meio de um rascunho de texto — deve ser restaurado.
6. Logout/login com outro usuário na mesma aba — nenhum draft do usuário anterior deve aparecer.
7. Adicionar um membro a um canal/DM com outra aba já aberta na mesma conversa — a mensagem de sistema deve aparecer sem reload.
8. Iniciar/encerrar uma chamada com outra aba aberta na mesma conversa — o evento de sistema deve aparecer sem reload.

## Riscos / limitações

- Anexos e gravação de voz em andamento sobrevivem só durante a sessão da SPA (perdem-se no F5); apenas texto e o id do reply persistem em `sessionStorage`.
- Não inclui suporte a colar arquivo via clipboard (não existia antes da issue, fora de escopo).
- Durante a verificação manual foram encontrados dois bugs pré-existentes, não relacionados a estas mudanças, fora de escopo desta PR: `GET /api/chat/channels/{id}/pins` retorna 500, e a busca de candidatos a membro (`member-candidates`) retorna lista vazia para pelo menos um canal privado testado. Recomendo issues separadas para isso.
- Recomendo uma segunda passada de Security Review e testes E2E/mobile antes do merge — não executados nesta sessão por restrição de tempo.

## Issue

Closes #769

author: iamvaln
body:
Le second temps de `08e8102`, qui avait retiré la surface. La table restait le
temps de vérifier qu'aucune ligne n'existait en production. **Vérifié** : le
produit n'est pas en ligne, et la base ne porte qu'un compte d'essai et un
administrateur d'essai.

## Ce qui part

```sql
ALTER TABLE "action_run" DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS "prompt_template_id";
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS "prompt_template";
DROP TYPE  IF EXISTS "prompt_kind";
```

Et le modèle, l'énumération et la relation côté Prisma — 34 lignes de schéma.

## La colonne mentait depuis le premier jour

C'est le point qui mérite d'être dit. `action_run.prompt_template_id` promettait
ceci, dans son propre commentaire :

> « La version EXACTE du gabarit qui a produit ce contenu. Sans elle, comprendre
> pourquoi les productions d'une semaine valaient mieux que celles de la
> suivante devient impossible — et c'est précisément la question qu'on pose
> après une publication ratée. »

**Aucune ligne de production ne l'écrivait.** Jamais. Une colonne qui ment est
pire qu'une colonne absente : une colonne absente se remarque et se réclame,
celle-là se lit en croyant savoir.

Ce que le Studio met à sa place répond mieux à la même question :
`studio_config` porte l'empreinte, la version publiée et l'essai qui l'a
justifiée — et `action_run` se rattache à ce qui a réellement tourné.

## Ce qui reste, délibérément

Les deux libellés d'audit `prompt_template_create` et
`prompt_template_activate`, dans l'administration. Le **journal** garde les
gestes qui ont eu lieu ; les retirer afficherait un code brut à la place d'une
phrase, sur des lignes qu'on ne peut plus réécrire. Un commentaire le dit à côté,
pour qu'on ne les supprime pas par zèle plus tard.

## Vérifié

- `pnpm typecheck` à la racine : **8 paquets, 8 verts**
- `@lehno/api` : **129 fichiers, 1684 cas**
- `@lehno/mobile` : **60 fichiers, 1126 cas**
- `@lehno/admin` : **47 fichiers, 584 cas**
- `@lehno/contracts` : **25 fichiers, 318 cas**
- `@lehno/web` : **40 fichiers, 316 cas**

Un fichier avait expiré à l'initialisation lors du passage groupé — la machine
faisait tourner deux choses à la fois. Rejoué seul : 15 cas, 15 verts.

body: ## Why `apps/snapshots/tests/control-surfaces.test.ts` "concurrent CLI captures > overlapping captures never fail with UNIQUE constraint errors" reddened shard 3 of #2181 (run 34626252771, job 103352393189) with only: ``` expect(result.exitCode).toBe(0) Expected: 0 Received: 1 ``` The test asserts the exit code before it looks at stderr, so the one process that failed left nothing to diagnose. The race did not reproduce locally: 20 rounds x 3 concurrent captures under 3x CPU load and 10 runs of the real test in `oven/bun:1.3.14` were 0/70 failures. ## What Each of the three assertions now carries the capture index, exit code, stderr and the head of stdout as its message. Nothing is weakened, reordered or skipped; the next CI occurrence will name the failing capture and print what it said. Test-only change, no version bump, no changeset. ## Proof ``` apps/snapshots: bun test tests/control-surfaces.test.ts -> all pass (unchanged behaviour) tsc --noEmit: no diagnostics for the touched file ``` Agent: fleet-alignment-w11-20260911 --- Need help on this PR? author: mdellanoce
body:
[INT-418](https://linear.app/pendo-io/issue/INT-418/move-the-pendo-button-contract-into-guide-components-so-novus-stops) — part (a) of two. Raised by @colingm while reviewing whether the theme-side fixes in [pendo-io/nova#1689](https://github.com/pendo-io/nova/pull/1689) were at the right layer.

Novus's theme formatter injects a block into **every theme's stored CSS** so the runtime's inner elements can read custom properties:

```css
pendo-guide[data-pendo-theme-id="…"] .pendo-button {
  font-size: var(--pendo-button-font-size, 0.9375rem);
  padding: var(--pendo-button-padding-y, …) var(--pendo-button-padding-x, …);
  border-radius: var(--pendo-button-radius, var(--pendo-radius));
}
```

That was never theme content. It is a shim for an API this component does not expose: `.pendo-button` paints from hard-coded values plus `--pendo-primary` and offers no way to set padding, radius, border, fill, elevation or typography — so Novus writes the missing plumbing into each customer's sheet, one copy per theme. Most of what is awkward over there follows from it. A stored theme is frozen at whatever was injected when it was last written; the "Theme update available" banner exists purely to prompt a rewrite so a theme picks up newer rules; and adding one declaration changes the injected block for all 896 themes at once, so the skip-if-unchanged guard never fires.

## Change

The declarations move here, with the values this sheet already hard-coded as the `var()` fallbacks.

- **`.pendo-button`** — `padding` (split x/y so a consumer's Padding control can stay an x/y pair), `border-radius`, `box-shadow`, `font-size`, `font-weight`.
- **`.pendo-button--primary`** — `background`, `border`. `border` had no vendored value at all (`all: unset` computes it away), which is why a theme wanting a bordered primary button needed a rule on the host and got a decoy second box instead.
- **`.pendo-button--secondary`** — `background`, border colour, `color`.
- **`.pendo-link`** — `color`.

`--pendo-button-shadow` is the only token with no prior hard-coded value: `all: unset` already computes `box-shadow` to `none`, so `none` is both the fallback and what buttons render today.

Two shapes are deliberate:

- The secondary border token sits in the **shorthand's colour slot** — `border: 1px solid var(--pendo-button-secondary-border, var(--pendo-border))` — so choosing a colour cannot silently drop the width and style with it.
- `--pendo-button-bg` stops at the **resting** rule, leaving `.pendo-button--primary:hover` reading `--pendo-primary-hover`, so a theme that sets a flat fill keeps its hover feedback rather than losing it.

## The names also ship as data

Five files across two repos restate these names (a formatter, a `buildingBlocks` emitter, a runtime-paint validator, a theme prompt, and the properties panel's `cssVar(…)` targets), and a one-sided rename produces **no error anywhere**: an unrecognised custom property is never read, so the control keeps accepting values and the button keeps rendering the default. That is the [INT-362](https://linear.app/pendo-io/issue/INT-362) class of defect, and it is invisible by construction.

So `src/styles/theme-tokens.js` becomes the single list — names, defaults, and the rule each one lands in — emitted as `dist/theme-tokens.json` and reachable as `@pendo/guide-components/theme-tokens`, for consumers to assert their own spellings against. It is an emitted rollup asset rather than an `index.js` export because no guide needs the manifest at runtime, and bundling it would put it on every page that renders one.

## Verified

Nothing in this repo renders CSS, so the claim worth checking — *a theme that sets none of these renders identically* — was measured off the browser's own resolved computed values, old sheet vs new, across a primary button, a secondary button and a link:

| scenario | result |
|---|---|
| unset theme, `main` → this branch | **identical** on all 30 computed values |
| theme sets all twelve tokens, on `main` | **nothing moved** — every token inert |
| theme sets all twelve tokens, this branch | each lands on exactly its own property and variant |

The middle row is the whole reason the injection exists. The third confirms the specificity design holds: `--pendo-button-secondary-*` cannot reach a primary button and `--pendo-button-bg` / `--pendo-button-border` cannot reach a secondary one.

One gotcha worth recording for anyone repeating this: `.pendo-button` transitions `background-color` and `.pendo-link` transitions `color`, so a synchronous `getComputedStyle` after swapping the sheet returns the *animating* value and those three read stale. The harness disables transitions, as the sheet's own reduced-motion block does.

`test/theme-tokens.test.js` holds the manifest and the stylesheet together in both directions, so the published artifact cannot describe a contract the sheet does not implement, and pins the button/link surface as API rather than a stylesheet detail. Mutation-checked against all four drift modes — a token renamed in the sheet, a token dropped from the manifest, the surface shrinking, and a read losing its fallback — each fails the suite. Full run: 58 passing.

## Safe to land ahead of Novus

The formatter keeps injecting until [INT-657](https://linear.app/pendo-io/issue/INT-657) lands, and that is fine: the injected rules read the same names with the same fallbacks at higher specificity, so every stored theme resolves to the same values either way. Version → 0.3.0 (additive public API), so consumers' vendored `VERSION.txt` moves forward.

## Not in scope

**Declaring the host unpaintable** — `pendo-button { background: none; border: 0; padding: 0 }` — is part (b), and it is the highest-leverage single fix in the investigation: it ends the doubled button for every theme via one agent release with zero writes to any theme record. But it makes legacy tag paint **inert rather than moved**, so a theme that said `padding: 10px 20px` on the tag loses that intent and reverts to component defaults. It needs this change in place first (it is why the sequence matters), plus confirmation that nothing outside Novus renders through these components. Staying on INT-418.

**Variant- and state-scoped tokens** are held for the same reason they are an API question rather than a Novus one: the panel's Padding control writes the base variable regardless of the selected variant, so introducing a higher-precedence `variant="link"` padding token would make that control inert on exactly those buttons. The panel has to become variant-aware in the same change.

body:
### Motivation
- Improve how public perception of policy is classified by detecting large unbiased swings that confuse markets. 
- Ensure the term performance band reflects end-of-term outcomes rather than starting conditions for more relevant assessment. 

### Description
- Add an `Erratic` classification to `classify_public_view` by computing `deviation_rmse` and `deviation_sigma` with `_rms` and returning a descriptive message when both thresholds are exceeded. 
- Change `_performance_band` signature to take `ending_loss` (renamed from `beginning_loss`) and update its first check to use `ending_loss`. 
- Update `evaluate_end_of_term` to include the `ending_loss` in its return payload and to call `_performance_band` with `ending_loss`. 
- Update unit tests in `tests/test_economy_components.py` to cover the new `Erratic` case and the adjusted performance-band behavior, and to align expected end-of-term messages with the code changes. 

### Testing
- Ran the test suite in `tests/test_economy_components.py` which includes new tests `test_public_view_classifies_large_unbiased_swings_as_erratic` and updated performance-band tests, and all tests passed. 
- Existing unit tests for `taylor_policy_deviations`, `mandate_loss`, and end-of-term message construction were executed and succeeded.

author: moritzbrantner
body:
Converges `moenarch-graph-analysis-core` on the shared graph mechanisms now owned by `rust-kernels`.

Changes:
- delegates strongly connected components to the deterministic Tarjan kernel while preserving existing Moenarch `GraphComponent` metadata and ordering
- exposes deterministic `topological_order` and the `graph.topologicalSort` library/CLI/server/WASM surface
- consumes the newly integrated deterministic PageRank kernel and exposes `graph.rank` with damping/tolerance/iteration policy plus residual/convergence evidence
- pins both `graph-kernels` and the existing `collection-kernels` facade to the same exact accepted rust-kernels revision and refreshes Cargo.lock
- keeps current `f64` weighted shortest-path and minimum-spanning-tree implementations unchanged because the current shared kernels use integer costs; no semantic narrowing is introduced

The PageRank mechanism landed separately in rust-kernels #66 after its exact-head CI, hardening, mutation, runtime/Moonlight, and public-contract checks all passed.

author: udene1
body:
Ballistic hardening pass for the orchestration foundation.

- persist runtime capability/preferred runtime intent from tool input via D1 triggers
- enforce high-risk runtime capabilities at the actual transport boundary
- canonicalize runtime intent from node metadata or tool input
- make graph model routing capability/risk aware by default
- extend capability-policy tests for transport enforcement

This closes the gap where durable graph/runtime intent existed in schema and shared types but could be lost before execution, and prevents high-risk runtime dispatch without explicit approval metadata.

author: aldomor00
body:
## Qué entra

`repodatos.atdt.gob.mx` sigue congelado en `2025-11_q2`, pero el programa nunca dejó de
publicar: se mudó al portal de Profeco, que sirve **un bundle por año** y publica mensual
con un mes de rezago. `scripts/ingesta_profeco.py` se mueve ahí.

- El token de cada año se resuelve leyendo `qqp.php` en cada corrida, así que **2027 entra
  solo** el día que aparezca su renglón. Si cambian la plantilla, el mapa sale vacío y la
  corrida truena.
- **Sonda antes de bajar**: el CSV de metadatos (877 bytes) dice hasta qué mes cubre la
  fuente. Sin ella, las tres corridas semanales que no encuentran nada se bajarían 186 MB
  cada una.
- **Detecta lo que la fuente reescribe.** El directorio central del zip trae tamaño y
  CRC32 de cada miembro sin descomprimir, así que cotejarlos contra el manifiesto no
  cuesta una lectura extra. Coge el caso que el tamaño solo no ve —corregir un precio de
  20 a 21 no mueve un byte— y lo reescrito entra como `intento` nuevo, sin pisar nada.
- **Valida que sea zip, no que sea 200**: un token inválido contesta `200` con HTML.
- **`--local`** procesa CSV ya extraídos a mano. Es la vía de 2025, que viene en `.rar`.
- Acepta las dos convenciones de nombre (`_02` hasta 2025, `_Q2` desde 2026).

Lo demás del script —`pendientes()`, los cortes, las rutas, `--rehacer`, el tope por
tanda— queda intacto. Decisión #34; `docs/fuentes.md` y el comentario del cron decían que
la fuente estaba muerta y se corrigen.

## Alcance de la detección de reescrituras

**Sólo se cotejan los años cuyo bundle hubo que bajar de todos modos.** Abrir uno nada más
por revisar tiraría el ahorro de la sonda. Como la fuente publica mensual, cada publicación
arrastra una quincena pendiente que obliga a abrir el año en curso y revisa sus catorce
miembros de paso. Un año ya cerrado no se vuelve a mirar solo; para eso está `--rehacer`.

## Qué no entra

**No se re-ingesta 2024–2025.** Las 46 quincenas previas tienen el mismo `sha256` que sus
copias dentro de los bundles del portal —las 46, byte por byte— y el corte regenerado para
`2025-11_q2` sale idéntico al parquet commiteado. Su `url_origen` apunta a un host que da
503 y se deja: es bitácora, no catálogo.

En `indice-gansito-datos`, en sus propios commits: las 16 quincenas nuevas, y las 62 líneas
del manifiesto selladas con su `crc32` —verificando antes el `sha256` de cada una, con un
diff estrictamente aditivo.

## Verificado contra la fuente real

- 50 pruebas, ninguna toca la red.
- Las 16 quincenas ingestadas; los 16 conteos del corte coinciden con los medidos aparte.
- Con 2026 al día, un bundle abierto salta sus 13 miembros sellados sin un solo falso
  positivo, y con un sello alterado a mano reprocesa esa quincena y sólo esa, dejando el
  parquet anterior intacto y el nuevo como `_i2`.

## Antes de mergear

Correr la cadena completa: con 62 quincenas en vez de 46, el +24.40% nominal y el +16.47%
real publicados son de una ventana que ya no existe.

author: camiloosorio2394
promodeler314-a11y
body:
## 何をしたか

順位条件の判定を入れると順位条件つきスキルが「ほぼ発動しない」側に振れる件を、実測で切り分けて設計書 `docs/order-field.md` にまとめた。
実測を再現する CLI `packages/sim/src/field/order-cli.ts`（`pnpm order-field`）を足した。計算モデルと画面には手を入れていない。

## 分かったこと

原因は四つ重なっている（設計書 2 節）。

1. 既定の相手が 1100-900-900-600-900 固定で、自分が 1400 なら中盤から先頭に居続ける。後方寄りの条件が終盤以降 0 % になる。
2. 相手 8 頭が同一ステータスでスキル無しなので、順位が脚質の塊の境目にしか出ない（差しの中盤末は 5 位が 100 %）。
3. 相手を 1 頭ずつ独立に走らせて束を作っており、隊列ができない。しかも自分だけ位置取りの規則が違う。
4. 出走前の同着で全員が「1 位」になり、序盤の順位条件が素通りする。

相手同士を一緒に走らせて束を作り、自分もその先頭に対して位置取りすると、全頭同時（勝率の面）と同じ形の順位分布になる（設計書 3 節、先行と差しの表）。

## 決めたこと（設計書 4 節）

- 束は相手同士を一緒に走らせて作る（64 本で 3.1 秒、現行 2.4 秒）。
- フィールドありのとき自分も `VIRTUAL` で束の先頭に対して位置取りする。
- 相手の既定は自分と同格にし、σ をつけ、脚質構成とスキルを束ごとに引き直す。
- 出走前は順位条件を判定しない。
- 発動率に相手の強さ ±100 の幅を添える。自己整合は相手のスキルに自分の構成を混ぜる形で入れる。

段取りは設計書 7 節。1 と 2 は `packages/sim` で閉じるので先に進められる。

## 確かめたこと

- `pnpm typecheck` が通る。
- 設計書の数字は `pnpm order-field --trials 200 --skipstart` の出力から取った。

author: copybara-service[bot]
body:
Fix type confusion in AsyncValueTensor tagged pointer resolution by validating root buffer and pointer alignment.

The type confusion vulnerability in `AsyncValueTensor::FromTensor` stems from an unsafe assumption regarding pointer tagging and tensor slicing.

To retrieve an `AsyncValueTensor` from a standard `Tensor`, `FromTensor` relied on a bit-tagging scheme: if the underlying `TensorBuffer` allocated an opaque handle (indicated by `AllocatesOpaqueHandle()`) and the least significant bit (LSB) of the data pointer was set (bit 0 == 1), the pointer was assumed to be a tagged `AsyncValueTensor` pointer.

However, this logic failed to account for tensor slicing. When a tensor utilizing an opaque handle allocator is sliced at an odd byte offset, a `SubBuffer` is created. The data pointer of this `SubBuffer` points to an unaligned odd address within the user payload, meaning its LSB is naturally set to 1. Because `AllocatesOpaqueHandle()` still returned true for the sliced tensor, `FromTensor` incorrectly identified this arbitrary, unaligned user payload address as a tagged `AsyncValueTensor` pointer. It then proceeded to "untag" the pointer (by clearing the LSB) and cast it to `AsyncValueTensor*`. Accessing this fake object resulted in type confusion, which could be exploited to achieve arbitrary code execution (ACE) when the runtime attempted to invoke virtual methods or access member variables on the corrupted pointer.

To resolve this vulnerability, we hardened the pointer resolution logic in `AsyncValueTensor::FromTensor` by introducing two strict validation checks before any pointer untagging or casting occurs:

1. **Root Buffer Validation**: We now verify that the underlying `TensorBuffer` is the root buffer and has not been sliced or offset. This ensures that we are not operating on a `SubBuffer` that could introduce arbitrary pointer offsets.
2. **Alignment Verification**: We enforce that the untagged pointer address is properly aligned according to the alignment requirements of `AsyncValueTensor` (i.e., `alignof(AsyncValueTensor)`). Since a valid, heap-allocated `AsyncValueTensor` will always satisfy this alignment, any pointer that does not align correctly after clearing the tag bit is safely rejected.

Corresponding unit tests have been added in `async_value_tensor_test.cc` to simulate sliced tensors with odd offsets and verify that they no longer trigger incorrect pointer resolution.

author: amanwaseem
body:
Closes #25.

`grep -r runbook` across the repository returned nothing. The procedure for
producing a prediction log entry was written in #4 and closed with it, so GW5
would have been re-derived from memory a week after GW4 — which is the opposite
of #4's claim that running it twice "demonstrates a repeatable process rather
than a one-off".

## `RUNBOOK.md`

#4's GW4-specific steps, generalised to any gameweek N. Nine sections:

| § | |
|---|---|
| 0 | Preconditions, and **one entry per (gameweek, model)** |
| 1 | Timing the snapshot — a hard edge on both sides |
| 2 | Fetch |
| 3 | Exploratory run, and what to read before trusting it |
| 4 | Write the entry |
| 5 | The verifier gate |
| 6 | The digest |
| 7 | Commit, PR, merge before the deadline |
| 8 | The PR body is the record |
| 9 | The fallback, decided in advance |

Three things it states that were previously only understood:

**The snapshot window has a hard edge on both sides.** #19 closed the forward
direction of `resolve_target_gw`, so a snapshot whose `is_next` is not N is
refused outright rather than discouraged. Verified against the current
snapshot, whose `is_next` is GW4:

```
$ python -m fpl.predict_baseline --gw 5 --out scratch/
Refusing to predict GW5 from a snapshot whose next gameweek is GW4.
chance_of_playing_next_round means 'next round as of this snapshot', so every
availability flag here is scoped to GW4. Predicting GW5 would scale its minutes
by the wrong gameweek's injury news, and nothing in the entry would show that it
had happened.
Take a snapshot closer to the GW5 deadline.
```

**A second entry for a logged gameweek is a phantom model, not a correction.**
Rule 1 means the committed entry cannot be replaced, and `model_version` is the
key #3 pools over — so a second one gets a one-gameweek track record that can
never be fairly compared. The measurement goes in `scratch/` and the diff goes
on the PR.

**The fallback is decided here rather than at the deadline.** If the fetch
fails, use the last good snapshot and commit anyway: a stale-flag prediction is
evidence, and a gap in the log is permanent.

The verifier section describes the six check families in the code rather than
#4's enumeration, which had drifted — the descriptive-column checks post-date it.

## Second commit: six wrong instructions

A runbook is followed under deadline pressure by someone who cannot check it
against the source, so a wrong instruction is a bug. Review found six, each
verified against the code before fixing:

1. **The one cross-reference meant to be followed when a fetch is failing was
   broken** — "if it is going to be tight, see §6" led to *The digest*, not the
   fallback at §9.
2. **`--resume` described too broadly.** `find_incomplete` also requires a
   non-empty `players/` and a name newer than `LATEST`, so a fetch that died
   during bootstrap, fixtures or `fetch_live` is unresumable and reports
   `Nothing to resume: every snapshot has a manifest` — untrue of the directory
   on disk.
3. **`--resume` silently freezes availability** at the failed attempt's start,
   by design. Listed only as a time-saver, it contradicted §1's "as late as
   availability allows".
4. **§0 read a file that did not exist yet** — the deadline came from
   `bootstrap.json`, which §2 fetches, and `data/raw/` is gitignored. §3's
   "confirm it matches the deadline you wrote down" then compared the run
   against itself.
5. **§4 pointed at a guard that does not cover the new entry.**
   `check_log_immutable.py` diffs against entries present at the ref; a file
   new there passes as "new entry" whatever it contains. Correct behaviour —
   appending is the point — but it means the fresh entry is protected by the
   verifier alone until the merge.
6. **§9 gave an instruction with no mechanism.** `predict_baseline` has no
   snapshot flag; it reads `data/raw/LATEST`. The fallback works because
   `LATEST` is written last and only on success, which the runbook never said.

## `CLAUDE.md` and `README.md`

The Timeline goes stale when the GW4 deadline passes, so it now points at GW5
and records that **the international break falls after GW5, not before it** —
the quiet stretch is the 18 Sep – 10 Oct gap, and GW5 is an ordinary week seven
days after GW4. Checked against `bootstrap.json`: GW5 has ten fixtures, kicking
off 18–20 Sep.

`README.md`'s four-command block now points at the runbook as the full
procedure, since those commands are the middle of it.

## Checks

```
$ python -m unittest discover tests
Ran 186 tests in 1.664s
OK

$ python tools/check_log_immutable.py --ref origin/main
1 committed entry unchanged since origin/main.

$ python -m fpl.verify_entry predictions/gw04_baseline-v1.csv
OK — entry agrees with snapshot 20260907T141922Z on every check.
```

Docs-only, so none of these are affected by the change; they confirm the
commands the runbook tells you to run still work as written.

## Not in scope

The scoring half, which needs a gameweek both predicted and played, and belongs
with #3.

author: broccolito
body:
**Follows per-model Versa deployments (#230), which is now on `main` together with #238 and #248.** This PR was stacked on #230 and has been retargeted to `main`. Against `main`, its diff is only the card, the card's test and the setup form.

This fixes the first follow-up #230 lists under known gaps: the onboarding card still writes a Versa deployment, and the setup form still carries dead Azure defaults for `versa_azure`.

## What was wrong

With #230, `versa_azure` posts each model to its own deployment. A configured `VERSA_AZURE_DEPLOYMENT_NAME` counts as an override only when the catalog doesn't know the value. In that case it serves **every** request, whatever model the chat selected (`explicit_override`). Since the public Azure card's keys stopped steering Versa (#238), it is the only deployment key Versa reads.

`InstitutionalSetupCard`, the UCSF Versa form in onboarding, had two problems:
- **It wrote `VERSA_AZURE_DEPLOYMENT_NAME = gpt-5.5-2026-04-24` on every connect.** That's a catalog deployment, so after #230 the daemon ignores it. The write only left a misleading key in the config.
- **Its Advanced panel had a free-text "deployment" box.** Any name the catalog doesn't know pinned every model to that one deployment, while the chat kept showing the model it picked. That is the label-only model switch #230 fixed, brought back through configuration from a first-run form.

## Decision: stop writing the key and remove the box

The alternative was to keep the box and write its value only when it isn't a catalog deployment. I rejected it:
- **No value makes the box do what its label says.** A catalog value is ignored, because choosing that model in the picker already reaches it. Any other value becomes the pin-every-model override.
- **It needs a second copy of the catalog.** The renderer would have to hard-code the nine ids in `VERSA_AZURE_DEPLOYMENTS`, which #230 calls "the ONE list", or derive them from `known_models`. That only works while every model name equals its deployment name. It does in today's map, but nothing guarantees it: the catalog is a list of (model, deployment) pairs precisely so the two can differ. Either way the renderer would redo a judgement the daemon already makes, and the copy would drift.
- **The escape hatch is for operators.** If UCSF adds a deployment the catalog doesn't list yet, it can still be set as an environment variable or in `config.yaml`. The daemon honours it and logs at `info` that an override is in force. The provider's own description already says "endpoint and deployment are pre-configured". #230 removed `with_unlisted_models()` for the same reason: a first-run form shouldn't offer a choice that can only fail or only change the label.

## What changes

1. **`InstitutionalSetupCard.tsx`** drops the deployment state, the `VERSA_AZURE_DEPLOYMENT_NAME` upsert and the deployment field. The Advanced label now reads "endpoint, API version". A ⚠ comment at `VERSA_AZURE_DEFAULTS` explains why, so the box doesn't come back by accident.
2. **`DefaultProviderSetupForm.tsx`** loses `PROVIDER_KEY_DEFAULTS.versa_azure`. The entries were never read:
   - Both readers, `loadConfigValues` and `getPlaceholder`, look up a default per **declared** config key.
   - `providerConfigSubmitHandler` submits declared keys only.
   - `versa_azure` declares only `VERSA_AZURE_API_KEY`, on `main` as well as on #230, so the three `AZURE_OPENAI_*` entries could never apply.

   A comment beside the table now states that rule. The Bedrock namespace split (#248) deleted the neighbouring `versa_bedrock` entry for the same reason, so the comment names both providers.
3. **`InstitutionalSetupCard.test.tsx`**: see Tests below.

## What stays the same
- **The key, endpoint and API version writes are unchanged**: same keys, defaults, trimming and order. None of the public `AZURE_OPENAI_*` keys is written.
- **The Bedrock tab is untouched.**
- **A deployment an earlier connect saved is left in place.** The card doesn't delete the key: the old default is a catalog value and inert, and any other value may be an operator's deliberate override. One side effect: reconnecting through the card no longer resets such an override to `gpt-5.5`, which it used to do on every connect.

## Why this had to wait for #230
Before #230, `from_env` fell back to `gpt-5.5-2026-04-24` when the key was unset, so dropping the write alone would have changed nothing. Removing the box would have: on those builds, the box was the only way to make a model other than gpt-5.5 actually answer. #230 is merged, so that ordering now holds.

## Tests
The Azure tests in `InstitutionalSetupCard.test.tsx` go from 2 to 5. The file's two Bedrock tests came from #248 and are unchanged.
- **Kept:** a connect never writes the public `AZURE_OPENAI_*` keys. The helper now waits for `onSuccess`, so the test also sees the writes that happen after `checkProvider`.
- **New:** a connect never writes `VERSA_AZURE_DEPLOYMENT_NAME`.
- **Updated:** a connect makes exactly these writes, in order: API key, endpoint, API version, `BIOROUTER_PROVIDER`. This replaces the test that asserted the deployment write.
- **New:** an endpoint and API version typed into Advanced are written, trimmed. This guards the wiring of the two fields that remain.
- **New:** Advanced shows the endpoint and API version, and "deployment" appears in neither a field nor the label.

**Fail-before check.** Run against the unmodified card, the 3 new and updated assertions fail for the intended reasons: the `gpt-5.5` write, and two "deployment" matches (the label and the field). The two regression guards pass. After the fix, all 5 pass.

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `npm run test:run -- InstitutionalSetupCard` | 5 passed |
| `npm run test:run` (full suite) | 442 files; 4,972 passed, 1 skipped |
| `npm run lint:check` | pass: typecheck, ESLint, themes, 332 contrast assertions, tokens |
| `npm run format:check` | exits 1, on **4 files this PR does not touch**, byte-identical to `main`: `contexts.test.ts`, `toasts.autoClose.test.ts`, `catalogSubscription.test.ts`, `workdirOutsideHome.test.ts`. All 3 files this PR touches pass. |

**Updates since the first push.**
- **#238 and #248 landed on the old base.** The two conflicts were unions: each side deleted a different dead defaults entry, and each added a different test helper.
- **The stack reached `main`.** Merging `main` was clean, because `main` had not touched these three files since the stack's merge-base.

Re-run after each merge: the onboarding and provider-settings vitests (9 files, 104 passed, including all 7 card tests), `npm run lint:check`, and Prettier on the 3 changed files all pass.

I didn't check this in the running app. The change removes one field from a vertical stack and one word from a label, and the DOM assertions above cover both.

author: johnitvn
body:
## Description

The self-release's second hosted run (34625474965, declaring `published`) completed all nine walk stages, minted tag 0.2.0 locally, and then lost the publish: the atomic, never-forced push was rejected non-fast-forward on `refs/release-craft/claims/0d6e4079…3605`, and all four minted refs (claims, ledger, register, tag) were refused together. Origin stayed clean and `verify-origin` printed BROKEN. No second release can ever publish.

Root cause: the claim register is one ref per release line — `refs/release-craft/claims/<sha256(lineId)>` — so the refname is stable across every release on the line. Release 1 created it on origin (tip `e1bd422a`). Release 2's runner checkout does not fetch `refs/release-craft/**` (actions/checkout fetches branches and tags only), so the run's claim store built the register from empty; its new tip has no ancestry with origin's, and the never-forced atomic push dies. The ledger ref is attempt-addressed and the register ref is plan-addressed — only the claims refname collides, but one collision kills the whole atomic push, tag included.

The fix is caller-side substrate posture, matching the architecture law that the caller closes the world and the CLI discovers nothing: a workflow step, immediately after the checkout and before the world closure, fetches the shared claims namespace into the local ref space (`git fetch --no-tags origin '+refs/release-craft/claims/*:refs/release-craft/claims/*'`). The repository is public and the checkout keeps no credentials (`persist-credentials: false`), so the fetch is unauthenticated — the same posture the snapshot step's `git ls-remote origin` already relies on. With the ref present locally, the claim store's compare-and-set append builds a child of origin's tip, the mint's push of that ref is fast-forward, and the atomic push lands; `local-refs-before.txt` is captured after the fetch, so the publish diff sees the moved tip and pushes it.

Consequences recorded in decision-log D65: the fetched record is release 1's version-scoped claim (`stable-version … 0.1.0`), which does not exclude a different version's acquisition, so release 2 still acquires normally; the engine never releases completed claims (no release call site in `src/app/`), so the register accumulates one record per released version — the shared cross-checkout released-version record. The fetched register's commits are off the line's ancestry, so the world closure declares none of it and plan identity is unchanged; the planner stays pure and the Action's input inventory stays closed. Two concurrent checkouts still race; #237 stays declared and out of scope. The dogfood workflow is untouched — it is read-only by design (`git ls-remote` only, zero pushes) and never writes the claims namespace. The product (claim store, engine, binding, dogfood scripts) is unchanged.

The new step is pinned, not hoped for: `scripts/dogfood/self-release-workflow.test.mjs` asserts the integration step exists, carries the exact refspec with `--no-tags`, and sits before the snapshot capture — the red-on-mutant proof is below.

Closes #274

## Could this fail silently?

- The runner-side fetch behaviour is unproven until the live re-dispatch: this PR proves the git mechanics two-sidedly on a scratch origin (below), but that a hosted checkout's `git fetch` of the claims namespace behaves identically is only settled by the next `published` dispatch landing all four refs on origin. Until then the failure mode is exactly the one this fixes — a loud non-fast-forward rejection, a BROKEN origin leg, a failed job — never a green-but-unminted run.
- If the fetch itself fails (private repo, renamed origin, network), it fails loudly in its own step before the snapshot and the run — the dispatch fails rather than minting over anything.
- The dogfood stays untouched and stays safe: it never pushes (its own write-absence proof hashes `git ls-remote` before and after), and this change edits only `self-release.yml`, its workflow-law suite, and the decision log.
- Force-pushing remains refused everywhere; the fix makes sequential releases publishable only. The concurrent-checkout race keeps its declared verdict path (#237).

## How was this verified?

All real, on this machine; the scratch area was `/home/johnitvn/tmp-work/rehearsal-274` (never `/tmp`).

Live origin checks (unauthenticated, the `persist-credentials: false` posture): `git ls-remote` on the real origin shows `refs/release-craft/claims/0d6e4079…` at `e1bd422a` carrying release 1's single `stable-version … 0.1.0` record; the exact fetch command lands the namespace into a scratch clone with exit 0; the built product recomputes the refname — `claimRegisterRefFor("main")` = `refs/release-craft/claims/0d6e4079…3605`.

Two-sided rehearsal on a scratch bare origin seeded with release 1's claims ref, labeled honestly: the claims leg, the publish, and the origin leg run the REAL built `GitClaimStore` (from `dist/`), `scripts/dogfood/publish-mint.mjs`, and `scripts/dogfood/verify-origin.mjs`; the ledger, register, and tag mints are mimicked with git plumbing in the binding's own commit shape (fixed identity, epoch clock, `git tag --no-sign`). (The independent re-review re-ran this rehearsal with the real run door minting all four refs — stronger than the mimic, same verdicts.)

- Leg A (no fetch — the defect): the store acquires `stable-version main 0.2.0` over an empty register (root commit, no ancestry); the real publish exits 1 with `! [rejected] … (non-fast-forward)` on the claims ref and `atomic push failed` on all four refs including the tag; origin byte-identical before/after; the real `verify-origin` prints BROKEN, exit 1 — run 34625474965's shape, reproduced.
- Leg B (with the fetch — the fix): fetch exit 0, origin untouched by it; `local-refs-before` captured after the fetch carries the shared tip; the store acquires normally over the shared register and the new tip's parent IS the shared tip (fast-forward); the record now holds both released versions (0.1.0 and 0.2.0 — the accumulate consequence); the real publish exits 0 pushing all four refs atomically, never forced; the real `verify-origin` prints HOLD, exit 0.

Red-on-mutant proof that the new step is gated (mutation: the `Integrate the shared claims register` step deleted from `self-release.yml`): the workflow-law suite goes red — 14 tests, 11 pass, 3 fail, exit 1 — and the three failures are exactly the new pins (`integrates the shared claims register — the run claims against the shared tip, never an empty one`, `fetches exactly the shared claims namespace — the refspec verbatim, --no-tags, nothing beside it`, `integrates before the snapshots are captured — the publish diff must see the shared tip the run moves`) while the eleven pre-existing rows stay green. Restoring the step (byte-identical, `cmp`-checked) greens the suite: 14/14, exit 0. Full gate-scripts suite after the fold: 114/114.

Gates, sanitized environment as the repo precedent: `pnpm check` exit 0 (25 Moon tasks: format · lint · typecheck · test · build · arch; vitest 107 files / 1718 tests, all passing; gate-scripts typecheck included); `pnpm check:policy` exit 0 (six gates); `pnpm check:workflows` exit 0 (7 workflows keep the security posture, including the edited one). Pre-push hooks green (test served from the warmed run). Every commit on the branch is signed (`git log --show-signature`: Good "git" signature, ED25519 — `%G?` = G on all of them). The diff against the base touches exactly `.github/workflows/self-release.yml`, `scripts/dogfood/self-release-workflow.test.mjs`, and `docs/design/decision-log.md` — no product file.

author: reallaksh19
body:
## Issue

Implements **#268** under Chemistry V2 roadmap #262 / programme #234.

## Governing invariant

```text
SOURCE / ASSESSMENT SCOPE decides WHAT must be teachable.
LEARNER INTELLIGENCE decides ORDER / DEPTH / BRIDGE / TREATMENT / SUPPORT.
```

## Delivered

- `chemistry-learner-study-scope.schema.json`;
- `chemistry-learner-study-model.schema.json`;
- versioned `chemistry-treatment-policy.json`;
- `chemistry-longitudinal-binding.example.json`;
- deterministic C-F synthesis/validation engine;
- no-attempt and attempt-present integration with C-E snapshots;
- per-capability source/question/external traceability;
- preservation of prerequisites, representation obligations, conditions/exceptions, conservation, problem families and verification routes;
- separate longitudinal dimensions for acquisition, reconstruction, retention, transfer, discrimination, representation/condition handling, fluency and timed performance;
- all 10 required C-F falsifiers;
- dedicated CI.

## Treatment semantics

```text
READY_VERIFY_ONLY
ACTIVE_STUDY
REPAIR_BEFORE
REPAIR_IN_UNIT
PROBE_FIRST
```

No-attempt required scope defaults to `ACTIVE_STUDY`, not invented repair. `READY_VERIFY_ONLY` is intentionally limited to activation + independent check. Mixed/probe-required evidence remains `PROBE_FIRST`. Demonstrated prerequisite strength remains credited even when a downstream capability needs repair.

## Scope closure

The learner-independent study-scope digest is derived only from C-C eligible records. AttemptSet presence cannot alter:

```text
required source obligations
required assessment questions/subparts
required external candidates
required capability universe
representation / condition / conservation authority
```

Non-eligible external candidates remain excluded and cannot expand Core1.

## Longitudinal closure

Current evidence never closes delayed retention or transfer. Even demonstrated capabilities retain open obligations for delayed reconstruction, near/far transfer, mixed discrimination, fluency and timed performance; representation/condition obligations are initialized separately when applicable.

## Falsifiers

```text
LEARNER_WEAKNESS_SHRINKS_REQUIRED_SCOPE
OUT_OF_SCOPE_PYQ_EXPANDS_CORE1
READY_CAPABILITY_FULLY_RETAUGHT_FOR_PAGE_DENSITY
NO_ATTEMPT_FORCES_REPAIR
ONE_CURRENT_SUCCESS_CLOSES_DELAYED_RETRIEVAL
STUDYMODEL_WITHOUT_SOURCE_TRACE
```
