body:
Refs #2986 — `Refs`, not `Closes`: gap 1 (`.cuh` unclassified) is fixed; gap 2 (the missing `--query-driver`) was REPRODUCED AND REFUTED on this host, so it is deliberately not implemented. The remainder is commented on the issue.

## Summary

Refs #2986. This change routes `.cuh` through the existing C++ language,
grammar, `cxx` file-kind, and clangd server projections. It records the
intentional divergence from clang's driver extension table and adds a
production-resolution guard named for #2986.

Gap 2 was reproduced first and refuted on this host. CMake generated a HIP
`compile_commands.json` with HIP enabled, and the production LSP path opened
`main.hip` through clangd. The compile database names
`/usr/lib/llvm-21/bin/clang++`; clangd reported only
`drv_no_rocm_device_lib`, not a `hip/hip_runtime.h` not-found diagnostic.
Therefore this round does not add `--query-driver` or a new config key. The
managed-bundle path was also attempted because clangd is absent from PATH, but
the downloaded archive failed extraction before launch. The successful
verification used the PATH-first path with a worktree-local clangd probe copy.

### Header conventions

In scope are `.cuh`, the NVIDIA/HIP community convention for CUDA/HIP C++
headers, plus existing `.h`, `.hpp`, `.hh`, `.hxx`, `.inl`, `.ipp`, `.tpp`, and
`.txx` spellings already covered by the C/C++ registry. `.cu` and `.hip` are
translation-unit spellings, not additional header spellings. `.h` remains
owned by the C entry because it is ambiguous and that ownership predates this
change. Module interfaces (`.c++m`, `.cppm`, `.cxxm`, `.ixx`), Objective-C
(`.m`, `.mm`), and OpenCL (`.cl`, `.clcpp`) remain classified as C++ kinds but
retain their existing grammar policy. No second CUDA/HIP header extension was
found that needs a new registry decision.

## Tests

| Test id | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `routes .cuh through every C++ production projection (#2986)` | Drives the language, grammar, file-kind, and LSP-server production projections; it failed before the fix at `resolveLanguage`. |
| `matches the committed fixture` | Pins the generated cross-consumer language snapshot, including `.cuh`. |
| `each family's projected extension set equals the golden value plus only its documented extras` | Records `.cuh` as the one deliberate C++ scan-family addition. |

Red-first output on the pre-fix build:

```text
FAIL ... routes .cuh through every C++ production projection (#2986)
AssertionError: expected undefined to be 'cpp'
at tests/clients/language-registry-drift.test.ts:228:24
```

Mutation output after removing `.cuh` from both registry projections and the
file-kind list, rebuilding, and rerunning the same file:

```text
Test Files 1 failed (37 tests | 3 failed)
FAIL ... routes .cuh through every C++ production projection (#2986)
AssertionError: expected undefined to be 'cpp'
```

The targeted registry, file-kind, and LSP registry suites passed: 12 files,
255 tests. Every `tests/config/` file passed: 53 files, 470 tests, 1 skipped.
The real HIP probes were run with `PI_LENS_HOME=$PWD/.probe-home`; the CMake
fixture and downloaded clangd copy were removed afterward.

Before the fix, the successful PATH-first HIP run returned:

```text
{"code":"drv_no_rocm_device_lib","message":"Cannot find ROCm device library; provide its path via '--rocm-path' or '--rocm-device-lib-path', or pass '-nogpulib' to build without ROCm device library"}
```

After the fix, the same production PATH-first run still returned no
`hip/hip_runtime.h` not-found diagnostic. A `.cuh` header opened through the
same path, selected `cpp`, and returned a clangd diagnostic
`fe_expected_compiler_job` because a header has no standalone compile command.

Local gates run:

- `npm run build`
- targeted Vitest command above
- all `tests/config/` files
- `npm run fmt:check`
- `npx tsc --noEmit`

Preflight result:

| Gate | Result |
| --- | --- |
| build | pass |
| lint | pass |
| fmt:check | pass |
| changelog:check | pass |
| check-changelog-fragments | pass |
| check:lockfile | pass |
| lockfile:complete | pass |
| tests/config | pass |
| generation-guard | pass |
| flake-shape-ratchet | pass |
| lsp-spawn-heavy-coverage | pass |
| ci-verdict | pass |
| knip | pass |
| check-pr-title | pass |
| check-close-keywords | pass |
| check-pr-body | pass |

### Test assessment

`tests/clients/language-registry-drift.test.ts` uniquely pins the canonical
registry projections and their generated scan-family snapshot. No existing
test became redundant; the new #2986 case catches the unclassified extension
through production seams rather than by asserting a source table entry.

## Blast radius

The changed production symbols are `LANGUAGES.cpp` and
`KIND_EXTENSIONS.cxx`. Their callers include language resolution, tree-sitter
grammar projections, file-kind routing, LSP server selection, scan-family
enumeration, and formatter/runner vocabulary guards. The change adds one
extension to existing arrays and adds no hot-path branch or callback.

The production verification plan covers the built registry projections, the
PATH-first clangd launch, and a `.cuh` touch through `LSPService`. A direct
`module_report` blast-radius report was unavailable in this fixer lane; the
dependent population was checked with repository-wide `rg` searches and the
registry/config suites.

## Observability

No new failure path; no record added.

## Class sweep

This is the unclassified-extension drift shape: a consumer extension list can
silently omit a community spelling even when the canonical language and LSP
server already exist. The whole-tree sweep searched `clients/`, `tools/`,
`mcp/`, `scripts/`, and `index.ts` for `.cuh`, CUDA/HIP extension lists, and
clangd registration. The only missing production members were the two
canonical registry projections and `KIND_EXTENSIONS.cxx`, all fixed here.

The population sweep checked `.cu`, `.hip`, `.cuh`, `.h`, `.hpp`, `.hh`, `.hxx`,
`.inl`, `.ipp`, `.tpp`, and `.txx`: existing members retained their results;
`.cuh` now matches the intended C++ path. The family stays distributed because
language ownership, grammar routing, and file-kind routing are separate public
projections of the canonical registry; the existing guards already consolidate
their consistency checks.

body:
## Why

Measured 2026-09-11 on memex.meshweaver.cloud: **zero pages in Google's index.** Every public page — documentation, course lessons, plugin covers — reached Googlebot with a rich `<head>` and an empty `<body>` (a Blazor Server page fills its body over the circuit, which a crawler never holds), and the sitemap listed only the 103 partition roots. Full design and measurements: `Doc/Architecture/PublicWebPresence`.

## What

- **`SeoPageData.Body`** — the page text for the first response: the node's mirrored HTML, else the content's `prerenderedHtml`, else its markdown (`content` for a markdown node, `body` for a plugin cover) rendered through the portal's own pipeline. Only for a node the anonymous gate admitted. `Remainder` records a URL that resolved past its node, so the head can `noindex` the ancestor-fallback.
- **Sitemap descends.** `EnumeratePublished` lists every page-shaped descendant (`Markdown`, `Space`, `Store/*`, `Edu/Module`, `Edu/Page`; no satellite segments) of an admitted root and asks `AnonymousGate` **per node** — the same grants and denies the installer writes for free and paid chapters. This replaces the `publicSegments` read through the raw storage adapter, which returned nothing on the partitioned deployment (no course chapter was ever listed).
- **`PublicSite`** (`Portal:PublicHost`, `Portal:LandingPath`): canonical, `og:url`, sitemap `<loc>` and robots' `Sitemap:` name the public host; the app host's robots is `Disallow: /`; `UsePublicHostRedirect` sends a stranger's HTML GET for a public page on the app host to the public host with 301; `UseHeadAsGet` answers `HEAD` (was 405 from every page). All off when the key is unset.
- Minimal-API endpoints taking `IMessageHub` declare `[FromServices]` explicitly (parameter inference classified it as the body in a host without a mesh).
- Chart renders `Portal__SiteName`, `Portal__PublicHost`, `Portal__LandingPath`.

## Verified locally

| `DocumentationLinkIntegrityTest`, `WhatsNewEntryIntegrityTest` | 2/2 pass |

## Counterparts

The Plugins half (Postgres readers mirror `prerenderedHtml` on the cross-schema path; `ApplicationPage` renders the stashed body visibly for signed-out visitors; landing at `/`; `/welcome` and `/login` noindex; middleware wiring) follows once this merges and the pin moves. The Memex config repo half adds the keys and points `www.meshweaver.cloud` at the portal.

Implementers: none — no interface member added.

author: jerrythomas
body:
**No Rust change.** `git diff main...develop -- src/ crates/ Cargo.toml Cargo.lock` is empty — the crate tree is byte-identical to v0.13.0.

## Security

- **devalue 5.8.1 → 5.9.2** — "reject out-of-bounds indices" (AIKIDO-2026-869882). Already inside kit's declared `^5.8.1`; only the lockfile was stale. It is an external import in the deployed worker, so this reaches production.
- **undici override 7.29.0 → 8.10.2.** The old pin dragged `jsdom@30` off its declared `^8.9.0`, which is the path the scanner flagged. Bun rejects nested overrides (verified — it warns and ignores), so one version serves both parents; 8.10.2 is the only fully patched release satisfying jsdom.
- Secret scanning + push protection enabled. Renovate owns security PRs (`vulnerabilityAlerts` + `osvVulnerabilityAlerts` — OSV is what covers crates.io) instead of adding Dependabot as a second bot. Every rule gained a 7-day `minimumReleaseAge`; the `@rokkit/*` group auto-merges, and automerge with no cooldown turns one compromised publish into a merged commit.

## Fixed

- **`bun run check` could not start at all** — svelte-check 4.x refuses a bare TypeScript 7. Paired `typescript@~6.0.3` with TS 7 as `@typescript/native` + `--tsgo`. Now 46 files, 0 errors.
- **`cookie` override was mis-documented** as build-time only; it ships in the worker. No version change — kit still declares `^0.6.0` and every 0.6.x carries GHSA-pxg6-pf52-xh8x. Renovate now caps it `<1.0.0`, because 1.0 delegates quote-parsing to `decode` (kit passes an identity decoder) and 2.0 renames `parse`/`serialize`.

## Added

- **CI gates the site** — `--frozen-lockfile`, check, test, build with `CF_PAGES=1`. Nothing ran the site before, which is how the broken type-check survived.
- **CodeQL** over `rust`, `javascript-typescript`, `actions`.
- **`sensei.library.json` completed per spec** (#13). `install` names `dbd install`, the command that exists — the issue's `dbd skills add <name>` was a template from another library. `make bump` now keeps `documents`/`ref` current.

## Verification

`cargo test --workspace` 1316 passed · clippy `-D warnings` clean · `cargo fmt --check` clean · `cargo audit` clean · site: check 0 errors, 47 tests, `CF_PAGES=1` build green.

Closes #13.

author: dogrucanemek-alt
body:
The retry added in #35 kept the processor while it waited. That is the worst
thing to do when what you are waiting for is **another process letting go of a
file**: the spin starves the reader whose open handle is blocking the rename,
so the wait makes the thing it is waiting for slower.

Idle, it never showed — forty attempts five milliseconds apart is more patience
than a reader on a quiet machine needs. Under the unit suite's own load, with
101 test files running at once, the two hundred milliseconds ran out and the
witness threw `EPERM` **on its own start-up path**:

```
EPERM: operation not permitted, rename witness.listen.json.tmp -> witness.listen.json
  at writeFileAtomic (packages/body/src/witness.ts:64)
```

Seen in one of three gate runs, caught by the test written for #35.

`Atomics.wait` yields the core instead of burning it, and the budget goes from
200 ms to two seconds. A reader holds this file for microseconds when the
machine is idle; the budget is for the machine that is not.

### Gate

`npm test` **×5** under that same load before the split, and ×3 on this branch,
exit 0 each: unit **390** (389 + 1 skip) / **128** suites · cost **17** ·
panel **63/63** · `tsc --noEmit` clean.

The failure appeared in 1 of 3 runs before the fix and in 0 of 8 after it.

author: theanswermanishere
body:
Workstream: #36

**David-merge-only.** This edits `claude-core.md` and `agents-core.md`, which is the carve-out: a change to my own working contract is David's merge, not mine.

Closes #75 for this container.

```plan-provenance
kind: private-plan
plan_filename: PLAN_FABLE_PHASE1_FOUNDATIONS_B1.md
plan_sha256: 9290a871a88ac01e342962bf394473dffcd60b7453d0ea22288d5d2087c458bf
approved_by: David
approved_on: 2026-09-11
```

**Review budget:** internal tier, 3 rounds. Declared before round 1.

---

## The reviewer's oracle

The four sections below are the approved plan's, verbatim. The plan itself was reviewed in session over round 0 plus three rounds, adjudicated to a stop at the cap, then simplified on David's instruction and approved at the digest above. It was never committed.

### Direction

AI-Handbook issue #36 — Fable as a third set of eyes: technical review in the loop and plain-English counsel at every decision David makes blind. Phase 1 is the second of six increments (Phase 0 through Phase 5), and the phases run back to back. This increment makes true: **every Codex finding in a code loop is classified against the approved oracle and the threat model by a judge that reads only script-derived inputs, and the fleet can see, roughly, whether that classification changed anything.**

### Product Intent

1. **The record's evidence path has no retyping step in the normal case.** A tool result that came back inline is recovered byte-exact from the harness's own session transcript by a script, selected by the call's recorded input (PR, method, page, full page size). `agent-written` remains a class the record names for the case where no transcript is found. The same script recovers the adjudicator's own answer, so no judge output is retyped either. (Closes #75 for this container: the value is cost, not security.)
2. **B1, conformance triage, ships inside the existing `review-loop-adjudicator`.** For every finding in the record the judge returns one class — *in scope*, *out of threat model*, *out of product intent*, *test precision*, *misdirection* — with a citation into the record (an oracle section, the threat model, or the diff), or *unclassifiable: no oracle* where the loop has none. Advisory in rounds 1–2: the builder triages with the classification in hand and may differ, saying so on the thread. Binding from round 3: a finding classed out of threat model, out of product intent or misdirection ships as a recorded gap citing the class; a finding classed in scope, test precision or unclassifiable goes through the ordinary write-or-stop verdict under the `Worth:` rule, exactly as today. A decline on an out-of-scope class must cite the classification; no citation, no decline.
3. **The record carries what B1 needs and lacks today.** The threat model for every tier at the reviewed commit; the bugfix oracle's fields as sections for a `bugfix` provenance (today they validate and reach the judge as `sections: null`); a patch cap under which #73's 127,061-character diff arrives uncut. Finding bodies and the four plan-oracle sections already exist and stay.
4. **A gut-level measurement.** `/maintenance` reports, for the window, how many B1 dispatches ran and how many findings B1 classed out of scope. Both are counted from the committed verdict files, nothing is stored, and the number is a trend indicator for David's "is this earning its keep" conversation — never an audit. The zero-for-fifteen retirement rule reads that trend.
5. **A harness-side observation of instruction isolation on every `fable-dispatch` run**, recorded beside the probe's self-report: the harness's own prompt-token accounting, the largest across the run's assistant events, bounded against the payload the script sent plus an allowance; and the debug log's loaded-skills and pending-async-hooks lines under their real names. Measured 2026-09-11 on Claude Code 2.1.268 (Haiku, replaced system prompt, no tools): 804 prompt tokens under the dispatch configuration from the repo root, 874 from outside the repo, 17,810 with default setting sources from the repo root — the repository instructions arriving despite the replaced system prompt. Stated as observed within a bound, never as "proven absent"; the managed-hook gap narrows and does not close.
6. **The three standing #73 gaps close**: the permitted-role set is a predicate (a role may dispatch iff its brief is script-generated), not a parameter; `briefSha256` hashes the text the reviewer was actually sent; a `result` event carrying neither `subtype` nor `is_error` is refused.
7. **No model id is hard-coded anywhere the machinery chooses a model** (David, 2026-09-11: "Fable" and "Astra" mean *the strongest Claude model* and *the strongest Codex or ChatGPT model*, not a version). Role definitions and the plan reviewer name a tier; one configuration value per tier, in `.agents/machinery.json`, maps it to the current full id; the dispatch resolves the tier there, records the resolved id and the model the answer was actually stamped with, and refuses when they differ. A new model is a one-value edit. The adjudicator's `model: best` already resolves in the harness and stays as it is.

### Must Not Change

- Codex's full fix-or-decline force on product code. B1 never vetoes a finding; every decline still carries `Class:` / `Worth:` / `Oracle:` / `Result:`.
- The adjudicator stays an `Agent`-tool subagent declaring `model: best` and `effort: xhigh`, dispatched with no per-invocation model; it is not migrated onto `fable-dispatch.mjs`. Its receipt validation in `review-budget.mjs` is unchanged: B1's output is not a receipt.
- The write-gate rule and its two invariants; the round-3-onward *verdict* dispatch; the leash and David-gate arithmetic; the tier budgets.
- `plan-review.mjs` and the plan loop: untouched, except that its reviewer model and effort pin read from the same configuration value as Product Intent 7 instead of a literal in the script.
- The dispatch transport (a subprocess, argv built by the script); role definitions under `.agents/fable-roles/`; never `--bare`. Every role except the probe stays refused in this increment; the refusal lifts in Phase 2 with the first role whose brief is a script-derived record.
- The never-list: no second Codex, no veto over Codex, no builder in-loop prose in any judge's input. The record's finding bodies are root comments only, replies excluded — true today, true after.
- The `Worth:` triage rule and the producer-scoped threat model: fleet contract as of 2026-09-10, applied here and not re-derived.

### Settled Decisions

1. **B1 is the adjudicator, extended** — one dispatch per round, on the record it already reads. A `fable-dispatch` B1 would be the migration decided *next* on 2026-09-10; that stays next.
2. **One plan, one implementation PR, sequenced inside it** (David, 2026-09-11). The capture path lands first because it makes every later round cheaper. Round 0's SC3 (split the dispatch-side work) is declined on that instruction.
3. **"Widen the record" is a delta, not a rebuild.** Bodies, the four oracle sections and the internal-tier threat-model note have been in the record since `68222ab` (#38, 2026-09-06); the delta is Product Intent 3.
4. **The isolation observation is the harness's usage report and debug log, not the reviewer's answer.** The self-report canary stays, labelled as such. The bound is calibrated in the implementation against the live probe and the saved contaminated control.
5. **The `worth` role candidate (#36 comment, 2026-09-10) is subsumed at round 3+** by B1's binding per-finding classification; no separate role.
6. **Threat model**: the builder's own mistakes, scoped by producer — and (David, 2026-09-11) **a mistake whose outcome is inconsequential is not guarded against.** Applied to this plan: no digest binding of the judge's answer to its record, no outcome lifecycle, no per-request token deltas, no advisory-on-retyped-evidence rule, no coverage refusals. body:
## Problem

Two code paths treated a dot in a name as a file extension, which broke every service whose model name carries a version — e.g. `llamacpp-glm-5.3-flash-q2kxl`:

1. **Rename API refused dotted names.** `ComposeManager.rename_service` (and `validate_service_name`, used by the legacy YAML path) rejected anything outside alphanumerics/hyphens/underscores, so the dashboard could not rename names it already hosts. Hit while renaming a live service: the request failed with `Service name must be alphanumeric with hyphens/underscores` after the container had already been stopped.
2. **`/v2` deep links 404'd.** The SPA fallback in `app.py` aborted 404 when the last path segment contained a dot, so a hard load of `/v2/services/llamacpp-glm-5.3-flash-q2kxl` failed while navigating from `/v2` worked. `/v2/services/<name>/logs` was unaffected because its last segment is `logs` — which is why the failure looked intermittent.

## Fix

- `compose_manager.py`: the name charset rule now lives in one `_valid_service_name` helper used by both call sites, and permits dots. Error message updated to match.
- `app.py`: the SPA fallback recognizes an asset request by a known suffix list (`.js`, `.css`, `.map`, …) instead of "contains a dot". Real asset requests still 404, which keeps the "browsers must not cache HTML as a JS/CSS resource after a deploy" protection intact, while dotted client routes fall through to `index.html`.

## Tests

- `tests/test_v2_routes.py` (new): a dotted client route is not an asset; hashed `.js`/`.css` assets are; a dotted deep link serves the SPA; a missing asset still 404s.

body:
## Summary

- Merge `wbs-tool-v1/main` through `259d2ebefd9b0eec4b19fbbb8e1865acb9b4a519` (107 upstream commits since the previous synchronized snapshot `87bf2931`). The final four commits arrived while the first snapshot's CI ran and are included in this sync.
- Bring in the backend ports/adapters extraction, Arrange by Schedule, and upstream browser, accessibility, repository-wiring, and devsync fixes.
- Include upstream PRs #409–410 for preview-close timing and hover-card takeover delay.
- Preserve puni's Twilight documents, economics review, custom OpenSpec workflow tooling and CI, and prior regression safeguards. The merge applied without conflicts; no additional product behavior changes were introduced for the sync.

## Verification

- Upstream CI for the fetched snapshot: passed, run `34584545513`.
- Pinned Bun 1.4.2: `nx run-many -t test,lint,typecheck,check,integration --projects=tool-git-hooks,tool-test-scratch,tool-workflows --parallel=2 --skip-nx-cache` — all 11 applicable tasks passed.
- `git diff --cached --check` passed; fork-specific Twilight documents and workflow implementation are unchanged from puni main.
- Initial-snapshot integration review (`4443897f`): no critical, important, or minor issues. A separate raw-tree comparison verified all 217 fork-only and 885 upstream-only changed path states against their parent blobs/modes (including deleted rename source paths), with zero mismatches. The three overlaps are coherent unions (orientation index, optimization cue browser test, and identical scratch helper).
- Pre-commit format, lint, secrets scan, and documentation-cap checks passed with hooks enabled; migration lint had no matching changed migration files.
- Initial-snapshot browser shards passed: 337 passed, 37 skipped, zero failures. Skips are 36 explicitly opt-in rendering-baseline experiments (`R10_BASELINE`) and the existing `test.fixme` for Gantt upward-boundary dragging. No skips were introduced for this sync. Initial-snapshot CodeQL passed.
- The initial snapshot (`4443897f`, through upstream `4bd9a0c5`) passed full CI run `34648217329`: all 31 Nx projects and one dependency task, solver image smoke, deploy/gate safety checks, OpenSpec 75/75, and pinned OpenSpec integration.
- After adding upstream `259d2ebe`, `fe-01:test:unit --skip-nx-cache` passed: 31 files, 528 tests. The additional 18 changed paths match upstream exactly. Hooks passed again. Full CI for updated head `730288c1` is run `34650067508`; the prior CI is not treated as verification of these later changes.

## Merge paused: newly imported hover-card regression

Follow-up review found one Important issue in `apps/fe-01/src/components/wbs/plan-cell-props.ts:105-123`. A cardable Depends cell's leave handler returns before calling `cellCards.leave`. Its document pointer bridge exists only once its own card is mounted, so it cannot cancel the new pending takeover while a different card remains open.

Sequence: open/hold notes card A → enter live Depends cell B → leave B for inert space before 100ms → B still opens and cancels A's close deadline. This contradicts `openspec/changes/card-takeover-delay/specs/wbs-domain/spec.md`, scenario "a takeover left behind still lets the reach close the first card".

A read-only Bun 1.4.2 probe using the actual `createPlanCellProps`, `createCellCards`, `createDepLights`, and a complete row fixture reproduced:

```text
after leaving: a:name
after takeover deadline: b::depends
after reach deadline: b::depends
error: The departed Depends cell took over and outlived the original reach
```

The probe exercised production handlers, not a browser; an end-to-end browser reproduction/regression test is still owed. The sandbox also emitted unrelated dconf warnings during module imports. No production fix or test-file edit has been made.

Recommended bounded fix, pending user approval: let the Depends leave handler cancel a pending takeover when its own card is not open, while preserving the document bridge's ownership for an already-open Depends card. Add a browser regression that crosses and leaves the cell before 100ms, watch it fail before the fix and pass after, and rerun the whole browser/CI gates. Do not merge until the finding is resolved or explicitly accepted by the user.

No deployment and no push to upstream.

author: mmasoomi-glitch
body:
Closes `002-5`. The handlers and the adapter were already tested; this is the socket they were missing.

Each route is one line:

```ts
export const POST = toRouteHandler(signInHandler(authHandlerConfig()), adapterConfig());
```

Every check the endpoint performs — rate limiting on both dimensions, the constant-time password comparison, the `__Host-` cookies, the CSRF pair, the 429 with `Retry-After` — lives behind the handler and is exercised by calling a function. There is no room in a route file for a check to be forgotten.

All four routes are `ƒ` (dynamic) and `runtime: nodejs`. A statically rendered auth response would hand the next visitor somebody else's session.

## ADR-0002, and the part it got wrong

`next dev` and `next build` **rewrite** `tsconfig.json` on first run. A repo that adds Next.js and does nothing else discovers that as an unexplained diff, usually in someone else's PR — so the decision had to be made first. ADR-0002 chose `bundler` resolution repo-wide, one config, and the file is committed pre-shaped. `git status` after the build is clean.

The ADR's first version then asserted that the `.js` import suffixes could stay, because `bundler` resolution maps `./y.js` to `y.ts`. **That is true of TypeScript and false of the bundler.** `tsc --noEmit` passed cleanly and `next build` failed on every route file:

```
Module not found: Can't resolve '../../../../server/http/adapters/web.js'
```

`moduleResolution: "bundler"` tells the *type checker* to behave as a bundler would. It does not configure, or describe, what webpack does — and webpack looks for a file called `web.js`, which does not exist.

The alternative was `resolve.extensionAlias` in `next.config`. Rejected: webpack-only, Turbopack has no equivalent, and `next build --turbopack` is stable in 15.5 — so it leaves a mine for whoever first builds with the other bundler. So the suffixes came out: 158 across 35 files, mechanical, verified by `tsc` and the full suite.

**The ADR records the correction rather than reading as if it had been right.** A plausible claim about a tool's behaviour went into a decision document unverified; the build tested it one commit later.

**`pnpm build` is now a CI gate in its own right**, for exactly that reason. And the CI grep that checks nobody imports the unguarded ledger services was looking for `posting.js` — after this it would have matched nothing and passed *vacuously*, which is the worst way for a check to fail. Pattern updated.

## Review found two more, and the server settled them

Fed the scaffold to an adversarial reviewer, then checked its claims against the running build with `curl` rather than reasoning about them:

**`Cache-Control` was absent from every API response.** Confirmed. `force-dynamic` controls *Next's* cache and says nothing to a CDN or a browser. A 200 from `GET /api/auth/session` — a JSON body naming the authenticated user, carrying a fresh `Set-Cookie` — is heuristically cacheable by any shared proxy that decides to. One cached copy served to the next visitor is an account takeover with no attacker involved. Now `no-store`, not `private`: `private` still lets the *browser* keep a copy, which is wrong on a shared machine after someone signs out.

**The page CSP was overwriting the API's.** Confirmed. `next.config` headers win over what a route handler sets, and a single `/:path*` rule applied the page policy everywhere:

```
$ curl -D- http://127.0.0.1:3999/api/auth/session
content-security-policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; ...
```

— where the handler had set `default-src 'none'`. The looser policy won on exactly the responses that needed the stricter one. Split into a page rule with a negative lookahead and an API rule. After:

```
$ curl -D- http://127.0.0.1:4001/api/auth/session
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
content-security-policy: default-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'
cache-control: no-store
```

**And one claim that was wrong.** The review said `source: "/:path*"` does not match the root path, leaving `/` with no headers. It does match; the headers were there all along. Checked rather than accepted — a review is evidence to test, not a verdict to apply.

## Also in this PR

`isolatedModules` — which Next requires, because SWC compiles each file alone — forbids inlining `@node-rs/argon2`'s `declare const enum Algorithm`. The value exists at runtime; only the compile-time reference does not.

A bare magic number for a cryptographic parameter rots silently, so the guard is not a comment. `P1` asserts the **encoded** hash prefix — argon2 writes its algorithm, version and cost into the output string — which is the observable fact rather than a restatement of the constant that produced it. Seven more tests cover salting, the refusal to distinguish a corrupt hash from a wrong password, the length bounds, and that the dummy verification stays memoised so a miss does not become *slower* than a hit.

## Evidence

```text
$ npx tsc --noEmit
(clean)

$ npx next build
 ✓ Compiled successfully in 4.5s
 ✓ Generating static pages (4/4)

Route (app)                                 Size  First Load JS
┌ ○ /                                      139 B         102 kB
├ ○ /_not-found                            995 B         103 kB
├ ƒ /api/auth/register                     139 B         102 kB
├ ƒ /api/auth/session                      139 B         102 kB
├ ƒ /api/auth/signin                       139 B         102 kB
└ ƒ /api/auth/signout                      139 B         102 kB

$ npx vitest run
 Test Files  14 passed (14)
      Tests  240 passed (240)
```

231 before, 240 now. The lockfile was regenerated locally and verified byte-identical to the build pod's — `md5 7c09515aaa55e027a918401f050b395e`, 72153 bytes on both — rather than eyeballed.

## Sprint and ownership

- **Sprint:** 002 · **Base:** `6fc4c1b` · **Agent:** PLATFORM-GUARDIAN (root config, `next.config.ts`, `tsconfig.json`, `package.json`, CI) with AUTH-TENANCY (`src/server/http/`)
- No migrations. No schema change.

## Known limitations

- **No UI.** `layout.tsx` and `page.tsx` are the minimum that produces a valid document. The home page says plainly that there is no interface and names where progress is tracked, rather than showing a dashboard with nothing behind it. FRONTEND-UX owns what replaces it.
- **No ESLint or Prettier**, so `next build`'s lint step currently does nothing. `eslint.ignoreDuringBuilds` is already `false`, so it starts enforcing the moment a config lands.
- **A `GET` to a POST-only route is answered by Next, not by our handler.** Next returns its own 405 before the handler runs, so the `allow` header the handler would have set is absent. The `next.config` security headers still apply. `H8` therefore tests the handler, not the deployed path — stated because the test name does not make that obvious.
- `style-src 'unsafe-inline'` in the page CSP is Next's requirement for hydration-critical CSS. It is not granted to scripts.
- The API security headers are set **twice** — per response by the handler, and at the edge by `next.config`. That is deliberate: the handler's version is what the tests assert and what protects a response served by anything other than Next; the config's is what wins. They must stay in agreement, and if they drift the handler's becomes decorative.
- `B-20260912-01`, `-02` and `-03` remain open against these endpoints.

author: congbinh99999
body:
**Motivation**
`email_verification_service.py` was fully implemented but no route ever reached it, so `verify_email`, `resend_email` and `has_pending_verification` were unreachable code. The practical effect: `register` sets `is_verified = false`, `login` rejects unverified users, and nothing in the API could flip that flag. Every account created through the API was permanently locked out. Reaching a logged-in state required `UPDATE users SET is_verified = true` by hand.

**Changes**

`fix(auth): reject already-used email verification token`
`verify_email()` never checked `verified_at`, so a token could be replayed forever — its own docstring already promised "Token không tồn tại hoặc đã sử dụng". The bug was unreachable before this branch; exposing the service is what makes it matter.

`feat(auth): add email verification endpoints`
- `GET /api/v1/auth/verify-email?token=...` — the URL `email_service.py:99` actually puts in the mail
- `POST /api/v1/auth/verify-email` — same operation for a client that holds the token
- `POST /api/v1/auth/resend-verification`
- `AuthService.resend_verification()` does the email lookup, so routes keep talking to services rather than repositories, matching every other route in the app

`resend-verification` returns an identical body for an address that exists, one that does not, and one already verified.

`fix(auth): keep old token when verification email fails to send`
`resend_email()` deletes the existing token before issuing a new one, and the boolean from `send_verification_email()` was discarded. With SMTP unconfigured — `email_service.py:71` returns `False` immediately — the API answered `200 {"success": true}` while destroying the user's only working link and delivering nothing. Reproduced: token gone, new token in the database, no mail sent, user unable to verify by any route. Now raises `EmailSendFailedException` (503) so `get_db` rolls back and the old link survives.

`fix(auth): serve verify-email link over get to match email url`
The endpoint was POST-only while the mail links to GET, so every user clicking the button in their inbox got 405. Caught only by end-to-end testing — the service-level tests all passed.

**Testing / Eval**
`tests/test_email_verification.py` — 8 tests on stubs, no server or database. Covers fresh, used, expired and unknown tokens, and all four resend paths including send failure. 12 unit tests pass in total; `uv run ruff check app tests` is clean.

End to end against real Gmail SMTP and local Postgres 18:

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `register` | mail delivered to a real inbox |
| click the link in the mail | `{"verified": true}` |
| database | `is_verified = t`, `verified_at` set |
| click the same link again | 401 |
| `login` after verifying | 200 |
| `resend` for a verified address | 200, no mail sent |
| `resend` with SMTP down | 503, previous token still valid |

The `register → verify → login` path now completes through the API for the first time.

The four pre-existing suites (`test_auth`, `test_devices`, `test_roles`, `test_users`) still fail: `conftest.py` drives a live server on `localhost:8000` instead of an ASGI transport. Unchanged by this PR.

**Notes for reviewer**
- Both GET and POST are registered for `/verify-email`. GET is what the mail links to and is the path users take; POST exists for a frontend that already holds the token. Dropping GET breaks the email link, which is the whole feature.
- The 503 on send failure is a deliberate trade. It tells an attacker the address exists while SMTP is broken, which is strictly better than silently stranding the user — the previous behaviour. Moving the send off the request path removes both.
- A review at high effort raised four further issues, all verified and all left out as pre-existing architecture rather than part of "add the missing endpoints":
  1. `resend-verification` is unauthenticated, unthrottled, and calls `smtplib.SMTP` with no timeout from inside `async def`, so it blocks the event loop; a hanging SMTP server stalls the worker.
  2. The uniform response leaks by timing — an existing address waits for a full SMTP roundtrip, an unknown one returns at once.
  3. The mail is sent before the transaction commits, so a failed commit leaves a live link to a rolled-back token.
  4. The single-use guard is read-then-write with no row lock; two concurrent requests can both pass it.
  Items 1 to 3 share one cause, synchronous sending inside the request, and one change fixes all three. That belongs in its own PR with rate limiting.
- `password_reset_service` has the same problem — four implemented methods, no routes. Planned as `feat/binh_password-reset` after this lands, kept separate because both branches edit `auth.py`.

**Related**
Follows #1 and #2. No ticket.

author: joelaforet
body:
This adds internal Sage assignment for an untyped GMSO topology and an authoritative explicit-hydrogen RDKit molecule. OpenFF's public parameter labels populate native harmonic and periodic GMSO potentials. Proper torsions retain their Fourier arrays, and impropers retain the three exact ordered terms and divisors used by Sage.

The adapter returns a topology copy and provenance report. It verifies the atom mapping, preserves site metadata and charges, and uses OpenFF masses. Nonbonded assignment can be disabled without reading sigma or epsilon. Equivalent atoms share types so DPD pair tables scale with force-field types rather than atom count.

Validation includes 33 Sage tests and 70 existing UFF and AllAtomDPD tests. OpenMM comparisons check each bonded category's energy and Cartesian forces, including signed coefficients and nonzero phases. Tests also cover mapping permutations, input preservation, epsilon toggles, invalid parameters, improper ordering and native potential serialization. Pinned hooks pass.

This layer assigns parameters only. HOOMD Fourier-array execution, improper force backends and the public initializer remain separate work. Isotopes and automatic proper-torsion divisors are unsupported. Full topology JSON reload retains the documented GMSO limitation; individual saved potential records roundtrip with their coefficients, units and tags.

author: copilot
body:
The `deploy` GitHub Actions job was failing before any deploy logic ran because `npm ci` rejected an out-of-sync lockfile. This change updates the repository lockfile to match the current manifest so the workflow can install its declared dependencies and proceed.

- **Root cause**
  - `package.json` declares the current linting/formatting toolchain in `devDependencies`, but `package-lock.json` did not include those entries.
  - The deploy workflow uses `npm ci`, which requires the manifest and lockfile to be fully synchronized.

- **Change**
  - Regenerated `package-lock.json` from the existing `package.json`.
  - No application or workflow logic changed.

- **Effect on deploy**
  - Restores compatibility with the existing install step in `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`.
  - Unblocks downstream validation and deployment steps that were never reached.

```json
{
  "devDependencies": {
    "@eslint/js": "^9.15.0",
    "eslint": "^9.15.0",
    "prettier": "^3.4.2",
    "typescript-eslint": "^8.18.0"
  }
}
```

## Summary

The package smoke now starts the installed HTTP entry from a disposable working directory, verifies authentication, compares every tool definition with installed stdio, and checks matching two-row ALE analysis with unchanged source bytes.

Closes #87.

The required landing audit is restored by updating sharp to 0.35.4 (incorporating the proposed change from #86) and locked js-yaml to 4.3.2. These address [the sharp advisory](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rgj7-g3m4-5g8c) and [the js-yaml advisory](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2883-xcg3-v3hh), retaining platform-specific native packages and constraints.

## Security and source safety
- [x] No credentials, private project data, customer media or proprietary SDK files.
- [x] Fixture access stays within configured allowed roots; source inputs remain read-only.
- [x] Inspection-only authority, random ephemeral token, bounded requests and task-owned child cleanup; no new product mutations.
- [x] Provider and telemetry settings are excluded from the child environment.

## Validation
- [x] npm run check: 841 TypeScript tests, 49 Python tests, build, stdio/HTTP smoke, pack dry run and fresh-package/Python/AAF checks passed.

author: dannbleeker
body:
Stamp thirty slides with the same marker and the deck carried **thirty identical copies of the same image**.

## Measured

Four inserts of `markeringer-1` into `template/validators.pptx`, before:

```
deck: 37879 -> 50161 -> 61761 -> 73394 -> 85061
growth per insert: 12282, 11600, 11633, 11667
ppt/media: 4 parts, 1 distinct
```

After:

```
deck: 37879 -> 50241 -> 52107 -> 54008 -> 55935
growth per insert: 12362, 1866, 1901, 1927
ppt/media: 1 part, 1 distinct
```

## How

A carried media part is named after its own content — a fingerprint of its bytes and their length — so the second insert finds it with one lookup and points at it.

**Derived rather than searched for, on purpose.** Searching means decompressing every picture in the user's deck on every insert, which on a deck full of photographs is exactly the cost [#45](https://github.com/dannbleeker/SSF-Slide-Elements/pull/45) took out of the base64 path. `pkg.has(name)` is one lookup in an index the package already holds.

The fingerprint is two 32-bit hashes rather than one 64-bit one, because 64 bits in JavaScript means `BigInt` and this runs over every picture an element carries. It is not used as a cryptographic hash: it names a part, with the byte length beside it, so two different pictures would have to collide in both.

**Media only.** An embedded workbook or a chart part is a document, not a picture — two charts sharing one workbook would mean editing one edits both. PowerPoint shares identical images itself and does not share those.

## Proven, both directions

```
with sharing off        — expected 'ppt/media/image2.png' to be 'ppt/media/image1.png'
with the name made      — expected 'ppt/media/ssf-shared.png' not to be 'ppt/media/ssf-shared.png'
content-blind
```

Three existing cases asserted the literal `icon2.png` a sequence produced. They now read the name out of the answer and assert what they were about: the copy is there, declared once, and pointed at.

## One number that needs a host round to mean anything

Also measured, and written into `remove.ts`: 50 insert-then-remove cycles cost **3.5–5.5 KB each** in orphaned parts (unlisted slides, their relationships, their tag parts).

Read that at the right scope — it is what chaining *this engine's* packages costs, an upper bound rather than what a user's file does. **Whether PowerPoint carries an unreferenced part through a save is a host question no round has asked.** The picture is the part of it that is the engine's whatever the host does, which is why this PR fixes that half and only records the other.

## Gate

`typecheck`, `lint`, `format`, `npm test` (46 files, 998 passed, 1 skipped), `test:count` (floor 999), `coverage` (functions 100%, statements 97.92%).

author: laithalsaadoon
body:
`atif-converter` no longer calls harbor's private methods. The Claude Code and Codex conversions are ours, ported from harbor 0.22.0 under Apache-2.0 and built on the two things harbor actually documents: the ATIF data classes in `harbor.models.trajectories` (RFC 0001) and `harbor.utils.trajectory_validator`.

## Why

harbor documents the data classes and the validator, and nothing that converts a native session log. We were calling `ClaudeCode._convert_events_to_trajectory` and `Codex._convert_events_to_trajectory` (1,029 and 741 lines), through a symlink-staging layer that rebuilt the directory shape those methods expect. The two upstream files took 26 and 18 commits between June and September 2026. That was the drift we were exposed to, and it was why the pin had a minor-version ceiling and a runtime probe with its own exit code.

## What changed

- **Conversion is ours.** `domain/claude_code_conversion.py` and `domain/codex_conversion.py` are parity ports (attributed), reached through `infrastructure/claude_code_converter.py` and `infrastructure/codex_converter.py`, which read the files directly. Staging, temp dirs, the private-API probe, `HarborPrivateApiMissing` and the exit 127 handlers are gone (the code stays in the table so it never renumbers).
- **Parity is measured.** harbor's private converters survive in one place, `tests/harbor_oracle.py`, as the oracle: asserted deterministic, frozen to goldens for both synthetic fixtures (the live oracle must equal the frozen one, so an upstream behavior change becomes a named JSON-path diff rather than a mystery), and diffed against our converters over the newest N local sessions with `ATIF_PARITY_LIMIT` (`0` = all).
- **The boundary is a gate.** An `ast` guard pins production imports to the two public modules; import-linter cannot express a sub-module of an external package. Proven to fail by dropping a `harbor.agents` import into `src/`.
- **Dependencies.** `harbor>=0.22.0,<1`; `litellm>=1.92.0` declared directly, since harbor's converters lazily import it for per-call cost and the port keeps that.
- **Two fidelity "gaps" retired** because their mechanism is gone: Claude Code's `workflow_subagents_missed` (our converter discovers every side file itself) and Codex's `single_rollout_per_directory` (one file in, one trajectory out). Values are not reused. The data-loss gaps stay on purpose: this is a parity port, and fixing one is a decision to diverge from the oracle, recorded in the fidelity policy.

## Measured

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Synthetic fixtures vs live harbor, both agents | 0 divergent paths |
| Frozen goldens vs our converters | 0 divergent paths |
| Live parity, Claude Code, `ATIF_PARITY_LIMIT=0` | 2,437 sessions, 0 divergences |
| Live parity, Codex, `ATIF_PARITY_LIMIT=0` | 78 rollouts, 0 divergences |
| `mise run check` | green, 1,080 tests |
| `mise run docs:gate` | green |

## Preserved harbor behavior worth a later decision (not changed here)

- `agent.extra` `cwds` / `git_branches` / `agent_ids` are built from Python sets, so list order for multi-element values is hash-seed dependent across processes. Pre-existing in every corpus on disk; a follow-up can sort them once we decide to diverge.
- Orphan tool_result steps carry the same metadata dict twice (`extra.metadata` and `extra.tool_result_metadata`).
- Codex `web_search_call` yields an empty `tool_call_id` and an empty observation result.
- Codex bundled-step timestamp is the first normalized event, which is the tool call whose output arrived first rather than the earliest call.

Docs updated: CONTRACT, CONTRIBUTING (the pin section is now the oracle section), AGENTS.md, README, RELEASING, the PR template, and every generated-docs passage that named the private method.

## After a pre-merge review (second commit)

The review found one real defect: litellm loads its pricing table from GitHub at import time, and the frozen goldens carry per-call `cost_usd` priced through it, so a remote price edit or an unreachable GitHub in CI would have failed the never-skipped golden gate with no change here. The converter conftest now pins `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=true` (the table bundled with the locked litellm), the Codex fixture model moved to one that table prices so the cost path stays frozen, and the goldens were re-frozen. Measured: the bundled table had no entry for the previous fixture model and the golden tests failed under it.

Also from the review: explicit utf-8 on the Codex reader to match its sibling, comments recording the set-ordered agent extras as harbor behavior kept on purpose, four doc sentences that still advertised exit 127 or the retired gap as live, and a test that an unreadable side file becomes a `ConversionError` carrying the `OSError`.

## Follow-ups this PR does not take

- Every `convert` process still pays litellm's import (about 2 s measured) and, unless `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP` is set, a GitHub fetch for the pricing table. That is harbor's cost path carried over. Pinning the bundled table in production too would make `convert` offline-safe; it is a pricing-freshness decision, so it is left for its own change.
- Sorting `agent.extra` `cwds` / `git_branches` / `agent_ids` would make multi-valued sessions reproducible across processes, at the price of a deliberate divergence from the oracle.
- The install-weight question in RELEASING stands: the port makes vendoring or a slimmer harbor distribution tractable.

author: chris1984
body:
### Problem Statement
Command Line Assistant (CLA / Red Hat Lightspeed) on content hosts is proxied through the Satellite's `/api/lightspeed` endpoint. When IoP is enabled, `cert_base_url` points at the local IoP gateway, which does not implement Lightspeed, so CLA breaks. foreman_rh_cloud#1247 (SAT-49361) adds a `force_cla_connection` setting that forwards `/api/lightspeed` traffic to `https://cert.cloud.redhat.com` even under IoP, while leaving it on IoP by default.

### Solution
Adds a positive and negative CLI test in `tests/foreman/cli/test_rhcloud_iop.py`, both running against an IoP-enabled Satellite with a registered RHEL host. Each triggers a CLA query from the host and inspects the Satellite's Foreman log for requests forwarded to the cloud, using a before/after count so the checks are order-independent:
- `test_positive_force_cla_connection_to_cloud_in_iop_mode`: with the setting enabled, the CLA request is forwarded to `https://cert.cloud.redhat.com/api/lightspeed`.
- `test_negative_cla_not_forwarded_to_cloud_in_iop_mode`: with the setting disabled (default), the CLA request is not forwarded to the cloud and stays on the local IoP gateway.

### PRT Example
```
trigger: test-robottelo
pytest: tests/foreman/cli/test_rhcloud_iop.py -k "force_cla_connection_to_cloud_in_iop_mode or cla_not_forwarded_to_cloud_in_iop_mode"
```

author: juan518munoz
ranjeetcao
body:
## `dp-atoms-2.0`: the contract half of ADR 0009

Stacked on #12 (the ADR and the plan); the diff here is the contract change alone.

**A text atom** is one block of text on one frame, as written: the verbatim `original`, its `script` read off the letters (ISO 15924), its `language` as a reader tagged it or `und`, its `english` once a renderer has written one, its `box` when the reader said where it sat, and its own harm items with modality `text`. **Audio atoms** carry `language` and `english` from 2.0 on and read as `None` from a 1.0 row. A **`dp-windows-3.0`** row carries `texts` and no transcription in its frames — a 3.0 window whose frames still carry one is refused. The JSON Schema of what a text reader and a renderer return sits beside the frame and audio ones, and the dialect round-trip covers them.

**`dp_contract/language.py`**: the script most of the letters are in (`Zyyy` when there are none — a number or an emoji is never writing in a script; `Zzzz` for a script not listed, which is a finding, not an error), and the rule that a language is never read off characters, a channel or a country.

## The frozen corpus is not touched

- Its version stays `dp-atoms-1.0`; the reader reads both; a directory holds one version, and a writer for another is refused.
- The 1.0 frame and audio schemas are held to the request that wrote the corpus, so `packages/describe`'s request-identity tests are untouched — `language` and `english` are fields a renderer fills, never something the describer is asked for.
- **One function is how the frozen corpus enters the text channel**: `TextAtom.from_frame_atom` turns a 1.0 frame's recorded text into a text record — one block, script from the letters, no language and no English yet. Run over every frozen frame: 38,812 frames → 24,693 text records, every one loading back. By majority script: Latin 24,090, no letters 356, Devanagari 152, Arabic 27, Cyrillic 21, Bengali 13, Han 13, Gurmukhi 13, Tamil 4, Hangul 2, Greek 2. (506 frames *contain* Devanagari letters; a mixed caption tags as the script most of its letters are in. A 2.0 reader records blocks, so mixed captions split.)

## From the review

- **One standard for the same thing**: a window's text is held to the text atom's rules (there is text; the language is a tag), so a blank block is refused in both places.
- **The version is corroborated against the row's shape in both directions**: a 3.0 window states its `texts` even when empty, and a 2.0-tagged row carrying `texts` is refused as mislabelled rather than silently losing them.
- **512 → 506**: the earlier figure came from a sample pool that excluded 25 videos; over the whole frozen corpus 506 frames contain Devanagari letters (518 contain a Devanagari-block codepoint, the 12 extra being the shared danda `।`, which `language.py` rightly does not count).
- Also, since the type was looser than the ones beside it: the text channel and the 2.0 audio fields are gated by the manifest's version (a 1.0 directory carrying either is refused); `script` and `language` have a shape (`Deva`, `hi-Latn`, `und` — not `latin` or `English`); an inverted box and an unrecognised script are quality findings the loader reports, as an audio atom's inverted interval is; a modifier letter such as the Arabic tatweel is not a letter, so padding cannot route a Latin caption to an Arabic reader; a zero-width space is not text; a harm item stating a modality other than its channel's is refused (the frozen corpus carries none); and a value the parser cannot coerce refuses that row by file and line instead of crashing the load.
- Not done here: a lint rule that no code derives a language from a script. The rule holds by review today; making it mechanical is a linter change with its own tests, and is noted for the describers step, where the first reader that could break it is written.

## Proof

```
make check         194 passed, 6 deselected · lint (29 documents) and ruff clean
make test-corpus   6 passed — every frozen row loads under the new reader; the rebuild is byte-identical
```

New tests: scripts read off the letters (15 scripts, ties, marks); text atoms round-trip, stamp `text`, refuse no-text and a bad box, and turn a reader's failure into a `DescribeFailure`; the 1.0→text conversion; audio atoms with and without the 2.0 fields; a 3.0 window beside a 2.0 one; a 2.0 records directory written through the `Writer` and loaded beside the frozen 1.0 one; one version per directory.

Docs: the contract README lists `schema.py` and `language.py` (it did not list `schema.py` before); the corpus README's file table gains the text channel; `data.md` states the version rule; the roadmap moves this step to Done.

author: jdylanmc
body:
## Result

Simplify and repair **Reinforce Skill's single-target improvement operation** before attempting the proposed library-wide queue. Related to #215; no batch runner or unattended loop is introduced.

- Remove the forwarding molecule and two prose-only atoms; one root owns the sequence.
- Commit the complete candidate, including changelog, then validate and independently review **that exact revision**. Range-sensitive commands receive the original-base-to-candidate range rather than silently scanning a previous or last-only commit. Final publication audits cannot precede candidate creation or silently bind a later unreviewed change.
- Preserve a genuine third-round human checkpoint when the shared ledger's clean-result presentation throws. Recovery is local and narrow; other errors propagate, and confirmation is never synthesized.
- Return `already-satisfied` only after sufficient evidence-backed verification against the unchanged baseline. No artificial change, changelog entry, commit or PR. Incomplete verification remains non-success.

## Explicit human decisions

The operator confirmed replacing only the intent's unconditional PR sentence with:

> Open a pull request with the evidence when a change was needed, and stop. When sufficient verification shows the requested improvement is already satisfied, report that evidence and stop without manufacturing a change, changelog entry, commit, or pull request. Incomplete evidence is not an already-satisfied result.

The unchanged prior intent already triggered the plain-intent screen on `AGENTS.md`, “validator,” and “deriver.” The operator separately authorized correcting that false positive **before storing the confirmed amendment**. The original refusal is retained, not relabeled as success.

The corrected gate permits only unchanged diagnostic lines/occurrences from an actual digest-bound prior. Added structural detail, stale/unavailable prior, unconfirmed bytes and mismatched storage remain refused. Exact approved draft SHA-256: `ea0ef1111b3b54c39359fef087432be898fce5dd94177e39716802e6be486342`.

## Scope and self-review safeguards

Target-local changes plus an insertion in existing `CHANGELOG.md`. No tool grants, other intents, doctrine, repository scripts, workflow, Roast, post-mortem or shared creation ledger changed. The original reinforcement-target guard implementation is byte-identical.

The immutable self-audit reproduces the guard from baseline `cbb57d65a72edd120638f98864ccf8cb5e150114`. Its unaccompanied audit refuses only `CHANGELOG.md`; the final audit admits that file through the existing exact-byte changelog companion contract. Both results are retained separately. Neither audit is approval.

## Validation and review

- Final committed-candidate local CI: **3,071 passed, 2 Windows-only skips, zero failures/cancellations**, with cumulative original-base-to-candidate range and observed PR title/body.
- Target and shared-safeguard suites: **310 passed**.
- Regression coverage includes fresh-baseline candidate chronology, correction and stale publication refusal, no-change verification for guidance/report sources, exact intent confirmation, and real clean-round persistence/confirmation.
- Integration tests use real temporary Git repositories and production helpers, with injected review/publication callbacks. They are not live model-review or provider-publication evidence.
- Repository-specific sensitive-identifier configuration is unavailable; high-precision credential/personal-data scan ran. Hosted setup is verified separately by CI.

Independent review: **Complete for the bounded changed-contract scope; no
findings**. Initial contract review covered `6651b8a`; subsequent reviews covered
the one-line fixture identity correction and the cumulative-validation correction.
Current reviewed commit: `77063f9b2f79727784e11da1845e116897ce8368`;
tree: `164edbc424110540118d5a6377148a6a709b3da3`. A whole-diff review
reported no significant issues but omitted coverage metadata; a supplemental
independent pass explicitly traced intent/no-change, checkpoint and publication
contracts and their relevant tests. Static review is not runtime proof or approval.

Initial hosted validation caught email-shaped synthetic fixture data. It now
uses the existing non-address `test-identity` convention. Investigation also
showed that the earlier pre-commit local scan covered the previous committed
range, not the pending candidate; those receipts are not claimed as candidate
scan evidence. The corrected workflow commits first, explicitly binds cumulative
range-sensitive validation, and has real scanner regressions for staged and
multi-commit retained-content misses. Scanner rules, workflow and assertions were
not weakened.

The separate 34-skill queue is a local, unexecuted proposal. Batch budget, open-PR policy and supported runtime cancellation remain decisions for its eventual execution.

body:
# Changes

Aside from tests, docs, and minor changes:

## process capability

- Fix `processCapability` where `nobs` returned the number of observations without omitting missing values. although the calculations and remaining code omits missing values.
-  Fix `processCapability` where supplying one-sided limits and omitting a target made the target equal the available specificatoin limit.

## sigma estimators

- Added the median moving range estimator (MMR) to sd.xbar.one. the current implementation does not finite-sample-bias-corrected like the MSSD. I did not implement the correction because:
  - SAS and Minitab only implement the MMR estimator for window sizes of 2. so the our implementation would have to be "invented" and verified against a Monte Carlo simulation.
  - because I want to verify the future implementation of the Ciminera-Tukey (CT) estimator against the MMR estimator. and I currently do not know if the CT estimator converges to the corrected or uncorrected MMR estimator. or whether the CT estimator itself requires a finite-sample bias correction.
- export `d4()`: the median of the studentized range distribution, intentionally avoiding `qtukey(0.5, vector, Inf)`
- test finite-sample unbiasedness of `sd.xbar.one` estimators. the test does not run on CRAN or test coverage reports because it is depends runs a Monte Carlo simulation, which obfuscates the number of times a line was covered by tests.

## Performance

- replace `apply` calls with `matrixStats` (`rowRanges rowSds rowCounts rowAlls rowAnys`): improves readability and sometimes hottest-path performance.

## ocCurves

- refactor chart-specific configurations from the constructor and plotting function.

author: hellia-be
body:
Addresses feedback that the picker can't tell identical monitors apart: same make/model means the same wlr-randr description, so only the connector name differs and it doesn't say which physical screen is which.

## What
Each picker row is now numbered and shows:
- the **current mode** (`1920x1080@60`),
- the **layout position** (`@0,0`),
- a **directional hint** (`left` / `right`, `top` / `bottom`, or a grid combination like `top-left`) derived from where the outputs sit relative to each other.

Position is the real discriminator — the leftmost monitor is `@0,0`, the one right of it `@1920,0`, etc. Rows are numbered so the planned identify overlay can flash the matching number on each screen.

`parse_wlr_randr` now also reads `Position:` and the active mode. Note: wlr-randr marks the current mode with the word `current` inside a parenthetical (`(preferred, current)`), so the match is on `current`, not the substring `(current)`.

body:
## Summary

Growth CRM's admin and agent appointment cards never had manual "Resend Appointment Notification" / "Send Appointment Reminder" buttons — Lead Gen CRM already has both (and keeps them, unchanged, in this PR). This adds the same two actions to Growth CRM, reusing only existing send paths.

### What was added
- **`sendManualWinsalotAppointmentEmail`** (`winsalot-consultation-reminders.ts`) — reuses the same Resend client/sender and the same `buildWinsalotConfirmationEmail` / `buildWinsalotReminderEmail` templates the automatic reminder job and immediate booking confirmation already use. Records the send in `crm_lead_emails` (the same delivery-tracking table + Resend webhook pipeline the automatic job already writes to via `recordCrmLeadEmail`, now generalized to accept an explicit `email_type` instead of always hardcoding `"appointment_reminder"`).
- **Migration `0155`** — widens `crm_lead_emails`' `email_type` check constraint to allow a new `"appointment_confirmation"` value, so a resent confirmation is labeled accurately instead of reusing the unrelated reminder type. Purely additive.
- **`sendManualWinsalotAppointmentSms`** — reuses `claimAndSendAppointmentSms` and the same SMS templates, gated on the existing automatic-SMS-reminders toggle, under a fresh always-unique occurrence key per click so a manual send is never deduped against the automatic job's own claim and never affects the 24h/1h automatic-reminder status badges.
- **`describeManualSmsOutcome`** moved from `leadgen-appointment-reminders.ts` into the shared `appointment-sms.ts` — it was always CRM-agnostic formatting; both CRMs' manual-send actions now import the one implementation. Re-exported from the Lead Gen file so existing callers/tests are unaffected.
- **`WinsalotAppointmentsListClient.tsx`** — two new buttons in the card's Actions row (Edit / Reschedule / Cancel / Delete / **Resend Appointment Notification** / **Send Appointment Reminder**), never mixed into the Email/SMS 24h/1h reminder-status badges shown above. Reuses Lead Gen's existing `AppointmentEmailConfirmModal` (generic component, no Lead-Gen-specific logic) for the confirm-before-sending step, disable-while-sending, and a combined email+SMS success/failure message (e.g. "Confirmation resent. SMS sent."). Every existing action — Edit, Reschedule, Cancel, Delete, Weekly Incentive review — is untouched.
- Wired into both `admin/crm/appointments` and `agent/appointments` (new `resendAppointmentNotificationAction` / `sendAppointmentReminderAction` in both `actions.ts` files, agent-side behind the existing `assertOwnAppointment` ownership check).

### Requirements checklist
1. Resend manually resends the original confirmation → yes, `buildWinsalotConfirmationEmail`.
2. Reminder manually sends a reminder → yes, `buildWinsalotReminderEmail`.
3. Reuses existing email/SMS sending functions, no duplicate endpoints/templates/reminder systems → yes — same Resend client, same templates, same `claimAndSendAppointmentSms`, same `crm_lead_emails`/`winsalot_appointment_sms_reminders` tables (only an additive enum-widening migration, matching the exact pattern already used for `'appointment_reminder'`).
4. SMS sent when enabled + valid phone → yes, gated on the automatic-SMS toggle and appointment's own phone/consent.
5. Delivery records updated after sending → yes, `crm_lead_emails` insert (email) + `winsalot_appointment_sms_reminders` insert via `claimAndSendAppointmentSms` (SMS).
6. Clear success/failure message → yes, surfaced through the confirm modal.
7. Button disabled while processing → yes (the confirm modal's own `submitting` state, same mechanism Lead Gen's buttons already use).
8. Kept inside the Actions area, not mixed into the reminder-status badges → yes.
9. No existing controls removed → confirmed (Manage/Edit, Reschedule, Cancel, Delete, Weekly Incentive review, and the 24h/1h automatic reminder badges are all untouched).
10. Fits the compact layout without overflow → yes, same `flex flex-wrap` pattern already used throughout.

## Files changed
- `supabase/migrations/0155_crm_lead_emails_appointment_confirmation.sql` (new)
- `src/lib/winsalot-consultation-reminders.ts` (new manual email/SMS functions + generalized `recordCrmLeadEmail`)
- `src/lib/appointment-sms.ts` (relocated `describeManualSmsOutcome`)
- `src/lib/leadgen-appointment-reminders.ts` (re-exports the relocated helper)
- `src/components/WinsalotAppointmentsListClient.tsx` (new buttons + modal + message)
- `src/app/admin/(dashboard)/crm/appointments/{actions.ts,AdminAppointmentsClient.tsx}`
- `src/app/agent/(dashboard)/appointments/{actions.ts,AgentAppointmentsClient.tsx}`
- `src/lib/__tests__/winsalot-manual-appointment-send.test.ts` (new)

## Database migration
Yes — `0155_crm_lead_emails_appointment_confirmation.sql`. Additive only (widens an existing check constraint), no data migration needed.

## Test results — "test appointment" run
New tests (`winsalot-manual-appointment-send.test.ts`) exercise a mock test appointment (`Acme Test Co.`, Phone Call type, valid phone + SMS consent) through both actions end to end:

1. **Resend Appointment Notification (email)** — sends via the mocked Resend client to the appointment's email, subject contains "Winsalot Corp", recorded in `crm_lead_emails` with `email_type: "appointment_confirmation"`, and a `crm_activities` note ("...confirmation resent... by Admin User") — **PASS**
2. **Send Appointment Reminder (email)** — recorded as `email_type: "appointment_reminder"`, activity note ("...reminder sent... by Agent User") — **PASS**
3. **Resend Appointment Notification (SMS)** — sent under a fresh `manual_resend_confirmation:<timestamp>` occurrence key, message correctly reads "...phone call appointment... is confirmed for..." — **PASS**
4. **Send Appointment Reminder (SMS)** — sent under `manual_reminder:<timestamp>`, message reads "...phone call appointment... is in..." — **PASS**
5. **SMS disabled** — when the automatic-SMS toggle is off, no SMS is attempted (`outcome: "disabled"`, `claimAndSendAppointmentSms` never called) — **PASS**
6. **Resend (email) failure path** — a mocked Resend rejection surfaces as `{ error: "Resend rejected the request." }` with nothing written to `crm_lead_emails` — **PASS**

Full suite: `npx vitest run` — **515/515 passing**. `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean (one pre-existing, unrelated `city-photos/vancouver.png` error present before this branch). `npx eslint` on every changed/added file — clean. `npm run build` — production build succeeds.

**Not independently browser-tested** (no live Supabase credentials in this sandbox, same constraint as the prior PR) — verification is the automated suite above plus code review.

Confirmed: every manual send goes through the pre-existing `claimAndSendAppointmentSms` / Resend-client send path and the pre-existing `crm_lead_emails` / `winsalot_appointment_sms_reminders` tables. No new table, cron route, or claim mechanism. The only new persistent state is the widened `email_type` enum value.

## Problem
1. The TUI used `keyring` with default features, which on Linux resolves to the in-memory mock store (`pub use mock as default` in keyring 3.6.3), and swallowed every store error with `.ok()`. Saved API keys vanished on restart with no diagnostic.
2. `medusa-cli/build.rs` only emitted `rerun-if-changed` for `.git/HEAD`, whose content never changes when the branch advances, so rebuilds kept embedding a stale `MEDUSA_BUILD_COMMIT`.

## Changes
- `medusa-tui`: enable `sync-secret-service` + `crypto-rust` keyring features so keys persist in the OS keychain (gnome-keyring); `saved_credential` now returns `Result` and open/read failures surface as startup errors instead of silent missing-credential.
- `medusa-cli/build.rs`: watch the resolved git-dir `HEAD`, `packed-refs`, and current branch ref so the revision re-resolves on every advance.
- `medusa-update/install.rs`: one-line `needless_return` fix required by the workspace clippy gate (pre-existing from 2ee585ed).
- `Cargo.lock`: secret-service transitive deps (additions only).

## Live verification (this machine, Linux + gnome-keyring)
- Key round-trips through the OS store across processes (fresh-process probe with identical keyring features: FOUND).
- Real MiniMax request through Medusa with the keychain-stored key: replied `minimax-ok`.
- Rebuild embeds the true commit: 2ee585ed -> empty commit 87c71830 picked up in 23s with only medusa-cli recompiling.
- Updater across two commits: binary at tip reports up to date; binary at divergent SHA detects the difference.
- medusa-tui lib 160/160, medusa-update lib 43/43, all integration suites pass; `cargo fmt --check` clean; clippy `-D warnings` clean on touched crates.

## Task

Validate protected producer authority consistently in controller snapshots and structured review intake.

## Owned files

- `.github/scripts/merge-policy-intake.mjs`
- `.github/scripts/merge-policy-github.mjs`
- `selftest/test_merge_policy_intake.mjs`
- `selftest/test_merge_policy_github.mjs`

## Validation

```text
node --test selftest/test_merge_policy_intake.mjs selftest/test_merge_policy_github.mjs
60 tests passed

node --test selftest/test_merge_policy_*.mjs
342 tests passed

Prettier and git diff --check passed.
```

The final source commit is `abc5d83e3057c1cf45539afcc6c2a19d2ec0c72d`, based on merged PR198 main `2672936a5dc485e9cf50d5182f5a90d3bec6d2e0`. The change validates every configured producer's shape, identity, lane and publisher authority before ordinary evaluation or intake. It returns detached frozen authority, preserves exact persisted bytes for the digest, permits an explicit empty suspension configuration, and keeps selected PR author separation in intake. Proxy inputs are rejected before reflection, with top-level, nested and revoked-proxy regressions.

## Scope and limits

This is a pure source validation improvement. It does not add producer administration, durable intake holds, live GitHub execution authentication, workflow changes, credential changes or staging activation. Existing configuration deletion/history and legacy no-producer behavior remain covered.

## HUMAN_READABLE_SUMMARY

The controller now refuses malformed, ambiguous or unauthorized protected review-producer configuration before using it as merge-policy authority. This prevents a clean historical review from being treated as valid under a malformed or revoked producer setup, while preserving exact-byte authority digests and explicit suspension behavior.

## Auto-merge rationale

The source change is limited to the policy validator/controller and its tests. It requires the repository's normal sensitive-path review and check gates; no bypass or self-approval is appropriate.

body:
## Resumen
Nueva funcionalidad en Registro de devoluciones y garantias (Mostrador), para recibir una garantia que se capturo via Garantia Express (sucursal) y cuyo cliente trae la pieza fisica al mostrador:

- Boton "Recibir garantia" junto a "+ Nuevo registro".
- Modal de busqueda por folio o nota de credito. Solo encuentra solicitudes con resultado Procede, que no se hayan originado en Mostrador y que no hayan sido recibidas previamente (evita recepciones duplicadas).
- Al encontrarla, muestra el detalle (cliente, producto, nota de credito, tipo de aplicacion) y una seccion de codigo/cantidad esperada/cantidad recibida igual en comportamiento a "Arribo de devoluciones": escaneo simulado o captura manual.
- "Marcar como recibida" se habilita solo cuando la cantidad recibida es completa, y pide confirmacion mediante el modal homologado (askQuestion/QuestionModalHost).
- Si la garantia aplico como Devolucion de efectivo, al confirmar aparece el mensaje solicitado y un flujo simple de entrega: Escanear QR (simulado) -> Confirmar entrega de efectivo, tambien con confirmacion homologada.
- La garantia recibida aparece en Solicitudes de garantia de Mostrador como pendiente de "Entregar a almacen" (reutiliza el boton y flujo ya existentes).

## Decisiones de diseno confirmadas con el usuario
- Elegibilidad: solo garantias Procede, no originadas en Mostrador, no recibidas previamente.
- Modelo de datos: se agrego un campo nuevo recibidaEnMostrador en Caso (en vez de reutilizar origenMostrador, que otras pantallas como la tabla de Central usan para mostrar el origen real de la solicitud).
- Flujo de efectivo: version simple (mensaje + escaneo simulado + confirmacion), sin paso adicional de captura de identidad.

## Plan de pruebas
- npm run build exitoso
- Flujo completo con una garantia Procede + Devolucion de efectivo (NC-1841): busqueda, recepcion, confirmacion, QR simulado, confirmacion de entrega de efectivo, aparece pendiente de entregar a almacen.
- Flujo completo con una garantia Procede sin devolucion de efectivo (NC-1842): busqueda, recepcion, confirmacion, cierra directo sin paso de QR.
- Verificacion de que buscar una garantia ya recibida (NC-1841 de nuevo) muestra el mensaje de error esperado.

author: dennisonbertram
body:
Brings the handoff up to date with what actually happened, including a live run
driven over iMessage on `c0d0de2`.

## The run

| Turn | Tools | What it shows |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 15 | `send_message` | Forcing engaged on a real backlog. Cohort `turn_4`, settled in an earlier session, still owed a summary, so the turn was steered into a report instead of acting on the message that had just arrived. |
| 16 | `browser-agent`, `send_message` | The very next turn was free. It delegated real work and acknowledged in 17 characters. |
| 18 | `send_message` | An ordinary message, owing nothing, delivered with nothing appended. |

Durable record for turn 15: one row in `completion_report_attempts` — cohort
`turn_4`, revision 0, part `text`, state **accepted**.

## What it establishes

Forcing activates from a real obligation rather than a flag. A report is composed
from the records, claimed durably, dispatched, and accepted by the provider.

And the behaviour that made the first activation hostile is gone. One message
discharged the whole backlog, so turn 16 was immediately free to do real work.
Under the previous code turn 16 would have been forced to report again, and turn
18 after it, until the backlog drained.

## What it does not establish

What the turn 15 message **said**. Nothing in the system can show that: the digest
is over the rendered payload rather than the text, the delivery receipts are
metadata only by design, and the runtime log carries tool names and a response
length but never content.

So the honest statement is that the mechanism fired, not that the report was true.
That is exactly the distinction the first activation got wrong when a green log
was read as a working feature, and this PR also corrects a sentence in the doc
that the run had already overtaken — it still claimed no report had reached a
phone.

Still unwatched: turn 16's browser task had not settled at the time of writing, so
the specific sequence of *worker settles, next turn carries its records* has not
been observed end to end. Turn 15 proves the same path with an older cohort.
