author: bjmeetsfo
body:
Five more whose help was the label plus "Defaults to N".

| setting | what it bounds |
|---|---|
| `..._APPEND_BATCH_RECORDS` | chunk records accumulated before one `append_many` — smaller store writes against more records held before the first is durable |
| `..._ASYNC_DEFAULT_TEXT_CHARS` | characters of inline text before an import goes to the background |
| `..._ASYNC_DEFAULT_PATH_COUNT` | files in a directory before the same |
| `..._EVENT_TEXT_CHARS` | how much of a document its `context_event` keeps |
| `..._IMPORT_WORKERS` | threads draining the resource import queue |

Three thresholds decide the async question between them, and the first one reached names itself as
the recorded reason; an explicit `wait` argument skips all three. The import queue holds
`..._IMPORT_QUEUE_MAX` (64) and **raises rather than waiting** when it is full, so the worker count
and that bound together set how much can be in flight before a caller is refused.

`..._EVENT_TEXT_CHARS` carries the measurement its module records: a resource document used to be
stored three times — in the chunks, in the event, and inside the session buffer envelope — and on
a 66.2 KB file the event alone was 1.05x the source. `0` stores it whole; message records are not
bounded by this.

### One note on wording

The two async thresholds name `MATRIXARK_RESOURCE_ASYNC_DEFAULT_BYTES` rather than using the word
for it. `test_matrixark_byte_settings_read_in_units` decides a setting holds a byte count from that
word appearing in its help — deliberately, because a name-suffix rule had already missed two real
byte settings. Neither of these holds bytes (one counts files, one counts characters), so the first
draft made the guard claim them, and it was right to.

Help text only, no behaviour change. 873 tests across the 68 suites that read the settings module
pass.

author: nickdavies1991
body:
**Found on the first real install.** Willie Mae's have been taking orders for months. The moment a tablet signed in, the screen came up chiming about *all of them*, and the only way to silence it was to tap Accept on every order in turn.

Nothing was broken. `unaccepted()` asks "has somebody here accepted this order" — and until that tablet existed, nobody had accepted anything, because there was nothing to accept it on. Every historical order answered honestly, and the chime counted all of them.

**Every future install would hit this**, at every restaurant with any history.

## The fix

The chime now also asks whether the order is still worth acting on: **six hours**. Past that nobody is going to cook it, and the alert is demanding an action that no longer exists.

Two things it deliberately does *not* do:

- **It governs the chime, not the list.** An old unaccepted order stays on screen where staff can see and open it. It just stops demanding to be dealt with this second.
- **A missing or unparseable `received_at` still chimes.** A field we cannot read must never be the reason a real order goes unannounced. Noise is recoverable; silence costs the restaurant the order.

## Why six hours

The window has to be wider than a service. A one-hour window would silence a genuine order on a busy night — which is the failure that actually costs money, and the opposite of the one being fixed here. Six is longer than any service and far longer than any honest accept window.

## Testing

`tsc=0`, `tests=0`, `build=0`. Kiosk suite 28 → 32 assertions, including that age alone never *widens* what chimes — a cancelled or accepted order stays silent regardless of how recent it is.

## Repo-scope note

pfd-order-monitor, not prs-crm, under Nick's explicit set-aside of the "Repo scope is explicit" rule in prs-crm/CLAUDE.md:

> I am explicitly setting aside the 'Repo scope is explicit' rule in CLAUDE.md for this project. You have read and write access to both prs-crm and pfd-order-monitor, both of which are my own clones under C:\Users\richa\dev. Everything else still applies — branch, PR, green CI, merge; never push to main, never deploy production, and don't create any repository.

body:
Ticket: CHAOS-5601

## SUMMARY

Syncs ask-dev's pinned acr contracts from `85f037db` to `57f25d5f` — acr PR #510's squash, now on acr
main. `refusal_basis`'s closed vocabulary gains a 4th value,
`continuation_context_unverifiable`.

### The invariants

1. **`refusal_basis` is a CLOSED vocabulary, and its absence means "not refused".** The new member
   says the server refused a window-only continuation whose prior semantic context it could not
   verify. That is not a frame refusal, and such a document carries its own fixed limitation
   sentence. Adding a member widens what validates and changes nothing else: absence of the key is
   still legal, and a value outside the vocabulary is still rejected.

2. **A member is only synced if it is synced everywhere the field is consumed.** This field is
   carried at the same place in BOTH vendored schemas — `context_fabric_common.v1` and
   `context_fabric_investigation_result.v1` — so a bump that updated one and not the other would
   accept a document through one validator and reject it through the other. Both move here, and a
   test asserts the member is present in both rather than in the result alone.

Additive only in both: no other field, `$def`, or required-list change; only the field's description
gains the sentence explaining the new member. `context_fabric_investigation_result.v2`, both `mcp_*`
response schemas, and `contracts/auth/v1/endpoint-profiles.acr.json` also moved between the pins, but
none of the four is part of this repo's vendored surface — the same exclusion every bump in
`scripts/sync-acr-contracts.mjs`'s history records. The pinned request schema, `error.v1`, and all
five examples are byte-identical to the prior pin; acr publishes no new example for this shape.

## TEST-EVIDENCE

### The pin is exactly acr 57f25d5f, and that sha is on acr main

```
$ git -C <acr worktree> rev-parse HEAD
57f25d5f85b967452fdbe8b2e4f96cfa706b367a
$ git -C <acr> merge-base --is-ancestor 57f25d5f origin/main && echo ON_MAIN
ON_MAIN
$ node scripts/sync-acr-contracts.mjs check --source <acr worktree>
ACR contracts are current.        # rc 0
```

`check --source` is the exact-digest guard: it fails on a hand-edited vendored copy, a hand-edited
generated type, or a stale type after a pin bump. It is also what proves this branch's rebase left no
conflict marker and no hand-resolved artefact behind (see RISK-NOTES).

### What moved between the pins, enumerated

```
$ git diff 85f037db 57f25d5f -- contracts/
20  20  contracts/auth/v1/endpoint-profiles.acr.json                    # NOT vendored here
 3   2  contracts/jsonschema/v1/context_fabric_answer_projection.v1.…   # NOT vendored here
 3   2  contracts/jsonschema/v1/context_fabric_common.v1.schema.json    # VENDORED
 3   2  contracts/jsonschema/v1/context_fabric_investigation_result.v1… # VENDORED
 3   2  contracts/jsonschema/v1/context_fabric_investigation_result.v2… # NOT vendored here
 9   6  contracts/jsonschema/v1/mcp_investigate_question_response.v1.…  # NOT vendored here
 6   4  contracts/jsonschema/v1/mcp_investigation_result_response.v1.…  # NOT vendored here

$ git diff 85f037db 57f25d5f -- contracts/examples/      # empty
```

4 commits span the pins, all on acr main (#507, #509, a parallel-group test, and #510 itself). In each
vendored schema the diff is exactly the new enum member plus the description sentence.

### RED at origin/main, GREEN here, proven twice

**(1) In-suite executed repro** (`src/lib/acr/validate.test.ts`): reconstructs the PRIOR pin's own
schema by removing the new member from a copy of the pinned result schema — asserting first that the
member IS there, so the repro cannot strip the wrong thing — compiles it with a fresh `Ajv2020`, and
proves the new value is REJECTED there while the same stand-in still accepts a live one.

**(2) Independent proof outside vitest and outside `validate.ts`**, compiling the schema GIT BLOBS with
the same ajv configuration production uses:

```
== ARM 1: refusal_basis = "continuation_context_unverifiable" ==
  pre-bump  (ask-dev main ddc8876a): valid=false errors=["/refusal_basis must be equal to one of the allowed values"]
  post-bump (this branch)          : valid=true
== ARM 2 (faithfulness control): an already-live refusal basis ==
  pre-bump : valid=true      post-bump: valid=true
== ARM 3 (the vocabulary stays closed): a value outside the vocabulary ==
  pre-bump : valid=false     post-bump: valid=false
== ARM 4 (nothing else moved): the canonical example, unchanged ==
  pre-bump : valid=true      post-bump: valid=true
EXPECTED pattern: HELD
```

**In-suite RED**: with both vendored schemas reverted to their `ddc8876a` versions, 3 of the 78 cases
in `validate.test.ts` fail; all 78 pass with them.

### The live failure this closes

On the pre-bump pin, a real leg returned HTTP 502 `acr_contract_violation` on `/refusal_basis` and
`/completeness/refusal_basis` for a response carrying the new value
(`req_a3051b329f4a8184c7f177d4c2fb6ed6`). acr main now serves that value, so the consumer pin is
load-bearing rather than speculative.

### Cells

| assertion | result |
|---|---|
| the already-live vocabulary still validates (`member_kind_unservable`, `frame_invariant_violated`, `unspecified`) | pass |
| `continuation_context_unverifiable` validates at this pin | pass |
| the vocabulary stays CLOSED against an unknown value | pass |
| absence of the key is still legal — "not refused" is still expressible | pass |
| the member is present in BOTH consumed schemas, not the result alone | pass |
| executed repro: the prior pin's own schema rejects it, and still accepts a live value | pass |

### Gates, through `ci/run_checks.sh <phase>` (the entry point CI uses)

```
format     rc=0   (prettier --check .)
contracts  rc=0   (acr:contracts:check — manifest digests + regeneration)
corpus     rc=0   PASS: 36 corpus rows validated; baseline sha256 pin matched
lint       rc=0   (eslint .)
typecheck  rc=0   (tsc --noEmit)
unit       rc=0   Test Files 59 passed (59) | Tests 885 passed (885)
ci/run_checks_fail_fast.test.sh -> PASSED
```

### Hosted CI and PR-ref CodeQL at this tip

CI is the clean-checkout run of the same phases, so it is also the fresh-setup evidence
(`pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` from nothing) and covers the two phases not run locally, `Build`
(`next build`) and `E2E smoke` (Playwright).

```
13 check-runs, pending 0, non-success 0 — 12 success, 1 matrix-skipped ("Unit tests")
PR-ref CodeQL: e595f054375d results_count=0 x3 (javascript-typescript, python, actions)
```

No job was re-run by hand.

## RISK-NOTES

- **This branch was rebased onto the answer-iff-supported sync, not merged around it.** That sync
  landed first as `ddc8876a` and touches the same seven files this PR does — `SOURCE_COMMIT`, the
  three generated types, the manifest, and both vendored schemas. Every one conflicted. The
  resolution took MAIN's version of each artefact and re-applied this PR's own content on top, then
  regenerated from the acr checkout; `check --source` rc 0 plus the full suite is what proves no
  conflict marker, stale type, or hand-resolved copy survived. Nothing of the earlier sync's work is
  reverted here.
- **The pin moved once, from a branch tip to the merged squash.** The earlier revision of this PR
  pinned `86d84fa9`, acr #510's unmerged branch tip. #510 has merged; this PR now pins its squash
  `57f25d5f`, which is an ancestor of acr main.
- **A third sync is queued behind this one.** ask-dev PR #62 (`sync/5611-fact-read-origin-state`)
  stays in draft until this lands, then rebases and re-pins to acr #513's squash. All three PRs edit
  `SOURCE_COMMIT`, `src/contracts/manifest.json` and the generated headers, so they cannot land in
  parallel.
- **Widening only.** Every document the prior pin accepted still validates; the bump adds one member
  to one closed vocabulary and changes no other rule. No rendering change is needed: nothing in this
  repo keys behaviour off `refusal_basis`, w

author: zmpersonal
body:
Unblocks post #2. Merging this publishes the article live.

## Scope: four paths, not five

Confirmed against the base:

```
$ git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD
site/public/images/og/is-austins-home-improvement-boom-cooling-off.png
site/scripts/generate-og-cards.mjs
site/src/data/analysis/is-austins-home-improvement-boom-cooling-off.md
site/src/data/og-cards/is-austins-home-improvement-boom-cooling-off.json
```

4 files, +142/-4. The proposal listed five because it assumed article 1's card would re-render. It does not — see below — so it never enters the diff. Nothing under `autoposter/`, nothing in `.github/`, no dependency, no layout or config change.

## The template fix is general, and here is the evidence

The generator **refused to render** article 2:

```
[x] is-austins-home-improvement-boom-cooling-off: content overflows the 1200x630 card
```

Two font sizes tuned against one article are not a template. `13.88¢/kWh` fits at 150px; `224 solar permits` does not, and wraps to two lines, which stops it reading as a single figure. The question is longer too.

Both now scale, in the order that protects the hierarchy: the hero gets the room it needs first (floor 84px, below which it is no longer a hero), then the question steps down through 52/48/44/40/36/32.

The log now reports what it chose, so the fit is observable rather than silent:

```
[ok] are-texas-electricity-prices-still-going-up.png   hero 150px / question 52px
[ok] is-austins-home-improvement-boom-cooling-off.png  hero 139px / question 40px
```

Article 1 is untouched at its original sizes; article 2 fits because it scaled. That is what makes this a template rather than a patch: the next article has a different question and a different figure, and without this the generator refuses roughly whenever the hero is longer than a price.

**The overflow guard is unchanged.** It is what caught this, and it still fails anything the fit pass cannot resolve.

## The approved card is byte-identical, and that was checked

An earlier version of this change widened the question's `max-width` from 17ch to 20ch. That re-broke article 1's headline from "Are Texas electricity / prices still going up?" to "Are Texas electricity prices / still going up?" — a visible change to a card you had already approved and that is already live. Reverted, and verified rather than assumed:

```
$ cmp <(git show origin/main:.../are-texas-electricity-prices-still-going-up.png) \
      site/public/images/og/are-texas-electricity-prices-still-going-up.png
IDENTICAL
```

A template fix that silently restyles an approved card is drift, not a fix.

## No embed on this article, deliberately

The site's permit dataset is `municipal-permits/austin` and its observations are individual permit records whose `value` is an object, not monthly counts. The embed template renders a two-column numeric table, so pointing it there would render an empty receipts table under a sourced article — the first article's exact failure. The reason is written into the frontmatter so the next person does not rediscover it.

## 🟡 One finding that is NOT in this PR and needs your call

The three-trade table in the article body renders **unstyled**. Tailwind Preflight resets `table`, and the site's table styling is scoped to `table.data-table`, which markdown does not emit. I looked at the rendered page rather than inferring it from the CSS: the figures are legible but sit with no rules, no padding and no header treatment, so the article's receipts do not read as the site's data table.

Fixing it is a fifth path, `site/src/styles/global.css`, which is outside what was approved, so it is deliberately not here:

```diff
+/* Markdown tables inside an analysis article. Preflight resets `table`, and the
+   site's own table styling is scoped to `table.data-table`, which markdown cannot
+   emit — so an article's figures render as unruled text without this. */
+.analysis table { width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; font-size: 0.92rem; margin: 12px 0 20px; }
+.analysis th, .analysis td { text-align: left; padding: 9px 10px; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--line); }
+.analysis td { font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }
+.analysis th { background: var(--paper-alt); font-size: 0.78rem; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.03em; color: var(--ink-soft); }
```

Three options: approve it as a fifth path here, take it as its own PR, or I drop the table from the article body and present the three trades as prose, which needs no site change at all. **Recommend approving it** — every future article will want a table, and this is the same class as the bullet-marker fix.

## Render-side verified, from the built HTML

- the page exists and emits its own card, with the full agency name in `og:image:alt` while the face carries `City of Austin`
- all three trade figures appear in served HTML
- article 1's page is unchanged
- `astro check`: 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 hints

A barra dizia **"Progresso"** e a pagina que ela abre diz **"Evolucao."** — o patch anterior renomeou so a metade da barra e deixou as duas metades discordando. O nome escolhido e **"Evolucao"**, que ja era o titulo da pagina.

## A escala de fonte da barra fica

Ela entrou no PR #79 porque cinco rotulos de 15px nao cabiam numa tela estreita, e **trocar a palavra nao resolve isso**. Medido em 360px, a folga entre "Nutricao" e o vizinho:

| rotulo | 15px fixos | com a escala |
|---|---|---|
| "Progresso" | 4px | 16px |
| "Evolucao" | **7px** | **16px** |

Em 375 / 390 / 412px, 15px fixos com "Evolucao" dao 10 / 13 / 18px. A escala leva a 16 / 17 / 18px — folga uniforme em toda a faixa. O comentario no CSS foi corrigido para contar essa medicao, e nao a antiga.

## A chave da aba continua "Progresso"

Ela e o identificador interno e o `data-testid` (`nav-progresso`). Renomear identificador junto com rotulo so criaria um segundo lugar para errar.

author: sidick
body:
Fixes #43. Implements the design decided there (including the follow-up comment on per-process `RAM:` uniqueness).

## The change

By default, `SYS:`, `C:`, `S:`, `LIBS:`, `DEVS:`, `ENVARC:`, `RAM:`, `T:`, and `ENV:` all now resolve out of the box — zero `-V`/`-a` needed. This is the fourth, lowest-precedence layer under #16's chain:

```
CLI > ./.volamos (cwd) > <program-dir>/.volamos > ~/.volamos > built-in defaults
```

Reproduces the exact bug report this issue came from:

```
$ volamos dos_examine_gcc sys:
Examine: SYS
<DIR> C
<DIR> Devs
<DIR> Libs
<DIR> Prefs
<DIR> S
ok
```

`--no-defaults`/`DEFAULTS=false` restores the original "nothing configured means no filesystem at all" behavior (reproducing the original `can't Lock(): 'sys:'` verbatim). `--volumes-dir`/`VOLUMES_DIR=` overrides where the persistent `SYS:` lives (default `~/.volamos.d/volumes`).

Deliberately **not** vamos's broader auto-assign machinery, which makes *any* name resolve somewhere — only these specific real-AmigaOS names are covered, so a typo'd volume name still fails loudly with an `IoErr()`.

## Design highlights

- **Lazy, not eager.** `config::built_in_defaults` does zero I/O — it only names paths. The actual directory creation happens inside `Vfs::lookup_volume`, on first real use. `volamos hello` (a program that touches no filesystem at all) leaves `~/.volamos.d` completely untouched — verified both by a unit test and by running the real release binary against a fake `$HOME`. This needed splitting `lookup_volume` into a pure `lookup_volume_path` (used by `Vfs::new`/`set_cwd`'s cwd-soundness validation, which must not eagerly create a directory just because the *default* cwd happens to be `SYS:`) and the side-effecting `lookup_volume` (used by real resolution).
- **Companion subdirectories.** A freshly-created, empty `SYS:` has none of the subdirectories its own standard assigns expect (`C:` → `SYS:C`). `LazyVolume` bundles a root with companions created alongside it in one shot, so `Lock("C:")` against a brand-new `SYS:` doesn't fail.
- **Override-shadowing is free.** Lazy-creation matches by *exact host path*, not name — so a user's own `-V SYS:~/amiga/wb31` is what `lookup_volume` actually returns; the default entry is never even consulted, so it's neither auto-created into nor (for `RAM:`) wrongly treated as ephemeral. This is also what lets `-V SYS:~/amiga/wb31` bring that volume's own real `C:`/`Libs:`/etc. along automatically, since they're assigns onto whichever `SYS:` is actually configured.
- **Ephemeral `RAM:` cleanup is deliberately not a `Drop` impl.** A nested `System()`/`Execute()` run builds its own `Vfs` from a *cloned* `VfsConfig` naming the same `RAM:` path — correct, since nested guests should share `RAM:` (real single-machine semantics) — so an early `Drop` when that nested `Vfs` goes out of scope would delete the directory out from under the still-running parent. Cleanup is `main.rs`'s own explicit job, once, right after the top-level `run()` returns and before `std::process::exit` (which skips pending destructors entirely, so a scope-guard wouldn't fire in time).
- **`RAM:` uniqueness**: pid + a nanosecond timestamp, no new dependency — per the issue's own follow-up comment, matching vamos's `tempfile.mkdtemp`-based reasoning (a shared/fixed `RAM:` would let one instance's exit cleanup delete a sibling's live files).

## Tests

- 4 new `vfs.rs` unit tests: root creation on first resolve, companions created alongside it, idempotency, and the override-shadowing property.
- 1 full-trap-dispatch end-to-end test in `doslock.rs`: a hand-assembled M68K program does a real `Lock`+`Examine` against a lazy default volume through actual CPU dispatch.
- 5 `config.rs` unit tests verifying `built_in_defaults`'s exact structure (SYS:'s assigns/companions, RAM:'s assigns/companions/ephemeral marking, the without-a-volumes-dir fallback, RAM: uniqueness across calls).
- 2 CLI-parsing tests for the new flags.
- 2 real-binary `hello_cli.rs` tests using a fake `$HOME`: the zero-touch property, and `--no-defaults` opting out cleanly.
- Manually reproduced the original bug report end-to-end against a real built release binary (shown above), and confirmed `--no-defaults` reproduces the original error verbatim.

Full suite: all passing, clippy/fmt clean.

author: abuzarmahmood
body:
## Summary
- Adds `RandomWalkChangepointParticipation1D`, extending `RandomWalkChangepointMeanVar1D` with a per-state, changepoint-blended participation probability that softly mixes between an engaged and a disengaged (zero-mean, high-variance) innovation distribution — allowing non-participation to be identified as (part of) a state, as requested in #208.
- Missing/sparse observations (`NaN`) are handled by fitting a full-length latent random-walk path and only evaluating the likelihood at observed timepoints, so no explicit missing-data likelihood is needed and the model stays fully ADVI-compatible (no discrete latents).
- Adds `gen_random_walk_participation_test_array` synthetic-data generator, fast init tests, and a slow recovery test verifying the disengaged state gets a distinctly lower participation probability than engaged states.
- Adds a demo notebook (`pytau/how_to/model_notebooks/RandomWalkChangepointParticipation1D.ipynb`) and documentation in `docs/models.md`, including a note on a discovered ADVI-stability caveat with imbalanced random segment sizes.

Closes #208.

## Test plan
- [x] `./venv/bin/pytest tests/test_changepoint_model.py -k participation -m "not slow"` — fast tests pass
- [x] `./venv/bin/pytest tests/test_changepoint_model.py -k participation -m slow` — recovery test passes deterministically (fixed seed)
- [x] `./venv/bin/pytest tests/ -m "not slow"` — 58 passed, no regressions
- [x] `./venv/bin/pytest tests/test_changepoint_model.py -m slow` — all pass except one pre-existing, unrelated flaky test from #206 (`test_random_walk_changepoint_elbo_state_selection`, does not seed ADVI) that this PR does not touch
- [x] Notebook built and executed end-to-end via the project venv; inspected output plots confirming correct recovery of changepoints and participation probability

Finishes the 0.2.0 work on this branch by fixing what a review of it turned up.

## Behaviour

- **Tab pinning is no longer sticky by accident.** A tab stays selected across tasks only when the agent itself switched or opened one. Previously any task pinned whatever tab was active, so the next question silently answered about the previous page.
- **The output cap is a setting, and truncation is reported.** `maxOutputTokens` replaces a hardcoded `4096`; a reply that hits the cap says so, because the model cannot resume a truncated answer.
- **Escape is scoped.** It no longer cancels a running task while a dropdown or text field has focus — dismissing the tab selector should not kill the work.
- **The Logs view is behind Developer mode again.** The debug ring buffer is recorded unconditionally and holds tool arguments, URLs and page text. `docs/SECURITY.md` now documents that buffer *and* the conversation written to `chrome.storage.local`, which §2.4 previously did not mention.
- **End-of-turn counts are honest.** Only the model's own tool results count. Continue's page refresh and placeholders for interrupted calls stay visible in the transcript but no longer inflate the score.

## Correctness and cost

- `budgetHistory` tracks its estimate incrementally instead of re-stringifying the whole history each pass — the budget goes up to 200k.
- One `idleMs` constant for the header and idle-stream deadlines, which must not drift apart.
- Switching provider now warns before discarding favourites and Ask/Act defaults.
- Focus composer opens the panel if it is closed.
- Dropped the dead `formatLogs`; the diagnostic export keeps a few shape-checked enum fields such as `finishReason`.

## Testing

Playwright is a real devDependency instead of a `PLAYWRIGHT_DIR` pointing at an unrelated global install — which is what broke it. Worth recording why the binary is unavoidable: **stable Chrome no longer honours `--load-extension`.** Verified on Chrome 152 headful and headless, with `--enable-unsafe-extension-debugging` and `--enable-automation`; the extension never loads and its computed ID returns `ERR_BLOCKED_BY_CLIENT`. The browser suites therefore need Playwright's Chromium build specifically, and the README says so.

`test/unit.cjs` gains coverage for the refresh-counting and truncation fixes.

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| `typecheck` / `build` | clean |
| `test:unit` | 8/8 |
| `test:e2e` | 12/12 |
| `test:resilience` | 12/12 |
| `test:quality` | 18/18 |

## Not addressed here

`npm audit` reports a pre-existing high-severity advisory in `sharp` (used only by `npm run icons`). The fix is a breaking major bump, so it is left for its own change.

body:
## Qué

**I-394.** Las dos acciones de cada cuenta del menor —«Inactivar» y «Quitar de mi lista»— se documentaban (comentarios, `aria-label`, `title`) como un **flag GLOBAL compartido que «también afecta al otro padre»**. Es **falso**: **SPEC-339 (D-4, 31-08) eliminó ese modelo** — cada padre tiene SU ficha (`Hijo.usuarioId`), sus interruptores y sus avisos.

Verificado en la fuente:
- `cambiarEstadoIdentificador` (`hijos.ts`) toca la fila de **ESE** padre (`exigirDueno`).
- `notificarHijosSiCorresponde` (`notificaciones.ts`) avisa **por fila / por padre**: desactivar tu identificador silencia **solo tus** avisos; la fila del otro padre sigue matcheando.

⇒ **Ambas acciones son LOCALES al padre; ninguna toca al otro.** La "catástrofe" (un clic deja al menor sin vigilancia para ambos) era el **defecto pre-339** que D-4 cerró.

## Alcance de esta PR: SOLO decir la verdad

Se elimina la afirmación falsa. **No se toca el diseño visible** — los labels nuevos («pausa y conserva» / «saca y BORRA»), el color (`hover:text-rubi` en «Quitar» viola «nunca rojo» / D-120) y las advertencias **esperan el re-corte de Diseño**.

Cambios, todos texto/comentario (sin cambio de conducta):
- **`aria-label` del botón: quita «para todos»** — es *lo que escucha una persona ciega*, y le afirmaba un alcance global que no ocurre; se quita el `title` falso.
- Comentarios stale de alcance global → verdad post-339: `hijos.ts:342`, `MisHijos.tsx` (docblock + handler), `HijoCard.tsx` (ambos botones), `route.ts` (PATCH y DELETE).
- `MisHijos.test.tsx`: `getByLabelText` sin «para todos» + comentarios/título del test al día (ya no dicen «global»).

## Por qué la limpieza es parte del arreglo
La raíz fue una **contradicción viva**: `hijos.ts:16` dice «**era** un flag global» (pasado, correcto) y `:342` decía «flag global compartido» (presente, falso). Quien llegó con la hipótesis se quedó con la mitad que la confirmaba. Mientras esos comentarios vivan, el próximo los cree igual — no es deuda de doc, es una trampa cargada.

## Verificación
- `tsc`, `eslint`, `arch:check` VERDE, `tokens:check` — verde.
- `MisHijos.test.tsx` 12/12. Sin cambio de conducta (el invariante per-padre ya lo cubre `notificaciones.test.ts`).

## Nota (fuera de alcance, señalada para seguimiento)
`hijos.ts:295` (`agregarIdentificador`) dice «El identificador es compartido entre los dos padres» y usa `IdentificadorHijoDesvinculado`, que el docblock de SPEC-339 declara «sin uso». Posible contradicción viva aparte — la dejo señalada, no la toco en esta PR acotada.

**Firmas: Datos + Diseño.**

author: chrimerss
body:
Follow-up to #36 (wflow_sbm). #36 was merged before anyone had read Copilot's review of it. This PR answers that review, wires the withdrawal prescribed by the new `mass/human-abstraction` probe (#32) into Wflow's own water demand, and answers the two reviews this PR itself received: an independent review and Copilot.

The adapter is now `1.0.4-ht.4`, and all 20 probes were re-run on the gate seeds.

## Review responses: Copilot on #36

| Comment | What changed |
| --- | --- |
| `gw = 0.0` fabricates a state | `gw` is no longer emitted. The sbm model type has no store below the soil column, and the README and `run.json` (`not_reported.gw`) say so. The evaluation skill's rule on stores a model lacks now matches AGENTS.md. |
| "every value used is written to `run.json`" was untrue | `run.json` now carries `wflow_model_options` and `wflow_parameters`, both read back from the built model, and `wflow_code_constants`. The constants include the kinematic-wave discharge floor of 1.0e-30 m3/s. |
| the `/tmp` wording contradicted itself | It now says what can write to `/tmp` (the first Julia depot, and the adapter's scratch schematisation) and what does in practice. `/tmp` was empty after every run. |
| proposer credited by handle only | Yuanhang Liu (Independent Researcher). A confirmation request is on #20. |

## The withdrawal, through Wflow's own code

- **Trigger:** when the forcing has an `abstr` column, the adapter turns on Wflow v1.0.4's domestic water demand, with gross = net = `abstr`, so there is no return flow.
- **Allocation:** Wflow takes the water first from the river cell (up to 0.80 of its storage), then from the saturated store (up to 0.75 of the subsurface storage). Both fractions are Wflow code constants.
- **`gwex`:** the allocated volumes are declared as negative `gwex`.
- **Result:** `mass/human-abstraction` PASS. The withdrawal is accounted for at 0.992, 0.989 and 0.990 of the 380 mm prescribed (residuals 0.81, 1.07 and 0.97 %, limit 5 %).
- **Configuration check:** at zero withdrawal, catchment-closure and dry-down reproduce the pre-wiring build's tables byte for byte, both without the column and with an all-zero column. The two variants of the probe therefore run the same configuration.
- **Delivery gap, now labelled in `run.json`:**
  - The river's allocated share (4.7–5.6 mm) is what Wflow's allocation records. The kinematic wave cannot deliver all of it at its discharge floor.
  - `run.json` now calls the volumes `allocated_surface_water_mm` and `allocated_groundwater_mm`, and adds `river_balance_error_mm`, the part of the river abstraction the wave did not deliver.
  - That gap is the whole 3–4 mm human-abstraction residual. It is not netted into `gwex`: that would declare a Wflow numerical error as an exchange.
- **Shortfalls:** unmet demand is reported, never forced. The unclamped `abstr` total and any ignored negative prescription are recorded.

## Copilot's review of this PR: two claims tested and refuted

- **"Pre-multiplying `abstr` by `dt_days` converts twice at PT1H."**
  - Test: a 72-hour case at 2.4 mm/day prescribes 7.2 mm. Σ(−`gwex` × dt) came out at 7.200000 mm; against the same hours with no column, ET, runoff and storage fall by 7.199 mm together.
  - Source: the demand forcing is written raw, in `mm dt-1` (`io.jl:158-159`, `standard_name.jl:258-261`). The `dt/BASETIMESTEP` factor applies only to the static value read when the model is built (`water_demand.jl:59,68`). No change was made.
- **"Domestic demand must be mapped under `[input.cyclic]`, so the withdrawal never updates."** `run_timestep!` calls `load_dynamic_input!` (`Wflow.jl:289`). That always runs `update_forcing!`, and runs `update_cyclic!` only when a cyclic table exists (`io.jl:180-184`). Entries of `config.input.forcing` (`io.jl:562`) update their field every step, which the archived −380 mm of `gwex` also shows. No change was made; the README cites these lines.
- **Byte-identity claim:** now scoped to the pre-wiring ht.3 build, which has the same columns.
- **"Switched off" list said all water demand was off:** now qualified with the domestic-withdrawal exception.
- **Archive detail for human-abstraction shows the closure residual:** the harness's `report._detail` does this for every model, so it is out of scope here and flagged as its own task.

## Result

### HydroTuring `wflow_sbm` v1.0.4-ht.4

**FAIL** (VIOLATION) · 15/20 probes passed · suite 0.1.0 · gate seeds, full record

| Probe | Verdict | Reason | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| three energy-flux probes | N/A | INCOMPLETE | does not report `hfls`, `hfss`, `hfg`; not scored |
| `mass/antecedent-monotonicity` | FAIL | VIOLATION | the 60 mm storm ran off +0.1 mm more on the wetter catchment; at least 0.02 of the storm expected |
| `mass/dry-down` | FAIL | VIOLATION | runoff rose 3.6 % between 7-day blocks 6 and 7 with no rain |
| `mass/human-abstraction` | **PASS** | OK | 0.989–0.992 of the prescribed withdrawal accounted for |
| the other 14 probes | PASS | OK | unchanged from `1.0.4-ht.2` |

**Changed against `main`:**
- `mass/human-abstraction` moves from VIOLATION to PASS.
- The contract row no longer lists `gw`.
- The other 19 rows change only in version.

Under #44's roll-up the three energy-flux probes are N/A, and the verdict comes from the 17 scored probes. A full `ht run --gate-seeds` on the merged harness agrees with every archived wflow_sbm verdict.

## Checks

- **Archive:** against `main`, `models/result.csv` changes only wflow_sbm's 21 rows; every other line is byte-identical and in order.
- **Gates:** `ht validate`, `ht gate` and `pytest` (381 passed) are green, with no CRLF.
- **Scope:** `src/`, `tests/` and `probes/` are untouched.
- **Base:** the branch contains `main` through #44 and #47 (`af33d9a`). The conflicts with summa's neighbouring rows, and with #44's restated standings, are resolved. The three energy rows were rewritten by the new harness at `1.0.4-ht.4`. `SKILL.md` keeps both edits: a store the model lacks is left out and named under `not_reported`, and a probe needing a flux the model lacks is N/A.

body:
## Summary

- Tapping a word inside an open line to hear its pronunciation cancels whatever line audio was playing, but the reader never found out about it - it only cleared its "currently speaking" state when audio ended naturally. That left the tapped line's "hear this line" button stuck showing "Stop" even though nothing was playing, so the first tap after looking up a word did nothing and it took an extra tap to recover.
- `speak()` now tells the previous request when it has been superseded mid-flight by a new one (a distinct `onInterrupted` callback, separate from `onEnd`), so the reader can reset its UI state immediately. A continuous read-aloud session does not skip ahead over text the reader never actually heard, since interruption is never treated as that line finishing.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` - clean
- [x] `npm run build` - clean production build
- [x] Playwright against a local production server: opened a line, started "hear this line" (mid-flight, before the mocked `/api/tts` call resolves), tapped a word inside it to trigger its own pronunciation, then confirmed the line's button correctly reset to "Hear this line" and replaying it fired a new audio request
- [x] Confirmed the test actually catches the bug: reverted the fix, rebuilt, reran the same script - button was stuck on "Stop" and never recovered, exactly matching the reported behavior. Restored the fix and reran - passed.

body:
## Summary

The Demo tour promised five recorded chapters with reproducible setup, but the repository only documented the workflow. This adds `scripts/demo-recorder/` as the canonical regeneration tool, pins the recording toolchain, and commits regenerated media.

## Root cause (issue #37)

`DEMO_WORKFLOW.md` described preparation, encoding, and verification but shipped no executable recorder and no deterministic fixtures, so future agents and humans could not reproduce the clips from a clean checkout.

## What changed

- `scripts/demo-recorder.ts`: entry point with `--chapter <slug|all> --output-dir <dir>` plus `--base-url`, `--force`, `--headed`, `--keep-raw`, `--contact-sheets`, `--trace`, `--dry-run`, `--help`.
- `scripts/demo-recorder/chapters.ts`: one function per chapter with captions, accessible-control locators, poster moments, exact-length trims; a `ChapterDriver` whose `openPanel`, `closePanels`, `selectPlayer`, `pick`, `paletteAction`, `tapField`, `download` helpers handle the compact (960 px) layout's overlay drawers.
- `scripts/demo-recorder/interactions.ts`: bounded state-confirmed retries and a nonblocking attribute probe so server-rendered controls attached after React hydration do not lose clicks.
- `scripts/demo-recorder/runtime.ts`: disposable Chromium profile, fresh Playwright video dir, per-chapter encoding with manifest-duration trim and PTS reset, ffprobe verification, staging-then-publish, contact sheets, classified failure output, failure screenshots.
- `scripts/demo-recorder/media.ts`: pure asset-contract checks (960×540, silent, 6–12 s, codecs, >1 KB, <1,250,000 set).
- `scripts/demo-recorder/fixtures.ts`: stable fictional Riverside Otters plays, playbook, team, and per-chapter starting draft seeded only into the app's own storage keys (`ffpd.draft.v1`, `ffpd.plays.v2`, `ffpd.playbooks.v1`, `ffpd.team.v1`, `ffpd.first-use.v1`).
- `scripts/demo-recorder/{interactions,media,options,fixtures}.test.ts`: 17 focused unit tests.
- `DEMO_WORKFLOW.md`: integrates the recorder instructions with the original desktop / 390×844 mobile / Safari / Offline ready / Offline updating / shared-offline-URL verification checklist.
- `package.json`, `bun.lock`: pins `@playwright/test` exactly to `1.63.0`; adds `demo:setup` and `demo:record` scripts.
- `public/demos/*.{webm,mp4,webp}` (15 files): regenerated by the completed recorder.

## Verification

| `bun test scripts/demo-recorder` | 17 pass, 0 fail |
| `bun test` (full) | 189 pass, 0 fail |

| `git diff --check` | clean |
| `bun run demo:record --chapter all --output-dir /tmp/.../dry-run --dry-run` | exit 0, profile created+removed |
| `bun run demo:record --chapter build-play --output-dir /tmp/.../single --contact-sheets` | exit 0 |
| All-chapter run #1 | exit 0, 1,144,846 bytes |
| All-chapter run #2 (independent profile) | exit 0, 1,123,358 bytes |

## Acceptance criteria coverage

author: yuta-yoshinaga
body:
Closes #7304

## 何が問題だったか

`KlaverjasPage.tsx:429` は固定文言しか渡していませんでした:

```tsx
restrictedTooltip={t('playButton')}
```

Klaverjas の `validatePlay` は**マストフォロー / 切り札強制 / 追い越し義務**という 3 段階の制約を持つ、このリポジトリでも屈指の複雑なプレイ規則です。それなのに制限中の札にフォーカスしても「出す」としか出ず、**どの規則で弾かれたのか区別できません**でした。`ScartoPage.tsx` / `FrenchTarotPage.tsx` は既に `cardTitleFor` で理由を出しています。

## 実装

判定を純関数 `frontend/src/utils/klaverjasPlayRestriction.ts` に切り出しました。

**`validatePlay` の順序をそのまま守っています。** 1 枚の札が複数の規則に該当し得るので、**順序が違うとサーバが返すのとは違う理由が出ます**:

1. リードスートを持っていれば従う → `followSuit`
2. ボイドで切り札を持っていれば切り札 → `mustTrump`
3. 切り札を出すなら追い越せるなら追い越す → `mustOvertrump`

TSDoc に **`internal/domain/Klaverjas.go:307-331` と対**であることと、規則を変えるときは両方直すことを明記しています。

### 切り札の強さは推測していません

Klaverjas の切り札は通常のランク順ではありません。`Klaverjas.go:431-448` の `trumpStrength` を読んで写しました:

| 札 | J | 9 | A | 10 | K | Q | 8 | 7 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 強さ | 8 | 7 | 6 | 5 | 4 | 3 | 2 | 1 |

スート番号の対応（1=Spade, 2=Clover, 3=Heart, 4=Diamond）も `internal/domain/Card.go:8-11` で確認しました。既存の Klaverjas 用の強さ表は `frontend/src/utils/` に無く、これが最初の TS 実装です。

### 出せる札には理由を出しません

```tsx
if (state.playableIndices.includes(idx)) return undefined;
```

Scarto が #6236 で踏んだ罠と同じで、**出せる札に「出せない理由」が付くと一覧と食い違います**。

文言は ja がドメインのエラー文言と一字一句同じです（`リードスートに従ってください` / `切り札を出してください` / `より強い切り札で追い越してください`）。

`PlayerHandSection.tsx` は共有部品なので変更していません。`internal/domain/Klaverjas.go` も変更していません。

## テスト

純関数側:
- 3 つの理由それぞれ
- **複数該当する状況でドメインと同じ優先順位の理由が返ること**
- リード時（トリックが空）は `undefined`
- **出せる札には `undefined`**（否定対照）

ページ側は受け入れ条件の 3 パターン + 出せる札に理由が出ない否定対照。

34 passed / `bun run check` / `bun run typecheck` すべて成功。

## 余談（この PR の範囲外）

`validatePlay` は `NewDomainError(ErrInvalidPlay, "リードスートに従ってください")` と**日本語をハードコード**しており、英語ロケールでも日本語が出ます。Easthaven の #7301（PR #7577）と同じ形なので、そちらのパターンが定着したら別 issue にします。

body:
Two things you noticed on the device, written down where they can be decided rather than re-noticed.

**One domain has a `+` and two do not.** `/training` has the floating `+`; `/food` puts add-a-food under the log; `/weight` has the form on the page. `DESIGN.md` §10.10 is why, and it is explicit that the button is "not a general licence for a FAB". That reasoning holds for weight, whose form is never off screen, and holds much less for a food day fifteen entries long. Three ways out are written down, and whichever wins, §10.10 gets the sentence that turns it back into a decision.

**The dashboard and nutrition are the same green.** They are, deliberately: `tokens.css` binds nutrition to moss, moss is merit's accent, and the dashboard is given no hue because it is where the three meet. The consequence is one colour carrying two meanings on one screen. The cheapest fix is not a new nutrition hue, it is taking accent off the dashboard chrome so the green there means nutrition and nothing else; the honest one is giving nutrition its own colour and keeping moss for merit, which costs a fourth hue that has to clear AA on three planes in both themes.

Documentation only. No code, no behaviour.

body:
Row #1 of [`TODO/20260910-24-day-sharded-ledgers-plan.md`](TODO/20260910-24-day-sharded-ledgers-plan.md) - "One answer to what a day file is, and what a day window costs".

**No collection changes grain here and no file under `state/` is touched.** This row moves one walk into a module of its own, renames the page that describes it, and takes the measurement the rest of the plan is priced against.

## The measurement, and it does not fire ESCALATE trigger 3

`backend/utilities/measure_day_window.py` builds a 120-day sight ledger at both grains from one row list, then reads a 90-day window from each, **interleaved in one process** - month, day, month, day - because a stopwatch here measures the page cache as much as the code.

| Arm | Files opened | Rows read | Median | Spread |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| month | 4 | 312,048 | 2,826.9 ms | 638.7 ms |
| day | 91 | 286,832 | 2,727.8 ms | 499.3 ms |

The day arm opens **87 more files** and reads **25,216 fewer rows** - 8.1 percent of what the month arm reads, every one of them a day outside the window. The day arm's median is **99.1 ms faster, 3.5 percent**, and both spreads are bigger than that gap, so **the clock does not separate the two layouts**.

**Trigger 3 fires when the day arm is SLOWER by more than its own spread. It is not slower.** The two numbers that have no spread both favour the day grain.

Taken 2026-09-11 on an Intel Core i7-1265U (10 cores, 12 threads), Windows 11 26200, CPython 3.14.2, 9 passes an arm, nothing else heavy on the box. `state/seen/` is the narrowest of the five row shapes at 118.5 bytes a row, so this is the arm least favourable to the day grain - which is why it is the one measured. The full record is [`docs/reference/benchmarks/2026-09-11-day-window-read.md`](docs/reference/benchmarks/2026-09-11-day-window-read.md); the instrument log carries the figure and a link.

## The structural finding

`ledger._day_files` matched a path segment with `re.fullmatch(r"\d{2}", ...)`. **`\d` matches another script's numerals**, so the walk accepted a day stem in Arabic-Indic digits and the refusal came from `date.fromisoformat` one level further down - the exact "a detail of the parser is not a rule" `month_partition.is_month_stem` was written to close, one grain over. Verified on CPython 3.14.2: `re.fullmatch(r"\d{2}", "\u0660\u0667")` matches and `date.fromisoformat("2026-09-\u0660\u0667")` raises.

`day_partition` writes the clause out. On every input the old walk reached, the answer is identical. **One input it did not reach**: an EMPTY month directory named in another script's digits. The old walk stepped into it, found nothing to refuse, yielded nothing, and the stray survived every read - in a tree whose entire rule is that nothing is tolerated. `test_an_empty_month_directory_that_is_not_ascii_digits_is_refused` is that case.

## The oracle

`backend/tests/test_day_partition.py` drives **every reader of a `<YYYY>/<MM>/<DD>.csv` tree under `state/`** - `day_partition.day_files`, `ledger.load_published` on its unbounded cover, and `ledger.load_visual_prunes` - over one built tree holding `2026/09/07.csv`, and then over that tree again with each of `2026/13/01.csv`, `2026/09/32.csv`, a day stem in Arabic-Indic digits, and a `notes.txt`. All three name the same one day; all three raise on the same four, plus the empty-directory case. 22 tests.

The good day file is written by the ledger's **own writer**, so the assertion is that the reader and the writer agree about the layout rather than that both agree with a third copy of it in a test.

## Rulings taken, and who ruled

Fowler was dispatched on two calls (`.github/agents/fowler.agent.md`).

1. **`oldest_day_kept` is NOT in this row.** The row's Scope named "which day an age in months keeps" as a fourth responsibility. It has no caller until rows #5 to #8, which are four singleton groups - so exactly one lands first and writes it with its caller in the same commit, and Fowler ruled it belongs beside `month_partition.oldest_month_kept` because the boundary stays a month and a month-anchored boundary is not what a day tree is. The Scope sentence is corrected in this PR. **What the next worker loses: whoever takes the first of rows #5 to #8 carries one extra function and its test.**
2. **`tests/fixtures/day-partition/` is dropped.** The month twin already builds its trees in `tmp_path` from constants (`test_retention.py`, `NOT_MONTHS` / `OTHER_STRAYS`, Arabic-Indic stem included), so this test does the same. Rule #7 is satisfied by real directories and a real walk, and no non-ASCII filename is committed (`CLAUDE.md` section 5). **What is lost: the case list is not readable without opening the Python.**

## Facts the plan handed this row, re-measured

| Fact the plan carried | On the tree at `03c130c9` | Moved? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 14 links in 7 files | 14 links in 7 files | **No** - held exactly |
| 36 mentions in 11 files | **39 mentions in 12 files** | **Yes** - `TODO/20260911-execution-order.md` was written after the plan and names the page twice |
| `day_partition.py` "written by no other" row | Row #7's own `Files touched` names it | **Yes** - the plan contradicted itself |
| Oracle drives "every day-tree reader in the repository" | Two day walks exist and they disagree by design | **Yes** - `retention._dated_days` reads day DIRECTORIES under `frontend/public/digest/` and skips a stray at its root; driven over a CSV tree it would refuse the good file too |
| `_day_files` on 4 lines, `_refuse_stray` on 6, `_days_in_window` on 2 | Same | No |
| seen ledger 64,315 rows / 19 days | **67,205 rows / 20 days** | **Yes**, and by design - the pipeline appends several times a day |

All four plan-doc corrections are in this PR, in the row that carried them.

## Four wrong facts on the pages this row touches

| Page | What it said | What the tree says |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `docs/concepts/partitions.md` | "Two collections partition by day" | **Four** do: the published digest tree, `state/published/`, `state/day-metrics/`, `state/visual-prunes/` |
| `docs/concepts/partitions.md` | `state/visual-prunes.csv`, listed under "What is not partitioned" | It is `state/visual-prunes/<YYYY>/<MM>/<DD>.csv` and has been since before this row |
| `docs/architecture/contracts/schemas.md` | the same stale flat-file row, and no row for `state/day-metrics/` or `state/day-validations.csv` | both exist |
| `TODO/20260911-execution-order.md` | the growing-reads plan carries "seven of the seventeen links" | **four of the fourteen** |

Row #1 decision 5 is also done: the four single files are now named in `schemas.md` as **deliberately unsharded**, with the reason, and with the note that two of them growing for ever is a retention question rather than a grain question.

## Scope widened, and why

- **`TODO/20260911-execution-order.md`** - it names the renamed page twice and carried the wrong link count.
- **`docs/reference/benchmarks/2026-09-11-day-window-read.md`** - `docs/reference/measurements.md` and `docs/reference/documentation-structure.md` (routing rule 9) both refuse a two-arm race as an append to the instrument log. The log carries the figure in force and links to the record. **This row therefore creates `docs/reference/benchmarks/`**, which plan 23 row #P5 and plan 26 row #1 both claim to create first - a defect `20260911-execution-order.md` already named, and its note is updated here so both rows know.

**Group A re-checked after the widening.** Row #2 writes `backend/idhazh/evals/writer.py`, `backend/idhazh/cli.py`, `backend/tests/test_evals.py`, `tests/fixtures/evals/index-rebuild/` and `docs/concepts/evaluation.md`. No new file is shared. The derived file-set table in section 1 is updated; **the Status Reckoner is untouched.**

## `publish_telemetry.py`, which is also row #4's file

**One line changed: a docstring that named `docs/concepts/month-partitions.md`.** Nothing else in that module is touched - no behaviour, no signature, n

author: iuoamc-official
body:
## Outcome

Adds a secure, trilingual self-service account portal for members and certificate recipients while preserving a strict administrative boundary around `/control`.

## User experience

- Public account registration, login, email verification, password recovery, and password reset.
- Responsive Arabic, English, and French account interface.
- One account view for profile, memberships, membership cards/certificates, professional certificates, documents, invoices, and receipts.
- Verified users can submit membership applications with identity details and a private portrait upload.
- Direct account-menu links to profile, memberships, certificates, and documents.
- Stable internal user reference for later accounting integration.

## Security boundary

- Registration creates an active role-less account and never grants control permissions.
- Every `/control` route now requires explicit role/permission-backed control access.
- The administration link is rendered only for authorized users.
- Account data is linked by an HMAC of the verified email; plaintext email is not stored in the ownership projection.
- Every download revalidates current ownership and underlying record/file integrity.
- Corrupt encrypted contacts fail closed.
- Private pages and downloads use no-store/noindex/no-referrer headers.
- Membership application data and photos remain encrypted/private and still require administrative approval before issuance.

## Account documents

- Adds immutable, organization-scoped PDF document/invoice/receipt records.
- Private file storage, SHA-256 file digest, sealed record hash, and institutional audit trail.
- New `account-documents.view` and `account-documents.manage` permissions, granted initially only to super-admin.

## Verification

- PHP AST parsing completed locally for all application PHP sources.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Added feature tests for control isolation, email-verification enforcement, and cross-account download denial.
- Added unit coverage for normalized-email HMAC behavior.

## Deployment requirements

Run the new migration, rebuild Laravel caches, reload PHP-FPM, and verify that the production mail transport is configured before enabling registrations.

Explicit saves and OAuth edits followed by authorization now enable the existing local-precedence preference after both OAuth clients are persisted. Unchanged sign-in/connect actions leave deployment precedence intact. Invalid saves and storage failures are surfaced without claiming success or changing precedence. Explicit config imports and re-enabling deployment defaults remain supported. Existing Drive runtime URL preservation follows the same policy.

Validation:
- Reproduced on a production build of main: save `email`, refresh, and observe it disappear. Verified the fixed production build retains it across two refreshes.
- All 1,457 app tests pass; required Runme build/test tasks pass. Type-check diagnostics match the existing baseline (128, none added).
- Added UI save/validation/authorization tests, real quota-failure and retry tests, singleton-reload/startup integration coverage, and a browser CUJ that forces production precedence, checks both visible and runtime scopes after two reloads, and restores deployment defaults.

The browser suite also needed a Jupyter recorder startup correction: wait for React mount, then start a fresh recording. Two CI runs produced zero video frames when restarting immediately after navigation, despite passing the notebook assertions. Video assertions remain enabled.

Final validation: all 12 browser scenarios passed on 88d6350, including all six authentication assertions and all 19 Jupyter assertions. Inspected the saved-scope screenshot and repaired Jupyter recording. [CI artifacts](https://storage.googleapis.com/runme-dev-assets/cuj-runs/runmedev-web/34651150240/1/index.html). author: jcnm
body:
L'image Docker du gateway ne compile plus depuis le merge de #6093 ([run 34646732312](https://github.com/isopen-io/meeshy/actions/runs/34646732312)). Cette PR la répare.

## La cause

`LINK_ADMISSION_MEDIA_RIGHTS_CANDIDATE_WHERE` était figé par `as const`. Son `OR` devenait donc un tuple **`readonly`**, inassignable au `ParticipantWhereInput[]` **mutable** qu'attend Prisma — deux `TS2345`, aux deux sites d'appel de `findMany`.

## Pourquoi rien ne l'avait dit

Les suites ciblées passent ce filtre à un **faux Prisma en mémoire**, qui accepte n'importe quelle forme : elles vérifient la DÉCISION du rattrapage, pas la validité de sa requête. Seul le `tsc` complet — celui que lance le `Dockerfile` — confronte ce littéral au type réel du client généré. La réserve était d'ailleurs écrite noir sur blanc dans le rapport de #6091 (« le `where` n'a été validé que contre un faux Prisma ») ; elle s'est réalisée au premier build d'image.

Ma part, sans détour : j'ai fusionné #6093 sur la foi de suites Jest ciblées sans passer `tsc` sur l'ensemble du gateway. **Un lot qui ajoute une requête Prisma se vérifie au compilateur, pas seulement au test** — le test peut mentir sur la forme d'une requête, le compilateur non.

## Le correctif

Le type vient maintenant de `findMany` lui-même :

```ts
type ParticipantFindManyWhere = NonNullable<
  NonNullable<Parameters<PrismaClient['participant']['findMany']>[0]>['where']
>;
```

Ce n'est pas un contournement de l'erreur — `as const` la masquait en fabriquant un type que Prisma n'avait jamais validé. L'annotation **rend la vérification au compilateur** : toute évolution future de ce filtre sera confrontée au schéma réel.

## Preuve

- **RED** : `bun run tsc --noEmit` sort **2**, deux `TS2345` nommant `linkAdmissionMediaRightsBackfill.ts`.
- **GREEN** : `bun run tsc --noEmit` sort **0**, journal **vide**.
- Suites `link-admission` : **4 suites, 67 tests**, 0 échec.

Refs #6091

author: helix4u
body:
## What does this PR do?

Use the authenticated Copilot ACP session as the first model-catalog source for the `copilot-acp` picker.

Copilot CLI can keep its login in an OS credential store without exposing a reusable token to Hermes. In that setup, token-based GitHub model discovery returns nothing and Hermes falls back to its static catalog, even though `session/new` from the signed-in ACP process advertises the models enabled for that account. The session model options are already the authority used when applying a selected model, so using the same response for discovery keeps the picker and runtime selection on one contract.

The probe is short-lived and closes the ACP process after `session/new`. It does not allow filesystem requests during discovery. If the ACP probe is unavailable or fails, the existing GitHub API discovery and static fallback behavior remain unchanged.

## Related Issue

No linked issue.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] Security fix
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- Add a reusable short-lived ACP session context and model-list discovery to `agent/copilot_acp_client.py`.
- Prefer authenticated ACP session models for the local `copilot-acp` picker in `hermes_cli/models.py`.
- Deny ACP file access while the picker is only discovering models.
- Preserve token-based GitHub discovery and the static model list as fallbacks.
- Add subprocess and picker-level regressions for enabled-model filtering, cleanup, file-request denial, tokenless discovery, and fallback behavior.

## How to Test

1. Sign in with Copilot CLI on a platform where the login is stored outside plaintext Copilot config.
2. Open the Hermes model picker and select `copilot-acp`.
3. Confirm the picker shows the enabled model options returned by the signed-in ACP session instead of the static fallback list.

Focused automated verification on Windows 11:

```text
python -m pytest tests/agent/test_copilot_acp_client.py tests/hermes_cli/test_copilot_in_model_list.py -q
25 passed in 11.99s

python -m ruff check agent/copilot_acp_client.py hermes_cli/models.py tests/agent/test_copilot_acp_client.py tests/hermes_cli/test_copilot_in_model_list.py
All checks passed!
```

The picker regression was also neutralized locally by bypassing ACP session discovery. It failed against the old static list and passed again after restoring the change.

body:
## Summary

Implements #654 D1, D2, D6 and D7 — the beekeeper's standard ("we work from axioms, the fewer the better, preferably zero; we only change an axiom because we have proven that it must") mechanised as a **gate, not a ratchet** (PATTERN-02).

| Deliverable | What landed |
|---|---|
| **D1 root GATE** | `scripts/root_audit.py`: every root (AXIOM-/POST-/META-/INTERP-) must sort into a four-bucket exit — PROVED (`forced_by` PROOF-*), FORCED (`forced_by` MEAS-* or `decision_state: ruled` + a JamesPagetButler/* cite), OPEN (`kill_condition` + open), RETIRED — or be an itemised, issue-linked entry in the shrink-only `docs/cth/root-audit-register.json`. A root-prefixed id in any non-root list is a smuggled root (no carve-out). No baseline file exists (tested). |
| **D2 chain-to-root** | Every chain must resolve (gated for every owner); every derived chain (principles / DERIV-* / PRED-*) must terminate in {root, PROOF, MEAS, experimental anchor}; seen-set cycle check. Other kinds are reported, not gated, because they carry no derivation obligation, never because they are many. |
| **D6 retro report** | `docs/cth/root-audit-report-2026-09-11.md` — the honest root list and every chain problem on the live ledger. |
| **D7 encoders** | `scripts/cth_ledger_edit.py`: the only sanctioned ledger writer — declares every record touched, proves the write is confined, refuses silent no-ops and formatting noise. Guard test: no top-level `scripts/*.py` writes the ledger directly. The eight applied one-shot encoders move unmodified to `scripts/applied-encoders/` (history). The pending `encode_ruling_bundle.py` is refactored onto the helper on `research/encode-bundle` (dry-run confinement proven). |
| CI | New gate step in `inverse-anchor-audit.yml`. |
| Tests | `tests/test_root_audit.py` (12) + `tests/test_cth_ledger_edit.py` (8), incl. the adversarial plants qbp-implementor asked for. |

## First honest run (ledger v5.4.0)

| Population | Result |
|---|---|
| Roots | 3 (META-1, AXIOM-1, AXIOM-2) — all UNSORTED → registered: #655, #647, #473 |
| Smuggled roots | 2 (`META-*-field` doc anchors) → registered: #657 |
| Chain ids cited but never encoded | 16 (INST-f0, DERIV-slater/tpd/teff/rge/ie…, PROOF-koide, PROOF-stabiliser-order-24) → registered: #656 |
| Derived chains that do not terminate | 18 → registered: #656 |
| Reported only (no derivation obligation) | 67 owners, enumerated in the report |

The register is a burn-down list on the clock: a fixed-but-still-listed entry HARD-FAILS, and adding an entry is a visible reviewed commit with an issue, never a CI-driven bump.

## Assumptions stated

- The eight applied encoders are archived, not refactored: each ran once and its PR is cited in the ledger changelog; refactoring dead scripts cannot be tested. The guard enforces the rule for every future encoder. Say the word and I refactor them instead.
- AXIOM-2's register entry goes stale (and is removed) in the encode PR that retires it.

## Review record

- Spec dovetailed on live-test: @qbp-implementor 1293/1296/1308/1310 (**APPROVE** at script level: gate-not-ratchet, whole-population, no baseline, register shrink-only + issue-linked, forcing must resolve, four-bucket labels); @cth-implementor 1297/1302 (D3 schema surface = `decision_state` + `kill_condition` only, later); @qbp-architecture 1292/1303 (D4 = MO §10b + `inter/decision-boundary.md`, pending the beekeeper's ratification).

## Test plan

- [ ] `python3 scripts/root_audit.py` → PASS on this head
- [ ] `python3 -m pytest tests/test_root_audit.py tests/test_cth_ledger_edit.py` → 20 passed
- [ ] `python3 scripts/check_anchor_manifest.py` and `anchor_inverse_audit.py --check` unchanged (PASS)

author: russfranky
body:
The production verification of #95 found that the Sheet and scene inherited the global monochrome dark theme: their computed primary token was `oklch(98.5% 0 0)`. The existing Portal selector covered a descendant `.dark`, while the new portaled roots carry both classes on the same element.

This PR adds `.hubzz-profile-panel-theme.dark` and keeps the Portal palette scoped to its own roots. Restoring that palette exposed insufficient contrast in the existing small-text and solid-button tones: the first CI run passed 469 tests but failed the Portal axe check in all three browsers. Reported ratios included 3.68:1 for Join and 3.96:1 for the count.

The scoped primary shade and muted-text tone now provide additional contrast while keeping the same hue and shared shadcn primitives. Calculated settled contrast is 5.26:1 for solid primary actions, 6.70:1 for muted text on the sidebar, and 5.47:1 on cards. Browser verification remains the acceptance gate.

The existing axe test waits for the panel to reach full opacity before measuring contrast. Its WCAG tags and zero-violations assertion are unchanged. No global tokens, primitive APIs, dependencies, registry entries, or workflow checks are changed.

Live dismissal, discovery, joining, HUD updates, and focus return were verified on #95. Required quality, browser/accessibility, and CodeQL checks must pass on the final head; production appearance will then be checked again.

author: jsnyder
body:
Closes #553.

## What was slow

`quorum feedback` took 7-9s wall, 6s user CPU per verdict on the production corpus. A 42-verdict batch after the #548 review took 8 minutes.

Sampling an unstripped build put 77% of main-thread samples on the `query_map(..).collect()` in `ReviewLog::resolve_finding_id`. The statement selects `review_finding_ids` by `file_path`, the table had indexes on `finding_id` and the PK only, and `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` showed `SCAN rfi`. On top of that, `run_feedback_inner` resolved the same title three times: `resolve_rule_id` resolved it internally, then the block called `resolve_finding_id` again.

## Change

- **schema v5**: `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_rfi_file_path ON review_finding_ids(file_path)`. Same shape as the v2 timestamp index.
- **`ReviewLog::rule_id_for(finding_id)`**: the rule lookup split out from `resolve_rule_id`, which now delegates to it.
- **`run_feedback_inner`** resolves once and passes the id to `rule_id_for`. With `--finding-id`, the rule lookup uses the given id instead of a fresh title match, which is the more correct behaviour anyway.

## Measured

Release binary, `QUORUM_HOME` on a copy of `~/.quorum` (13,673 `review_finding_ids` rows):

| | user CPU |
|---|---|
| as shipped | 4.7s |
| with the index | 0.5s |

## Verified

- `cargo test --lib -- storage:: review_log::` 14 passed, `cargo test --bin quorum -- feedback` 38 passed, clippy `-D warnings` clean, fmt clean.
- Mutation: replacing the `CREATE INDEX` with `SELECT 1` makes `migrate_v4_to_v5_creates_file_path_index` fail.

Not in this PR: the 40x gap between this statement in-process and from the `sqlite3` CLI is unexplained (noted on #553). The index removes the scan either way.

author: rudi193-cmd
body:
**For review, not to merge as-is.** See *Relationship to #16* below — that branch has moved past two of the files this touches, and the findings should be carried forward rather than the diffs.

`§18` blocker 3 named one gate before the lane schema could be promoted: *"Open Part III before this becomes `migrations/001_lanes.sql`."* The charter turned out to be readable — `willows-grove/governance/PROTECTED_AGENTS.md`, blob `2886a41` — so the read is done. `docs/PART-III-READ.md` is the record item 0 asks every such pass to leave behind, *"because an unverified table and a verified one look identical."*

## What the read found

**W-1, W-2 and W-6 came through the translation whole.** The structural encodings resting on them stand unchanged. W-6 is the only clause quoted complete anywhere in the tree (`records/exit.py`).

**Three did not, and all three the same way:**

| Clause | The half that was lost |
|---|---|
| **W-3** | the crossing envelope — *found 2026-07-30, repaired in `crossing.py`* |
| **W-5** | *"envelopes name the ward as co-signer for enumerated matters"* — quoted nowhere, encoded nowhere |
| **W-7** | *"resolutions accumulate as precedent the guardian may ratify into standing envelopes"* — and lost **again** inside a docstring labelled *at source* |

A clause carrying a prohibition *and* the sanctioned path through it compresses to the prohibition, and every later reader works from the compressed copy. `records/crossing.py` predicted W-5 would go this way and was right; nobody ran it down.

The two halves fail differently, which is what makes the loss expensive rather than untidy. **A dropped prohibition** means an illegitimate act is not stopped — loud, and the tests look for it. **A dropped permission** means a *legitimate* act is not representable, so the only way to serve a real case is to not record that it happened — quiet, and nothing looks for something that was never specified.

## The document was contradicting itself

`§18` blocker 3, `LANE-MODEL.md`'s provenance note, and the DDL header all said Part III had not been read at source. `§14` and `docs/FLEET-READS.md` had marked it **VERIFIED** since the same day it was first read. One document saying both, for six weeks.

And the VERIFIED rows were themselves wrong: they claimed all seven clauses were *rendered faithfully*; five were. **Presence is cheap to check and faithfulness is not, and the table did not distinguish them.** Corrected in place at all five sites, struck rather than deleted (`§16` rule 20).

## It lengthened the list

Four items opened, none enforced here:

1. **W-5's co-signature has nowhere to live.** One `signer_id`, no enumerated-matters column, and — the sharper half — **no proposed state**, so *"the steward may propose a widening… it may never enact one"* has no representation other than writing the live grant, which is enacting it.
2. **W-7's escalation halts forever.** No `Precedent` type, no ratification path. The human register is explicit about what is missing: *"watching your answers, learn to bring it to you better."*
3. **`access_grant.signer_id` may be the lane's own subject** — W-4 and I-2 at once. **Not a flat rule:** after W-6's threshold, a grant signed by the subject over their own lane is exactly how a graduate re-admits their guardian. A naive `signer_id <> subject_id` would forbid the act W-6 requires.
4. **`edge` is the one office-bearing table with no exit written at entry.** Arguable under I-3 — the DDL says an edge authorizes nothing, but W-6 says *"the threshold written into the office at entry"* and I-4 puts the office at `edge`. Either it needs an exit or the DDL should say why not; it currently says neither, which is rule 12.

## The middle, and the citation

`tests/test_clause_quotes.py` ships in the same commit (`§16` rule 12): citations must re-fetch, and a two-halved clause must be quoted whole **by the module that owns it** (scoped to the subject clause, so a module may reference a neighbour in passing). All four guards were ablated — each shown failing before being shown passing (I-12, rule 19).

The charter is **deliberately not vendored.** A copy here would be a pair whose reconciler this repository cannot build, because the authoritative `Willow` copy is not reachable.

**`c8c96b4` resolves in none of the twelve repositories reachable from this session** — §15's warning about un-refetchable citations, made concrete. `crossing.py`, `exit.py` and `conflict.py` are re-anchored on a blob that does. A dead object name may now appear only on a line that says it is dead.

## Relationship to #16

This branch is cut from `main`. #16 is far ahead of it, and the overlap needs a decision rather than a merge:

- **Superseded by #16:** the `docs/schema/001_lanes.proposed.sql` header edit (that branch has the file down to a stub and `migrations/001_lanes.sql` live), and the `§18` blocker 3 bullet, which #16 closes by promotion. **Carry the four opened items forward into `migrations/001` rather than taking these hunks.**
- **Live on both, verified:** `records/conflict.py` at `9bbc568` carries the *identical* truncated W-7 quotation and the same dead `c8c96b4` citation. The clause findings, the re-anchoring and `test_clause_quotes.py` apply to #16's head unchanged.
- **Worth reconciling:** #16 reports the `§14` pass complete at 41 of 41 verified. That pass checked *presence*. This read shows presence and faithfulness are different claims, and the row that prompted it was VERIFIED and wrong about the second. Whether the other 40 were checked for faithfulness is a question this raises and does not answer.

## For a reviewer

`docs/PART-III-READ.md` is the whole argument and is the file to read first. The finding I would most like a second opinion on is **W-7** — `records/conflict.py` is good work and the `Escalation` genuinely cannot carry an order, but the clause does not end at the halt, and whether `Precedent` is worth building is a design question left open rather than answered.

Full suite: **33 test files, all passing.** Three of those failures were mine first — the meta-tests caught a narrowed runner and an unpinned VERIFIED row before I did.
